cleaned_text: fix(crawl): surface API errors and failed pages from crawl status Summary firecrawl_check_crawl_status , and the polling inside firecrawl_crawl , read job state through the SDK's HTTP layer directly. That path has two defects: A non-2xx answer reaches the caller as the raw transport error. Checking an unknown or expired crawl ID returns Tool 'firecrawl_check_crawl_status' execution failed: Request failed with status code 404 instead of the API's Job not found . While following next links, a page that answers success: false stops the loop without an error. The call returns the pages read so far with status: "completed" and next: null , so a partial crawl looks finished. Changes Add getCoreJson , which runs a GET through the SDK's HTTP layer and raises a non-2xx answer as CoreHttpError carrying the API's error message, HTTP status and agent hints. Because the status is preserved, the existing 401 credential recovery still applies. Use it for the first status request and for every pagination request. Throw when the first response has success: false , and when a later page has success: false , instead of breaking out of the loop. Add tests/crawl-status.test.mjs with a fake API covering a two-page crawl, an unknown job, and a page that fails mid-pagination. Add a changelog entry. Test plan pnpm run build node --test tests/crawl-status.test.mjs Before the change: 3 tests, 1 pass, 2 fail ( reports the API error for an unknown crawl , fails when a result page cannot be read ). After the change: 3 tests, 3 pass. npx eslint src/index.ts and npx tsc --noEmit report no problems. The two-page test passes both before and after the change, so it guards against regressions in the join behavior. Summary by cubic Makes crawl status checks surface the API's real error messages and fail loudly when a paginated result can't be read. Previously, firecrawl_check_crawl_status (and polling inside firecrawl_crawl ) returned raw transport errors like Request failed with status code 404 for unknown jobs, and silently returned partial results as a completed crawl when a follow-up page failed. Now both cases fail with the API's own error message while preserving the HTTP status so the existing 401 credential recovery still applies. Throws CoreHttpError carrying the API's error message, status, and agent hints for non-2xx responses and for 2xx replies with success: false . Raises an error when the initial response or any paginated page returns success: false . Adds tests/crawl-status.test.mjs with a fake API covering a two-page crawl, an unknown job, a mid-pagination failure, and a first-response failure. title: Search results are cut to a 2 KB preview in Claude Code above ~50k characters
cleaned_text: Search results are cut to a 2 KB preview in Claude Code above ~50k characters Problem In Claude Code, a firecrawl_search or firecrawl_gov_search result can be replaced by a file path and a short preview before the model sees it. The model then works from roughly the first 2 KB of the results. When Claude Code runs without file tools ( claude -p --tools "" , common in automated and evaluation setups), the model cannot open the saved file, so the rest of the results are lost to it. Claude Code applies two separate checks to MCP tool output: Size check. A text result over a character threshold (about 45,000 to 52,000 characters by default) is saved to ~/.claude/projects/ / /tool-results/ and replaced with , the file path, and a 2 KB preview. MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS does not move this threshold. A tool raises it by declaring _meta["anthropic/maxResultSizeChars"] in its tools/list entry, up to a ceiling of 500,000 characters. Token check. A result over MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS (default 25,000 tokens) is replaced with an "exceeds maximum allowed tokens" message and a file path. For a tool that declares anthropic/maxResultSizeChars , text content skips this check and only the declared character limit applies. Search results with scrapeOptions (page markdown per hit), or with many hits carrying long snippets, reach these sizes easily. Sources: the Claude Code MCP docs (section on MCP output limits), and a measured write-up for Claude Code 2.1.273: https://rulestack.hashnode.dev/claude-code-s-25-000-token-mcp-limit-let-a-49-964-token-result-through-we-measured-both-checks Proposed change Declare the limit on the search tools in their addTool definitions. fastmcp 4.3.2 passes a tool's _meta through to the tools/list response: _meta: { 'anthropic/maxResultSizeChars': 500000 }, on firecrawl_search ( src/server.ts ) and firecrawl_gov_search ( src/gov.ts ), and on any other tool whose results are meant to be read whole ( firecrawl_developer_search , firecrawl_scrape ). The key is ignored by other clients. Verify Run claude -p --tools "" --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config --output-format stream-json --verbose with a firecrawl_search query using scrapeOptions: {formats: ["markdown"]} and enough results to exceed 60,000 characters. Before the change, the tool_result in the stream starts with . After it, the stream carries the full JSON. Check that tools/list returns the _meta key for each tool.

title: feat(mcp-apps): experimental inline view for Alexandria results (off by default)
cleaned_text: feat(mcp-apps): experimental inline view for Alexandria results (off by default) Spike, draft. This server returns no UI today. It adds one MCP Apps view behind a flag so we can try server-provided inline UI for Alexandria in ChatGPT and Claude. What the clients need (Oct 2026) There are two separate things called "inline UI". Model-generated: ChatGPT's GPT-6 "Intelligent UI" (launched 10-07) and Claude's in-chat visuals. The model composes charts, forms and widgets from its own component library, using whatever data it has. That data includes our tool results, so the "one prompt, something visual" demo works today with no server change. Server-provided, MCP Apps ( io.modelcontextprotocol/ui , stable 2026-01-26): ChatGPT and Claude both render it. A tool declares _meta.ui.resourceUri pointing at a ui:// resource served as text/html;profile=mcp-app . The host renders it in a sandboxed iframe and sends it the tool result over the ui/* postMessage bridge. ChatGPT also accepts openai/outputTemplate and window.openai as aliases, but recommends the standard keys. Claude's help center says it uses a connector's interactive interface when one fits, and generates its own visuals only otherwise. What this PR adds When FIRECRAWL_MCP_APPS=true is set (or mcpApps: true for createFirecrawlMcpServer embedders): firecrawl_scrape gets _meta.ui.resourceUri = "ui://firecrawl/alexandria-results.html" , added next to the existing anthropic/alwaysLoad . The server serves that resource: a self-contained HTML view with no external scripts, styles or network access, so it needs no CSP domains. The view runs the ui/initialize handshake and reads structuredContent from ui/notifications/tool-result . It renders each Alexandria call as a table (up to 50 rows and 6 scalar columns). When one column is numeric it adds a bar chart, and when a call fails it shows the error. It follows the host's theme variables and reports its size. Tool inputs, outputs and text content are unchanged, and the flag is off by default, so the contract snapshots don't change. Hosts without MCP Apps ignore _meta.ui . The screenshot comes from a local host harness that runs the real ui/initialize handshake and tool-result flow with a FRED result. It is not a ChatGPT or Claude session: testing in those needs this build deployed behind a connector. Known limits before this could leave the flag The view is bound to every firecrawl_scrape call, not just Alexandria ones. resourceUri is static per tool, so URL scrapes also get the frame, which renders empty. In Claude, that may also take the place of its own generated visual. A clean fix means splitting Alexandria execution into its own tool or switching the binding per call, which changes the public tool contract. That is a separate proposal, not part of this PR. No per-session gating yet. The spec says servers SHOULD register UI tools only when the client advertises io.modelcontextprotocol/ui . This prototype uses a process flag instead. No "Connect Firecrawl" view. An MCP App renders only after a connected server's tool is called, so it can't help a user install the server in the first place. One-click install stays with ChatGPT and Claude directory links. Tests tests/mcp-apps.test.mjs : With the flag off, the scrape tool has no ui metadata and no resources are listed. With the flag on, the tool metadata, resource list and resources/read (mime type, _meta.ui.prefersBorder , no external assets) are checked, and an Alexandria call still returns the same result. The view's table and chart extraction skips find-tools calls, flattens nested records, charts numeric columns and shows errors. tsc , lint and pnpm test (170 tests) pass locally. Summary by cubic Adds an experimental MCP Apps inline view that renders Alexandria results from firecrawl_scrape in hosts like ChatGPT and Claude. It's off by default, and tool inputs, outputs, and text content are unchanged. New Features With FIRECRAWL_MCP_APPS=true (or mcpApps: true for embedders), the scrape tool declares _meta.ui.resourceUri pointing at ui://firecrawl/alexandria-results.html . The server serves a self-contained HTML view, advertised as text/html;profile=mcp-app , that runs the ui/initialize handshake and renders each Alexandria call as a table, adds a bar chart when one column is numeric, and shows call errors. Hosts without MCP Apps support ignore the metadata; when the flag is off, tool metadata and the resource list are unchanged. Known Limits The view is attached to every firecrawl_scrape call, not just Alexandria ones, so URL scrapes render an empty frame. There's no per-session gating yet; the spec recommends registering UI tools only when a client advertises io.modelcontextprotocol/ui , whereas this uses a process flag. title: fix: make Browserbase sessions re-attachable by ID (STG-2446)
cleaned_text: fix: make Browserbase sessions re-attachable by ID (STG-2446) [!IMPORTANT] Re: STG-2446 escalation. The "No active session" failure in the ChatGPT Workspace is served by the hosted MCP in browserbase/core ( apps/stagehand-api-v3/mcp/ ), which does not use this OSS package. The escalation fix (reattach-by- sessionId , ported into the code that actually serves mcp.browserbase.com ) is browserbase/core#10363 , validated on local dev. This PR remains valuable as self-hosted / OSS parity for @browserbasehq/mcp , but it does not affect the hosted endpoint. Recommend unlinking it from STG-2446 so it doesn't auto-close the escalation on merge. Problem Users hit "No active session" when driving the Browserbase MCP server from ChatGPT: start creates a session successfully, but the follow-up navigate fails even though the session is live. Root cause: browser-session state was connection-scoped and unrecoverable . No tool accepted a session identifier. navigate / act / observe / extract all resolved their target via context.getStagehand() → SessionManager.activeSessionId . The only thing linking start → navigate was the in-process SessionManager staying alive across MCP calls, keyed by the Mcp-Session-Id transport header. On the hosted, autoscaled server ( mcp.browserbase.com ), a follow-up request can land on a different replica — or a client can rotate/drop the Mcp-Session-Id . Either way the call hits a fresh SessionManager with no record of the session start created, and getStagehand throws No session found for ID: … → surfaced to ChatGPT as "No active session." The reconnect capability already existed ( createNewBrowserSession(..., resumeSessionId) ) but was dead code — never called with a resume ID and never exposed through any tool. Fix Make sessions re-attachable by Browserbase session ID so correctness no longer depends on sticky routing: start accepts an optional sessionId to resume an existing Browserbase session (returns the id as before). navigate / act / observe / extract accept an optional sessionId , passed through to context.getStagehand(sessionId) . Omitting it preserves the existing active-session behavior. SessionManager.getSession reconnects to an unknown non-default session by ID (via the existing browserbaseSessionID resume path) instead of returning null , so any replica can rehydrate the session the client holds. Verification tsc --noEmit , eslint , and pnpm build all clean; vitest run — 17/17 pass (added schema coverage for the new sessionId param). Ran the HTTP server locally and reproduced the ChatGPT failure mode: start on transport A, then navigate on a fresh transport B (no knowledge of A) with sessionId set. Server logs confirm the reconnect path: [SessionManager] Session 78d08715-… not tracked locally, attempting to reconnect to Browserbase session. [SessionManager] Resuming Stagehand session 78d08715-… [SessionManager] Session created and active: 78d08715-… Navigation succeeded where it previously threw "No session found for ID". Note This removes the dependency on sticky routing for correctness, but the hosted transport's streamableSessions map is still per-process in-memory. title: MCP tool-surface audit: small surface, but action tools may benefit from clearer trigger/safety wording
cleaned_text: MCP tool-surface audit: small surface, but action tools may benefit from clearer trigger/safety wording Hi! I’m working on audit-mcp , a local CLI that reviews MCP tool surfaces for discoverability issues: overlapping tools, unclear primary vs follow-up actions, weak trigger language, and places where agents may not have enough signal to pick the right tool. I ran it against the current Browserbase MCP tools/list surface from this repo. This is not a bug report, just a lightweight audit/share in case useful. Summary Tools exposed: 6 Default-visible tools: 6 Average discoverability score: 80.8 CI-style verdict: pass, with warnings Top recommendation: make navigate and the action tools more explicit about when to use them and what safety/session assumptions apply. Findings that looked actionable The tool surface is already compact, which is good. The main thing the audit noticed is that several tools are intentionally short, but may be underspecified for agent selection: navigate : description is short; url input could use clearer examples or constraints. act : action input could be clearer about when to use this versus observe or extract . observe : instruction input could be clearer about expected output and when it should precede act . start / end : these are lifecycle tools, but the descriptions do not say when an agent should call them automatically versus rely on session reuse. A possible pattern: Use when: the agent needs to inspect possible interactions before taking action. Returns: actionable page elements / observations. Do not use when: the task is only to extract page data or navigate to a known URL. Safety: does not mutate the page; use before act when the next step is uncertain. For example, observe and act are naturally a progressive pair, but the current descriptions leave more of that sequencing to the model. Why I’m sharing I’m trying to learn whether MCP maintainers find this kind of tool-surface feedback useful or noisy. If this is off-base, I’d love to know. If useful, I’m especially curious whether you’d want something like this as: local CLI only warn-only CI PR comment report artifact something else

title: Claude Code plugin: .mcp.json has "url" but no "type", so the 21st MCP server is skipped
cleaned_text: Claude Code plugin: .mcp.json has "url" but no "type", so the 21st MCP server is skipped What happens On Claude Code 2.1.273, installing the plugin ( claude plugin marketplace add 21st-dev/magic-mcp , claude plugin install 21st@21st-dev ) loads the 21st-ui skill but the 21st MCP server never appears. Nothing is shown on screen; with --debug mcp Claude Code logs, at every session start: [ERROR] "Invalid MCP server config for 21st in C:\Users\ \.claude\plugins\cache\21st-dev\21st\1.0.1\.mcp.json: [ { "code": "invalid_union", "errors": [ [ { "expected": "string", "code": "invalid_type", "path": ["command"], "message": "Invalid input" } ], [ { "code": "invalid_value", "values": ["sse"], "path": ["type"], "message": "Invalid input" } ], ... [ { "code": "invalid_value", "values": ["http", "streamable-http"], "path": ["type"], "message": "Invalid input" } ], ... ], "path": [], "message": "Invalid input" } ]" The server is dropped and no mcp 21st * tools are registered. API_KEY_21ST is set; a direct initialize POST to https://21st.dev/api/mcp with the same key returns 200, so the key and the endpoint are fine. Cause .mcp.json as shipped (same at current main , 6b5299e): { "mcpServers": { "21st": { "url": "https://21st.dev/api/mcp", "headers": { "x-api-key": "${API_KEY_21ST}" } } } } Claude Code's MCP configuration docs (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp): A JSON entry that has a url but no type is a configuration error, because Claude Code reads an entry with no type as a stdio server. Claude Code skips that server and reports MCP server " " has a "url" but no "type"; add "type": "http" (or "sse" / "ws") to this entry . Before v2.1.202, Claude Code reported this misconfiguration differently as command: expected string, received undefined . Fix Add one line: { "mcpServers": { "21st": { "type": "http", "url": "https://21st.dev/api/mcp", "headers": { "x-api-key": "${API_KEY_21ST}" } } } } Workaround until then Register the server directly, outside the plugin (the plugin can stay installed for the skill): claude mcp add --transport http --scope user 21st https://21st.dev/api/mcp --header 'x-api-key: ${API_KEY_21ST}' Single quotes so the literal ${API_KEY_21ST} is stored and expanded at connect time. Verified: claude mcp get 21st reports Connected and 14 mcp 21st * tools load. Once the manifest is fixed, claude mcp remove 21st -s user to avoid two registrations of the same server. Environment Claude Code 2.1.273, Windows 11, plugin 21st 1.0.1 from marketplace 21st-dev

title: Optional tools/call hook for per-call authorization
cleaned_text: Optional tools/call hook for per-call authorization When mcp-proxy puts a stdio server on the network, whoever can reach it can call every tool with any arguments. #187's bearer token is a good front door, but it's still all-or-nothing: the token holder can overwrite your CI config through the filesystem server just as easily as they can read the docs they were sent for. Several open requests want something finer, each in its own shape: per-key server permissions (#201), an audit layer (#224), agent verification (#251). Would you take one small, neutral hook instead of any of those? Something like: mcp-proxy --call-tool-hook mypkg.authz:check --port 8096 -- npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /work where check(name, arguments, meta) runs in the proxy's tools/call handler before the call is forwarded. It returns allow (optionally with cleaned arguments and meta) or deny with a message, and a denied call is answered by the proxy and never reaches the server. Unset means no change. It's roughly 20 lines in proxy_server.py plus a CLI flag, and every stdio server behind the proxy gets it for free. To check it's worth having, I built the hook outside the repo by wrapping create_proxy_server and running the stock CLI over streamable HTTP, with the real @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem behind it. The same agent calls, with and without a check in the hook: stock mcp-proxy: read the guide ran write docs/notes.md ran overwrite CI workflow ran read ../.env ran move the guide ran with a per-call check (agent may read docs/ and write docs/notes.md): read the guide ran write docs/notes.md ran overwrite CI workflow REFUSED Constraint 'path' not satisfied read ../.env REFUSED Constraint 'path' not satisfied move the guide REFUSED Tool 'move_file' is not authorized The check in that demo is Tenuo (Apache-2.0): the caller attaches a signed warrant in _meta listing the tools and argument values its task allows, and a sub-agent's warrant can only be narrower than the one it was given. Code and tests (they run the real proxy and server): https://github.com/tenuo-ai/tenuo-demos/tree/demo/mcp-proxy-scoped-files/mcp-proxy-scoped-files Disclosure: I maintain Tenuo. The hook itself wouldn't depend on it, and a per-key allowlist like #201 would fit the same signature. Happy to send the PR with tests if the shape works for you, or adjust it (named servers, async hook, where the flag lives).

title: fix: skip named servers that fail to start instead of crashing the proxy
cleaned_text: fix: skip named servers that fail to start instead of crashing the proxy Problem If a single named server fails to start (missing command, broken dependency, network error), the entire proxy crashes and every server becomes unavailable — see #198. Change Wrap each named server's startup (spawn + initialize handshake) in a try/except. A server that fails to start is logged with its full traceback and skipped; the remaining servers keep serving. The failed server is omitted from the routes and from /status server_instances . This is the same approach as the earlier #194. Testing Verified locally: with one good and one intentionally-broken server, the proxy stays up, the healthy server serves normally, and the broken one is logged and skipped.

title: bug: single named server failure crashes entire proxy
cleaned_text: bug: single named server failure crashes entire proxy Problem When running mcp-proxy with multiple named servers via --named-server-config , if any server fails to start (missing dependency, wrong command, network issue), the entire proxy crashes and all servers become unavailable. This is because the server initialization loop in run_mcp_server() uses AsyncExitStack without per-server error handling. One exception in stdio_client(params) propagates up and tears down the entire stack. Steps to reproduce Create a config with 3+ servers where one has an invalid command: { "mcpServers": { "good-server": {"command": "uvx", "args": ["mcp-server-fetch"]}, "bad-server": {"command": "nonexistent-command", "args": []} } } Run mcp-proxy --named-server-config config.json --port 3100 Expected : good-server starts, bad-server is skipped with a warning Actual : entire proxy crashes Real-world impact Running 8+ servers across 3 machines. Some servers depend on VPN or specific venvs that aren't always available. One missing dependency takes down memory-service, task-orchestrator, and everything else. Implementation PR #194 wraps each server initialization in try/except. Failed servers are logged and marked as failed in /status . If all servers fail, the proxy exits gracefully.

title: fix: include uv and uvx in the runtime container image
cleaned_text: fix: include uv and uvx in the runtime container image The final container image drops the build stage's uv and uvx executables, so Python MCP servers configured with those commands fail to start with FileNotFoundError / executable-not-found errors. Copy both binaries from the existing build stage into the final image and update the README's custom-image instructions. Fixes #249. Add four opt-in container integration checks and a CI job that builds the image and runs them. The tests execute both launchers, install and run a dependency-free local wheel through uvx , then start an MCP stdio server through uv and list/call its echo tool through the production proxy. Test containers use --network=none , --pull=never and read-only fixture mounts; they require no credentials or downloaded test packages. Normal test runs skip these checks unless MCP_PROXY_TEST_IMAGE is set. The new CI job is included in the existing aggregate check and does not push images or use registry credentials. Validation on Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.13.11 / Docker 29.8.2, linux/amd64: Original image: all four new integration checks fail because uv / uvx is absent. Updated image: all four integration checks pass. Full suite with the image checks enabled: 112 passed , no skips; three existing SDK deprecation warnings. coverage report --fail-under=83 : 87.99% , passing the repository's existing gate. mypy --python-version 3.10 src : passed. Ruff 0.15.13 check and format check across src and tests : passed. actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yaml and git diff --check : passed. Reproduce from the repository root: uv sync --frozen --all-extras --all-packages docker build -t mcp-proxy:test . MCP_PROXY_TEST_IMAGE=mcp-proxy:test uv run --frozen pytest -q tests/test_container_image.py MCP_PROXY_TEST_IMAGE=mcp-proxy:test uv run --frozen coverage run -m pytest uv run --frozen coverage report --fail-under=83 The runtime image now includes the same uv binaries already used during its build; its size increases accordingly. Base image tags, Python dependencies, lockfile, entrypoint and runtime user are unchanged. Runtime checks were executed on amd64; arm64 runtime execution was not tested locally.

title: fix: avoid duplicate milliseconds in proxy log timestamps
cleaned_text: fix: avoid duplicate milliseconds in proxy log timestamps Problem The CLI logging formatter uses both %(asctime)s and an explicit %(msecs).03d suffix. Without datefmt , Python's default asctime already includes milliseconds, producing duplicate fields such as 2026-10-14 17:10:11,123.123 and inconsistent formatting for timestamp consumers. Fix Set datefmt="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S" so milliseconds are appended exactly once. Correct %(msecs).03d to the standard %(msecs)03d width syntax. Add a behavioral test confirming the rendered timestamp has one .500 suffix. Scope and verification Based directly on upstream main at 701a045 . Changes only src/mcp_proxy/ main .py and the new test. All 109 upstream tests passed on Windows/Python 3.12; Ruff check and formatting clean, mypy passed, pylint errors-only clean. Full pylint shows only three pre-existing broad-exception warnings in unrelated lines. No change to request handling, logging contents, credentials, transport behavior, or workflows.

title: fix: bound Streamable HTTP reverse-client session DELETE teardown
cleaned_text: fix: bound Streamable HTTP reverse-client session DELETE teardown Problem In MCP Python SDK 1.30, legacy streamablehttp_client delegates to modern Streamable HTTP teardown, where session DELETE goes through request_within_origin() and AsyncClient.send() rather than necessarily calling client.delete() . A stalled remote teardown can block reverse-client exit indefinitely. Fix Set a five-second bound only on reverse-client DELETE requests at the AsyncClient.send() boundary. Preserve normal GET/POST request and long-lived stream timeouts, TLS/auth settings, and server stateful/stateless behavior. Add five focused regressions, including real SDK session teardown, stalled DELETE cancellation, GET/POST non-interference, and options passthrough. Document the shutdown behavior. Verification Based directly on upstream main at 701a045 , no fork-only dependencies. 113 upstream test cases pass (Windows, Python 3.12). Ruff check/format clean; Pylint 10.00/10; mypy passed. Identical patch passed the fork's Python 3.10–3.14t CI matrix and coverage. Exactly three non-workflow files changed: README.md , src/mcp_proxy/streamablehttp_client.py , tests/test_reverse_client_termination.py .

title: fix: add session-free /healthz transport liveness probe
cleaned_text: fix: add session-free /healthz transport liveness probe Why Monitoring and load balancers need a lightweight liveness check that does not initialize or allocate an MCP session. The existing /status endpoint is for reporting activity, not verifying backend readiness. Change Add GET and HEAD /healthz to each server instance, returning HTTP 204 with no body. Route these requests before the MCP StreamableHTTP handler, including named-server prefixes. Keep /status unchanged and explicitly treat /healthz as transport liveness, not child-server readiness. Verify no session-manager request is made for stateful or stateless servers, including named prefixes. Validation 107 tests passed (Python 3.12, including new parametrized tests); Ruff lint/format, mypy and pylint --errors-only all passed. Based directly on upstream v0.13.0. No Sanity Cloud-specific features included.

cleaned_text: build(deps-dev): bump coverage from 7.14.1 to 7.16.2 Bumps coverage from 7.14.1 to 7.16.2. Release notes Sourced from coverage's releases . 7.16.2 Version 7.16.2 — 2026-09-27 Fix: on Python 3.14 and later, a for loop completing immediately before a function return could mistakenly report an uncovered branch. This is now fixed, closing issue 2168 . Fix: on Python 3.14 and later, the else clause of a try whose body is a with statement could incorrectly be reported as covered when the with raised. This is now fixed, closing issue 2289 . Fix: with dynamic_context = test_function , test methods written as @staticmethod or @classmethod were not given a context of their own. Now they are, on Python 3.11 and later. Closes issue 1923 . :arrow_right: PyPI page: coverage 7.16.2 . :arrow_right: To install: python3 -m pip install coverage==7.16.2 7.16.1 Version 7.16.1 — 2026-09-13 Fix: when the body of an irrefutable case (like case _: ) is entirely excluded, the case line is now excluded too, just as an excluded else: body removes the else: line. Previously the case line was left behind and reported as missing. Closes issue 1563 with pull 2269 . Fix: using CoverageData.update() twice on an in-memory database would fail, as described in issue 2279 . This is now fixed. :arrow_right: PyPI page: coverage 7.16.1 . :arrow_right: To install: python3 -m pip install coverage==7.16.1 7.16.0 Version 7.16.0 — 2026-08-28 When combining files, now path separator slashes will automatically be converted to the local file system style. This makes it less necessary to define [paths] configuration to combine data across operating systems. Fixes issue 2266 . The Coverage.switch_context() method now returns the previous context. Fix: previously, a [paths] pattern would be replaced everywhere in a file path when it was only meant to be replaced once, in the leading portion of the path. This is now fixed, in pull 2268 . Fixes to validation of options and configuration settings: Negative precision settings now always cause useful error messages ( pull 2261 ). An invalid regex in the --contexts option (or the [report] contexts setting) reported a confusing “Couldn’t use data file …: user-defined function raised exception” error. Now it raises a proper configuration error naming the bad regex, like other regex settings do ( pull 2262 ). Non-string values in TOML configuration settings now produce a helpful error message instead of a traceback. title: [Bug] mcp-pandoc 0.8.1 crashes on startup with mcp SDK 2.0.0 (`AttributeError: 'Server' object has no attribute 'list_tools'`)
cleaned_text: [Bug] mcp-pandoc 0.8.1 crashes on startup with mcp SDK 2.0.0 ( AttributeError: 'Server' object has no attribute 'list_tools' ) What were you trying to accomplish? Using mcp-pandoc from an MCP client (Kiro IDE) to convert documents between formats (Markdown, DOCX, etc.). The server is launched with uvx mcp-pandoc . Expected Behavior The mcp-pandoc server starts, completes the MCP handshake, and exposes the convert-contents tool so the client can connect and run conversions. Actual Behavior The server crashes on startup during import, before any MCP handshake, so the client reports it as failing to connect. The crash is an AttributeError raised while defining the tool handlers: Traceback (most recent call last): File " ", line 198, in _run_module_as_main File " ", line 88, in _run_code File ".../Scripts/mcp-pandoc.exe/ main .py", line 5, in from mcp_pandoc import main File ".../site-packages/mcp_pandoc/ init .py", line 1, in from . import server File ".../site-packages/mcp_pandoc/server.py", line 20, in @server.list_tools() ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ AttributeError: 'Server' object has no attribute 'list_tools' Root cause: mcp-pandoc 0.8.1 does not cap its mcp dependency, so a fresh install resolves the latest mcp Python SDK (2.0.0). SDK 2.0 removed the low-level Server.list_tools() / call_tool() decorator API that server.py relies on, so import fails. Environment Information Operating System: Windows 11 (x64), build 10.0.26100 Python Version: Python 3.13.1 (uv-provisioned for the mcp-pandoc environment; system Python 3.13.2) mcp-pandoc Version: 0.8.1 (latest on PyPI) mcp (Python SDK) Version: 2.0.0 (resolved automatically because it is uncapped) MCP Client: Kiro IDE 1.0.242 (also reproduces by running uvx mcp-pandoc directly) Steps to Reproduce Configure mcp-pandoc with the standard unpinned command: uvx mcp-pandoc . Start the MCP client (or just run uvx mcp-pandoc in a terminal). uvx resolves mcp-pandoc 0.8.1 + mcp 2.0.0, and the process exits immediately with the AttributeError above. The client shows the server as not connecting. Screenshots or Logs Verified workaround (pin the SDK back to 1.x): uvx --from mcp-pandoc==0.8.1 --with "mcp==1.29.0" mcp-pandoc With mcp 1.29.0 the server initializes and returns its tool: INIT OK -> serverInfo mcp-pandoc 0.8.1 tools/list -> convert-contents Suggested fix for the project: Short term: cap the dependency to mcp =x,<2 ) in pyproject.toml and release a patch. Longer term: migrate server.py to the mcp SDK 2.0 API and require mcp>=2 . title: fix: validate reference-doc supplied through a defaults file (#60)
cleaned_text: fix: validate reference-doc supplied through a defaults file (#60) Closes #60 Summary The guard from #59 only checked the reference_doc parameter. A reference-doc: key inside a defaults file was never checked. On pandoc 3.7.0.2 that exits 0, writes a broken file, and the tool reports success. The four checks from #59 now live in one function, _validate_reference_doc(reference_doc, output_format, origin) . Both paths call it. Having the rule in two places is how this bug appeared. The guard moved below the defaults-file block, because it has to run after the YAML is parsed. Errors now name the source: reference_doc parameter or reference-doc in .yaml . When both are given, the success message says the parameter was used and the defaults-file value was ignored. Version 0.11.2. Bug fix, so PATCH under CONTRIBUTING.md. Environment pandoc: pandoc 3.7.0.2 OS: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (WSL2) Python: 3.11.15 Essential Checklist [x] uv run pytest passes → 133 passed, 39 skipped , same over three runs [x] uv run ruff check . passes [x] uv run yamllint . passes [x] uv run pre-commit run --all-files passes [x] Code follows existing patterns in src/mcp_pandoc/server.py [x] Documentation updated [x] Every format I documented is present in the matching enum in server.py Screenshots Nothing visual here, so output instead. The broken behaviour is the one in #60; I did not reproduce it myself. A mismatched reference in a defaults file is now rejected: reference_doc must be a '.odt' file when output_format is 'odt', but 'ref.docx' was given (from reference-doc in d.yaml). Pandoc does not reject a mismatched reference document; it silently produces an unstyled or unreadable file. ... When both sources are given, the conversion runs and the message says which one was used: Content successfully converted using defaults file: d.yaml with reference document: param.docx (reference-doc in the defaults file was ignored) and saved to: /tmp/out.docx What I measured first The bug is about pandoc being quiet, so I tested the behaviour before writing code. All on pandoc 3.7.0.2: Test | Result both sources set | the parameter is applied; the defaults value never reaches the document relative reference-doc: in a defaults file | resolved against the CWD, not the defaults file folder resource-path: in a defaults file | also resolved against the CWD relative reference found through resource-path | exit 0, while os.path.isfile says the file is not there reference-doc: with html output | exit 0, the key is ignored Two rules follow. Existence is only checked for absolute paths. A relative or interpolated path is left to pandoc, because checking it here would reject a setup pandoc resolves correctly. The extension check still runs every time, since the file name alone answers that. A defaults-file reference is only validated when the output format accepts one. Pandoc ignores the key for other writers, so rejecting it would break a defaults file reused across formats. The parameter path still errors there, because the user asked for styling explicitly. I can move this table into docs/audits/ if you prefer. Tests Four new cases, all through handle_call_tool : a mismatched reference-doc in a defaults file is rejected, the error names the defaults file, and no output is written the parameter overrides the defaults-file value. Two assertions: a tagged font is absent from the output's styles.xml , and the message says the defaults value was ignored. The second one catches forgetting to pass the new arguments to the formatter, which fails silently. a relative reference found through resource-path succeeds a reference-doc is ignored for an unsupported output format, so a reused defaults file keeps working Plus one in TestFormatDirectionality pinning REFERENCE_DOC_FORMATS ⊆ ADVANCED_FORMATS , which is what makes the inline branch unable to carry a reference. I mutation-tested the four behaviour tests: I commented out the line each one protects and confirmed it turns red. The fifth has no line to remove — it only fails if one of the two constants is edited. Things you may ask about Error order changed. The guard is now below the defaults-file block, so if both are wrong, the defaults error comes first. Unavoidable. AGENTS.md treats error semantics as public API, so I am listing it. A relative reference_doc parameter behaves differently now. Before, a relative path that did not exist gave our own "Reference document not found". Now it goes to pandoc and the user sees pandoc's message through our handler. The rule is documented, but the error is worse on that path, and it has no test. I can add one. The type check on the YAML value has no counterpart on the parameter. Not an inconsistency: the parameter passes the JSON Schema in call_tool , the YAML passes no schema. The second output_format in REFERENCE_DOC_FORMATS check before extra_args.extend([...]) is now dead. Anything reaching it has already passed the guard. Left alone. Two doc fixes are not strictly about #60. The CHEATSHEET row said reference docs work with DOCX and ODT, forgetting pptx; it is in a table this PR edits anyway. The CONTRIBUTING versioning table listed two files, but this PR had to change a third ( tests/test_server_startup.py ). Known limits, not fixed here A defaults file can inherit another through the defaults: key. A reference-doc one level down is not seen, so the same bypass survives. Same bug in another shape, so I think it needs its own issue. reference_doc: "" is quietly ignored while reference-doc: "" raises. The success message for the input_file path duplicates the contents one and has no test. The print() in the defaults-file block breaks AGENTS.md's "never print() in src/", and this is a stdio server where stdout is the protocol channel. Different defect, so not in a PATCH bug fix. I will open an issue. I used an assistant to read the code and draft tests. I measured the pandoc behaviour, ran the checks on my machine, and verified the four behaviour tests by removing the line each protects. The diff is mine.

title: [P2] reference_doc type validation is bypassed by defaults_file
cleaned_text: [P2] reference_doc type validation is bypassed by defaults_file Links Epic: #44 Introduced alongside: #59, which added the guard this bypasses Code: src/mcp_pandoc/server.py → handle_call_tool , the reference_doc validation block Problem #59 added a guard rejecting a reference_doc whose type does not match output_format , because pandoc does not check this and fails silently when it is wrong. The guard only inspects the reference_doc parameter . Pandoc's --reference-doc can also be set inside a defaults file, via the reference-doc: key, and that path is passed through to pandoc unvalidated. my-defaults.yaml reference-doc: /templates/house.docx convert-contents(output_format="odt", defaults_file="my-defaults.yaml") │ ▼ reference_doc parameter is None ──► guard never runs ✅ skipped │ ▼ extra_args = ["--defaults", "my-defaults.yaml"] │ ▼ pandoc applies reference-doc from the YAML, exit 0, silent │ ▼ "Content successfully converted and saved to: out.odt" ← file is broken Behaviour being bypassed Verified on pandoc 3.7.0.2. All combinations exit 0 with nothing on stdout or stderr. Output | Reference type | Result docx | .odt / .pptx | Reference silently discarded. Output byte-identical to using no reference, so the document ships unstyled odt | .docx / .pptx | Writes an ODF package containing the OOXML word/ tree and no root styles.xml . Pandoc cannot read back the file it just wrote: Could not find styles.xml Scope Pre-existing, not a regression from #59. The parameter path is now guarded; this one is not. Lower severity than the parameter path: a defaults file is a deliberate artifact a user authors once, rather than something a model fills in per call. But the failure mode is identical, and the tool still reports success. Acceptance criteria [ ] reference-doc inside a defaults_file is validated with the same rule as the reference_doc parameter [ ] Decide precedence when both are supplied, and document it [ ] Same actionable error message, so a model can self-correct either way [ ] Test covering the defaults-file path Out of scope Whether to validate other pandoc options reachable through defaults_file . Worth a separate look at what else the defaults path can smuggle past validation.

title: ci: add Windows and Python 3.13 to the test matrix
cleaned_text: ci: add Windows and Python 3.13 to the test matrix Closes #45. CI only ran ubuntu-latest + Python 3.11, while requires-python is >=3.11 — so Windows and 3.13 (the environment #40 was reported on) went untested. Changes Matrix : split into a lint job (ubuntu / 3.11) and a test job over {ubuntu-latest, windows-latest} × {3.11, 3.13} . Pandoc is installed cross-platform via r-lib/actions/setup-pandoc . PDF without TeX : PDF conversions now skip cleanly when no PDF engine is installed ( shutil.which over pandoc's known engines) rather than failing. TeX Live is installed on Linux only, so the Windows legs — which don't carry a TeX distribution — stay green. *(Acceptance criterion: "PDF tests skip cleanly where no TeX engine is present.")* Required check : added a ci-ok aggregation job ( needs: [lint, test] ) as one stable check to require in branch protection. Verification Environment: macOS (Apple Silicon), Python 3.11, pandoc 3.9.0.2, no TeX installed . $ uv run pytest -q 127 passed, 40 skipped $ uv run pytest 'tests/test_conversions.py::test_bidirectional_conversions[pdf-md]' -rs SKIPPED tests/test_conversions.py:62: Skipping PDF conversion: no PDF engine (e.g. a TeX distribution) is installed. $ uv run yamllint .github/workflows/ci.yml # exit 0 $ uv run ruff check . # All checks passed! $ uv run pre-commit run --files .github/workflows/ci.yml tests/test_conversions.py # all Passed Could not verify locally: the windows-latest and Python 3.13 matrix legs (no Windows machine / that interpreter here). Those — including the test_server_startup.py handshake on Windows — are verified by this PR's CI run. Since #40's root cause was the uncapped mcp SDK dependency (now fixed on the SDK-v2 path), there shouldn't be a Windows-specific startup blocker, but the CI is the source of truth. For the maintainer: marking the check *required* is a branch-protection setting; ci-ok gives you one stable name to require rather than pinning each matrix leg.

title: feat: widen reference_doc support to odt and pptx (#52)

title: [Feature] Decide whether PDF input belongs in scope
cleaned_text: [Feature] Decide whether PDF input belongs in scope Links Epic: #44 Evidence: docs/audits/2026-08-agent-workflow-audit.md → Finding 1 Related: #47, which removes the false enum value Summary Decide whether mcp-pandoc should ever support reading PDFs, and if so, how. This is a scope decision, not a bug . #47 removes pdf from the input enum because it does not work. This issue asks the separate question of whether it should be made to work. Why it is not simply "add the format" Pandoc has no PDF reader and never has. Checked the last 25 releases; none added one. $ pandoc -f pdf file.pdf -t markdown Pandoc can convert to PDF, but not from PDF. Unlike pptx, this cannot be resolved by requiring a newer pandoc. Any support would require a non-pandoc dependency , which the project philosophy in CLAUDE.md treats as a red-light item: Requires external tools not related to Pandoc → Default: No The case for reconsidering anyway PDF is one of the most common formats a document arrives in. An agent-driven workflow that can read docx and pptx but not pdf has a conspicuous hole. "Convert this PDF to markdown" is a request users will keep making. The case against A text-extraction dependency is a real maintenance burden, and quality varies enormously by document Scanned PDFs need OCR, which is a much larger commitment The MCP ecosystem has specialised servers for PDF extraction; composing two servers may be the better answer Requirements if pursued [ ] Decide explicitly: in scope or out, and record the reasoning in CLAUDE.md [ ] If out of scope, the error message for PDF input should name a recommended alternative rather than just refusing [ ] If in scope, evaluate extraction libraries on real documents before committing, and treat it as an optional extra rather than a core dependency Recommendation Default to out of scope, and improve the error message to point users somewhere useful. Revisit only if it becomes the most requested capability.

title: feat: expose pptx as an output format (#49)
cleaned_text: feat: expose pptx as an output format (#49) Closes the output half of #49. Audit Findings 2 and 3. Stacked on #59. Merge that first. Until it lands, the diff below also shows its commits; afterwards it shrinks to the two commits here. Why this is safe The only thing that has ever blocked pptx output is our own enum. | pptx output | pptx input Pandoc support | Writer since 2.0.5 (2017) | Reader since 3.8.3 (2025-12-01) Ubuntu 24.04 ( apt , pandoc 3.1.3) | ✅ works | ❌ Debian trixie (pandoc 3.1.11.1) | ✅ works | ❌ Our CI ( apt-get install pandoc ) | ✅ works | ❌ In this PR | Yes | No, stays blocked on #54 pptx input is deliberately excluded. Exposing it would advertise a capability most users installing via a package manager do not have. #54 now carries the evidence and a recommendation for per-feature version checks rather than a global floor. What changed The enum split, which is the structural part. input_format and output_format were two copies of one ten-value list, telling the model that anything readable is writable. They are now INPUT_FORMATS and OUTPUT_FORMATS , deliberately different, with the schema enums generated from them. The separately-maintained supported_formats set is gone, so the advertised contract and the runtime check can no longer drift. ADVANCED_FORMATS is now a constant and gains pptx and odt . Both are binary and cannot be streamed back inline, so both need an output_file . pptx needs this from day one, or a request without a path would reach pandoc and fail there. Adding odt at the same time fixes a pre-existing wart: it was categorised as Basic despite never working without a path. BEFORE AFTER pptx, no output_file n/a, format did not exist "output_file path is required for pptx format" odt, no output_file reached pandoc and failed: "output_file path is "Output to odt only works by required for odt format" using a outputfile" Neither message existed before for these formats. Pandoc's version does not name the parameter the caller has to supply; ours does. REFERENCE_DOC_FORMATS regains pptx , removed in #59 precisely because the enum did not have it. It is honest now. Verified through the client path Through call_tool , which is what an MCP client actually hits, not handle_call_tool : Request | Result output_format: pptx + output_file | ✅ 28,446 byte deck pptx output + .pptx reference | ✅ styled .pptx reference against docx output | ❌ rejected, names the expected extension input_format: pptx | ❌ rejected at schema validation pptx without output_file | ❌ output_file path is required for pptx format odt without output_file | ❌ same message, ours not pandoc's Tests 120 passed, 39 skipped , up from 100 and 27. New TestFormatDirectionality asserts the two lists differ only by pptx , that the schema enums are generated from the constants, that every reference-doc and advanced format is writable, that pptx output works through the client path, and that pptx input is refused. The reference-doc end-to-end test is now parametrized over REFERENCE_DOC_FORMATS , so pptx is covered automatically. test_conversions.py treats pdf and pptx uniformly as write-only rather than special-casing pdf. Docs The matrix now states that rows are sources and columns are targets, carries pptx alongside pdf, and explains that both lack a row because pandoc cannot read them. The explanation is version-scoped: pandoc has never had a pdf reader, whereas pptx input is a question of which binary you have. Format categories corrected: odt was listed as Basic while requiring an output_file in practice. The audit doc gains a "What has been acted on" table, including the fact that #59 surfaced a mismatched-reference failure the audit missed entirely. Version 0.10.0 → 0.11.0. New backwards-compatible feature. Nothing that worked before behaves differently, apart from two error messages becoming more actionable. Follow-ups, not in this PR Issue | #47 | pdf is still wrongly in the input enum. One line now that the lists are split #57 | input_format: "txt" is broken. Same #54 | Per-feature pandoc minimums, which unblocks pptx input #60 | The reference-doc type check is bypassable through defaults_file Also noticed: tests/output/ and tests/fixtures/ are tracked but rewritten by every test run, so git status is dirty after pytest . Worth its own cleanup.

title: Remote repository misconfiguration during setup
cleaned_text: Remote repository misconfiguration during setup Problem Description There was an issue with the remote repository configuration during the initial setup. The origin remote was pointing to an incorrect repository ( https://github.com/juananpe/mcp-server-langfuse.git ) instead of the intended repository ( https://github.com/LukenLarra/mcp-server-langfuse.git ). This caused a permission error when attempting to push changes. Steps to Reproduce Initialize a Git repository locally. Attempt to create a GitHub repository using the gh repo create command. Push changes to the remote repository. Observed Behavior The origin remote was set to an incorrect URL. A 403 Permission Denied error occurred when pushing changes. Expected Behavior The origin remote should point to the correct repository URL. Changes should push successfully without permission errors. Resolution The issue was resolved by manually updating the origin remote URL using the following command: git remote set-url origin https://github.com/LukenLarra/mcp-server-langfuse.git

title: read_neo4j_cypher's token_limit truncates the finished JSON string, producing invalid JSON
cleaned_text: read_neo4j_cypher's token_limit truncates the finished JSON string, producing invalid JSON read_neo4j_cypher 's token_limit ( NEO4J_RESPONSE_TOKEN_LIMIT ) truncates the already-serialized JSON string, so any result that actually exceeds the limit comes back as invalid JSON. server.py builds results_json_str = json.dumps(sanitized_results, default=str) , then when token_limit is set, pipes that finished string through _truncate_string_to_tokens ( utils.py ), which re-tokenizes it with tiktoken and hard-cuts the token list before decoding back to text. The cut has no idea it's sitting inside a JSON string, so it lands mid-string or mid-object. Repro, no live Neo4j needed, calls _truncate_string_to_tokens directly with a JSON string that's actually over the limit: import json from mcp_neo4j_cypher.utils import _truncate_string_to_tokens results = [{"id": i, "name": f"node_{i}", "description": "x" * 40} for i in range(200)] truncated = _truncate_string_to_tokens(json.dumps(results, default=str), 500) json.loads(truncated) json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 1763 (char 1762) A result under the limit passes through unchanged and stays valid, so this only bites once truncation actually happens, which is exactly the case the feature is for. Confirmed on current main (1c7ad079). The existing test for this function, test_utils.py::test_json_data_truncation , only checks len(result) < len(json_data) and the token count, never json.loads(result) , so it doesn't catch this. Happy to send a PR if useful, looks like it'd need to truncate before serialization (drop rows, or truncate individual long string values) rather than truncate the finished JSON text.

title: fix(data-modeling): add explicit type beside bare $ref in tool schemas
cleaned_text: fix(data-modeling): add explicit type beside bare $ref in tool schemas Description Fixes #189. The type is missing on the $ref branch of every Union[str, ] tool parameter, which is why Gemini CLI's schema check drops the tool. Pydantic emits that branch as {"$ref": "#/$defs/Node"} with no sibling type , valid JSON Schema on its own but not enough for a client that checks every node for a literal type without resolving $ref first. Rather than patch each tool's signature, create_mcp_server() now walks every registered tool's parameter schema after registration and copies the referenced definition's own type onto any bare $ref ( add_missing_ref_types in utils.py ). That also reaches a few nested refs the pasted Gemini CLI log didn't get to before the connection error cut it off: Node.key_property , the items schema on list fields, Property.source . Same shape, same fix. Runtime behavior of the tools (string or object input) is unchanged; this only touches the schema FastMCP hands to the client. Verification: New test asserts no tool's parameter schema has a $ref without a type , across all 16 tools. It fails without the fix, listing 11 affected tools. title: mcp-neo4j-cypher: `get_neo4j_schema` always fails with "Variable `None` not defined" when no schema sample size is configured
cleaned_text: mcp-neo4j-cypher: get_neo4j_schema always fails with "Variable None not defined" when no schema sample size is configured Expected Behavior get_neo4j_schema works out of the box when the server is started without --schema-sample-size . The CLI help implies a default exists: --schema-sample-size SCHEMA_SAMPLE_SIZE Default sample size for schema operations (default: 1000) Actual Behavior When neither --schema-sample-size nor the NEO4J_SCHEMA_SAMPLE_SIZE environment variable is set, every get_neo4j_schema call fails with: Neo4j Client Error: {neo4j_code: Neo.ClientError.Statement.SyntaxError} {message: Variable None not defined (line 1, column 32 (offset: 31)) "CALL apoc.meta.schema({sample: None}) YIELD value RETURN value" ^} The Python literal None is interpolated into the Cypher query, where it is parsed as an (undefined) variable. Root Cause In servers/mcp-neo4j-cypher/src/mcp_neo4j_cypher/ (v0.6.0, still present on current main ): init .py — the argparse default is None , despite the help text claiming default: 1000 : parser.add_argument( "--schema-sample-size", type=int, default=None, help="Default sample size for schema operations (default: 1000)", ) utils.py ( process_config ) — when the CLI arg and the env var are both absent, it explicitly sets config["schema_sample_size"] = None (the log message suggests the intent was "scan entire graph", but that value is later interpolated literally). server.py — the None passes through both fallbacks and reaches the f-string: effective_sample_size = sample_size if sample_size else config_sample_size # None if None else None -> None get_schema_query = f"CALL apoc.meta.schema({{sample: {effective_sample_size}}}) YIELD value RETURN value" So the documented default of 1000 ( config_sample_size: int = 1000 in create_mcp_server ) is always overridden by the explicit None coming from process_config . Steps to Reproduce Start any Neo4j with APOC Core (reproduced on neo4j:2026.06.0 Community via Docker with NEO4J_PLUGINS='["apoc"]' ). Start the server without a sample size: uvx mcp-neo4j-cypher --db-url neo4j://localhost:7687 --username neo4j --read-only Call the get_neo4j_schema tool from any MCP client (no arguments). The tool returns the syntax error above. Passing --schema-sample-size 1000 at startup makes the same call succeed. title: mcp-neo4j HTTP transport allows anonymous tool access
cleaned_text: mcp-neo4j HTTP transport allows anonymous tool access How to Reproduce the Problem Start the mcp-neo4j-cypher server in HTTP mode with valid Neo4j credentials. Then interact with the MCP endpoint without any Authorization header. Initialize an MCP session: curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp/ \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"curl-test","version":"1.0"}}}' Send the initialized notification using the returned session id: curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp/ \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \ -H 'mcp-session-id: ' \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' List available Neo4j MCP tools anonymously: curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp/ \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \ -H 'mcp-session-id: ' \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' Expected Behavior (Mandatory) HTTP and SSE deployments should require an explicit authentication mechanism before exposing Neo4j-backed MCP tools. Actual Behavior (Mandatory) The anonymous request with no authorization header was accepted, and the server returned a successful MCP response instead of an auth failure: HTTP 200 {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": {...}} Specifications (Mandatory) Versions OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Linux 6.5.13-5-pve, x86-64 Library: mcp-neo4j-cypher-v0.6.0 Neo4j: 5.26.1

title: read-only tool bypass via APOC: file read and SSRF through read_neo4j_cypher
cleaned_text: read-only tool bypass via APOC: file read and SSRF through read_neo4j_cypher reported on 5 June 2026 https://github.com/neo4j-contrib/mcp-neo4j/security/advisories/GHSA-2rgm-qm78-ggx5 - no response, so trying here: Summary The read tool (read_neo4j_cypher) enforces read-only by running EXPLAIN on the query and rejecting it only if Neo4j classifies it as a write ("Only MATCH queries are allowed for read-query"). APOC procedures that read files or make network requests, such as apoc.load.json, are classified by Neo4j as read operations, so they pass the check and run via the read tool. As a result, on a server with APOC installed, the read tool can read local files (apoc.load.json('file://...')) and make HTTP requests to internal endpoints (apoc.load.json('http://...')), bypassing the read-only restriction. Confirmed on 0.6.0 + APOC: read_neo4j_cypher read a file via apoc.load.json. Details The read-only guard, server.py (around lines 31-39): async def _is_write_query(query, driver, database) -> bool: explain_query = "EXPLAIN " + query ... # query_type is 'r', 'w', 'rw', or 's'; anything containing 'w' is a write return "w" in (summary.query_type or "") enforced in read_neo4j_cypher at server.py (around line 196): if _is_write_query(...) -> raise "Only MATCH queries are allowed for read-query". The query then executes with routing_control=RoutingControl.READ (around line 150). CALL apoc.load.json(...) EXPLAINs as query_type 'r', so it is not a write and passes the gate; apoc.load.json then reads the given file:// path or fetches the given http(s) URL. CREATE/MERGE/SET and apoc procedures that write are correctly blocked (they classify as 'w'). PoC validated on mcp-neo4j-cypher 0.6.0 against neo4j:5 with APOC, using the read path: EXPLAIN query_type: r (r = read => passes the read-only gate) apoc.load.json file:// -> {'db_password': 'NEO4J_EXFIL_SECRET_9931'} LFI BYPASS: CONFIRMED read_neo4j_cypher with CALL apoc.load.json('file:///var/lib/neo4j/import/secret.json') YIELD value RETURN value returned the file contents through the read-only tool. The SSRF variant CALL apoc.load.json('http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/...') likewise EXPLAINs as read and fetches the URL, returning the body. (File reads depend on APOC file settings; the apoc.load.json(http://) SSRF needs no file settings and is the more universally reachable variant.) Impact On a deployment exposing the read-only Cypher tool (to give an agent read-only graph access) with APOC available, an attacker who can influence the Cypher (LLM-produced, prompt-injection steerable) can read local files and reach internal/metadata HTTP endpoints, returning their contents into the model context. The read-only safety control is bypassed because the EXPLAIN write-classification does not capture APOC's file/network side effects. Remediation Do not rely solely on EXPLAIN write-classification. Block APOC (and other) procedures that perform file or network I/O in the read tool (deny CALL to apoc.load.*, apoc.import.*, apoc.export.*, dbms.* and similar, or use a procedure allowlist), and/or run the connection under a Neo4j role/configuration that disables file import and external access (apoc.import.file.enabled=false, restrict unrestricted procedures). Consider parsing for CALL clauses and rejecting non-allowlisted procedures.

title: Fix MCP auth error for Lovable: handle multi-scope OAuth requests
cleaned_text: Fix MCP auth error for Lovable: handle multi-scope OAuth requests Summary Root cause: Lovable requests both scopes ( platform-user tenant ) from the auth server metadata, but the upstream Membrane API's /oauth/authorize only accepts a single scope value Adds an OAuth authorize proxy ( /oauth/authorize ) that selects the highest-permission scope before redirecting to the upstream API Serves corrected /.well-known metadata advertising only ["tenant"] to prevent the issue at the metadata level Adds 15 unit/integration tests covering scope priority selection and authorize proxy behavior Why Lovable sends both scopes The authorization server metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server advertises scopes_supported: ["platform-user", "tenant"] . Per the MCP spec's scope selection strategy, clients request all supported scopes — this is standard OAuth 2.0 behavior. How the fix works Metadata fix (belt): The server now serves /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server with scopes_supported: ["tenant"] only, so compliant clients won't request multiple scopes Authorize proxy (suspenders): /oauth/authorize parses space-delimited scopes and selects the highest-priority one ( platform-user > tenant ) before redirecting to the upstream Membrane API Test plan [x] selectHighestPriorityScope returns correct scope for all cases (empty, single, multi, unknown) [x] Authorize proxy preserves all non-scope query params in redirect [x] Authorize proxy reduces platform-user tenant → platform-user [x] Authorize proxy works regardless of scope order [x] Metadata endpoints return corrected scopes_supported: ["tenant"] [x] All 15 new tests pass ( npx vitest run tests/oauth/ ) 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

cleaned_text: ext-auth may forward a request twice when DispatchHttpCall fails synchronously in fail-open mode [x] I have searched the issues of this repository and believe that this is not a duplicate. Ⅰ. Issue Description When the ext-auth plugin's DispatchHttpCall fails synchronously and failure_mode_allow is enabled, the original downstream request may be continued twice and reach the application backend as two concurrent requests. This is especially risky for non-idempotent API calls such as LLM inference, image generation, video generation, and payment-related operations. The issue was observed with the ext-auth:2.0.0 plugin. The same control-flow structure also appears to remain in the current main branch. Ⅱ. Describe what happened The external authorization target cluster was not present in the Gateway's Envoy cluster configuration. DispatchHttpCall therefore returned synchronously with: failed to call ext auth server: error status returned by host: bad argument The plugin was configured with: failure_mode_allow: true status_on_error: 503 http_service: endpoint_mode: forward_auth endpoint: service_name: ext-auth-not-pushed.example.svc.cluster.local service_port: 8081 path: /internal/auth/resolve request_method: POST timeout: 3000 For one incoming Gateway x-request-id , the application backend observed two requests with: the same parent request ID; two different application request IDs; two different upstream TCP source ports; the exact same calculated start timestamp; one response with HTTP 200 and the other with HTTP 400 or 500. This was reproduced on multiple API protocol paths, so it was not specific to one model or request converter. A representative sanitized backend observation: parent_request_id: request_id: started_at: status: 200 parent_request_id: request_id: started_at: status: 400 The current code appears to use the same error handler for synchronous dispatch errors and asynchronous authorization responses: Client.Call(...) returns an error synchronously. callExtAuthServerErrorHandler(...) is invoked. With failure_mode_allow=true , the handler calls proxywasm.ResumeHttpRequest() . Control returns to checkExtAuth , which also returns types.ActionContinue . Relevant source: Synchronous error path: https://github.com/higress-group/higress/blob/cda15289c8daa7ce1ebbe4e464f9e0ad9ca7b2ac/plugins/wasm-go/extensions/ext-auth/main.go#L100-L126 Fail-open resume: https://github.com/higress-group/higress/blob/cda15289c8daa7ce1ebbe4e464f9e0ad9ca7b2ac/plugins/wasm-go/extensions/ext-auth/main.go#L178-L184 A missing Envoy cluster is a deployment/configuration problem, but fail-open should still continue the original request exactly once. Ⅲ. Describe what you expected to happen The request should be continued exactly once in every fail-open scenario: synchronous DispatchHttpCall error: return ActionContinue without calling ResumeHttpRequest ; asynchronous authorization HTTP 5xx: call ResumeHttpRequest exactly once; successful authorization response: call ResumeHttpRequest exactly once; fail-closed mode: send the configured local error response and do not forward the request to the application backend. Ⅳ. How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible) Enable ext-auth 2.0.0 for a test route. Set failure_mode_allow: true . Configure service_name so that the corresponding Envoy cluster is absent. Send a POST request with a unique X-Request-Id and a JSON body. Confirm the Gateway logs a synchronous bad argument error. Count requests reaching the backend for the same X-Request-Id . Expected backend request count: 1 Observed backend request count: 2 The two observed backend requests may also race for the downstream request body, causing one request to succeed while the other fails request validation. Ⅴ. Anything else we need to know? A possible fix is to distinguish whether the original request has already been paused: func callExtAuthServerErrorHandler( cfg config.ExtAuthConfig, statusCode int, responseHeaders http.Header, responseBody []byte, requestPaused bool, ) { if statusCode >= http.StatusInternalServerError && cfg.FailureModeAllow { if cfg.FailureModeAllowHeaderAdd { _ = proxywasm.ReplaceHttpRequestHeader( HeaderFailureModeAllow, "true", ) } if requestPaused { proxywasm.ResumeHttpRequest() } return } // Existing fail-closed response handling. } The synchronous Client.Call error path should pass requestPaused=false . The asynchronous response callback should pass requestPaused=true . Suggested regression coverage: synchronous BadArgument + fail-open: action is ActionContinue ; resume count is zero; backend request count is one; asynchronous HTTP 503 + fail-open: initial action pauses the request; resume count is one; backend request count is one; successful authorization: resume count is one; fail-closed: backend request count is zero. Ⅵ. Environment Higress version: not captured yet ext-auth plugin image: ext-auth:2.0.0 Deployment: Kubernetes OS: Linux containers

title: refactor(ingress): assemble mcp-server filter config with typed structs
cleaned_text: refactor(ingress): assemble mcp-server filter config with typed structs I. Describe what this PR did Replace the raw fmt.Sprintf JSON-text assembly in the mcp-server controller path with typed-struct marshaling, and tighten the render pipeline: The match-rule JSON for the mcp-session filter (assembled from Ingress annotation-derived rules plus ConfigMap MatchList ) is now built from typed structs and marshaled with encoding/json , so field values are escaped by the encoder. Output schema (field names, nesting, value types) is unchanged for all existing valid configs — the new round-trip tests compare parsed JSON trees. Annotation values flow through the same parse-time validation as other rule sources: non-empty domain/path and rejection of control characters, so malformed annotation values are rejected at parse instead of flowing into the filter config. util.BuildPatchStruct now propagates marshal errors instead of returning an empty struct; per-rule render failures are logged and skipped, and no failure path can silently emit a degenerate patch. Sibling sites found by the survey ( annotations/mcpserver.go , model.go , and BuildPatchStruct call sites incl. registry/ ) follow the same pattern. II. Why is this change needed Assembling JSON by interpolating operator-controlled strings into raw text makes the produced configuration depend on the textual shape of those values rather than their meaning. Struct-based marshaling makes the produced document a pure function of the typed data, keeps the escaping responsibility with the standard library, and turns silent degenerate outputs into visible errors. title: fix(ai): reject request bodies with a duplicated top-level model member
cleaned_text: fix(ai): reject request bodies with a duplicated top-level model member I. Describe what this PR did Make interpretation of the OpenAI-compatible request body deterministic when the model member is declared more than once at the top level: such bodies are now rejected with 400 before any model-based routing, authorization, or mapping decision. New shared helper plugins/wasm-go/pkg/jsonbody : DuplicateTopLevelMember(body, name) — a single-pass structural scan that counts top-level occurrences of a member name without decoding the body. It tracks container nesting and string literals only (a mention of "model" inside a prompt string or a nested object is never counted) and short-circuits on the second occurrence. Wired into the AI plugin family's body handling (ai-proxy, model-router, and the other extraction sites listed in the diff) ahead of the first model read. Truncated/unbalanced input reports ErrMalformedJSON so callers fall through to their existing malformed-body handling. II. Why is this change needed The gateway reads model with gjson (first-wins) while sjson-based rewrites preserve later duplicates and mainstream upstream parsers (Go encoding/json , Python json.loads , Node JSON.parse — i.e. vLLM/OpenAI/DashScope backends) are last-wins. A body with two model members is therefore interpreted differently by the gateway and the upstream, which is a consistency hazard for model mapping, model-based routing, and endpoint selection. Rejecting the ambiguous shape at the edge makes every downstream consumer agree on the request's meaning. III. How has this PR been tested jsonbody_test.go (176 lines): duplicate detection; string-value mentions not counted; nested-object keys not counted; truncation/balanced-ness; first-occurrence short-circuit. Per-plugin wiring tests: duplicate-model body → 400; single-member body unaffected; prompt text containing the word "model" unaffected. Full CI (plugin build + unit + conformance) runs on push. IV. title: ai-intent logs every user's question and the full LLM request body at Info level
cleaned_text: ai-intent logs every user's question and the full LLM request body at Info level Description #4564/#4566 removed the *configuration-time* logging of sensitive values in ai-intent (the configured Prompt, proxyUrl, proxyApiKey). title: Fix ai-rag panic when the embedding response has no vectors

title: chore(controller): reduce exposure of the xDS config-push gRPC listener
cleaned_text: chore(controller): reduce exposure of the xDS config-push gRPC listener I. Describe what this PR did Reduce the exposure of the controller's xDS config-push gRPC listener (:15051) as shipped: Drop gRPC server reflection from the production listener. It is a debugging aid, unused in the shipped co-located topology (istiod reaches the controller at xds://127.0.0.1:15051 ), and it makes service/rpc enumeration trivial for anything that can reach the port. Pin the shipped defaults with unit tests so they are explicit and regression-guarded: GrpcAddress remains :15051 (wildcard bind). Narrowing the default to loopback would break hgctl code-debug start , which rewrites istiod's configSources entry to xds:// :15051 for a developer-run controller. Operators wanting a loopback-only bind can pass --grpcAddress=127.0.0.1:15051 . features.XDSAuth is already true by default in the vendored istio, so initAuthenticators wires the xDS authenticators today. On this plaintext listener they are inert by design ( pkg/security/authentication.go returns early for non-TLS peers unless XDS_AUTH_PLAINTEXT is set), and istiod's xds:// client attaches no bearer token — enforcing plaintext authentication here would reject config push without a coordinated istiod-side credential change. This PR documents that pairing requirement in code comments rather than flipping a switch that breaks default connectivity. II. Why is this change needed The listener is the controller's control-plane surface; nothing in the shipped topology needs reflection on it, and the shipped defaults around address binding and authentication were implicit rather than tested. This change removes the unused debugging surface and makes the intentional defaults explicit and guarded. III. How has this PR been tested New unit tests in pkg/cmd/server_test.go cover the reflection removal and the shipped default assertions (listener address, authenticator wiring gate). title: fix(ai-cache): make the allQuestions cache key unambiguous
cleaned_text:
fix(ai-cache): make the allQuestions cache key unambiguous I. Summary Make the allQuestions cache key of ai-cache unambiguous: escape the separator inside each user message before joining, so the key identifies the message sequence and not merely the text it contains. onHttpRequestBody built that key by joining the raw text of every user message with "
" ( cacheKeyStrategy: allQuestions ). Because the separator was not escaped, a single message containing a line break and two messages with one line each produced the same key ( ["first line
second line"] and ["first line", "second line"] both became first line
second line ), so two different conversations shared one cache entry — the second could be answered with the first one's cached response, and on a shared Redis cache that can cross client boundaries. The fix escapes the escape character and then the separator in each message before joining. The transformation is reversible, so splits are unambiguous and no two distinct message lists can collide; conversations whose messages contain neither a backslash nor a newline keep exactly the key they had before, so no cache flush is needed for the common case. No configuration change; the lastQuestion strategy (a single gjson path, no join) is untouched. II. Related issue Fixes N/A — there is no bug report issue for this defect. title: fix(ai-image-reader): keep each image OCR text with its own image
cleaned_text: fix(ai-image-reader): keep each image OCR text with its own image I. Summary Keep each image's OCR text attached to its own image in the prompt that ai-image-reader builds. executeReadImage collected OCR results with imageContents = append(...) inside the callout callback — i.e. in completion order — while the prompt builder labelled them by dispatch position ( 第%d张图片内容为 , iterating the slice backwards). OCR is an asynchronous HTTP callout, so the two orders only coincide when every callout completes in the order it was dispatched. When the first image's OCR is slower: labels swap: the prompt tells the model that image 1 contains image 2's text and vice versa — a silent wrong-answer corruption for the user; a missing result shifts the surviving text to the wrong image number. The fix stores each result in the slot of the image it was dispatched for ( imageContents[imageIndex] ) and numbers the labels by position, so the mapping no longer depends on completion order. No configuration, prompt-template, or provider change. II. Related issue Fixes #4987 III.
