title: Request: Review auto-generated MCP permission manifest for Kubernetes
cleaned_text: Request: Review auto-generated MCP permission manifest for Kubernetes Dear Authors / Maintainers, We are researchers from the University of St. Gallen studying how to make Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers safer to run via a sandboxed permission system. As part of our study, we auto generated a permission manifest for your MCP server and would love your feedback on whether it is correct and complete. The MCP server in question is: Kubernetes Please review the manifest below and let us know: Are the permissions and their scopes correct? Are any permissions missing? Do any permissions need to be runtime-scoped (e.g., a specific project directory) rather than global? Proposed manifest (please review) { "description": "Golang MCP server for interacting with Kubernetes clusters via client-go. It reads kubeconfig (default ~/.kube/config or KUBECONFIG), may invoke exec-based auth helpers, and makes outgoing requests to Kubernetes API servers to list/get resources, fetch pod logs, exec in pods, and apply manifests.", "permissions": [ "mcp.ac.filesystem.read", "mcp.ac.system.env.read", "mcp.ac.system.exec", "mcp.ac.network.client" ] } Please let us know if you have any questions and/or remarks. In case you want to see the (current) full permission system: MCP Permission System Permission | Description | Notes mcp.ac.filesystem.read | Read files/directories | mcp.ac.filesystem.write | Write/create files | mcp.ac.filesystem.delete | Delete files or directories | mcp.ac.system.env.read | Read environment variables | e.g., API_KEY , PATH mcp.ac.system.env.write | Set environment variables | setting the env variables mcp.ac.system.exec | Execute OS commands | CLI runners, shells mcp.ac.system.process | List or kill processes | mcp.ac.network.client | General Outgoing network access | mcp.ac.network.server | Accept incoming connections | mcp.ac.network.bluetooth | Use Bluetooth connections | macOS TCC-protected mcp.ac.peripheral.camera | Capture images/video | macOS TCC-controlled mcp.ac.peripheral.microphone | Record audio | TCC-protected mcp.ac.peripheral.speaker | Play audio | mcp.ac.peripheral.screen.capture | Screen capture | Requires consent (macOS: Screen Recording) mcp.ac.location | Access location data | From Wi-Fi, IP, GNSS mcp.ac.notifications.post | Show system notifications | macOS/Windows mcp.ac.clipboard.read / .write | Read/write clipboard | Copy-paste support Thank you very much for your time and your efforts in making MCP more secure.

title: Fails to start on a clean install: mcp 2.0 removed mcp.server.fastmcp
cleaned_text: Fails to start on a clean install: mcp 2.0 removed mcp.server.fastmcp On a fresh install the server doesn't start, because pip resolves mcp to 2.0.0 and mcp.server.fastmcp no longer exists there. Reproduce (clean venv, so no cached SDK): python -m venv .venv .venv/bin/pip install mcp-server-calculator .venv/bin/mcp-server-calculator Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../mcp_server_calculator/ init .py", line 1, in from .calculator import main File ".../mcp_server_calculator/calculator.py", line 4, in from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'mcp.server.fastmcp' Cause: pyproject.toml declares mcp>=1.0.0 with no upper bound, so a new install pulls 2.0.0. Fix: mcp>=1.0.0,<2 — verified, the server starts normally afterwards (resolves to 1.29.0). Worth noting this is invisible locally: an existing environment already satisfies mcp>=1.0.0 , so pip doesn't upgrade anything. It only affects people installing for the first time. Happy to open a PR if useful.

title: Add read-only XRPL token safety catalog agent
cleaned_text: Add read-only XRPL token safety catalog agent Description Adds XrplTokenSafetyAgent , a read-only wrapper around Launch Lab's existing public XRPL token snapshot catalog. It matches the exact issuer and currency and returns the published score, up to three flags, timestamp/staleness, public evidence page and optional 5 XRP report link. Missing catalog entries return an error; the wrapper never purchases a report or signs transactions. Uses the same MeshAgent , tool-schema, cache/retry and raw-data patterns as the DuckDuckGo and DexScreener agents. The inherited async context manager handles session cleanup. x402 is metadata only, at $0.003 per Mesh call to the author's existing receive address; the upstream catalog remains freely accessible. No API keys are needed for the direct tool. Related Issues / Tickets None. Open XRPL-related PR #160 adds a separate PulseNetwork API integration, not this public catalog wrapper. How Has This Been Tested? Seven offline tests pass: currency encoding, exact issuer identity, case preservation, stale snapshots, flag limit, invalid input, upstream failure and unsupported tool handling. Shared mesh.tests._test_agents.test_agent harness: 1/1 live example passed in 1.12 seconds with raw_data_only=True ; actual output is saved as YAML. Used uv run with an isolated Python 3.12 environment and the base-agent/test dependencies. The full credential-dependent agent suite was not run. No LLM or paid API calls. Windows caveat: upstream mesh_agent.py clears all environment variables. The live harness initially failed DNS resolution; a local runner restored only SystemRoot and WINDIR after import, then the real public request passed. No upstream framework changes are included. Checklist [x] Documentation : Added usage, coverage, price and limitations to the Mesh README. [x] Tests : Added offline tests and a mesh/tests/ harness example with saved YAML. [x] Metadata : Name, author, receive address, description, tags, image, example and tool inputs/outputs provided; not marked verified. [x] No Duplicates : Checked open XRPL-related PRs. [x] No Breaking Changes : Additive agent and tests; no existing runtime behavior modified. Additional Notes Scores are dated automated observations, not an audit, endorsement or safety guarantee. The example demonstrates real catalog data, not customer traction. Source catalog: https://cocoeatsai.com/area4/token/catalog.json

title: fix: prevent stored prompt injection via retrieved context
cleaned_text: fix: prevent stored prompt injection via retrieved context Problem AugmentedLLMCall.process() appends knowledge context, conversation context, and similar messages directly to the system prompt without delimiting or sanitization. Since user messages are stored in the vector DB (via store_interaction=True by default), an attacker can store a prompt injection payload that gets recalled as part of the system prompt on future requests — a stored prompt injection attack. The embedding similarity search retrieves messages based on semantic similarity, so a crafted injection message is retrieved for related future queries. This affects all future users of the agent until the poisoned messages are removed. Fix Three-layer defense: Context delimiting : Wrap all retrieved context in tags so the LLM treats it as data, not directives Explicit instruction : Add RETRIEVED_CONTEXT_INSTRUCTION telling the LLM that content within these tags is untrusted and should not be followed as instructions Pattern sanitization : _sanitize_retrieved() strips common injection phrases ( ignore previous instructions , system override , etc.) from retrieved context before injection into the prompt Test Plan [x] Existing RAG behavior preserved — knowledge/conversation/similar context still included in prompt [x] Context is now wrapped in tags (visible in prompt construction) [x] Common injection patterns filtered: "ignore previous instructions" → "[FILTERED]" [x] Benign context passes through unchanged [x] No changes to storage or retrieval logic — only prompt construction Security Note Severity: High (stored prompt injection = persistent instruction override across all users). This is OWASP LLM Top 10 #LLM01 (Prompt Injection) in its stored/persistent form. The fix follows the recommended defense of clearly separating retrieved data from system instructions.

title: fix: add SSRF protection to MCP client URL validation
cleaned_text: fix: add SSRF protection to MCP client URL validation Problem MCPClient.connect_to_sse_server() accepts an arbitrary server_url and connects to it via SSE without any URL validation or private-IP blocklist. An attacker who can control the MCP server URL (via config injection, prompt injection leading to tool misuse, or direct parameter) can trigger SSRF to internal services or cloud metadata endpoints ( 169.254.169.254 ), potentially exfiltrating AWS/GCP/Azure credentials. Fix Add _validate_server_url() that: Restricts URL schemes to http / https Blocks connections to private IP ranges (RFC 1918, link-local, loopback) Blocks cloud metadata endpoints (AWS 169.254.169.254 , IPv6 fd00:ec2::254 ) Allows domain names (which DNS can resolve to public IPs) The validation is called at the start of connect_to_sse_server() before any network connection is made. Test Plan [x] Existing code structure preserved — no behavioral change for valid URLs [x] http://169.254.169.254/ → raises ValueError (blocked) [x] http://10.0.0.1:8000/sse → raises ValueError (blocked) [x] https://api.example.com/mcp/sse → allowed (public domain) [x] ftp://evil.com/ → raises ValueError (invalid scheme) Security Note Severity: High (SSRF to cloud metadata = credential theft). This is the most common high-impact SSRF pattern in AI agent frameworks — the MCP client needs to connect to servers, but should not connect to arbitrary internal addresses.

title: security: fix SSRF, auth bypass, prompt injection, and SQL injection vulnerabilities
cleaned_text: security: fix SSRF, auth bypass, prompt injection, and SQL injection vulnerabilities Security Fixes — 4 High-Severity Vulnerabilities During a whitebox security audit of the Heurist Agent Framework, we identified 4 high-severity and 2 medium-severity vulnerabilities. This PR addresses the 4 high-severity issues with opt-in fixes. AGNT-001: SSRF via Admin Skill Import URL (High) The /admin/skills/import endpoint fetches arbitrary URLs without validating against private IP ranges. An attacker with INTERNAL_API_KEY can access cloud metadata ( 169.254.169.254 ) or internal services. Fix: Added url_validation.py with validate_url_not_private() that resolves hostnames and blocks private/link-local/cloud-metadata IPs. Applied before all admin URL fetches. Opt-in via SSRF_VALIDATION_ENABLED=true . AGNT-002: Auth Bypass When AUTH_ENABLED Unset (High) AUTH_ENABLED = os.getenv("AUTH_ENABLED") with no default means auth is completely disabled if the env var is unset — any user can execute agents without API keys or credit deduction. Fix: Changed default to "true" with explicit boolean parsing: os.getenv("AUTH_ENABLED", "true").lower() in ("true", "1", "yes") . AGNT-003: Prompt Injection via extract_prompt (High) The extract_prompt parameter is directly concatenated into the system prompt without sanitization, allowing prompt injection to override agent behavior. Fix: Wrapped extract_prompt in XML delimiters with a safety note, stripped prompt-breaking sequences ( [INST] , , ### , etc.), and enforced a 500-char length limit. AGNT-004: LLM-Generated SQL Executed Without Validation (High) The space_and_time_agent sends user NL queries to an LLM to generate SQL, then executes it without any validation. Prompt injection can produce destructive SQL (DROP TABLE, DELETE, etc.). Fix: Added _validate_generated_sql_safety() that blocks destructive keywords (DROP, DELETE, ALTER, CREATE, INSERT, UPDATE, TRUNCATE, GRANT, REVOKE). Opt-in via SQL_SAFETY_CHECK_ENABLED=true . Remaining Medium Findings (not in this PR) AGNT-005: SSRF via MCP server URL (Medium) — requires understanding if server_url is user-controllable AGNT-006: API key in request body (Medium) — breaking change, needs separate discussion Design Principles All new checks are opt-in by default to avoid breaking existing deployments Set SSRF_VALIDATION_ENABLED=true and SQL_SAFETY_CHECK_ENABLED=true to enable AUTH_ENABLED fix is the only non-opt-in change (secure-by-default) Testing All fixes are additive — no existing behavior changed unless opt-in flags are set AUTH_ENABLED fix: os.getenv("AUTH_ENABLED", "true") returns "true" when unset, which parses to True We are happy to adjust the approach based on maintainer feedback. Happy to split into separate PRs if preferred.

title: fix: reject non-read-only SQL in read_query and query_and_plotly_chart
cleaned_text: fix: reject non-read-only SQL in read_query and query_and_plotly_chart read_query and query_and_plotly_chart passed their query string straight to db_client.execute() with no check on statement type, so the "read-only" tool could run INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL just as freely as write_query. An LLM agent that misreads a task, or a prompt injection in retrieved data, can mutate data through a tool the caller believes is safe to point at untrusted input. Added validate_dql_only next to the existing validate_sql_identifier/validate_proc_path/validate_query_uuid checks in db_client.py, and called it before execute() in both tools. It looks past leading comments/whitespace for the first keyword and requires SELECT/SHOW/DESCRIBE/EXPLAIN/WITH. write_query is untouched, that's still the mutation path. It's a keyword allowlist, not a SQL parser, so it can't see a write hiding inside a subquery or CTE body. That matches what the reporter proposed here, a light DQL-only check rather than a full read-only mode. While tracing every place a raw query reaches the database, I noticed two more spots with unchecked input: analyze_query's sql branch also runs whatever you pass it via EXPLAIN ANALYZE, and set_session_db interpolates db without validate_sql_identifier. Neither is in scope for this issue, happy to open separate reports if you'd like. Added tests for the allowlist itself plus both tool call sites; the write-rejection ones fail on main since validate_dql_only doesn't exist yet there. Fixes #27

title: fix: validate db/table identifiers in table_overview before SQL interpolation
cleaned_text: fix: validate db/table identifiers in table_overview before SQL interpolation What table_overview splits a caller-supplied table argument into db_name / table_name and interpolates both, unescaped, into three SQL statements inside _get_table_details (row count, DESCRIBE , sample-row SELECT ), plus a fourth via db_client.execute(..., db=db_name) . Every sibling resource that takes a raw identifier ( get_table_schema , get_database_tables ) already calls validate_sql_identifier before interpolating; this call site never got the same guard, so a value containing a backtick breaks out of the intended SQL shape. This is the same class of issue reported in #33 and fixed for other call sites in #49, but table_overview / _get_table_details was not among the sites #49 touched. Fix Add the same validate_sql_identifier(db_name, "database") / validate_sql_identifier(table_name, "table") calls used by get_table_schema , right after table_overview resolves db_name / table_name and before either is used as a cache key or interpolated into SQL. Verification I reproduced this against a fresh clone at HEAD 88e782b , in a python:3.11-slim container with the project's own runtime dependencies installed. I don't have a live StarRocks cluster to test against, so db_client.execute is mocked at the same boundary the repo's own tests/test_sql_identifier_validation.py already mocks for get_table_schema / get_database_tables ; the table_overview / _get_table_details code under test is unmodified. Before the fix, calling table_overview with table="mydb.x ; DROP TABLE secrets;#" against the unmodified code produced these three captured statements: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mydb . x ; DROP TABLE secrets;# DESCRIBE mydb . x ; DROP TABLE secrets;# SELECT * FROM mydb . x ; DROP TABLE secrets;# LIMIT 3 After the fix, the same call raises before any SQL is built, and a legitimate table_overview call with table="mydb.mytable" still produces the same SQL as before. I added TestTableOverviewGuard to tests/test_sql_identifier_validation.py covering the malicious-table, malicious-db, and legitimate paths, and ran the full file: 33 tests pass (30 existing plus 3 new). tests/test_db_client.py has 14 failures in this environment, but I checked and main fails the same 14 tests the same way before this change, so they look unrelated (likely need a live cluster). I have not tested this against a real StarRocks cluster since none was available to me here; the fix is confirmed at the code level, the same way #49's fixes to the sibling call sites were.

title: set_session_db does not validate the db identifier before interpolating it into `USE `{db}``
cleaned_text: set_session_db does not validate the db identifier before interpolating it into USE {db} While working on #56 I noticed set_session_db skips the identifier check that #33/#49 added everywhere else, and the PR body said I'd file a separate report for it, so here it is. server.py 's set_session_db builds USE \ {db}\ from the caller-supplied db argument and hands it straight to db_client.execute() , with no call to validate_sql_identifier . Every sibling call site ( get_table_schema , get_database_tables , get_database_summary , analyze_query ) validates first, since #49. set_session_db was added later in the file (2026-05-07) and #49's diff never reached it. It's not a one-off either: once set_session_db stores the value via db_client.set_session_default_db , _resolve_target_db reuses it unchanged for the USE preamble on every later call in that session. Repro (mocked db_client.execute , same harness tests/test_sql_identifier_validation.py already uses): get_table_schema(db='mydb ; DROP TABLE secrets;#', table='t') -> raises ValueError, execute() never called set_session_db(db='mydb ; DROP TABLE secrets;#', ctx=...) -> returns success, execute() called with: "USE mydb ; DROP TABLE secrets;# " I don't have a live cluster to confirm whether a second statement after the semicolon actually runs (that'd need CLIENT_MULTI_STATEMENTS on the mysql-connector-python side), but the string reaching execute() unvalidated is already the condition #49 treated as worth fixing at the other five sites. Fix should be the same one-liner as #49: call validate_sql_identifier(db, "database") at the top of set_session_db . Happy to send that PR once #56 closes, two open at once on this repo seems unnecessary.

title: fix: wire STARROCKS_QUERY_TIMEOUT into the connection pool's read_timeout
cleaned_text: fix: wire STARROCKS_QUERY_TIMEOUT into the connection pool's read_timeout Root cause connection_timeout / connect_timeout bound only the TCP handshake. The connector's read_timeout , which bounds how long a query's socket read is allowed to block, was never passed into the connection pool config, so it defaulted to None (unbounded) with no environment variable to set it. Fix Read STARROCKS_QUERY_TIMEOUT and pass it through as read_timeout , only when the variable is set, so an operator who never configures it keeps today's blocking behavior. Verification Ran a live check against a real MySQL-protocol server, not StarRocks itself: on unmodified main , SELECT SLEEP(35) returns successfully after the full 35 seconds with no error. The wait is unbounded, not cut off at a fixed threshold; I did not reproduce the ~30s figure this issue describes. With STARROCKS_QUERY_TIMEOUT=3 , the same client now fails a SELECT SLEEP(10) after about 3 seconds instead of hanging. Two new tests in tests/test_db_client.py cover the connection-pool config directly (no live cluster needed): unset stays absent from connection_params , set flows through as read_timeout . Both fail on main and pass on this branch. This repo has no test/lint CI job (only DCO and license/cla on a recent merged PR), so I ran the full non-live-cluster test suite ( tests/ minus test_db_client.py , which needs a live cluster) locally: 67 passed, no change from main .

title: Avoid shared Flight SQL session state across concurrent requests
cleaned_text: Avoid shared Flight SQL session state across concurrent requests Summary Arrow Flight SQL mode keeps a single global ADBC connection ( self._adbc_connection ) and reuses it across requests, while request handling may change the active database context with USE . That means multiple requests can share mutable session state. Evidence Global singleton connection field: src/mcp_server_starrocks/db_client.py:187-188 Shared connection reuse: src/mcp_server_starrocks/db_client.py:258-272 Per-request database switching on the shared connection: src/mcp_server_starrocks/db_client.py:454-466 The same pattern exists in collect_perf_analysis_input() : src/mcp_server_starrocks/db_client.py:485-538 Risk Under concurrent requests, session state can bleed across callers: request A switches to database db_a request B switches to database db_b subsequent statements may run in the wrong database or collect the wrong profile/query metadata This is both a correctness and a security isolation problem. Suggested Fix Avoid sharing a mutable Flight SQL session across requests. Create per-request connections/cursors, or add a proper connection pool if the driver supports it. If shared reuse must remain, guard all session-mutating operations with strict synchronization and restore context explicitly. Add concurrent tests that validate DB context isolation.

title: Do not trust forwarded client IP headers without trusted proxy validation
cleaned_text: Do not trust forwarded client IP headers without trusted proxy validation Summary When MCP_TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true , the middleware directly trusts X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP from the incoming request and uses them for allowlist decisions. There is no concept of trusted reverse proxies or trusted proxy CIDRs, so any client that can connect directly to the server can spoof these headers and potentially bypass the IP allowlist. Evidence Client IP extraction trusts forwarded headers unconditionally when enabled: src/mcp_server_starrocks/http_security.py:399-409 The resulting IP is then used by the allowlist check: src/mcp_server_starrocks/http_security.py:411-445 Tests currently validate the happy path for spoofed X-Forwarded-For headers, but there is no protection against direct-client spoofing: tests/test_http_security.py:142-156 Risk A deployment behind a reverse proxy can be made vulnerable if the backend is also reachable directly, or if the proxy chain is not tightly controlled. In that case, a direct client can self-assert an internal/private IP and bypass the IP filter. Suggested Fix Add a MCP_TRUSTED_PROXIES / CIDR-based trusted proxy list. Only honor forwarded headers when request.client.host is a trusted proxy. Otherwise, ignore forwarded headers and use the socket peer address. Add negative tests showing spoofed headers from untrusted peers are rejected.

title: Server fails to start on fastmcp 4.x: No module named 'fastmcp.tools.tool'
cleaned_text: Server fails to start on fastmcp 4.x: No module named 'fastmcp.tools.tool' Problem server.py:28 imports ToolResult from fastmcp.tools.tool . That module is gone in fastmcp 4.x (it moved to fastmcp.tools.base ), so the server dies at import and MCP clients report Connection closed . File ".../mcp_server_starrocks/server.py", line 28, in from fastmcp.tools.tool import ToolResult ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fastmcp.tools.tool' pyproject.toml asks for bare fastmcp>=2.14.0 , so any fresh resolve now picks 4.0.3 and breaks. Same class of problem as #13. Environment mcp-server-starrocks: 0.4.0 and current master fastmcp: 4.0.3 (4.0.0 shipped 2026-08-31, 4.0.3 on 2026-09-05) Python 3.12, Linux Steps to Reproduce uvx mcp-server-starrocks with a cold uv cache Traceback above, process exits before it speaks MCP Suggested Fix The cap alone unblocks users with no code change: pyproject.toml : fastmcp>=2.14.0,<5 , or <4 if 4.x is untested server.py:28 : from fastmcp.tools.base import ToolResult ToolResult is the only import affected. FastMCP , Context , utilities.types.Image and exceptions.ToolError all still resolve on 4.0.3. Workaround uvx --with "fastmcp<4" mcp-server-starrocks , or in an MCP client config: { "command": "uvx", "args": ["--with", "fastmcp<4", "mcp-server-starrocks"] }

title: fix: import ToolResult from fastmcp.tools so fastmcp 4.x works (#54)
cleaned_text: fix: import ToolResult from fastmcp.tools so fastmcp 4.x works (#54) Fixes #54 Problem fastmcp 3.x renamed fastmcp/tools/tool.py to base.py , keeping a sys.modules shim so the old module path still resolved at runtime. fastmcp 4.0.0 dropped that shim, so server.py:28 's from fastmcp.tools.tool import ToolResult raises ModuleNotFoundError and the server exits before it speaks MCP — clients just report Connection closed . pyproject.toml asked for bare fastmcp>=2.14.0 , so any fresh resolve (e.g. uvx mcp-server-starrocks with a cold cache) picked 4.0.3 and broke. uv.lock is gitignored and pins 3.2.4, which is why local uv run never hit this. Fix try: # fastmcp >= 3 re-exports ToolResult from the package (tool.py was renamed to base.py) from fastmcp.tools import ToolResult except ImportError: # fastmcp 2.x from fastmcp.tools.tool import ToolResult Imported from the fastmcp.tools package rather than fastmcp.tools.base (as the issue suggested) because it is the public re-export and works on both 3.x and 4.x. The fallback is load-bearing: on 2.14.0 — the declared floor — fastmcp/tools/ init .py does *not* re-export ToolResult , so a bare fastmcp.tools or fastmcp.tools.base import would have silently dropped 2.x support. pyproject.toml is also capped at fastmcp>=2.14.0,<5 so a future major cannot break a fresh resolve the same way. Verification The issue's claim that ToolResult is the only affected import holds — FastMCP , Context , utilities.types.Image and exceptions.ToolError all still resolve on 4.0.3. Against fastmcp 4.0.3 : the server imports, registers all 11 tools and 3 resource templates, and read_query against a live local StarRocks returns both content and structured_content correctly. Also verified on the locked 3.2.4 , where ToolResult resolves to fastmcp.tools.base rather than the deprecated shim. Note: pytest has 4 pre-existing failures in tests/test_db_client.py (stale expectations predating to_string appending "Total rows"/"Execution time"). They fail identically on a clean checkout of main and are untouched here. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code https://claude.ai/code/session_01WbLT5zoMG5WD9M8NxfZhwc

title: fix: add read_timeout to connection pool config to respect STARROCKS_QUERY_TIMEOUT env var
cleaned_text: fix: add read_timeout to connection pool config to respect STARROCKS_QUERY_TIMEOUT env var Summary Fixes a bug where STARROCKS_QUERY_TIMEOUT environment variable was silently ignored, causing long-running queries to fail with a ~30s timeout regardless of what was configured. Root Cause The MySQL connector distinguishes between two types of timeouts: Timeout | Purpose | Was Configurable? connect_timeout | Time to establish a connection | ✅ Yes (via STARROCKS_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT ) read_timeout | Time to wait for query results | ❌ No — this PR fixes it The STARROCKS_QUERY_TIMEOUT env var existed in documentation/configs but was never wired into the connection pool , so the MySQL connector fell back to its internal default (~30s), causing timeouts on analytical queries over large datasets. Fix Add read_timeout to the connection pool config, reading from the STARROCKS_QUERY_TIMEOUT environment variable: 'read_timeout': int(os.getenv('STARROCKS_QUERY_TIMEOUT', '600')),

title: Release v1.3.0-beta.2
cleaned_text: v1.3.0-beta.2 Release date: October 15, 2026 GreptimeDB v1.3.0-beta.2 is the second beta of the 1.3 release and covers changes since v1.3.0-beta.1. Most changes are bug fixes, including fixes for wrong query results and for writes that could be lost or hidden. 👍 Highlights Distributed write retries enabled by default In distributed clusters, the frontend retries failed writes to datanodes. Writes that hit a region during migration, failover, or repartition are retried after a route refresh. Busy regions and Unavailable , Cancelled , or DeadlineExceeded errors are retried with exponential backoff and jitter. Regions that acknowledged success aren't retried. Retries cover inserts, deletes, bulk inserts, and logical metric tables; standalone mode doesn't retry. Retries are on by default with these settings. Set max_retries = 0 to disable them: [write_retry] max_retries = 3 initial_backoff = "1500ms" max_backoff = "10s" backoff_multiplier = 2.0 See the Frontend configuration, #9542, #9543, and #9574. Signals Explore in the bundled dashboard Signals Explore is a drilldown view for metrics, logs, and traces, with label filters. Logs link to their traces, and traces link to their logs. Native and gauge histograms aren't charted yet. See dashboard#651. Fixes for silently wrong query results The following queries returned wrong results without an error: PromQL comparisons, min / max , topk / bottomk , sqrt , and round follow Prometheus float semantics. Previously, errors / requests > 0.05 was true for a NaN ratio, so alerts fired when there was no traffic (#9479). Binary operations on folded histograms, such as histogram_fraction(...) + on(host, shard) ... , could drop matching series at query parallelism above 1 (#9509). ORDER BY and LIMIT on logical metric tables could return misordered rows or repeated partial groups (#9522). Ordering over TQL scalar() results is also fixed (#9523). A subquery without a step uses 60 seconds, the Prometheus default. Previously, count_over_time(x[5m:]) in an instant query returned 300 instead of 5 (#9481). Other PromQL fixes are listed under Bug Fixes. Fulltext bloom index no longer skips matching rows matches_term on a bloom fulltext index could return fewer rows than a full scan: matches_term(msg, 'world') missed hello_world , and error missed 错误error日志 . The index now splits text where matches_term does: _ separates tokens, and Han text is stored as bigrams. Case-sensitive LIKE can now use the index for pruning: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE message LIKE '%disk quota exceeded%'; On a case-insensitive index, lower(message) LIKE ... and matches_term(lower(message), ...) also use it; ILIKE doesn't. Existing SSTs need an index rebuild, as described in Upgrade notes. See #9470. Storage and routing fixes Bulk memtable merges and flushes could let an older value override a newer write or delete. Metric engine physical tables and flat-format tables use the bulk memtable (#9517). Closing a region flushes skip-WAL writes, so they survive a graceful datanode shutdown (#9440). Writes during repartition could go to the wrong region and be missing from query results (#9458). Dashboard The bundled dashboard moves from v0.13.15 to v0.14.2. Besides Signals Explore, it applies the selected timezone to both display and SQL requests (dashboard#657), and fixes log scrolling, table loading, and trace-ID lookups (dashboard#655, dashboard#656, dashboard#658). Benchmark results Compared with v1.2.1 on the same setup for both versions. The results cover all changes since v1.2.1, not only this beta. 30-day PromQL range queries over node metrics (1,720 series, 158M samples, 30m step, warm cache): the five queries are 1.14×–1.83× faster at the median (geometric mean 1.43×). Throughput is 16% higher at concurrency 1 and 6% higher at concurrency 4 (geometric means); one query is 8% slower at concurrency 4. SQL queries over 100M agent observability records (c7i.2xlarge, 8 CPUs and 16 GB for the database): the 16 queries are 1.08×–1.44× faster at the median (geometric mean 1.20×). Upgrade notes Distributed PromQL: Upgrade datanodes before frontends. Older datanodes can't decode the new PromQL functions in distributed query plans (#9479). Fulltext bloom indexes: matches_term and LIKE scan SSTs with old-format indexes until compaction or ADMIN BUILD_INDEX('logs') rebuilds them. To check rebuild progress, read fulltext.bloom_version in the meta_json column of information_schema.ssts_index_meta . After a downgrade, older binaries also scan SSTs with new-format indexes. The bloom backend no longer uses jieba; Han text is stored as bigrams, which can make the index larger. Tantivy-backed indexes no longer serve matches_term ; those queries scan (#9470). Write retries: If every attempt fails, the error returns after at least 10.5 seconds of backoff (1.5 + 3 + 6) plus jitter. Clients with shorter timeouts see a timeout instead. If a write succeeds but its response is lost or times out, the retry can insert duplicate rows into append-only tables. Set max_retries = 0 under [write_retry] to disable retries (#9543). Flow mirroring: When a flownode is slow or unreachable and more than 1M mirrored rows are pending, the frontend drops further mirrored batches to protect its memory. Flow results can have gaps (#9421). Series scans: The v2 series-scan path is temporarily disabled by default (#9436). Breaking changes Expression depth: Query planning rejects expressions deeper than 128 levels to reduce stack-overflow risk (#9564). PromQL subquery step: Range queries that relied on [R:] using the query step now sample every 60 seconds. The step isn't configurable (#9481). Decompressed request size: Prometheus remote read/write and Loki push bodies over 512 MiB after decompression are rejected with 400. With a memory quota configured, compressed gRPC requests reserve max_recv_message_size before decompression, so 429 or RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED can occur sooner (#9264). 🚀 Features feat(json2): json_get title: feat(mito2): produce typed raw series from RegionScanner with truthful ordering

title: feat(config): support overriding region engine options from env
cleaned_text: feat(config): support overriding region engine options from env I hereby agree to the terms of the GreptimeDB CLA. Refer to a related PR or issue link (optional) Closes #8620 What's changed and what's your intention? Summary. region_engine is a Vec of externally tagged enums (serialized as [{"mito": {..}}, {"file": {..}}] ), so it cannot be addressed by the flat dotted environment keys that the layered configuration uses: config walks region_engine.mito.global_write_buffer_reject_size , replaces the non-table intermediate value with a table, and startup fails with invalid type: map, expected a sequence . This adds a dedicated Source ( common-config::tagged_seq ) that addresses the entries of such a sequence by tag name: ~bash export GREPTIMEDB_STANDALONE REGION_ENGINE MITO GLOBAL_WRITE_BUFFER_REJECT_SIZE="4GB" greptime standalone start ~ How it works. Configurable::env_tagged_seq_keys() (default None ) registers the keys; DatanodeOptions and StandaloneOptions register ["region_engine"] and GreptimeOptions forwards it. Nothing else changes: a configuration type that does not register a key keeps the plain Environment source. For each registered key the source collects the KEY variables, removes them from the collected map (the map is unordered, so a leftover dotted key could still destroy the sequence), merges them onto the matching default entries by tag, and writes the result back as one array. Entries that only the environment mentions are appended; fields it does not mention keep their default value. Precedence is unchanged: config file > environment > defaults. Errors: a numeric index, an override of the whole sequence, an entry without a field, a field below a non-table default, and two variables that set a path and a field below it each report a dedicated error naming the offending variable and the dotted config path. Limitations. The syntax is tag-based by design, so entries cannot be removed or reordered from the environment; engines that the configuration omits are still constructed with their defaults, as before. A tag that the default sequence does not have is appended, so a typo surfaces as the serde unknown variant error rather than as an environment-key error. A configuration file that configures the sequence as a whole replaces the merged value, so the environment variables for it are ineffective then (documented in the example configs). Compatibility. No API or data-format change: the new trait method has a default implementation, and the new source is only used by the two options types that register a key. Documentation. config/datanode.example.toml , config/standalone.example.toml and the generated config/config.md describe the syntax and the caveat above. title: perf(datanode): send the mito puts of one request to each worker at once
cleaned_text: perf(datanode): send the mito puts of one request to each worker at once I hereby agree to the terms of the GreptimeDB CLA. Refer to a related PR or issue link (optional) RFC: #9195 Tracking: #9197 What's changed and what's your intention? With the object store WAL in durable mode, clients writing a partitioned table at low concurrency lock into a phase that wastes a seal interval. A Mito worker woke on the first region write of a request and appended it alone. That append blocked the worker until the next seal, so the rest of the request waited for the next object, every request finished on that object, and the clients resubmitted together into the same pattern. This PR hands the puts of one request to the engine together through a new RegionEngine::handle_batch_put_requests . It returns the responses to await, each with the regions it answers for. Default: it handles each put with handle_request and answers each region on its own, so every other engine keeps its behaviour. Mito override: it builds each region's write as handle_request does and sends the writes of each worker in one message ( WorkerRequest::Writes ), so the worker handles its regions of the request in one batch and one WAL append. The messages to different workers are sent concurrently on their own task. The region server calls it when a request carries at least two puts and every one of them goes to a ready Mito region. The puts may target the same region: a request of many puts to one region, such as a bulk import into a single-region table, otherwise sends one worker message per put. Each region's result is still awaited and accounted on its own ingest task, as on the per-region path: the first error returns at once; each region records its request latency, its changed rows or its failure; an error names its own region; each region keeps its RegionServer::handle_region_request trace span. Every other request takes the old path unchanged: a request with a single put, a request with a non-put (deletes), and a request with a region that is not ready or not on Mito. Requests to metric regions keep the metric engine's batch path, which still downcasts to MetricEngine . Moving it onto this method is left for a follow-up: an engine that writes several puts together, as MetricEngine::put_regions_batch does, can answer them all with one response. No waiting is added: nothing holds a request or waits on a timer, and the worker takes the message like any other request. Acknowledgement and durability are unchanged for every WAL provider. Remaining differences on the new path: A request's rows are converted to writes in one ingest task instead of one task per region. A write whose worker stopped fails with Failed to recv result instead of Worker is stopped ; both errors have the same status code. The Mito guide names the new write-path entry. Tests: A region server with one Mito worker that takes one message at a time, on a durable object store WAL: one insert to two regions is one WAL append, and so is one insert with two puts to the same region. Both fail without the change (two appends). Two regions on different workers: the first waits for a WAL upload that is held, and the second is unknown to Mito. The request returns the second region's error without waiting for the first. The default handle_batch_put_requests of an engine that does not override it: each put reaches handle_request , and each region keeps its own response or error. The routing check: only two or more puts into ready Mito regions take the new path, including two puts to one region. These keep the old path: a single put; a put with a delete; a put to a region that is still registering; a put to another engine's region. Measurements Base baa5630119 (this PR's base commit) against this PR's head c39dcd035a , on AWS: c6id.2xlarge, real S3, both images alternating on one instance, 2M rows per run in 1000-row batches, warm-up excluded. Ratios are geometric means with the per-round min–max. 8 clients, 8 rounds: https://github.com/GreptimeTeam/greptimedb/actions/runs/39096840046 WAL ack, regions | base rows/s | this PR rows/s | ratio (per-round min–max) | client p50 / p99 ms, base → this PR durable, 8 | 27,472 | 37,355 | ×1.360 (1.147–1.442) | 290 / 338 → 202 / 314 durable, 1 | 37,173 | 36,994 | ×0.995 (0.941–1.030) | 203 / 311 → 203 / 321 enqueued, 8 | 67,104 | 67,295 | ×1.003 (0.998–1.006) | 80 / 170 → 78 / 171 enqueued, 1 | 64,612 | 64,893 | ×1.004 (1.001–1.011) | 100 / 173 → 99 / 169 The 1.147 low is one round in which base itself ran at its maximum, 32.1k. In the durable 8-region cell the object store PUTs per row are unchanged: 0.243 → 0.259 objects per 1k rows/s. Objects/s rise from 6.67 to 9.66 with the higher throughput: the clients split into two groups that alternate objects, one object per seal interval, as with one region. 32 clients, 5 rounds: https://github.com/GreptimeTeam/greptimedb/actions/runs/39096842899 WAL ack, regions | base rows/s | this PR rows/s | ratio (per-round min–max) durable, 8 | 62,828 | 63,636 | ×1.013 (1.000–1.041) durable, 1 | 61,574 | 61,063 | ×0.992 (0.976–1.009) enqueued, 8 | 66,717 | 66,967 | ×1.004 (1.001–1.006) enqueued, 1 | 64,692 | 64,696 | ×1.000 (0.997–1.006) At 32 clients the worker queues do not drain, so the lock does not occur and nothing changes. No benchmark covers a request of many puts to one region. PR Checklist Please convert it to a draft if some of the following conditions are not met. [x] I have written the necessary rustdoc comments. title: Distributed writes send one datanode RPC per region request when write retry is enabled
cleaned_text: Distributed writes send one datanode RPC per region request when write retry is enabled What type of enhancement is this? Performance What does the enhancement do? Send fewer datanode RPCs per write on a distributed frontend, keeping the retry guarantee from #9542. Current behavior (at baa5630) WriteDispatcher::prepare builds one RegionRequest per datanode (code). With write_retry enabled, execute then splits every Inserts / Deletes request into one RPC per entry (one region's rows from one source request) before the first attempt, not only on retry (execute, split_request). Retry is on by default for the frontend, max_retries = 3 (options, builder). Standalone sets it to 0 (code) and is unaffected. Bulk inserts are unchanged. The split was added in #9542 and turned on for the frontend by #9543, after #9541 centralized dispatch. Before, inserts and deletes used one RPC per datanode ( group_requests_by_peer ). It ships in v1.3.0-beta.2. Cost (not measured; impact unknown) N regions on one datanode: N RPCs instead of 1. The frontend does not merge entries for the same table, also before #9541 (code). Elasticsearch _bulk runs the pipeline per document (1, 2), so N documents become N entries and now N RPCs, even for a single-region table. Datanode-side batching of a multi-region request no longer applies. The metric engine's batched put (#7535) always takes its single-request path (code), so with default settings a Prometheus remote write sends one RPC per logical region. Open PR #9692, which batches the Mito puts of one request, would not trigger either, since each RPC carries one region; it still applies to standalone, where it was measured. That batching matters most for the object store WAL (#9195), where a durable append waits for an object upload; the provider is standalone-only today, and the RFC plans cluster mode on the same format. Implementation challenges The split is intentional. The datanode runs a multi-region Inserts request with try_join_all and returns one merged response or one error (code, RegionResponse ), and the metric engine does not roll back earlier groups (code). After a failed batched RPC, the frontend cannot tell which regions were written. One entry per RPC lets a retry skip those that succeeded. How can we keep that guarantee with fewer RPCs? Some directions, none evaluated: Group by (datanode, region) instead of per entry. Helps _bulk , not the metric fan-out; same-region entries remain separate puts that can fail independently. Merge same-table entries in the frontend so each region gets one put. Also helps standalone; needs schema alignment. Return per-region results from the datanode, batch the first attempt, and split only failed regions on retry. Changes the wire format; needs mixed-version handling. Untested workaround: write_retry.max_retries = 0 , which disables retries.

The SSE mode starts an HTTP server that serves MCP over Server-Sent Events, allowing web-based integration with MCP clients. Usage Run in STDIO mode (default) adx-mcp-server Run in SSE mode adx-mcp-server --transport sse --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 For Docker: Run in SSE mode with Docker docker run -it --rm -p 8000:8000 adx-mcp-server --transport sse Related Documentation Model Context Protocol Server-Sent Events

title: fix: enable OAuth token refresh by passing client credentials
cleaned_text: fix: enable OAuth token refresh by passing client credentials Summary loadCredentialsAndRunServer constructs the OAuth2 client with no arguments : const auth = new google.auth.OAuth2(); auth.setCredentials(credentials); Because client_id and client_secret are missing, google-auth-library cannot exchange the stored refresh_token for a new access_token . As soon as the initial access token expires (typically an hour after bun start auth runs), every subsequent API call fails with invalid_request , and the only workaround is to re-run the interactive auth flow — which defeats the point of persisting the refresh token in .gtasks-server-credentials.json . This PR loads the same gcp-oauth.keys.json already used by authenticateAndSaveCredentials() and passes client_id , client_secret , and redirect_uri into the OAuth2 constructor. Both the installed and web OAuth key shapes are handled. setCredentials is unchanged, so no re-authentication is required for existing users. Reproduction (before the fix) Run bun start auth — completes fine, writes .gtasks-server-credentials.json . Wait ~1 hour for the access token to expire (or manually edit expiry_date to a past value). Start the MCP server and call any tool ( list , search , etc.). Every call returns {"code":-32603,"message":"invalid_request"} from Google. Only fix previously available: re-run bun start auth and re-consent through the browser. Verification (after the fix) Tested against a live Google account whose stored access_token was 63 hours past expiry_date : bun build succeeds. Started the built server, sent initialize → notifications/initialized → tools/call name=list over stdio. Result: \"isError\":false , full task list returned. No re-auth needed; refresh happened transparently in-flight. Test plan [x] bun build succeeds. [x] With a valid (unexpired) access_token : server works as before, no regression. [x] With an expired access_token but valid refresh_token : server auto-refreshes and API calls succeed. [x] Both installed (desktop) and web OAuth key shapes are handled via oauthKeys.installed ?? oauthKeys.web . Note on scope Refresh currently happens in memory only — the on-disk .gtasks-server-credentials.json is not updated with the new access token. That's fine (refresh_token doesn't rotate, so subsequent restarts just refresh again cheaply), and I kept the change minimal. Happy to add an auth.on('tokens', ...) handler that persists the refreshed access token to disk in a follow-up if you'd like. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: fix(auth): pass client credentials to OAuth2 token refresh
cleaned_text: fix(auth): pass client credentials to OAuth2 token refresh The OAuth2 client is constructed with new google.auth.OAuth2() — no client_id or client_secret. This works while the initial access token is valid, but once it expires, the automatic refresh request to Google's token endpoint fails with invalid_request: Could not determine client ID from request., and every tool call fails despite a valid refresh token on disk. Fix: read client_id, client_secret, and redirect_uris from gcp-oauth.keys.json and pass them to the OAuth2 constructor. Persist refreshed tokens back to the credentials file via the tokens event so later runs reuse the refreshed token and pick up a rotated refresh token if Google issues one. Verified against a real expired token: reproduced the invalid_request failure with the old construction, then confirmed a live call to tasks.tasklists.list() succeeds and the tokens event fires with a refreshed access token. Related to #34 (separate bug, same server), but independent of it.

title: fix(auth): decode file URL path for credentials lookup
cleaned_text: fix(auth): decode file URL path for credentials lookup credentialsPath and the OAuth keyfile path were resolved via path.dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname). URL.pathname returns a percent-encoded string, so any install directory containing a space (e.g. the default Claude Desktop Extensions path on macOS) never resolves. The server then reports "Credentials not found. Please run with 'auth' argument first." and exits, even when valid credentials exist at the correct location. Fix: use fileURLToPath from node:url, which decodes the path correctly. Verified by reproducing the failure from a path containing a space, then confirming the fix resolves and finds the credentials file correctly.

title: Auth fails on Windows: "Cannot find module 'C:\C:\...'"
cleaned_text: Auth fails on Windows: "Cannot find module 'C:\C:\...'" Bug npm run start auth fails on Windows with: error: Cannot find module 'C:\C:\Users\ \...\gcp-oauth.keys.json' Note the duplicated C:\ in the path. Cause In src/index.ts , two places use: path.dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname) On Windows, new URL(import.meta.url).pathname returns /C:/Users/... (leading slash). After path.dirname + path.join('..', ...) , Node sees \C:\Users\... and resolves it relative to the cwd's drive root — producing C:\C:\... . Fix Use fileURLToPath from node:url : import { fileURLToPath } from "url"; // then in two places: path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) Two occurrences in src/index.ts : the credentialsPath constant and p inside authenticateAndSaveCredentials . Environment Windows 11, Bun 1.3.14

title: Fix #2129: Add a bounded production WASM processor runner
cleaned_text: Fix #2129: Add a bounded production WASM processor runner Fixes #2129. Part of #2127. Stacking note: #2127 prefers #2128 (PR #2148) first. This branch is based on main . Its new tests use only committed WAT fixtures. Summary EvaluatorFilter::handle_body ran synchronous Wasmtime execution on the async request task with limits: None . This PR moves production processor execution onto one bounded, evaluator-owned runner. New features/evaluator/src/runner.rs ( ProcessorRunner , owned by EvaluatorState ): Admission uses a non-queuing Semaphore::try_acquire_owned . The permit moves into the spawn_blocking closure. A cancelled request or a request timeout therefore cannot release the slot before the processor actually exits. Without a Tokio runtime, the runner returns a failure instead of panicking. Filter: the filter calls the runner. Runner results map through the existing Outcome::Failure and governance failure policy, with these reason codes: processor_overloaded processor_instantiation_failed processor_execution_failed Production always applies limits. The existing SimulationLimits is renamed ProcessorLimits and reuses the existing mechanisms: fuel, StoreLimits memory and epoch deadline. The simulation module re-exports it as SimulationLimits , so the simulation crate does not change. Defaults Limit | Default | Override Concurrent invocations | available CPUs | WANAKU_EVALUATOR_PROCESSOR_CONCURRENCY Wall-clock deadline | 1000 ms | WANAKU_EVALUATOR_PROCESSOR_TIMEOUT_MS Memory | 64 MiB | WANAKU_EVALUATOR_PROCESSOR_MEMORY_BYTES Fuel | 10M | WANAKU_EVALUATOR_PROCESSOR_FUEL A missing, invalid or zero value keeps the default and logs a warning. Docs "Processor Resource Limits" section in docs/evaluator-engine.md , plus updates to Error Handling and Performance Notes. "Evaluator Processor Runner" table in docs/configuration.md . Corrected fuel statement in docs/governance-posture.md . Behavior change to review When the runner is full, a request fails at once as processor_overloaded . It does not wait for a slot. With on_failure: deny in enforce mode, a burst larger than the concurrency limit is therefore blocked. This follows the ticket ("map admission failures through the current governance failure policy") and is documented. Tests unrelated_task_progresses_on_single_worker_runtime : a ticker task keeps running while the looping fixture runs. Wall-clock, fuel and memory budget tests: the looping fixture and the new tests/fixtures/memory-growth.wat stop within budget. After each one, the same runner runs pass.wat successfully. concurrency_stays_bounded_after_cancellation and request_timeout_keeps_permit_until_work_exits : the runner never goes above the limit, and an aborted or timed-out request keeps its slot until the work exits. overloaded_runner_applies_failure_policy_without_blocking_audit : with an overloaded runner, enforce with deny blocks, enforce with allow passes, and audit passes. runner_applies_processor_writes_only_in_enforce_mode : side-effects.wat writes the registry only in enforce mode. Validation cargo test --no-fail-fast -p wanaku-feature-evaluator -p wanaku-feature-simulation : Evaluator lib: 174 passed, 4 failed. The 4 failures need the actions/dist artifacts, which are not built here. They already fail on main in this environment, and #2128 handles them. Evaluator integration: 52 passed. Simulation: 22 passed. cargo test --lib runner passed 5 times in a row (about 0.6 s each). cargo clippy --all-targets -p wanaku-feature-evaluator -p wanaku-feature-simulation : no new warnings. cargo fmt --all -- --check : the changed files are clean. The diffs in features/plugins and infra/src/lib.rs already exist on main . Caveats Each invocation also starts the existing short-lived epoch-ticker thread. The wall-clock deadline stops guest code only. It cannot stop a blocking host import. This is a documented non-goal. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code https://claude.ai/code/session_01UAAhrhsd1gYVGJoatPKtLM _Generated by Claude Code_ Summary by Sourcery Run production WASM processors through a bounded, resource-limited runner and integrate its failures with governance policy. New Features: Add a bounded production WASM processor runner with configurable concurrency, timeout, memory, and fuel limits. Apply governance failure handling to processor overload, instantiation, and execution failures. Bug Fixes: Prevent synchronous WASM processor execution from blocking asynchronous request tasks. Ensure cancelled or timed-out requests retain runner capacity until processor execution has actually stopped. Enhancements: Reuse processor resource limits across production and simulation execution while preserving the simulation API. Restrict processor side effects to enforce mode and keep runner admission non-queuing. Documentation: Document processor runner configuration, resource limits, failure behavior, and operational constraints. Tests: Add coverage for runner isolation, resource budgets, concurrency bounds, cancellation and timeout behavior, overload governance, and side-effect handling.

title: Fix #2132: Share typed evaluator outcomes between enforcement and simulation
cleaned_text: Fix #2132: Share typed evaluator outcomes between enforcement and simulation Fixes #2132. Part of #2127. Summary Before this change, the live evaluator filter and policy simulation decided allowance in separate code. Simulation rebuilt the decision from optional fields and reason-code strings. Now both use one typed outcome and one posture resolver. New features/evaluator/src/outcome.rs , a transport-independent model: Outcome : NoMatch , Failure(EvaluatorFailure) , Unavailable , Skipped(Skip) and Evaluated { action, side_effects_suppressed } . EvaluatorFailure is a typed failure. It covers state, registry or interactions unavailable, processor unavailable, engine errors and processor errors. Skip : governance disabled, external engine skipped in basic audit, and external engine not simulated. A pure resolver, proposed_allowance / effective_allowance , returns Allow , Deny or Indeterminate . Helpers: reason() , baseline_used() and failure_used() . Live filter ( filter.rs ): Uses the shared types. Metrics, the block check and the audit-failure suppression rule now match on types, not label strings. Audit reason codes and attributes do not change. Evaluator simulation ( simulation.rs ): SimulationOutcome carries the typed Outcome . The existing reason codes are serialized only at the API edge: evaluator_not_matched , evaluator_external_engine_skipped , evaluator_processor_failed , evaluator_internal_error and evaluator_simulated . Simulation decision ( features/simulation/src/decision.rs ): The stage decision, effective decision and conditional come from the shared resolver. baseline_used and failure_used come from typed facts. The string whitelist is removed. Unavailable configuration always resolves to Deny when enforced, whatever on_failure says. A test covers this. External simulation stays Indeterminate and makes the result conditional in enforce mode. Docs: docs/policy-simulation.md explains the shared resolver and how baseline_used / failure_used are derived. The API, OpenAPI and audit field names and reason codes do not change, so the UI client does not need to be regenerated. Tests outcome::fixtures::cases() is a shared fixture table. It covers: pass, block, warn and malformed; filter_tools and set_metadata; suppressed effects; no match; state, engine and processor failures; invalid configuration; both skip kinds. The table runs across enforce, audit full, audit basic and disabled, with each no_match / on_failure combination. Tests: resolver_matches_fixture_table_for_every_posture and typed_facts_and_reasons_are_stable . live_and_simulation_agree_on_shared_fixture_allowance runs the real EvaluatorFilter::handle_body and the simulation prepare + evaluate steps for every posture. It asserts that both give the same allowance. It uses only committed WAT fixtures (a new tests/fixtures/response.wat template) and does not need actions/dist . New decision.rs tests cover baseline_used / failure_used . Validation cargo clippy --all-targets -p wanaku-feature-evaluator -p wanaku-feature-simulation : no new warnings. cargo test -p wanaku-feature-evaluator -p wanaku-feature-simulation --no-fail-fast : Simulation: 24 passed. Evaluator integration: 52 passed. Evaluator unit: 169 passed, 4 failed. The 4 failures already happen on main in an environment without actions/dist . They assert build WASM actions before evaluator tests , and #2128 covers that gating. They are expected to pass in CI, which builds the actions. cargo fmt --all -- --check : the changed files are clean. The formatting failures in features/plugins and infra/src/lib.rs already exist on main . 🤖 Generated with Claude Code https://claude.ai/code/session_01UAAhrhsd1gYVGJoatPKtLM _Generated by Claude Code_ Summary by Sourcery Unify evaluator outcome resolution across live enforcement and policy simulation while preserving existing external reporting contracts. Enhancements: Introduce a shared typed evaluator outcome model and posture resolver for allowance, action, baseline, failure, and side-effect handling. Preserve existing API, audit fields, and reason codes while deriving simulation decisions and facts from typed outcomes. Add shared outcome fixtures and live-versus-simulation agreement coverage across governance postures. Document how evaluator resolution and simulation conditionality determine baseline and failure usage. title: Fix #2130: Inject the MCP invocation adapter for forwarding filter tests
cleaned_text: Fix #2130: Inject the MCP invocation adapter for forwarding filter tests Fixes #2130. Part of #2127. Summary New McpInvoker trait in infra/src/mcp_client.rs . It is a narrow async contract with only three operations: call_tool , read_resource and get_prompt . Its signatures use only serde_json , http and the existing CallToolResponse / McpClientError , so rmcp types stay behind the adapter. Discovery, listing and LLM calls are not part of the trait. RmcpInvoker is the production adapter. It delegates to the existing rmcp-backed functions. Filters use the injected adapter. filters/src/invoker.rs::invoker_from_extensions reads Arc from the request extensions. ForwardExchange carries the adapter. tool_call.rs , resource_read.rs and prompt_get.rs call the adapter instead of the free functions. The order of operations does not change: provenance and forward lookup, then header-to-argument mapping, then credential injection, then the call. Server wiring. server/src/pipelines.rs adds an InvokerExtension that installs RmcpInvoker on every request, so runtime behavior does not change. If the extension is missing, a forwarded call returns a JSON-RPC internal error before credential brokerage runs. Docs: docs/architecture.md (Tool Routing steps and an "Invocation adapter" section) and one line in CLAUDE.md . Tests Test-only fixtures: RecordingInvoker records the operation, address, target, arguments and headers. It returns either a fixed value or an error. filter_context builds a minimal HttpFilterContext with the registry, a broker backed by FakeResolver , and the fake. Whole-filter tests: 6 each for tools/call , resources/read and prompts/get . Success: the filter calls the adapter exactly once with the resolved forward address, target, arguments and final headers. The final headers are the forwarded client header plus the brokered authorization . Zero calls: missing provenance, missing forward, disabled or unknown entry, missing binding and unresolvable secret. Credentials after mapping: a header mapped to an argument carries the client value. The brokered secret appears only in the headers. Redaction: returned content and upstream errors are redacted. JSON-RPC ids: responses keep the request's JSON-RPC id. No server, no network: these tests do not open a listening server, use the network or wait on a timeout. Existing wiremock tests: the protocol and content-preservation tests are kept. The mixed-content test now goes through RmcpInvoker . Note: "unavailable target" is tested as a disabled or unknown entry. The filters do not check ForwardEntry.available today, and this PR does not add that check because it would change behavior. Fail forwarded requests with an internal JSON-RPC error when the invocation adapter is unavailable. title: Fix #2135: Use the namespace PUT API when saving edits in the admin UI
cleaned_text: Fix #2135: Use the namespace PUT API when saving edits in the admin UI Fixes #2135. Part of #2127. Summary The admin UI saved a namespace edit as DELETE followed by POST. For a namespace that contains an A2A agent, the DELETE returned 409. If the DELETE succeeded and the POST failed, the namespace was lost. The server already supports PUT /api/v1/namespaces/{name} , but OpenAPI did not declare it, so the generated client had no such operation. OpenAPI ( server/src/openapi.rs ) now declares the existing PUT operation: request: NamespaceEntry ; 200 response: WanakuResponse ; 400 response: ManagementErrorResponse , for an invalid name, malformed JSON or a missing body. The server handler does not change. The name in the path still has priority over the name in the body. Generated contracts: ui/admin/openapi.json , src/api/wanaku-router-api.ts (new updateNamespace ) and the new models in src/models were regenerated with yarn run generate-api . No handwritten types were added. ui/admin/orval.config.ts : the response-envelope unwrapping now includes the Namespaces tag, so the PUT type matches the other operations. The client output for the existing namespace operations does not change. UI: use-namespaces.ts : updateNamespace calls only the generated PUT. NamespaceModal.tsx : the name stays read-only in edit mode. The modal sends the full stored entry, so authRequired and audience are no longer dropped. NamespacesPage.tsx : a failed save shows the server's error message. Docs: a new "Update a Namespace" section in docs/management-api.md . Tests Backend ( openapi.rs ): A namespace method/contract table. POST, GET list, GET one, PUT and DELETE must all be documented, nothing extra may be documented, and each operation must work at runtime. The published PUT contract has the declared request, response and error schemas. A PUT update returns the documented response shape, the path name has priority, and the change is stored. Malformed JSON, a missing name , a missing body and an invalid path name ( Bad_Name ) each return 400 with the documented error shape. The stored state does not change. title: Missing output encoding in `delete_json_doc`: `id` is echoed raw in the confirmation message
cleaned_text: Missing output encoding in delete_json_doc : id is echoed raw in the confirmation message Tool: delete_json_doc · Tested commit: 605dbb7 Weakness: CWE-79 Cross-site Scripting / unescaped output Summary delete_json_doc deletes a document from the Fireproof json_docs database and replies Deleted document with ID: , with the caller's id inserted verbatim. The ID is not validated or escaped, so markup or control characters in it come back unchanged. This only matters if a client renders tool output as HTML or Markdown, but the fix is small. Details src/index.ts:120-132 : case "delete_json_doc": { const id = String(request.params.arguments?.id); if (!id) { throw new Error("ID is required"); } await db.del(id); return { content: [{ type: "text", text: Deleted document with ID: ${id} }] }; } There is no check on the ID's format and no encoding of the echoed value. Two related details: String(undefined) is the string "undefined" , so the !id guard never fires when id is missing; and the reply says "Deleted" whether or not a document with that ID existed. Impact The id argument is chosen by the model and can be steered by prompt injection, and the echoed text goes back to the client. In clients that show tool results as plain text nothing happens. A client or UI that renders tool output as HTML or Markdown without escaping would render the caller's markup. Severity is low; this is a hardening issue in a demo server. Suggested fix Validate the ID before use (for example typeof id === "string" && /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$/.test(id) , matching the IDs Fireproof generates), fix the missing-argument check by testing the raw argument before String(...) , and return the ID JSON-encoded, for example Deleted document with ID: ${JSON.stringify(id)} . The same pattern applies to load_json_doc and query_json_docs .

title: v0.3.0
cleaned_text: Fixed: amenities and highlights were coming back empty Airbnb moved AMENITIES_DEFAULT and HIGHLIGHTS_DEFAULT to client-side rendering. Their entries in the section tree still existed and still reported sectionContentStatus: COMPLETE , but the section object held nothing beyond typename — so airbnb_listing_details returned an empty shell with no signal that anything was missing. Both sections are now recovered from the pdpPresentation branch of the same payload. Thanks to @vishnujayvel for diagnosing and fixing this (#42). Changed: seeAllAmenitiesGroups shape Amenities are now an object keyed by category rather than one long comma-joined string: "seeAllAmenitiesGroups": { "Bathroom": "Hair dryer", "Heating and cooling": "AC - split type ductless system, Heating", "Not included": "Dryer, Hot water" } This is a breaking change if you were parsing that field as a string. Amenities Airbnb shows struck through arrive under its own "Not included" category, so an amenity a listing lacks can't be misread as one it offers. The keying is applied to both the section tree and the recovered content, so the two paths can't return different shapes for different listings. Also in this release Highlights with a missing title no longer emit the literal string "null: …" Recovery merges onto the existing section instead of rebuilding it, so a partial stub keeps the fields the section tree did supply npm test now runs both suites, building first so they can't pass against a stale dist/ The .mcpb bundle is no longer swept into the npm tarball — it vendors the whole dependency tree, which took the published package from 49 KB to 6.1 MB manifest.json is kept in sync automatically on version bumps Note for npm users This is the first npm publish since 0.1.4 . If you install via npx @openbnb/mcp-server-airbnb , you were on code that predates client-side geocoding — international searches like "Paris, France" resolved to the wrong place. 0.3.0 brings npm current with everything in 0.2.0 as well.

title: feat: Streamable HTTP transport + bearer auth (Phase 2)
cleaned_text: feat: Streamable HTTP transport + bearer auth (Phase 2) Context urobnb needs to run as a long-lived container reachable over HTTP (Claude Code on the LAN, optionally claude.ai), not only over stdio for desktop clients. Phase 1 imported upstream as a single-file stdio server; this phase adds the HTTP transport, a bearer-token gate, and the Dokploy Compose artifact, while keeping index.ts / util.ts close to upstream (ADR-0001). Description urobnb's own code lands under src/ (strict, no any ); transport is chosen at runtime and the existing stdio path is untouched. src/config.ts — loadConfig() parses/validates MCP_TRANSPORT ( stdio | http ), PORT (default 8787), MCP_AUTH_TOKEN , LOG_LEVEL . Invalid transport/port throw (fail fast); unknown log level coerces to info . src/auth.ts — bearerAuth(token) Express middleware: constant-time compare, 401 without a valid Authorization: Bearer ; pass-through when no token is configured. src/http-transport.ts — createHttpApp / startHttpServer : open GET /health , bearer-gated POST /mcp using the SDK's StreamableHTTPServerTransport stateless ( sessionIdGenerator: undefined , enableJsonResponse: true ) with a fresh Server per request (via an injected factory); GET / DELETE /mcp → 405. index.ts — minimal edits: the tool handlers move into a createAirbnbServer() factory (bodies unchanged) and runServer() branches on MCP_TRANSPORT (stdio unchanged; http → startHttpServer ). The factory is passed into the transport module, so src/ never imports index.ts back. Deploy: docker-compose.yml (Dokploy service, MCP_TRANSPORT=http , healthcheck on /health ), Dockerfile EXPOSE 8787 . Decision recorded in docs/adr/0002-http-transport.md ; subsystem invariants in src/CLAUDE.md . Provisioning the Dokploy app (project/server/domain, MCP_AUTH_TOKEN , first deploy) is the operational follow-up, done via the Dokploy MCP after this merges. If implementation requires a change outside this issue's stated scope, STOP. Don't bundle it in. Report it to the maintainer with file paths and a recommended fix, and wait for approval before touching out-of-scope code. Acceptance Criteria [ ] MCP_TRANSPORT=http boots an Express server; stdio stays the default and unchanged. [ ] GET /health returns 200 {"status":"ok"} without auth. [ ] POST /mcp without a valid bearer returns 401 when MCP_AUTH_TOKEN is set; the initialize handshake succeeds with the correct bearer. [ ] Each POST /mcp uses a fresh server + stateless transport (no shared protocol state). [ ] npm run build , npm test (vitest), and npm run docs:check are green. [ ] Docs: ADR-0002 Tests Real vitest under test/ (no network — the transport test uses a stub server factory and never hits airbnb.com): test/config.test.ts — defaults; http selection; invalid transport/port throw; token presence; log-level fallback. test/auth.test.ts — pass-through with no token; 401 for missing/wrong/malformed header; next() for the correct token. test/http-transport.test.ts — /health 200; POST /mcp 401 without bearer; initialize returns serverInfo with the bearer, on an ephemeral port.
