title: fix: detect Airbnb country-domain handoff and allow overriding the domain
cleaned_text: fix: detect Airbnb country-domain handoff and allow overriding the domain Fixes #60. Problem Airbnb runs a per-country domain ( airbnb.co.uk , airbnb.fr , …) and hands requests off to the one matching the request origin. When it does, www.airbnb.com does not return the requested page — it returns a ~1KB stub that POSTs to /v2/domain_switch/handoff via JavaScript: It arrives as HTTP 200, not a 3xx , so no HTTP client follows it, and it contains none of the data the parsers look for. BASE_URL was hardcoded to https://www.airbnb.com with no way to change it, so from an affected region both tools failed unconditionally : { "error": "Failed to parse search results from Airbnb. The page structure may have changed.", "details": "Could not find data script element - page structure may have changed" } That message points at scraper rot rather than the redirect that actually happened, which is a slow thing to diagnose. Measured from a UK IP, same path, same geocoded bbox, same user-agent: URL | Status | Size | data-deferred-state www.airbnb.com/s/Lisbon--Portugal/homes?… | 200 | 964 B | absent www.airbnb.co.uk/s/Lisbon--Portugal/homes?… | 200 | 946 KB | present Replaying the bev / everest_cookie values from the handoff payload back to www.airbnb.com still returns the stub, so this is decided by request origin and can't be cookied around. DISABLE_GEOCODING is unrelated — geocoding resolves the right bbox; the failure is downstream of it. Changes AIRBNB_BASE_URL — BASE_URL now honours it and defaults to https://www.airbnb.com , so existing behaviour is unchanged. It applies to robots.txt, search and listing requests alike. Values are normalized to an origin, so a trailing slash can't yield https://host//s/... ; a value that can't be used (missing scheme, ftp:// ) is logged and ignored rather than failing later at request time. Handoff detection — both handlers check for the stub and report what actually happened: Airbnb handed this request off to its www.airbnb.co.uk country domain instead of serving , so there was no page to parse. Set AIRBNB_BASE_URL=https://www.airbnb.co.uk to query that domain directly. Startup log now includes the effective baseUrl alongside ignoreRobotsTxt / disableGeocoding . manifest.json exposes an "Airbnb domain" string field, so MCPB hosts get it without editing env vars by hand. README — documented under Configuration, plus a "Country domains" section explaining the mechanism. The detector bails out above 8KB. A real page is ~1MB, so this keeps the regex off large bodies and stops a page that merely *mentions* the handoff path from being misread as a redirect. Testing New test-domain-handoff.js (wired into npm test ) covers detection against a stub captured verbatim from the failing request, the cases that must not be treated as a handoff (real page, empty body, full-size page mentioning the path, non-handoff form, non-string input), and base URL normalization — 17 cases. It needs no network, so unlike the existing two suites it's safe as a CI gate. detectDomainHandoff: 7 ok normalizeBaseUrl: 10 ok all cases passed End-to-end against the built server over stdio from a UK IP: Scenario | Before | After airbnb_search , default domain | "page structure may have changed" | actionable handoff error naming .co.uk + the env var airbnb_search , AIRBNB_BASE_URL=https://www.airbnb.co.uk | same failure | listings returned, rooms/ URLs on the configured domain airbnb_listing_details , same override | same failure | amenities, house rules and policies returned test-extension.js and test-amenities.js assume airbnb.com serves a parseable page, so from an affected region they need AIRBNB_BASE_URL set to pass; I've noted that in the README rather than changing them, since they're deliberately live-network tests. I couldn't run them unmodified against airbnb.com from here — that's precisely the bug — but both pass with the override set. Notes for reviewers Default behaviour is unchanged: with AIRBNB_BASE_URL unset, the only difference is a clearer error when Airbnb hands the request off, and one extra key in the startup log. I deliberately did not auto-retry on the country domain, though it would make this work with zero configuration. Following the handoff means requesting a different host than the one whose robots.txt was fetched and checked at startup, and robotsTxtContent / isPathAllowed are currently single-host. Doing it properly means making robots state per-host, which felt like it deserved its own PR rather than riding along with a bug fix. Happy to write it if you'd like it in this one. Alternatively, if you'd rather not have the env var at all and prefer only the improved error message, I can trim the PR to that.

title: Hardcoded BASE_URL breaks both tools from non-US IPs: airbnb.com returns a domain-handoff stub, not the page
cleaned_text: Hardcoded BASE_URL breaks both tools from non-US IPs: airbnb.com returns a domain-handoff stub, not the page Summary BASE_URL is hardcoded to https://www.airbnb.com ( dist/index.js:137 , src/index.ts ), with no way to override it. From a non-US IP, www.airbnb.com does not serve the search page at all — it serves a ~960-byte JS domain-handoff stub that POSTs to the country domain. There is no data-deferred-state element in that stub, so both tools fail. From a UK IP, every airbnb_search call fails with: { "error": "Failed to parse search results from Airbnb. The page structure may have changed.", "details": "Could not find data script element - page structure may have changed", "diagnosis": "Could not parse script content as JSON" } The message points at Airbnb changing its page structure, but the structure is fine — the server is being handed a redirect stub instead of a results page. Root cause Requesting the exact URL the server builds returns HTTP 200 with a 964-byte body: Redirecting to www.airbnb.co.uk Redirecting to www.airbnb.co.uk Because the handoff is a JS-submitted POST form returned as HTTP 200 (not a 3xx), no HTTP client will follow it — follow: redirect in node-fetch doesn't help. Same path, same geocoded bbox, same user-agent, on the country domain: URL | Status | Size | data-deferred-state www.airbnb.com/s/Lisbon--Portugal/homes?... | 200 | 964 B | absent www.airbnb.co.uk/s/Lisbon--Portugal/homes?... | 200 | 946 KB | present Things that do not fix it: Replaying the bev / everest_cookie values from the handoff payload back to www.airbnb.com — still returns the stub, so it is IP-based rather than cookie-based. The DISABLE_GEOCODING flag — geocoding works correctly here (Photon resolves "Lisbon, Portugal" to the right bbox). The failure is downstream of it. airbnb_listing_details shares the same BASE_URL and is affected identically. Reproduction Requires a non-US IP (reproduced from the UK). airbnb_search({ location: "Lisbon, Portugal", adults: 2 }) Note that --ignore-robots-txt is needed to get this far at all, since Disallow: /s/*/* applies to User-agent: * ; the parse failure above happens after that check passes. Environment @openbnb/mcp-server-airbnb 0.3.0 Node v24.13.1, darwin arm64 stdio transport, self-hosted (not the openbnb.ai hosted server) Client: Claude Code Request origin: UK Suggested fix Make the domain configurable, defaulting to current behaviour: const BASE_URL = process.env.AIRBNB_BASE_URL || "https://www.airbnb.com"; Applying exactly that one-line patch locally and setting AIRBNB_BASE_URL=https://www.airbnb.co.uk makes both tools work — airbnb_search returns full listings, and airbnb_listing_details returns amenities, house rules and policies as documented. Two possible improvements beyond the env var: Detect the stub and retry. The handoff response is recognisable ( action="https://www. /v2/domain_switch/handoff" ). The server could parse the target host out of the form action and re-request the same path there, which would make this work with no configuration. Improve the error message. "The page structure may have changed" sends people looking for a scraper-rot bug. Detecting the handoff stub and saying "Airbnb redirected to a country domain" would be a much faster diagnosis — worth doing regardless of which fix above is chosen. Happy to open a PR for the env var plus the stub detection if that direction sounds right. Possibly related #40 — also a search-returns-nothing report, though the symptom differs (0 results with no error, on the hosted connector) and a commenter there says the local server works for them. Plausibly the same geo root cause for some users, so noting it rather than filing this as a duplicate.

title: fix: highlights recovery from #42 never matched the live field names
cleaned_text: fix: highlights recovery from #42 never matched the live field names Follow-up to #42 — my mistake there, and it left airbnb_listing_details returning no highlights at all. #42 restored the amenities and highlights sections by reading them out of pdpPresentation after Airbnb moved both to client-side rendering. The amenities half works. The highlights half doesn't: extractHighlights reads title / subtitle from each pdpPresentation.highlights[] item, but Airbnb ships those as headline / body , each wrapped in a LocalizedContent object: { " typename": "ListingPdpHighlight", "type": "LISTING_GUEST_FAVORITE", "headline": { " typename": "LocalizedContent", "localizedContent": "Top 10% of homes" }, "body": { " typename": "LocalizedContent", "localizedContent": "This home is highly ranked based on ratings, reviews, and reliability." } } Because no item has a title , every entry is filtered out and extractHighlights returns null , so the HIGHLIGHTS_DEFAULT section is omitted from the response entirely. The call still succeeds, so consumers can't tell the difference between "this listing has no highlights" and "the extractor no longer matches the payload." That silence is why #42 looked like it worked. The tests added in #42 used fixtures I wrote from the old field names, so they passed against a shape the live API doesn't serve. The fixture in this PR is copied from a real payload instead, typename fields included. Verification Checked against 20+ live listings spanning entire homes, private rooms, hotels and a hostel. Every one used headline / body ; none used title / subtitle . Before this change all of them returned null . Example (listing 53610715 ) — before: null . After: {"highlights": [ "Top 10% of homes: This home is highly ranked based on ratings, reviews, and reliability.", "In Rhododendron, near Mt. Hood: At the base of Mt. Hood, ...", "Private hot tub in the woods: A private hot tub ...", "Clean, cozy, and well-equipped: Guests praise ..." ]} The change A small localizedStr helper normalizes a localized field across every shape seen so far — a plain string, { localizedContent } , or { text } — and it is applied to both sides of the pair. headline / body take precedence, with title / subtitle kept as a fallback so older payloads (and the existing tests) behave exactly as before. Non-string values are rejected rather than interpolated, since an object would otherwise render as "[object Object]" , and an empty value is treated as missing so the legacy key still gets its turn. Output shape is unchanged: { highlights: string[] } , or null when nothing maps. Tests npm test : 31 pass, 0 fail. New coverage: the nested LocalizedContent shape (fixture taken from a real payload), the legacy title / subtitle shape, { text } bodies, non-string values, empty-value fallback to the legacy key, items missing every title key, and a guard asserting output elements are always plain strings containing no typename . Reverting extractHighlights to the previous title -only logic (without rebuilding) fails 5 of the new tests on assertions — expected highlights, got null and deep-equal mismatches — rather than crashing at import, so the tests fail with the symptom under test.

title: fix: surface Superhost status on search badges and listing details
cleaned_text: fix: surface Superhost status on search badges and listing details Fixes #24. airbnb_search and airbnb_listing_details both had Superhost data in the raw Airbnb payload and both dropped it before returning: Search — allowSearchResultSchema.badges only projected { text: true } . Airbnb assigns one badge per card, and Guest favorite wins over Superhost, so a Superhost listing often surfaces as "Guest favorite" with no type. The machine-readable loggingContext.badgeType ( SUPERHOST , TOP_X_GUEST_FAVORITE , …) was present and discarded. Details — Superhost does not live usefully on MEET_YOUR_HOST (that section is a stub today). It lives on pdpPresentation.hostInfo.passportData.isSuperhost (and related passport fields), which the tool never projected. Issue evidence also shows a stats array (Reviews / Rating) on the host section when Airbnb provides it. Approach Output-only; no new tool parameters. Keep searchBadgeSchema as { text: true } so the flattened badges string stays byte-identical to pre-fix output (e.g. "Guest favorite" — not "Guest favorite: SUPERHOST" ). Attach the machine-readable type as a sibling key on the result card ( badgeType: "SUPERHOST" ) after flatten, via extractBadgeType — same attach-after-flatten pattern this repo uses for priceBreakdown . Add extractHostInfo(pdp) (same small pure-extractor style as extractAmenities / extractHighlights ): returns { isSuperhost, name?, titleText?, stats? } or null when passport data is absent. stats is an array of { label, value } when present on the hostInfo branch ( passportData.stats or hostInfo.stats ); omitted otherwise. Live payloads may not always carry stats — they surface when Airbnb provides them. Wire an additive HOST detail entry from that extractor. Tests Offline fixture suite ( npm test ): Search: flattened badges string remains exactly "Guest favorite" while badgeType: "SUPERHOST" is attached as its own key; TOP_X_GUEST_FAVORITE and text-only badges; extractBadgeType null when loggingContext is absent. Details: extractHostInfo true/false/absent; Superhost on the healthy PDP fixture; null when branch missing; stats present and stats omitted fixtures. Revert-proof (stub, not full-file restore): temporarily stub searchBadgeSchema to { text: true } , extractBadgeType to always return null , and extractHostInfo to always return null in the built dist/util.js , then run node --test test/*.test.mjs (no rebuild). That yields assertion-level failures matching the issue symptom — Superhost signal absent ( badgeType undefined / extractHostInfo returns null) — 7 fail / 27 pass . Restore the real dist/util.js → 34 pass / 0 fail . Verification $ npm test ℹ tests 34 ℹ pass 34 ℹ fail 0 Spot-check on a live Superhost listing (e.g. id 30326310 ): raw passportData.isSuperhost: true / titleText Superhost while pre-fix MCP search returned badges "Guest favorite" only (no badgeType ) and MCP details contained no Superhost signal. Base projection of {text:"Guest favorite", loggingContext:{badgeType:"SUPERHOST"}} under { text: true } drops to {text:"Guest favorite"} — gap still holds without the post-flatten badgeType attach.

title: feat: expose cancellation policy, house rules, and occupancy
cleaned_text: feat: expose cancellation policy, house rules, and occupancy Fixes #50. airbnb_listing_details recovered amenities and highlights from pdpPresentation , but three other decision inputs stayed buried in the payload: Cancellation policy options (non-refundable vs refundable upgrade), including a description of the refund window and an upgrade price when Airbnb attaches one. House rules with item subtitles (e.g. quiet-hour windows), not just bare titles. Occupancy ( personCapacity ) so a caller can compare it against the "N guests maximum" house-rule line when the two disagree. Where the data actually lives Live payloads (listing 1425762021690163826 with dates selected) put these in slightly different places than the section tree: Field | Source personCapacity | niobeClientData[*][1].data.node.pdpPresentation house rules (+ subtitles) | POLICIES_DEFAULT.section.houseRulesSections cancellation options | sections.metadata.bookingPrefetchData.cancellationPolicies House rules were already partially returned via allowSectionSchema , but item subtitles were dropped. Cancellation and occupancy were absent from the tool output entirely. Approach Pure extractors in util.ts , matching extractAmenities / extractHighlights : extractOccupancy(pdp) → { personCapacity } extractHouseRules(policiesSection) → grouped rules with labeled subtitles; falls back to the short houseRules preview extractCancellationPolicies(prefetch) → dual-rate options; tolerates both snake_case and camelCase keys; optional price when present findBookingPrefetchData(clientData) → locates the prefetch branch Wired in handleAirbnbListingDetails : expand POLICIES_DEFAULT schema to keep house-rule subtitles and the cancellation title/display fields when they are on the section push OCCUPANCY and CANCELLATION_POLICY detail entries when recovered recover POLICIES_DEFAULT from extractHouseRules if the section is stubbed or dropped No new tool parameters; output-only surface. findBookingPrefetchData iterates niobeClientData rather than assuming the prefetch branch's position; a fixture places it at a non-zero index to prove it. Tests Offline fixture suite ( npm test ): occupancy present / absent / non-numeric house rules subtitles (string and { text } ), preview fallback, null cancellation dual-rate + upgrade price, camelCase, null / empty findBookingPrefetchData path walk, including prefetch at a non-zero index Revert-proof: stub the four extractors to return null → new tests fail with the issue symptom (fields absent) → restore → full suite green (34 pass / 0 fail). Verification $ npm test ℹ tests 34 ℹ pass 34 ℹ fail 0 Live spot-check (not a gate): listing 1425762021690163826 with check_in=2026-10-01&check_out=2026-10-05 yields personCapacity: 10 , dual-rate cancellation names + tooltips, and Quiet hours: 11:00 PM - 7:00 AM under house rules. Note: the refundable-upgrade dollar amount is often missing from the initial SSR payload even when both rate names are present; the extractor surfaces price when Airbnb attaches it (fixture covers $138.67 ). Stacked on #52: the diff includes its test-infrastructure commits until #52 merges; the feature itself is the top commit.

title: feat: preserve the structured price breakdown instead of flattening it to a string
cleaned_text: feat: preserve the structured price breakdown instead of flattening it to a string Stacked on #43 (which is stacked on #42). Review the last commit only. Why explanationData.priceDetails is an array of line groups , each holding typed items — DefaultExplanationLineItem for the nightly subtotal, DiscountedExplanationLineItem for a reduction, HighlightExplanationLineItem for the post-discount summary. flattenArraysInObject joins that whole tree into one string: "3 nights x $890.67: $2,672.00, Special offer: -$52.50, " which loses the grouping, the item types, and any way to tell a discount from a subtotal. It also arrives with a trailing separator. Separately, allowSearchResultSchema never picked accessibilityLabel — the only place Airbnb states whether a total excludes tax. What "priceBreakdown": { "lineItems": [ {"description": "3 nights x $630.00", "price": "$1,890.00"}, {"description": "Last-minute discount", "price": "-$85.00", "type": "discount"}, {"description": "Price after discount", "price": "$1,805.00", "type": "total"} ], "note": "$1,805.00 total before taxes" } On the tax note, and what this deliberately does not claim I looked for a per-listing all-in vs pre-tax flag and there isn't one. Across ~90 listings in five US markets (Welches OR, Rhododendron OR, Leavenworth WA, Chelan WA, New York NY): displayPriceStyle was TOTAL_ONLY on every single listing no listing showed a tax line item anywhere pricingToggle was null in every response The "total before taxes" accessibility label is the only tax signal in the payload, and it appears solely on highlight items — so only listings with an active discount carry it. It is surfaced as note when present and omitted otherwise, never defaulted , because a missing note must not be read as "taxes are included." So this PR claims faithful structure plus the caveat where Airbnb actually states it. It does not claim a reliable all-in/pre-tax boolean, because that data isn't there. Ordering extractPriceBreakdown must run before cleanObject , which strips the typename it reads. The two calls sit adjacent in handleAirbnbSearch with a comment. It deliberately does not throw when typename is missing. A hard failure would lose all 18 results over a cosmetic field, and for a scraper that is the wrong trade — the items are still emitted, just untyped. Partial output beats all-or-nothing. Tests 8 new, 39 total, all offline against committed fixtures. Covers the discounted and plain shapes, the note being present and absent, sign preservation on discounts, and that compactSearchResult prefers a structured breakdown over the lossy string when one is supplied.

title: feat: add compact mode to airbnb_search (~60% fewer tokens), plus a test suite
cleaned_text: feat: add compact mode to airbnb_search (~60% fewer tokens), plus a test suite Why An MCP server's consumer is a context window, and airbnb_search currently spends most of its response on structure rather than information. One search is roughly 4,900 tokens for 18 results , and a large fraction of that carries nothing a caller can act on: demandStayListing.id is base64 of "DemandStayListing: " — it restates the id already extracted next to it the listing name arrives at demandStayListing.description.name.localizedStringWithTranslationPreference , which costs more in key names than the name itself explanationData.title is the constant string "Price details" , repeated once per result mapSecondaryLine and secondaryLine are usually empty strings two-space indentation is about a quarter of the payload What compact: true flattens each result to a shallow object and emits unindented JSON. Measured end to end against a live Welches, Oregon search (2026-08-15 → 2026-08-18, 7 adults, 18 results): | bytes | ~tokens current | 19,577 | 4,894 compact: true | 7,303 | 1,826 saved | | 62.7% Re-measured after the 0.3.0 refresh, on the branch's fixture set with the structural harness from the test suite: 59.9% (minified verbose → minified compact) and 69.2% end to end (pretty verbose → minified compact). The live-search number above predates the 0.3.0 merge. No information is dropped. Every field a caller can act on survives, including the bedrooms/beds/baths line and the full price breakdown: {"id":"53610715","url":"https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/53610715","name":"Hilltop Home w/ Hot Tub near Skiing, Golf & Trails","layout":"4 bedrooms, 5 beds, 2.5 baths","badges":"Guest favorite","rating":"4.95 out of 5 average rating, 191 reviews","price":"$1,012 for 3 nights, originally $1,212","priceDetails":"3 nights x $337.33: $1,012.00","latitude":45.3388,"longitude":-121.93688} Absent and empty fields are omitted rather than serialized as null , so a sparse result costs nothing to represent. It is opt-in — no existing caller changes behaviour. I'd happily flip the default in a follow-up if you'd prefer, but that seemed like your call rather than mine. Tests This adds the repo's first test suite, which felt worth doing regardless of this feature. compactSearchResult is a pure function in util.ts and is covered directly, along with pickBySchema , cleanObject and flattenArraysInObject , which had no coverage at all. Fixtures are captured from a live search and committed, so tests run offline — no network, no flakiness. Uses the built-in node:test runner, so no new dependency . $ npm test ℹ tests 18 ℹ pass 18 ℹ fail 0 The suite includes a regression guard asserting compaction stays above a 50% reduction, so the saving cannot silently erode. Notes One test documents that pickBySchema over an empty object returns an empty object rather than throwing. That behaviour is correct here, but it is also why a stubbed section reads as "no data" instead of "extraction broke" — see #41. npm test builds first, since the tests import from dist/ .

title: chore(deps): bump fastmcp from 2.5.1 to 2.14.0
cleaned_text: chore(deps): bump fastmcp from 2.5.1 to 2.14.0 Bumps fastmcp from 2.5.1 to 2.14.0. Release notes Sourced from fastmcp's releases . v2.14.0: Task and You Shall Receive FastMCP 2.14 begins adopting the MCP 2025-11-25 specification, headlined by protocol-native background tasks that let long-running operations report progress without blocking clients. This release also graduates the OpenAPI parser to standard, adds first-class support for several new spec features, and removes deprecated APIs accumulated across the 2.x series. Background Tasks (SEP-1686) Long-running operations (like tool calls) normally block MCP clients until they complete. The new MCP background task protocol (SEP-1686) lets clients start operations, track progress, and retrieve results without blocking. For FastMCP users, taking advantage of this new functionality is as easy as adding task=True to any async decorator. Under the hood, it's powered by Docket , the enterprise task scheduler at the heart of Prefect Cloud that handles millions of concurrent tasks every day. from fastmcp import FastMCP from fastmcp.dependencies import Progress mcp = FastMCP("MyServer") @​mcp .tool(task=True) async def train_model(dataset: str, progress: Progress = Progress()) -> str: await progress.set_total(100) for epoch in range(100): ... training work ... await progress.increment() return "Model trained successfully" Clients that call this tool in task-augmented mode (for FastMCP clients, that merely means another task=True !) receive a task ID immediately, poll for progress updates, and fetch results when ready. Background tasks work out-of-the-box with an in-memory backend, and users can optionally provide a Redis URL for persistence, horizontal scaling, and single-digit millisecond task pickup latency. When using Redis, users can also add additional Docket workers to scale out their task processing. Read the docs here ! OpenAPI Parser Promotion The experimental OpenAPI parser graduates to standard. The new architecture delivers improved performance through single-pass schema processing and cleaner internal abstractions. Existing code works unchanged; users of the experimental module should update their imports. MCP 2025-11-25 Spec Support This release begins adopting the MCP 2025-11-25 specification . Beyond the core SDK updates, FastMCP adds first-class developer experiences for: SEP-1686 : Background tasks with progress tracking SEP-1699 : SSE polling and event resumability, with full AsyncKeyValue support SEP-1330 : Multi-select enum elicitation schemas SEP-1034 : Default values for elicitation schemas SEP-986 : Tool name validation at registration time As the MCP SDK continues to adopt more of the specification, FastMCP will add corresponding high-level APIs. Breaking Changes & Cleanup This release removes deprecated APIs accumulated across the 2.x series: BearerAuthProvider , Context.get_http_request() , the dependencies parameter, legacy resource prefix formats, and several deprecated methods. The upgrade guide provides migration paths for each. What's Changed ... (truncated) Changelog Sourced from fastmcp's changelog . title: "Changelog" icon: "list-check" rss: true tag: NEW v3.0.2: Threecovery Mode II Two community-contributed fixes: auth headers from MCP transport no longer leak through to downstream OpenAPI APIs, and background task workers now correctly receive the originating request ID. Plus a new docs example for context-aware tool factories. Fixes 🐞 fix: prevent MCP transport auth header from leaking to downstream OpenAPI APIs by @​stakeswky in #3262 fix: propagate origin_request_id to background task workers by @​gfortaine in #3175 Docs 📚 Add v3.0.1 release notes by @​jlowin in #3259 docs: add context-aware tool factory example by @​machov in #3264 Full Changelog : v3.0.1...v3.0.2 v3.0.1: Three-covery Mode First patch after 3.0 — mostly smoothing out rough edges discovered in the wild. The big ones: middleware state that wasn't surviving the trip to tool handlers now does, Tool.from_tool() accepts callables again, OpenAPI schemas with circular references no longer crash discovery, and decorator overloads now return the correct types in function mode. title: feat: add Streamable HTTP transport + Docker image
cleaned_text: feat: add Streamable HTTP transport + Docker image Summary Adds two capabilities to ghost-mcp : Streamable HTTP transport — the server currently speaks stdio only. This adds an HTTP transport (opt-in via MCP_TRANSPORT=http ) so multiple MCP clients can connect concurrently over a shared endpoint — the case that matters when running the server as a shared service for agents like Hermes. A multi-stage Docker image so the server can be built and deployed as a container. What changed src/server.ts Transport selection on MCP_TRANSPORT — stdio remains the default (no behavior change for existing users); http serves the MCP Streamable HTTP transport. PORT (default 3210 ) and HOST (default 0.0.0.0 ) env vars for the HTTP path. GET /health liveness probe returning {"status":"ok"} , for container orchestrators (Docker/Podman healthchecks, systemd). Dockerfile + .dockerignore Multi-stage build: node:22-bookworm-slim (devDeps, runs tsc ) → node:22-alpine (production deps only). npm ci --omit=dev --ignore-scripts — the --ignore-scripts matters because the package's prepare hook runs tsc , which fails in the runtime stage where TypeScript is absent. ENV MCP_TRANSPORT=http PORT=3210 so the image serves HTTP out of the box; EXPOSE 3210 . README.md Documented the Streamable HTTP transport, its env vars, and Docker/Podman usage. package-lock.json Regenerated to align its top-level name / version / bin with package.json . The committed lock still said ghost-mcp-ts 1.0.0 (no bin ), which is stale relative to @fanyangmeng/ghost-mcp 0.2.0 . Design note: why stateless mode The HTTP transport runs in stateless mode ( sessionIdGenerator: undefined ). A stateful session latches _initialized after the first client and then rejects every subsequent initialize with 400 "Server already initialized" — correct for a single long-lived client, but exactly wrong for a shared server that many agents connect to and reconnect against. Stateless mode has no session latch, so any number of clients can connect, disconnect, and reconnect cleanly. Test plan There is no test suite in this repo ( npm test is a stub), so I verified by exercising the real path: Build : npm run build (tsc) passes. title: feat(posts): add newsletter + email_segment params to posts_edit
cleaned_text: feat(posts): add newsletter + email_segment params to posts_edit Summary Adds the newsletter and email_segment parameters to posts_add and posts_edit so that publishing a post through this MCP can trigger the subscriber email send, matching Ghost's native Admin API behavior. These two parameters already exist on Ghost's Admin API as query parameters on the post create/update endpoints (https://docs.ghost.org/admin-api/posts/sending-a-post). Without them, calling posts_edit with status: "published" transitions the post state but does not send the post as email, because Ghost only sends when a newsletter is specified on the request: "Posts are sent by email if and only if an active newsletter is provided." Same gap was raised for the n8n Ghost node (https://community.n8n.io/t/add-newsletter-email-segment-to-ghost-node/106617) and on the Ghost forum (https://forum.ghost.org/t/email-segment-syntax-for-creating-a-post/50275). Changes src/tools/posts.ts : new emailSendParams schema fragment ( newsletter , email_segment ), spread into both posts_add and posts_edit input schemas. src/tools/posts.ts : both handlers now forward these two values via the @tryghost/admin-api SDK's query-parameters argument (the same channel the existing source: "html" option uses), rather than in the post body. This matters because Ghost expects newsletter and email_segment as query parameters, not post fields, so they are destructured out of the post data before the create/update call. Why a separate fragment instead of postMutableFields postMutableFields is spread into the request body. email_only (added earlier) belongs there because it is a real post property. newsletter and email_segment are send-control query parameters, not post fields, so they are kept in their own fragment and routed to the SDK's query-param argument. Putting them in the body would get them ignored or rejected by Ghost. Testing Tested against a live Ghost Pro site via a local linked build, draft-only so no subscriber emails fired: created a draft post, then called posts_edit with newsletter , email_segment , and status: "draft" . Captured the outgoing request and confirmed the URL was: PUT /ghost/api/admin/posts/{id}/?newsletter=default-newsletter&email_segment=all Ghost returned 200, the post stayed in draft, no email object was attached, and the draft was deleted afterward. npm run build passes clean. Side observation (not this PR's bug to fix): the SDK's JWT auth chain ( @tryghost/admin-api -> jsonwebtoken -> jwa -> buffer-equal-constant-time ) throws on Node 24+ because it reads the removed SlowBuffer.prototype . I ran the smoke test under Node 20 LTS. The code in this PR is Node-version-agnostic; flagging in case it helps your own QA path. Context Filed in response to your invitation on https://github.com/MFYDev/ghost-mcp/issues/20 (2026-06-05): "let's just make a large PR should be good enough." I kept this one narrow to the two missing email params. Happy to adjust naming, types, or the body-vs-query split if you have a preferred convention.

title: Build fails with @modelcontextprotocol/sdk >=1.12: capabilities not valid in McpServer first argument
cleaned_text: Build fails with @modelcontextprotocol/sdk >=1.12: capabilities not valid in McpServer first argument Description Running npm run build (or npm install , which triggers prepare ) fails with a TypeScript error: src/server.ts:20:5 - error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'capabilities' does not exist in type '{ version: string; name: string; ... }'. 20 capabilities: { ~~~~~~~~~~~~ Root Cause The McpServer constructor signature changed in newer versions of @modelcontextprotocol/sdk . The capabilities property moved from the first argument ( Implementation ) to the second argument ( ServerOptions ). The current code passes capabilities inline with name / version : const server = new McpServer({ name: "ghost-mcp-ts", version: "1.0.0", capabilities: { ... } // TS2353 — not valid here }); Fix Move capabilities to the second argument: const server = new McpServer( { name: "ghost-mcp-ts", version: "1.0.0" }, { capabilities: { resources: {}, tools: {}, prompts: {}, logging: {} } } ); Reproduction git clone https://github.com/MFYDev/ghost-mcp.git cd ghost-mcp npm install # fails during prepare → build step Installed SDK version at time of report: 1.29.0 (resolved from ^1.10.1 in package.json).

cleaned_text: feat(posts): accept Ghost metadata fields in posts_add + posts_edit Summary Surface the full mutable post field set on posts_add and posts_edit so MCP clients can manage SEO metadata, social preview fields, tags, authors, and code injection without bypassing the wrapper. Problem Before this change, posts_edit accepted only {id, title, html, lexical, status, updated_at} . Fields like meta_title , og_* , twitter_* , tags , codeinjection_head , feature_image_alt , and custom_excerpt could not be set via the MCP. Real-world impact: a workflow that drafted a blog post through Claude + this MCP still required a manual round-trip through Ghost admin to fill in SEO metadata, tags, and Open Graph cards before the post was shippable. Clients had to either call the Ghost Admin API directly (JWT-signed REST, Cloudflare UA handling, etc.) or paste metadata manually. Change Both posts_add and posts_edit now accept the documented mutable fields from the Ghost Admin API post resource. Fields are extracted into a shared postMutableFields object so the two schemas stay in sync. New fields (all optional, backwards compatible) slug , visibility , featured , email_only , published_at custom_excerpt feature_image , feature_image_alt , feature_image_caption meta_title , meta_description og_title , og_description , og_image twitter_title , twitter_description , twitter_image codeinjection_head , codeinjection_foot canonical_url tags — accepts string (slug) or { id?, slug?, name? } authors — accepts string (slug) or { id?, slug?, email? } What I did NOT touch Existing fields ( title , html , lexical , status , id , updated_at ) are unchanged posts_browse / posts_read / posts_delete untouched No version bump — leaving that to the maintainer's release flow package-lock.json — restored after npm install drift so the diff stays focused on the schema change Why @tryghost/admin-api already handles it The underlying SDK forwards arbitrary fields on posts.edit(args, options) and posts.add(args, options) to Ghost's REST API, which validates server-side. The only thing blocking clients was the Zod schema on the MCP tool — this PR just widens the gate. title: Missing output encoding and validation in `update-connection-settings`: `url` is accepted as any string and echoed raw
cleaned_text: Missing output encoding and validation in update-connection-settings : url is accepted as any string and echoed raw Repository: meilisearch/meilisearch-mcp · Tool: update-connection-settings · Tested commit: b764c9f Weakness: CWE-79 Cross-site Scripting / unescaped output Summary update-connection-settings replaces the Meilisearch URL and API key that every other tool uses. It accepts any string as url , rebuilds the client, and returns Successfully updated connection settings to URL: with the value inserted unchanged. The reflected text itself has low impact. The more important part is the missing validation: there is no scheme or host check, and the value is also logged raw. Details src/meilisearch_mcp/server.py:95-103 : @mcp.tool(name="update-connection-settings", annotations=WRITE) def update_connection_settings( url: Optional[str] = None, api_key: Optional[str] = None ) -> CallToolResult: """Update Meilisearch connection settings""" self.update_connection(url, api_key) return _result( f"Successfully updated connection settings to URL: {self.url}" ) update_connection ( src/meilisearch_mcp/server.py:71-82 ) stores the value and builds a new MeilisearchClient(self.url, self.api_key) ( src/meilisearch_mcp/client.py:17-26 ), with no check of scheme, host or characters. It then logs logger.info(f"Updated Meilisearch connection settings: url={self.url}") ( server.py:82 ) to stderr ( server.py:423 ). If api_key is omitted, the previous key is kept ( server.py:77-78 ). So the existing key stays attached to whatever URL was just set. Steps to reproduce Prerequisites: Python and uv (or pip ). No running Meilisearch instance is needed for this tool, and no environment variables are needed. Start the server as the README describes: uvx -n meilisearch-mcp . To test the tested commit, run pip install -e . in a checkout at b764c9f , then meilisearch-mcp . Call the tool: {"url": " tofu-poc "} import asyncio from mcp import ClientSession, StdioServerParameters from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client async def main(): server = StdioServerParameters(command="uvx", args=["-n", "meilisearch-mcp"]) async with stdio_client(server) as (read, write): async with ClientSession(read, write) as session: await session.initialize() result = await session.call_tool("update-connection-settings", {"url": " tofu-poc "}) print(result) asyncio.run(main()) The returned text is Successfully updated connection settings to URL: tofu-poc . The value was accepted as a URL and is echoed with the markup unchanged. A follow-up get-connection-settings call shows it is now the active URL. Expected behavior The tool rejects values that are not http:// or https:// URLs with a host. It does not echo raw markup, and it neutralizes CR/LF before logging. Actual behavior Any string is accepted and echoed. From the fuzzing run: input: {'url': '${urmmmm', 'api_key': 'mmmm'} output: 'Successfully updated connection settings to URL: ${urmmmm' Impact The model chooses the arguments, and prompt injection in untrusted content (for example, a document being indexed) can steer them. The echoed URL is plain text, so the reflection alone is low severity. The missing validation matters more. A steered call can point the server at any host, and every later tool call (search, document reads, key management) then sends its requests there with the configured API key. That can leak the key and redirect data to a host the user did not choose. Suggested fix Parse url with urllib.parse.urlsplit . Require scheme http or https and a non-empty hostname, and reject control characters. Consider requiring the API key to be supplied again whenever the host changes, so an existing key is not silently reused for a new host. Optionally, support an operator-configured allowlist of hosts. Log the URL with %r (or strip \r and \n ), and keep the echoed URL out of the success message, or return it in structured content only.

title: Migrate to MCP Python SDK v2 (spec 2026-07-28)
cleaned_text: Migrate to MCP Python SDK v2 (spec 2026-07-28) Why The MCP 2026-07-28 specification landed this week — the largest revision since launch (stateless core, server/discover , multi round-trip requests, deprecation of the legacy logging capability) — together with the stable mcp==2.0.0 Python SDK . The v1.x SDK line is now maintenance-only, and our low-level Server -based implementation doesn't compile against v2. What changed Client-facing interface is preserved : same 26 tool names, same argument names (camelCase, including from on get-tasks ), same text responses. Existing Claude Desktop / uvx stdio configs keep working — the v2 server still answers the legacy initialize handshake. Server rewrite (server.py): the 823-line low-level implementation (26 hand-written JSON schemas + a 300-line if/elif dispatch) is now ~450 lines of @mcp.tool() -decorated functions with schemas inferred from type hints. New protocol features : Structured output : every data-returning tool now returns structuredContent alongside the legacy text (additive). Tool annotations : readOnlyHint / destructiveHint on all 26 tools. OpenAI Agent SDK compat kept (#27): additionalProperties: false is still applied to all input schemas. Logging : deleted the custom MCPLogger (its file logging was silently broken due to a handler-dedup bug, and the MCP logging capability is deprecated in the new spec) in favor of stdlib logging to stderr. Version unification : 0.7.0 everywhere (was 0.6.0 / 0.5.0 / 0.1.0 in three different places). CI : Meilisearch service image bumped v1.16 → v1.28. Behavior changes for clients Tool errors are now spec-standard isError: true results (previously ordinary results with "Error: ..." text). Clients string-matching "Error:" should check isError instead. Inferred schemas express optional params as anyOf [T, null] with title / default keys — cosmetic churn for schema-diffing consumers, harmless at runtime. Removed the delete-tasks entry from the README tool list — that tool never existed. Testing (real MCP round-trips) tests/test_mcp_client.py now drives the server through a real MCP client over the SDK's in-memory transport (the old harness poked private v1 SDK internals) — all previous scenarios kept, plus structured-output and annotation assertions. New tests/test_stdio_e2e.py : spawns python -m src.meilisearch_mcp as a subprocess and runs a full CRUD round-trip (list tools → create-index → add-documents → search → delete-index) over the actual stdio transport . ✅ 40 passed, 2 skipped (Docker-gated) against a live Meilisearch ✅ black --check clean ✅ MCP Inspector CLI ( tools/list , tools/call ) round-trip — confirms an external TypeScript client on the older protocol still connects and sees structuredContent 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: fix(sql): keep ClickHouse plugin macros intact when substituting $__from and $__to
cleaned_text: fix(sql): keep ClickHouse plugin macros intact when substituting $ from and $ to What The ClickHouse dialect's SubstituteMacros replaced $ from , $ to , $ interval_ms and $ interval as plain substrings. The ClickHouse datasource plugin has macros that start with the same characters and are expanded server-side, so they reached Grafana already mangled: $ toTime → 1792159528507Time (ClickHouse: unknown identifier) $ fromTime → 1792155928507Time $ interval_s → 3s_s Any panel using those macros failed through run_panel_query (and the same SQL through query_sql ). Observed on Grafana 12 with grafana-clickhouse-datasource panels that use $ fromTime / $ toTime and greatest($ interval_s, 60) . The substitution now replaces whole tokens only (word boundary after the macro name), leaving $ fromTime , $ toTime , $ fromTime_ms , $ toTime_ms , $ interval_s , $ timeInterval and the other plugin macros for the plugin. Tests Four new cases in TestClickHouseDialect_SubstituteMacros : $ fromTime / $ toTime untouched, the _ms variants untouched, $ interval_s untouched, and $ from / $ to next to punctuation still replaced. go test -tags unit ./tools/sql , go vet , gofmt pass. Scoped to the ClickHouse dialect; the other dialects use the same substring replace but their plugins have no $ from… / $ to… -prefixed macros.

title: Consolidate the tool surface into action-based read/write tool pairs
cleaned_text: Consolidate the tool surface into action-based read/write tool pairs Placeholder / umbrella issue. The shape of the proposal matters more than the specifics below; individual categories can be split into their own issues as work starts. The problem The tool surface has grown past what clients handle well. Measured against the current main (2026-08-21), the hosted Grafana Cloud MCP server advertises: | Tools | JSON schema | ≈ tokens Full surface (write enabled) | 110 | 178 KB | ~44,600 Read-only grant (scope-filtered) | 82 | 102 KB | ~25,500 (Token figures are a rough 4-chars-per-token estimate over the serialized mcp.Tool values, so treat them as an order of magnitude, not a measurement.) That is ~45k tokens of tool definitions before the model has read a single word of the user's question. #569 raised this at ~16k tokens in February; the surface has since roughly tripled. Beyond the context cost, many clients degrade in tool-selection accuracy well before 100 tools, and some cap the list outright. Proposal Consolidate related tools into action-based tools , and split each into a read tool and a write tool as two distinct names : dashboards_read { action: "get" | "search" | "summary" | "panel_queries" | "property", ... } dashboards_write { action: "create" | "update" | "delete", ... } rather than today's roughly one-tool-per-endpoint layout. alerting_manage_rules and the agento11y_manage_* family already do the action-parameter half of this, so the pattern is established — the new part is the read/write split. Why split the names rather than keep one gated tool The current consolidated tools register one tool name from two variants — ManageRulesRead and ManageRulesReadWrite both register as alerting_manage_rules , with enableWriteTools selecting which. That shape has a real downstream cost: it is invisible to any consumer that classifies tools by name. The hosted Cloud MCP server has to gate tools on OAuth scope ( grafana:read / grafana:query / grafana:write ), and it derives the write set by registering the library twice — once with write off, once with write on — and diffing the tool names. Same-name variants produce an empty diff, so every one of them has to be hand-listed as write-capable, with a cross-check test against the readOnlyHint annotation to catch new ones. That list currently carries alerting_manage_rules , alerting_manage_silences , generate_deeplink , grafana_api_request and five agento11y_manage_* tools, and it grows with every new consolidated tool upstream adds. Two distinct names make the boundary self-describing: name-based classification works, a read-only deployment or a read-scoped grant loads only the read half, and the write half never appears in a list it shouldn't be in. It also means the read tool's schema does not have to document actions the caller cannot invoke — which is where a chunk of the token saving comes from, on top of simply having fewer tools. Sketch of the groupings Rough starting point, not a committed plan: dashboards_read / dashboards_write datasources_read / datasources_write alerting_read / alerting_write (absorbing today's alerting_manage_* ) incidents_read / incidents_write oncall_read / oncall_write annotations_read / annotations_write folders_read / folders_write Per-datasource query tools (Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, …) probably stay separate — they are read-only, their schemas carry genuinely distinct query-language guidance, and collapsing them would hurt tool selection rather than help it. Open questions Does an action parameter hurt tool-selection accuracy relative to distinct tool names? Worth measuring before committing — the token saving is worthless if the model picks the wrong action. An eval over the existing alerting_manage_rules consolidation would give a real signal. How do we stage this without breaking every existing consumer? Probably: add the consolidated tools, keep the granular ones behind a flag for a deprecation window, then flip the default. Do the _read / _write names want a category prefix that matches the existing --disable- flags, so the two surfaces stay navigable together? How does this interact with clients that support deferred / lazy tool loading? If a client only materializes schemas on demand, consolidation matters less for them — but it still matters for the ones that don't, which today is most of them. Related #569 — the original "reduce the size of the MCP" issue, filed at ~16k tokens #572 — "Consider only adding certain tools if they will be useful" (closed)

It supports the 2026-07-28 revision of the Model Context Protocol and serves every earlier revision from the same server. pip install mcp now installs 2.x. pip install "mcp[cli]" or uv add "mcp[cli]" Documentation Rewrite The documentation has the full tutorial and API reference. Coming from v1? What's new in v2 is the tour of what changed and why, and the migration guide lists every breaking change with before-and-after code. V1 Maintenance mode v1.x is in maintenance mode and will only receive security fixes from now on The 1.x line lives on the v1.x branch, continues to receive critical bug fixes and security patches, and is documented at . If your project is not ready to migrate, keep a =1.28,<2 ). Highlights One SDK, both protocol eras v2 speaks the 2026-07-28 revision (stateless requests with no handshake, server/discover , subscriptions/listen , multi-round-trip requests) and still serves every 2025-era client from the same MCPServer , over Streamable HTTP and stdio, with nothing to configure. Client(target) negotiates the version automatically. FastMCP is now MCPServer , and there is a first-class Client The decorator API is unchanged; the low-level Server is rebuilt around a shared dispatcher engine, and one Client object replaces v1's transport-plus- ClientSession -plus- initialize() layering. It connects to a URL, a stdio subprocess, a custom transport, or straight to a server object in memory for tests. Multi-round-trip requests and resolver dependency injection At 2026-07-28 the server can no longer call the client, so tools return the question instead. A Resolve(fn) parameter is filled by your function invisibly to the model and can put a question to the user; one tool body serves both eras. Extension APIs, OpenTelemetry, and a standalone types package Servers and clients compose protocol extensions through pluggable extension APIs (MCP Apps built in); OpenTelemetry tracing ships on by default; every protocol type is its own package, mcp-types (imported as mcp_types ), published in lock-step with mcp . Hardened stdio and auth stdio servers keep handler subprocesses and stray prints off the wire, and stdout is diverted to stderr while serving. OAuth adds RFC 9207 issuer validation, the SEP-990 identity-assertion flow, and the client-credentials extension. Coming from a v2 pre-release Since the last release candidate: the per-version wire packages are private ( mcp_types._v* ), mcp.types is a permanent alias for mcp_types , the auth registration request model is split from the registered-client record, cancelled requests are no longer answered, and log notifications are gated on the per-request log-level opt-in at 2026-07-28. Since the betas: Client(cache=False) is now cache=None with CacheConfig() the default; Context.client_id , RFC7523OAuthClientProvider , and OAuthClientProvider(timeout=) are removed; the client-credentials providers take scope= ; message_handler receives notifications and exceptions only; FileResource(is_binary=) becomes encoding ; MCP_* env vars are gone with pydantic-settings ; Streamable HTTP servers reject bodies over 4 MiB with HTTP 413. The migration guide covers all of it. Known gaps The tasks extension (SEP-2663) is not part of this release. On the client, the DPoP proof binding (SEP-1932) and the workload-identity jwt-bearer grant are not implemented; both are additive and can land in 2.x. Feedback Something rough, confusing, or broken? Open an issue or find us in #python-sdk-dev on the MCP Contributors Discord. title: Empty-result hints: make them specific to the cause, concise, and machine-readable
cleaned_text: Empty-result hints: make them specific to the cause, concise, and machine-readable Problem When query_prometheus / query_loki_logs return no data, the response includes a hints object with a fixed list of ~4–6 possibleCauses and ~4–6 suggestedActions . The text is the same regardless of *why* the result is empty. Chat clients: it's several hundred bytes of generic advice on every empty result, and it rarely names the actual cause. Code-mode clients: scripts just check for emptiness, so the prose is pure noise. A script that fans out N queries pays for it N times. Concrete example: querying rate(foo_count[5m]) where foo is only exported as a native histogram returns empty, and none of the hints mention it. The fix ( histogram_count(rate(foo[5m])) ) is cheap to detect: the series metadata / list_prometheus_metric_names shows foo exists without a _count suffix. Proposal Make hints specific where we can cheaply detect the cause , e.g. for Prometheus: metric name not found → suggest close matches (prefix/suffix matches, _total / _count / _bucket variants); _count / _sum / _bucket requested but only the native-histogram base series exists → suggest histogram_count / histogram_quantile on the base name; selector label doesn't exist on the metric → list the metric's actual labels; range shorter than ~2× scrape interval inside rate() . Similar for Loki (stream selector matches no streams vs. line filter removed everything — query_loki_stats can distinguish these). Make the generic fallback short : a one-line summary plus a pointer to the relevant discovery tool, instead of the full list. Keep a stable machine-readable field (e.g. hints.reason: "metric_not_found" | "no_matching_series" | ... ) so scripts can branch on it without parsing prose. This ties in with the structured-output work.

title: v2.1.1: PivotTables over mixed-type data, faster edits
cleaned_text: PivotTables now accept everything Excel pivots: columns mixing text, numbers and dates, formulas, booleans, errors and times. Workbooks with large PivotTables edit as fast as those without. Fixed create_pivot_table (and the slicers and timelines that make PivotTables again) accept the sources Excel pivots without complaint, and show what Excel shows: columns that mix text, numbers, dates, booleans and blanks; cells with errors or formulas (their stored results, or the calculator's); times and durations. Row, column and filter fields list every kind of item in Excel's order; sum, average, min and max use the numbers (and dates, as serial numbers) and skip the rest, count counts what is not blank, and an error among the values is the result, including in the counts of totals. The cache holds the flags and items Excel writes ( containsMixedTypes , b , e , d ...), a field's number format is the one all its cells share, and a timeline needs a field of dates only. Grouping a mixed field is refused as in Excel ("Cannot group that selection"). Fixes #215. Changed Editing a workbook that holds a large PivotTable no longer parses its cache records: any tool on a 134,000 by 13 source now takes as long as on the same workbook without the PivotTable ( add_slicer 93 s to 40 s, write_range 90 s to 36 s, describe_sheet 60 s to 19 s) and peaks at 1 GB instead of 2.9 GB. The records are kept as they are in the file; a slicer on a field without shared items reads that one column from them.

cleaned_text: fix: PivotTables over mixed-type columns, formulas, booleans and errors, as in Excel Fixes #215 What create_pivot_table (and the slicers and timelines that make PivotTables again) now accept the sources Excel pivots without complaint, and the cells and cache match what Excel writes and shows: columns that mix text, numbers, dates, booleans, errors and blanks, as row, column, filter and value fields; cells that are formulas (the results Excel stored, else the calculator's, else a clear error), errors and booleans; times and durations. What Excel does, recorded through COM (hidden) and now covered by 82 more cases in tests/fixtures/pivot_golden.json (290 in all, every one equal to Excel after PivotCache().Refresh() ): Items are sorted numbers, text, FALSE/TRUE, errors (#N/A down to #NULL!), dates and times, blank last; text compares regardless of case ("b" and "B" are one item, the first spelling stays); text "3" and number 3 are two items. Booleans are labelled TRUE / FALSE text, errors are error cells, dates and times are numbers: in a field whose cells all share a number format they use it, else the host's short date, date and time, or time format (built-in ids 14, 22, 19). Value fields : sum, average, min and max use the numbers and dates (as serial numbers) and skip text, booleans and blanks (a group of only text gives sum 0, min 0, max 0 and average #DIV/0!); count counts everything that is not blank; a group with only blanks is empty. An error among the values is the result (the first one); the count of a single line of figures still counts it, but a total of lines (subtotal, Grand Total) counts as that error too. Which error: the first in source order for a line, the first in table order for a total. Calculated fields sum the numbers (text and booleans count as 0) and take the last error. show_as with errors: running totals carry an error until a later one replaces it; ranks and shares of a parent leave error cells blank; "percent of" and the like leave a cell blank when the base is an error and show its own error otherwise; a share of the running total of a Grand Total shows only the error. Cache : sharedItems flags as Excel writes them ( containsMixedTypes , containsSemiMixedTypes , containsString , containsNumber / containsInteger only without dates, containsNonDate , containsBlank , min/max); record items b , e , d , s , n , m , x (also in the fast XML writer); a field's numFmtId is the format all its cells share, else General (blank cells count). Grouping : Excel refuses to group a field that mixes types ("Cannot group that selection"), and so does the server; timelines need a field of dates only (checked from the cache flags). Tool contract create_pivot_table : the source description no longer says columns hold only text, numbers or dates and no formulas. Nothing is removed or renamed; the "mixes", "holds a formula" and "not numbers" errors are gone, as is the error for summing a text field. How it was tested scripts/pivot_golden.py now saves through the package layer ( save_atomically ), as the server does (the show-as extensions were missing before), and builds one source sheet per SOURCES entry; new sources and cases in scripts/pivot_mixed_cases.py . Excel opened the workbook with no repair log, and every case equals Excel's refreshed table (290 stored, 0 differ). tests/test_pivot_rebuild.py makes every case again from its own definition. tests/test_pivot_mixed.py : cache flags per column kind (as recorded from Excel), sort order, number formats, tool-level figures, records written, formulas with stored results ( tests/fixtures/excel_pivot_source.xlsx , made in Excel) and without (calculator), an uncalculable formula, grouping refused, slicers on a mixed field and over formulas, timelines. End to end in real Excel (hidden, COM; no screen capture): a file made through the MCP client (two PivotTables over mixed text/number/date/boolean/error/formula columns, a calculated field, a slicer with selected items on the mixed field, a timeline with a period) opens without a repair log; RefreshTable changes no value the server wrote (one cell differs in the 16th digit); the slicer lists the items in Excel's order with exactly the requested ones selected; the timeline loads with its period and is connected to the PivotTable. uv run pytest (1972 passed), ruff check , ruff format --check , pyright clean. Fields with one number format use it (verified). Text order uses a case-insensitive comparison, not Excel's locale collation for punctuation (unchanged). title: perf: edit workbooks with large PivotTables without parsing their records
cleaned_text: perf: edit workbooks with large PivotTables without parsing their records What Editing a workbook that holds a large PivotTable no longer parses the pivot cache records part. openpyxl turned each of the ~1.7M record items of a 134,000 x 13 source into an object on load and again on save, so every tool on such a workbook cost minutes and gigabytes. How package/lazy_records.py makes openpyxl load the records part as LazyRecords (the bytes of the part) and write it back unchanged, the same way chart_roundtrip adjusts openpyxl on Workspace start. Slicer filtering recalculates from the source range, so only one thing needs records: giving a field without shared items its items for a slicer ( ensure_items ). That reads one column and rewrites that column as shared indexes in two streaming passes (iterparse, one record in memory), with no openpyxl objects. Tool contract: unchanged. Security invariants: unchanged (the records XML is parsed with openpyxl's defusedxml-aware iterparse ; no new paths or formulas). Measured (134,000 x 13, 1 PivotTable, in-process, one run per process) Tool | Before | After | Same workbook without a pivot describe_sheet | 60.0 s, 2845 MB | 18.6 s, 1016 MB | 18.1 s, 987 MB write_range (other sheet) | 90.4 s, 2845 MB | 36.3 s, 1014 MB | 35.4 s, 987 MB copy_sheet (pivot sheet) | 91.3 s, 2845 MB | 36.5 s, 1015 MB | add_slicer (row field) | 93.5 s, 2937 MB | 39.8 s, 1104 MB | add_slicer + selection (row field) | 83.8 s, 2845 MB | 44.5 s, 1136 MB | add_slicer + selection (field without shared items) | 83.9 s, 2845 MB | 53.1 s, 1138 MB | The remainder is openpyxl loading and saving the 1.7M source cells, which any edit of that workbook pays. cleaned_text: feat: pivot tables over large sources, configurable limits Fixes #210 What and why A sheet of 134,000 rows by 13 columns (1.74 million cells) could not be used as a PivotTable source: the source was read under the general per-call range limit ( max_cells , 100,000), which was not configurable. Pivot sources now have their own limit, max_pivot_source_cells , default 3,000,000 cells. Limits is passed through the pivot and slicer rebuild code instead of one integer, so the rendered PivotTable area still uses the general limit. New options: --max-pivot-cells / EXCEL_MCP_MAX_PIVOT_CELLS , --max-cells / EXCEL_MCP_MAX_CELLS (the general per-call limit, which users with such sheets also hit when formatting or writing), and EXCEL_MCP_MAX_FILE_MB for the existing --max-file-mb . Documented in the README and the site options table. The oversized-source error names --max-pivot-cells ; the general range error names --max-cells . Performance: the pivot cache records were one openpyxl object per value (1.3 million objects for the issue's sheet). They are now written straight to XML text ( operations/pivot_records.py ), with the same output as openpyxl writes (tested against openpyxl's own serialisation). Measurements (134,000 x 13, in-process client, one create_pivot_table ) | before | after create_pivot_table | 92 s | 54 s peak memory | 2.1 GB | 1.0 GB add_slicer (reload + rebuild + save) | 160 s, 2.9 GB | 92 s, 2.9 GB 3,000,000 cells (230,768 rows), after | | 66 s, 1.7 GB The remainder of the time is openpyxl loading and saving the 1.7 million cells of the data sheet (about 20 s each), which every edit of such a workbook pays. Pivot-specific work (reading the source, building the cache, writing records) is now about 10 s. Reloading a workbook that already holds such a pivot still makes openpyxl parse every record into objects, which is why add_slicer stays slow and memory-heavy; a lazy records reader would be a follow-up. copy_sheet of the pivot sheet only deep-copies the definition (no source read); it is bound by load and save. Tool contract No tool signature changed. Behaviour: sources up to 3,000,000 cells are accepted (was 100,000). Tested New tests: default limit fits a 110,000-cell source; a source over the limit is refused with the option named and the file unchanged; flags and environment set the limits; the records writer matches openpyxl's output. Full suite, ruff, ruff format and pyright are clean. The pivot golden tests pass. Real Excel (COM, hidden, CorruptLoad=0 ): opened the 134,000-row workbook with a PivotTable made by the server using the default limits (creation 38.9 s, with row, column and page fields and two values). No error*.xml repair log appeared on open or after refresh. RefreshTable rebuilt the cache from the 134,000 source rows (RecordCount 133,999) and all 612 cells of the table matched the values the server wrote. title: Add a read-only mode to the MCP server (independent of WildFly RBAC)
cleaned_text: Add a read-only mode to the MCP server (independent of WildFly RBAC) Summary Add an opt-in read-only mode to the WildFly MCP server, enabled via a system property ( -Dorg.wildfly.readonly=true ) or environment variable ( WILDFLY_MCP_SERVER_READONLY=true ), that prevents the server from performing any mutating operation regardless of the WildFly user's RBAC role. Motivation Today the only way to restrict the MCP to read operations is to rely on WildFly RBAC by connecting with a Monitor -role user (as documented in the README). This has two limitations: It requires configuring RBAC and a dedicated user on every target server. When the MCP connects with an admin user, there is no protection at all. Several tools are inherently destructive ( deployWildFlyApplication , undeployWildFlyApplication , shutdownServer , enableWildFlyLoggingCategory , removeWildFlyLoggingCategory , and arbitrary invokeWildFlyCLIOperation ). When the MCP is wired to an LLM, an accidental or hallucinated call can modify or stop a production server. A server-side read-only switch provides defense-in-depth: the MCP itself refuses to mutate, so safety no longer depends on per-server RBAC configuration. Proposed behavior When read-only mode is enabled: Mutating tools fail fast with a clear message (or are not registered): deployWildFlyApplication , undeployWildFlyApplication , shutdownServer , enableWildFlyLoggingCategory , removeWildFlyLoggingCategory . invokeWildFlyCLIOperation validates the operation against an allow-list of read operations ( read-resource , read-attribute , read-children-names , read-children-resources , read-children-types , read-operation-names , read-operation-description , read-resource-description , query , whoami , :read-* , etc.) and rejects everything else. This also resolves the existing // TODO, implement possible rules if needed to disallow some operations. in WildFlyMCPServer.invokeWildFlyCLIOperation . Read-only tools remain fully available. Notes Default remains the current behavior (mode off) for backward compatibility. Intended to work for both the stdio and SSE servers, and via the container image env vars. I'm happy to submit a PR implementing this if the approach is acceptable.

title: Require fastmcp>=4.0 so the server speaks MCP 2026-07-28 (fixes #110)

title: Bump anyio from 4.13.0 to 4.14.2
cleaned_text: Bump anyio from 4.13.0 to 4.14.2 Bumps anyio from 4.13.0 to 4.14.2. Release notes Sourced from anyio's releases . 4.14.2 Changed ByteReceiveStream.receive() implementations to raise a ValueError when max_bytes is not a positive integer ( #1191 ) Fixed CapacityLimiter.total_tokens rejecting float("inf") when the limiter was instantiated outside of an event loop. The adapter setter checked for infinity by identity ( value is math.inf ), so only the exact math.inf singleton was accepted, while every backend setter (using math.isinf() ) accepts any positive infinity ( #1189 ; PR by @​greymoth-jp ). Fixed to_process.run_sync() deadlocking when the worker function writes enough data to sys.stderr to fill the (undrained) pipe buffer. The worker process now redirects sys.stderr to os.devnull as well, matching the documented behavior Fixed TLSStream.wrap() matching an internationalized (unicode) host name against the peer certificate using IDNA 2003 (via the standard library) instead of IDNA 2008, which could cause the host name to be matched against the wrong certificate ( #1208 ) Fixed anyio.open_process() (and run_process() ) ignoring the extra_groups argument, as it mistakenly passed the value of the group argument instead ( #1209 ) Fixed CapacityLimiter.acquire_nowait() and CapacityLimiter.acquire_nowait_on_behalf_of() raising trio.WouldBlock instead of anyio.WouldBlock on the trio backend when there are no tokens available ( #1218 ) Fixed CapacityLimiter on the asyncio backend over-granting tokens ( borrowed_tokens exceeding total_tokens and available_tokens going negative) when a non-blocking acquire was made in the window between a token being released and the notified waiter resuming. The freed token is now reserved for the woken waiter right away, so the non-blocking acquire correctly raises WouldBlock ( #1170 ; PR by @​gaoflow ) Fixed unnecessary CPU spin when delivering cancellation from CancelScope on asyncio under certain conditions, including improper cancel scope nesting ( #1111 ) 4.14.1 Fixed teardown of higher-scoped async fixtures failing on asyncio with RuntimeError: Attempted to exit cancel scope in a different task than it was entered in when an async test raise an outcome exception (e.g., pytest.skip() , pytest.xfail() , or pytest.fail() ) ( #1179 ; PR by @​EmmanuelNiyonshuti ) Fixed CapacityLimiter.total_tokens rejecting a value of 0 when the limiter was instantiated outside of an event loop, contradicting the documented behavior of allowing 0 total tokens ( #1183 ; PR by @​nyxst4ck ) 4.14.0 Added support for Python 3.15 Added an asynchronous implementation of the itertools module ( #998 ; PR by @​11kkw ) Added the local_port parameter to connect_tcp() to allow binding to a specific local port before connecting ( #1067 ; PR by @​nullwiz ) Added support for custom capacity limiters in async path and file I/O functions and classes Added the create_task() task group method for easier asyncio migration (returns a TaskHandle ) ( #1098 ) Changed TaskGroup.start_soon() to return a TaskHandle Added an option for TaskGroup.start() to return a TaskHandle (which then contains the start value in the start_value property) Added the cancel() convenience method to TaskGroup as a shortcut for cancelling the task group's cancel scope Improved the error message when a known backend is not installed to suggest the install command ( #1115 ; PR by @​EmmanuelNiyonshuti ) Improved anyio.Path to preserve subclass types by returning Self in methods that return path objects ( #1130 ; PR by @​EmmanuelNiyonshuti ) Changed the parameter type annotation in anyio.Path.write_bytes() to accept any ReadableBuffer , thus allowing it to accept bytearray and memoryview to match pathlib.Path.write_bytes() ( #1135 ; PR by @​SAY-5 ) Changed several type annotations to only accept callables returning coroutine-like objects instead of arbitrary awaitables: TaskGroup.start_soon() TaskGroup.start() anyio.from_thread.run() This reverts an earlier change from v3.7.0 which was made in error. ( #1153 ) Changed anyio.run to support callables returning arbitrary awaitables at runtime on all backends. Previously, this only worked on asyncio ( #1171 ; PR by @​gschaffner ) Changed several classes (and their subclasses) to have slots (with weakref ): anyio.CancelScope ... title: Bump pyjwt from 2.13.0 to 2.15.0
cleaned_text:
Bump pyjwt from 2.13.0 to 2.15.0 Bumps pyjwt from 2.13.0 to 2.15.0. Release notes Sourced from pyjwt's releases . 2.15.0 See the 2.15.0 changelog for complete release details. 2.14.0 See the 2.14.0 changelog for the complete release details and related security advisories. Changelog Sourced from pyjwt's changelog . v2.15.0 Security Wrap recursion errors from deeply nested JWT payloads in DecodeError instead of exposing a raw RecursionError .
