title: feat(mcp): show MCP server status and restart servers from the session
cleaned_text: feat(mcp): show MCP server status and restart servers from the session Summary Restart an MCP server from the session's MCP menu without restarting the app, and see how each server is doing. Every server row in the input-bar MCP menu shows a status dot: green connected (hover: tool count), amber connecting, red failed (hover: the error), grey not connected yet. A restart button per server, available in any state (failed, connected, never started). The dot switches to "connecting" at once and settles to the outcome. The "MCP n/m" trigger shows a red dot when a server switched on for the session is failing. Opening the menu refreshes the states, so a server whose process exited shows as failed. How it works mcp_client : McpServerConnection::is_closed() (session cancelled or transport gone) and close() (stops the session, terminating a stdio server's process). ConfigToolRegistry records each server's McpServerHealth from its connects and registry builds (previously the per-server results were discarded) and publishes changes as the app-scoped UiEvent::McpServerStatusChanged . New McpServerControl seam on SessionManager . SessionService::restart_mcp_server closes the server's pooled connections, drops the cached registries and rebuilds the session's registry outside the manager lock, on its own task so the session's commands are not held up. The session then holds the new registry, which keeps the new connection alive. Other sessions pick it up on their next run. SessionService::refresh_mcp_server_statuses publishes the current states. Trade-off: tool calls in flight on the restarted server fail, which is what an explicit restart means. Testing New tests: closing a connection and detecting a vanished server ( mcp_client ); a failing server reports its error, restart goes through "connecting" to the outcome and rebuilds the registry, restarting an unknown server settles ( registry_provider ). cargo fmt , cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings , cargo test pass. Tried manually in the GPUI app with one working and two broken stdio servers.

title: fix(llm): bound stalled requests instead of waiting forever
cleaned_text: fix(llm): bound stalled requests instead of waiting forever Problem Sometimes a session kept showing as running after a message was sent, but nothing happened for a long time, and there was no hint why. The LLM HTTP clients were built with reqwest::Client::new() , which has no connect or read timeout. When a connection silently dies mid-stream (network change, proxy or gateway dropping it), response.chunk().await never returns. On top of that, the GPUI app only logs to stderr, which nobody sees when it runs as an app bundle. Changes Timeouts All providers use a shared client with a 30s connect timeout and TCP keepalive ( utils::http_client ) A streaming response must start within 60s (headers via utils::send_request , first chunk via streaming::HttpChunkStream ). Providers send an event right away once a response starts (Anthropic's message_start , OpenAI's response.created and reasoning items, even those without summary), so a longer wait means the request is stuck. Nothing was shown yet, so it is retried Once started, a stream may stay silent for up to 5 minutes between chunks (a model may reason for minutes without output); after that it fails without retry Non-streaming requests only get their headers once the full answer is generated, so they are not bounded there. Ollama keeps the long wait for the first chunk, since a local server may load the model first Token and auth requests (AI Core token, Codex OAuth, AI Core realtime deployment lookup) get a 60s timeout Retries and errors handle_retryable_error only recognized errors wrapped in ApiErrorContext , so the plain ApiError::NetworkError raised when sending fails was never retried. Bare ApiError s are now handled too Mid-stream failures (including the new stall timeout) are intentionally not retried: part of the answer may already be on screen and would be repeated The AI Core token fetch maps network/5xx failures to retryable errors and no longer underflows on expires_in < 60 The session error banner shows the full error chain ( {e:#} ) instead of only the outer context Retries are visible New StreamingChunk::Retrying { reason, attempt, max_attempts } → AgentUi::notify_retrying → session state SessionActivityState::Retrying , shown in the GPUI activity indicator ("… — retrying (1/3)…"), as a "Retrying" sidebar status and in the terminal spinner, until the new attempt responds A stop request during the retry delay ends the retry loop A rate limit without timing info now shows the same countdown as one with it, instead of waiting 60s+ silently UTF-8 across chunk boundaries Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama and Vertex decoded each network chunk on its own, so a multi-byte character split between two chunks failed the whole request. They now share streaming::Utf8Decoder (OpenAI Responses already buffered) Logging The GPUI app also logs to /code-assistant/app.log (rotated to app.log.old above 20 MB at startup); agent_core added to the default filters Testing New unit tests: UTF-8 decoding across chunk boundaries, a local server that stalls before and after the first chunk, retry of bare network errors, retry notice and cancellation, Retrying state transitions, error chain rendering Observed in practice: a request whose response never started now gets retried and continues cargo fmt , cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings and cargo test pass (except web::tests::test_web_search , which depends on a live web search)

title: fix: two bugs from pal's first ChatGPT run (WS log excerpt panic, doubled error strip)
cleaned_text: fix: two bugs from pal's first ChatGPT run (WS log excerpt panic, doubled error strip) Two bugs found in pal's first run with the ChatGPT provider. 1. WS request log excerpt panic ( llm ) The WebSocket provider logs the first 1000 bytes of each request ( WS request (N bytes): … ) by slicing the serialized JSON at byte 1000. When that byte falls inside a multi-byte character, the slice panics, and the agent task dies before the request is sent. pal's system prompt has an em dash spanning bytes 999..1002, so every turn failed with Agent panicked: end byte index 1000 is not a char boundary . The excerpt is now cut at floor_char_boundary . Only the log line changes; the request itself was never truncated. Test: the_request_log_excerpt_never_splits_a_character . 2. Doubled error strip ( ui_terminal ) The layout formats the error as Error: … (Press Esc to dismiss) , and the paint formatted that text a second time. The result was Error: Error: … (Press Esc to dismiss) (Press Esc to dismiss) . test_error_message_rendering now checks that the prefix and the hint each appear exactly once.

title: fix(llm): keep prompt_cache_key within OpenAI's 64-char limit
cleaned_text: fix(llm): keep prompt_cache_key within OpenAI's 64-char limit Problem The OpenAI clients (Chat Completions, Responses, Responses over WebSocket) send the session ID verbatim as prompt_cache_key . Since session IDs became paths ( / - ), they exceed 64 characters for longer project names, and the API rejects the request: Invalid 'prompt_cache_key': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 64, but got a string with length 66 instead. Fix New helper prompt_caching::prompt_cache_key() used by all three clients: IDs of up to 64 chars are sent unchanged. Longer IDs are replaced by their SHA-256 hex digest (exactly 64 chars). title: DiskStore atomic saves fail on transient Windows rename errors
cleaned_text: DiskStore atomic saves fail on transient Windows rename errors Problem The atomic replacement introduced in #420 fixes partial reads, but DiskStore.save() can now fail on Windows while another operation reads the destination file. The temporary file is removed and the save rejects immediately on a transient rename error. Reproduced on unchanged main 913aa06de58abc651a64382fe2c17ccf7f1e85cf , Windows / Node 24.20.0: node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/auth/utils/diskStore.test.ts 15 passed, 1 failed, 2 skipped FAIL should not clean up an entry while it is overwritten Error: EPERM: operation not permitted, rename ' .json. .tmp' -> ' .json' That existing test races 20 overwrites of a 100 KB value against cleanup. The earlier get() /overwrite case has also failed in other Windows runs, as recorded in #433 and #434. There is no overlapping open PR touching DiskStore when checked. Proposed correction and validation Retry only Windows EPERM , EACCES and EBUSY from the atomic rename, with five retries and 310 ms of total backoff. Reuse the same temporary file and preserve the previous entry; do not unlink the destination. Persistent or unrelated errors still propagate, and the existing temporary-file cleanup remains in place. The entry's original expiry is retained. A prepared patch has 15 deterministic regression/control cases: six fail on the base and all pass with the change. The existing DiskStore tests then pass too (31 passed, 2 POSIX-only permission tests skipped on Windows). The full offline suite passes: 1062 passed, 2 skipped. Ten additional runs of the existing read/cleanup overwrite races pass, totaling 400 concurrent overwrite iterations. No provider credentials or external model calls are used. title: Feature request: support flat objects in simple-style path parameters
cleaned_text: Feature request: support flat objects in simple-style path parameters Would you consider supporting flat object parameters in OpenAPI style: simple paths? The current OpenAPI documentation says object-valued path parameters are sent as "[object Object]" . The OpenAPI 3.0.4 specification defines serialization for simple-style objects: with {R: 100, G: 200, B: 150} , explode: false is R,100,G,200,B,150 , and explode: true is R=100,G=200,B=150 . Minimal case: openapi: 3.0.4 info: { title: Colors, version: '1.0' } servers: [{ url: https://api.example.com }] paths: /colors/{color}: get: operationId: getColor parameters: - in: path name: color required: true style: simple explode: false # also observed with true schema: type: object properties: R: { type: integer } G: { type: integer } B: { type: integer } required: [R, G, B] responses: '200': { description: OK } Calling the generated MCP tool with { color: { R: 100, G: 200, B: 150 } } currently requests /colors/%5Bobject%20Object%5D for either explode value, losing the properties. In a local MCP client and localhost HTTP-server characterization, all six object/array/scalar cases passed; this confirms current behavior and is not a failing regression test. Scalar and array controls reached the server successfully. Would you want flat objects supported for simple path parameters, including the path defaults when style/explode are omitted? title: fix: do not hand out a port the OS refuses to bind
cleaned_text: fix: do not hand out a port the OS refuses to bind isFreeOn treats every bind error other than EADDRINUSE as "free": // src/getTestPort.ts:14 resolve(error.code !== "EADDRINUSE"); That is right for the case the comment names — an address this machine does not have, such as the IPv6 loopback on a host without IPv6, cannot hold a port for anyone. But it is wrong for a port the OS refuses to bind , and on Windows that is the common shape: a port inside an excluded range reports EACCES , not EADDRINUSE , so the port reads as free and getTestPort() hands it to a test server that can never bind it. Measured on Windows 11, Node v24.21.0, netsh int ipv4 show excludedportrange protocol=tcp listing 5357 : port host bind result isFreeOn() 5357 127.0.0.1 error EACCES true <- handed out, unusable 5357 ::1 error EACCES true The same code with the fix returns false for both, so the retry loop moves to the next port. The distinction bind error | means | free? EADDRNOTAVAIL , EAFNOSUPPORT | the address is not on this machine, so it cannot hold the port | yes EADDRINUSE | something is listening | no EACCES , EPERM | this machine refuses the bind — a reserved or privileged port | no anything else | unknown → treat as taken, the safe direction | no Two notes on that table, because both were traps: The check has to be a real listen() , not a scan of the exclusion list. On this machine 50000 – 50059 is listed as an admin-excluded range yet binds fine, so a list-based test skips itself on a host that does have the bug. The new test probes the bind. Only the address-absent codes may count as free. Answering false for everything unknown is what keeps the allocator moving instead of throwing. Tests src/getTestPort.reserved.test.ts finds a port this host refuses to bind, asserts it is refused on both loopbacks, then offers it through the mocked getRandomPort ahead of a usable port: | result without the fix | AssertionError: expected 5357 to be 62981 — the refused port was returned with it | Tests 3 passed (3) It skips itself with a message on a host that refuses to bind no TCP port. The control case asserts an ordinary free port still comes straight back. src/getTestPort.test.ts (the existing ::1 test) still passes, and the full suite is unchanged: 6 failed | 1041 passed | 2 skipped (1049) both before and after, on the same machine in the same run. Those 6 failures are pre-existing and unrelated — additionalProperties deep comparisons and two specs that resolve specs.example.com . tsc --noEmit reports nothing for either file.

Bumped minimum mcp/sdk version from 1.7.0 to 1.24.0 for zod 4 support and the tool handler API used by mailgun_call_tool . Added server.ts with a baseline for server initialization functions. title: feat: add MIZAN plugin to check an agent's track record before paying or copying it
cleaned_text: feat: add MIZAN plugin to check an agent's track record before paying or copying it Closes #605 What Adds @goat-sdk/plugin-mizan , a chain-agnostic, read-only plugin with five tools: mizan_check_agent : call before following, copying, paying or allocating to any agent or wallet that claims returns. Takes a name or alias, credential id, wallet address, ERC-8004 id, agent-card URL or sha256, plus the intended action. Returns PROVEN , REFUSED , NOT_SIGNIFICANT or UNVERIFIED with the matching credentials. UNVERIFIED means unproven, which is not the same as false. mizan_list_proven_agents : credentials with a PASS verdict (Bitcoin-confirmed only by default). mizan_verify_credential : looks a credential up in the public registry, downloads the proof bundle, checks its sha256 against the registry anchor, and returns the verdict exactly as issued, or UNVERIFIED if it is missing or the bundle does not match. mizan_search_credentials : searches the registry by free text, alias, issuer or verdict. mizan_list_datasets : lists the canonical public markets a credential can be minted on. Why Agents pay other agents for signals, copy trades, or allocate to vaults based on self-reported performance. A MIZAN credential is a zero-knowledge (STARK) proof under the open VTR-1 standard (CC BY) that a track record was computed as claimed, under committed costs and data, without revealing the strategy. This plugin gives a GOAT agent a one-call check before money moves. FAIL verdicts are published alongside passes, and every result carries the caveat that a credential is a seal on a past record, not a forecast. Notes No API key, no wallet calls, HTTPS only. supportsChain returns true. Same layout as the other data plugins ( @Tool service, createToolParameters with zod, tsup, turbo, changeset). Root README table updated. pnpm-lock.yaml gets only the new importer block (same devDependency versions as plugin-dexscreener ). Tests: 11 passing ( pnpm --filter @goat-sdk/plugin-mizan test , mocked fetch). The HTTP logic is in a decorator-free MizanApi class so vitest (esbuild, no decorator metadata) can test it; the @Tool service is a thin wrapper. pnpm lint clean. Built with Node 22 and pnpm 9.14.2. Smoke-tested the built plugin against the live API: mizan_check_agent returns UNVERIFIED for an unknown wallet and REFUSED for a refused agent, mizan_list_proven_agents returns PASS rows, and mizan_verify_credential({ credentialId: "v12-btc-trend-4h" }) returns PASS with a matching sha256. Disclosure: I work on MIZAN. Every credential issued so far was minted by MIZAN itself. Docs for agents: https://mizan.market/skill/ · MCP server: https://studio.mizan.market/mcp 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: Plugin proposal: MIZAN, check an agent's track record before paying or copying it
cleaned_text: Plugin proposal: MIZAN, check an agent's track record before paying or copying it Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe it. Agents built with GOAT can pay other agents for signals, copy their trades, or put funds into a vault. Today the only evidence they get is the other side's own performance claim: a screenshot, a tear-sheet, a number in an agent card. There is no tool for the agent to check that claim before money moves. Describe the solution you'd like A small read-only plugin, @goat-sdk/plugin-mizan , that checks a counterparty's track record with MIZAN before the agent pays, copies or allocates. MIZAN issues zero-knowledge (STARK) credentials under an open standard (VTR-1, CC BY) that prove a track record was computed as claimed, under committed costs and data, without revealing the strategy. Failed records are published too. Tools: mizan_check_agent : give it a name, wallet, credential id, ERC-8004 id or agent-card URL plus what you are about to do. It returns PROVEN, REFUSED, NOT_SIGNIFICANT or UNVERIFIED. UNVERIFIED means unproven, not false. mizan_list_proven_agents , mizan_verify_credential (re-checks the proof bundle hash against the registry), mizan_search_credentials , mizan_list_datasets . No API key, no wallet calls, chain-agnostic. It follows the same layout as the other data plugins (dexscreener, rugcheck). I have it built with tests and can open the PR. Describe alternatives you've considered Calling the MIZAN HTTP API or MCP server directly from each agent. That works, but a plugin makes it one line in getOnChainTools , so the check happens by default. Additional context I work on MIZAN. A credential is a seal on a past record, not a forecast, and every credential issued so far was minted by MIZAN itself. Docs: https://mizan.market/skill/

title: Plugin proposal: @goat-sdk/plugin-invinoveritas — pre-execution governance gate with recomputable proof
cleaned_text: Plugin proposal: @goat-sdk/plugin-invinoveritas — pre-execution governance gate with recomputable proof Problem GOAT ships 200+ tools for agent-controlled value movement — swaps, transfers, contract calls. There's no standard way for an agent to get an independent, recomputable verdict on whether a *specific* action is sound before it fires — one a downstream system can verify without trusting the agent or the gate that issued it. Token-safety checks (SafeAgent #562, Raven #592) run static analysis on the *target* and answer *is this token safe?* The missing layer judges the *action in context*, and answers two questions they don't: Is this action safe to sign? — pre-sign on-chain-action review: unlimited-allowance drainer, honeypot/scam token, address poisoning, wrong-chain recipient, slippage/MEV. Deterministic and recomputable (decode the calldata yourself). Is this action sound right now? — account-aware governance: size / leverage / timing vs current equity, open positions, drawdown, mandate. Both come back as one signed verdict anyone can recompute against a published key. Proposed solution: @goat-sdk/plugin-invinoveritas A pre-execution verdict gate that wraps any GOAT action with a /review call before signing. Posture-configurable : run it advisory (annotate, never block) or as a hard gate (a reject stops the sign). The integrator picks per action class — the same verdict, two postures. import { getOnChainTools } from "@goat-sdk/core"; import { invinoveritasPlugin } from "@goat-sdk/plugin-invinoveritas"; const tools = await getOnChainTools({ wallet, plugins: [ uniswap({ ...config }), invinoveritasPlugin({ apiKey: process.env.INVINOVERITAS_API_KEY, // optional — advisory mode skips cleanly on 402 posture: "gate", // "gate" = block on reject (fail-closed) · "advisory" = annotate only artifactTypes: ["onchain_action", "swap", "transfer", "contract_call"], }), ], }); Before any covered action executes, the plugin calls /review , attaches the signed, recomputable verdict proof to the action record, and in gate posture holds on a reject before signTransaction . In advisory posture an unreachable endpoint degrades cleanly to annotate (never blocks). The maintainer decides which action classes are hard-gated and which are advisory. How this differs from the other layers Layer | Question | Receipt Token safety (Raven, SafeAgent) | Is the *target* a honeypot/rug? | scan result Pre-execution verdict (this) | Is *this action* safe to sign and sound in context? | signed proof, recomputable from public bytes — verify without trusting us Complementary, not competing: token-safety scans the target, this judges the action. The distinction that matters downstream: unlike a proprietary receipt, this verdict is independently recomputable — a downstream system checks it against our published key, trusting neither the agent nor us. A receipt you can't recompute is an attestation (trust the auditor); one you can is a proof (check it yourself). What's live today /review MCP: https://api.babyblueviper.com/mcp → tools/call → review · REST: POST https://api.babyblueviper.com/review artifact_type=onchain_action : deterministic pre-sign safety engine (drainer / honeypot / poisoning / wrong-chain / slippage) — recomputable Every verdict signed + published to a public Nostr- and Bitcoin-anchored ledger — fully recomputable, not a black-box receipt; free /verify-proof for anyone Pay-per-call via x402 (USDC on Base) or Lightning Live dogfood: a Hyperliquid bot passes every entry through /review before placement Community integrations requesting this exact pattern: AlgoVaultLabs #28, HKUDS/Vibe-Trading advisory interface #330 We also run an open conformance registry that grades verifiers — ours included, no green by assertion — on whether their receipts recompute from public bytes Implementation path Happy to contribute this as an actual plugin PR ( packages/plugins/invinoveritas ) following the plugin guide and PR checklist (changeset, tests, Tools-table row, docs entry). title: Node ESM apps load the CommonJS build (no exports map), so a client extended with publicActions fails to wait for receipts
cleaned_text: Node ESM apps load the CommonJS build (no exports map), so a client extended with publicActions fails to wait for receipts Describe the bug The GOAT TypeScript packages ( @goat-sdk/core , @goat-sdk/wallet-evm , @goat-sdk/wallet-viem ; checked on the latest releases and on main ) ship both a CommonJS build ( main: ./dist/index.js ) and an ESM build ( module: ./dist/index.mjs ), but have no exports map and no "type" . Node.js ignores module , so in a Node ESM application import { viem } from "@goat-sdk/wallet-viem" loads the CommonJS build, which require s viem's CommonJS build, while the application uses viem's ESM build. The process then has two copies of viem, and errors from one copy fail instanceof checks in the other. One visible effect: when the wallet client passed to viem() has been extended with viem's publicActions (a common pattern), sendTransaction fails with TransactionReceiptNotFoundError whenever the transaction is not mined on the first receipt poll. ViemEVMWalletClient.waitForReceipt calls this.#client.extend(publicActions).waitForTransactionReceipt(...) ; that waitForTransactionReceipt comes from viem's CommonJS build and, through getAction , calls the client's own getTransactionReceipt , which is the ESM one. The ESM TransactionReceiptNotFoundError it throws is not an instanceof the CommonJS class ( viem/_cjs/actions/public/waitForTransactionReceipt.js , catch (err) { if (err instanceof TransactionNotFoundError || err instanceof TransactionReceiptNotFoundError) ... ), so instead of polling again, the wait rejects. To Reproduce No chain or network is needed: a local custom transport returns no receipt on the first poll and the receipt on the second. npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module npm install @goat-sdk/core@0.5.0 @goat-sdk/wallet-viem@0.3.0 viem@2.23.4 // repro.mjs import { viem } from "@goat-sdk/wallet-viem"; import { createWalletClient, custom, publicActions } from "viem"; import { baseSepolia } from "viem/chains"; const hash = 0x${"ab".repeat(32)} ; const from = "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111"; let receiptPolls = 0; let block = 0x10; // A local EIP-1193 stand-in: the receipt appears on the second poll, as for any transaction that is not mined yet. const transport = custom({ async request({ method }) { switch (method) { case "eth_chainId": return "0x14a34"; case "eth_sendTransaction": return hash; case "eth_blockNumber": return 0x${(block++).toString(16)} ; case "eth_getTransactionByHash": return { hash, from, to: from, input: "0x", value: "0x0", gas: "0x5208", nonce: "0x0", blockHash: null, blockNumber: null, transactionIndex: null, type: "0x2", chainId: "0x14a34", maxFeePerGas: "0x1", maxPriorityFeePerGas: "0x1", accessList: [], v: "0x0", r: "0x1", s: "0x1", yParity: "0x0" }; case "eth_getBlockByNumber": return { hash: 0x${"cd".repeat(32)} , parentHash: 0x${"00".repeat(32)} , number: "0x10", timestamp: "0x0", nonce: "0x0000000000000000", difficulty: "0x0", gasLimit: "0x1c9c380", gasUsed: "0x0", miner: from, extraData: "0x", baseFeePerGas: "0x1", logsBloom: 0x${"00".repeat(256)} , transactions: [], uncles: [], size: "0x0", stateRoot: 0x${"00".repeat(32)} , receiptsRoot: 0x${"00".repeat(32)} , transactionsRoot: 0x${"00".repeat(32)} , sha3Uncles: 0x${"00".repeat(32)} , mixHash: 0x${"00".repeat(32)} }; case "eth_getTransactionReceipt": receiptPolls++; if (receiptPolls === 1) return null; return { transactionHash: hash, transactionIndex: "0x0", blockHash: 0x${"cd".repeat(32)} , blockNumber: "0x10", from, to: from, cumulativeGasUsed: "0x5208", gasUsed: "0x5208", effectiveGasPrice: "0x1", contractAddress: null, logs: [], logsBloom: 0x${"00".repeat(256)} , status: "0x1", type: "0x2" }; default: throw new Error( unexpected ${method} ); } }, }); let client = createWalletClient({ account: from, chain: baseSepolia, transport, pollingInterval: 50 }); if (process.env.WITH_PUBLIC) client = client.extend(publicActions); const wallet = viem(client); setTimeout(() => { console.log("timed out"); process.exit(2); }, 15000).unref(); try { console.log(await wallet.sendTransaction({ to: from, value: 0n })); } catch (error) { console.log( ${error.name}: ${error.shortMessage ?? error.message} ); process.exitCode = 1; } $ node repro.mjs { hash: '0xabababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababab', status: 'success' } $ WITH_PUBLIC=1 node repro.mjs TransactionReceiptNotFoundError: Transaction receipt with hash "0xabababababababababababababababababababababababababababababababab" could not be found. The Transaction may not be processed on a block yet. Importing the ESM build directly ( import { viem } from "@goat-sdk/wallet-viem/dist/index.mjs" ) with WITH_PUBLIC=1 returns status: 'success' , which shows the CommonJS build is what breaks it. Expected behavior A Node ESM application gets the ESM build, so GOAT and the application share one viem, and the receipt wait keeps polling until the transaction is mined. Additional context Node.js v24.21.0. Bundlers that read module are not affected; plain Node ESM (and tools that follow Node's resolution) is. A possible fix is an exports map in each package, for example ".": { "types": ..., "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.js" } , plus the subpaths that are imported today. I'm happy to open a pull request adding the exports maps (with a test that imports each package from Node ESM) if that direction works for you.

title: Plugin proposal: read-only AssetFare multichain route quotes
cleaned_text: Plugin proposal: read-only AssetFare multichain route quotes Plugin proposal Would GOAT accept a read-only AssetFare route-quote plugin? AssetFare exposes a capped public REST/OpenAPI v2 service for 72 directed conversions among nine asset endpoints on Solana, Base, Arbitrum, and Robinhood Chain. A first quote requires no AssetFare API key, wallet authentication, private key, session, signature, or transaction. The proposed plugin would expose only: get_capabilities : current route scope and server safety boundary; quote_route : a fresh fee-inclusive $1–$1,000 route quote. It would fail closed unless server signing and submission remain disabled, and its action description would require the agent to compare the quote with other fresh executable routes. It would not expose AssetFare preparation or execution actions. Working reference Independent pilot: https://assetfare.dev/pilot/ OpenAPI: https://api.assetfare.dev/v2/openapi.json Tested quote-only AgentKit implementation: https://github.com/odaiin/assetfare-mcp/tree/main/integrations/coinbase-agentkit If this fits GOAT's plugin scope, I can adapt the provider to GOAT's current plugin interface and submit tests and documentation. If quote-only external route candidates are intentionally out of scope, closing the proposal is fine.

cleaned_text: feat(tool): adding an explicit tool to search through profile attributes This pull request adds a robust user search feature that allows searching for users by any profile attribute, with flexible matching operators and improved handling of personally identifiable information (PII). User search enhancements: Added a new schema getUserByAttribute to userSchemas , supporting attribute-based search with operators ( eq , sw , ew , co , pr ), result limits, and the option to include inactive users. Implemented the find_users_by_attribute function, which: Attempts Okta's native search first for performance, falls back to free-text or client-side filtering if necessary. Applies filtering logic based on the selected operator and handles status filtering for active/inactive users. Formats results with relevant user details and includes notes about search method and limitations. title: Support built-in polling in create_prediction to return full prediction result
cleaned_text: Support built-in polling in create_prediction to return full prediction result Description: When using the MCP Replicate, the create_prediction action today only returns a prediction ID. This requires to issue a separate GET /predictions/:id call in a loop, polling until status === "succeeded", before they can access the actual output. It would be far more ergonomic if create_prediction could optionally wait for completion and return the output in a single call. Current behavior tool: create_prediction { "model": "owner/model:version", "input": { "prompt": "Generate image", } } // → { type: "text", text: Created prediction ${prediction.id} , } let result; do { await sleep(1000); result = await https://api.replicate.com/v1/predictions/:predictionId } while (result.status !== "succeeded"); Desired behavior // Option A: optional parameter tool: create_prediction { "model": "owner/model:version", "input": { "prompt": "Generate image", }, "wait": true } // → { type: "text", text: Created prediction ${prediction.id}, Output: ${prediction.output} , }, // Option B: Introduce a separate helper create_and_wait_prediction tool: create_and_wait_prediction { "model": "owner/model:version", "input": { "prompt": "Generate image", }, } // → { type: "text", text: Created prediction ${prediction.id}, Output: ${prediction.output} , }, Technical details • Environment: N8N, MCP client • Tool: create_prediction (MCP Replicate) • Additional API to get prediction https://api.replicate.com/v1/predictions/:predictionId Possible solutions Add a wait parameter to create_prediction that internally polls until the job succeeds, then returns the prediction output. Introduce a separate helper like create_and_wait_prediction(...) that wraps create + polling in one call.

title: fix(agent_run): emit a valid JSON Schema pattern for run ids
cleaned_text: fix(agent_run): emit a valid JSON Schema pattern for run ids The runId and previousRunId inputs used zod's startsWith, which zod-to-json-schema serializes as "^agent\_run\_". \_ is not a valid escape in the ECMAScript regex grammar JSON Schema requires, so validators using the strict grammar (for example some model-provider tool validators) reject every request that carries the tool. Switched both fields to .regex(/^agent_run_/), which serializes as "^agent_run_" and accepts exactly the same values. Added a test that reads the schema over an in-memory MCP client and checks the patterns compile with the u flag. Fixes #447.

title: Docs: add an AG2 integration page (AG2 ships ExaToolkit built on exa-py)
cleaned_text: Docs: add an AG2 integration page (AG2 ships ExaToolkit built on exa-py) Why this is filed here The same request is open as exa-py#252 and has had no maintainer response in three weeks. Filing it in this repo, which is the most-starred repo in the org, in the hope it reaches whoever owns the docs site. Happy to have it closed as a duplicate of #252 — the ask is identical, and it is docs-only: nothing needs to be built or maintained on the Exa side. Summary AG2 now ships a first-class Exa integration built on exa-py , but there's no AG2 page in the Exa docs (there are ones for LangChain, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, Google ADK, …). We'd like to get one added, and we're happy to provide the content. What landed on the AG2 side As of ag2>=1.0.0 (current release 1.0.4 ), AG2 ships ExaToolkit in ag2.extensions.tools.search . It wraps exa_py.AsyncExa and exposes four Exa endpoints as agent tools sharing a single client: Tool | Exa endpoint exa_search | search / search_and_contents exa_find_similar | find_similar exa_get_contents | get_contents exa_answer | answer Each tool is also a factory method ( toolkit.search() , toolkit.answer() , …), so per-tool Exa filters — search type, category, include/exclude domains, published/crawl date ranges, livecrawl , num_results , max_characters — can be bound per agent, and an agent can be given only the tools it needs. pip install "ag2>=1.0.0" "exa-py>=2.12.1,<3" import os from ag2 import Agent from ag2.config import AnthropicConfig from ag2.extensions.tools.search import ExaToolkit agent = Agent( "researcher", config=AnthropicConfig(model="claude-sonnet-4-6"), tools=[ExaToolkit(api_key=os.environ["EXA_API_KEY"])], ) reply = await agent.ask("Find recent papers on neural retrieval and summarise them.") Links: AG2 docs page: https://docs.ag2.ai/docs/user-guide/extensions/tools/search/exa/ Source: ag2/extensions/tools/search/exa.py in https://github.com/ag2ai/ag2 The ask Add an AG2 page to the Exa docs — exa.ai/docs/integrations/ag2 (or /docs/reference/ag2 , whichever matches your current grouping) plus a nav entry alongside the other agent-framework integrations. We can't open the PR ourselves: exa.ai/docs is deployed from the private exa-labs/monorepo repo ( docs/ directory), so this issue is the closest thing to one. Below is a ready-to-drop .mdx written in the style of your existing integration pages — feel free to edit or trim it. docs/integrations/ag2.mdx (ready to drop in) title: "AG2" description: "Use Exa search, find-similar, contents, and answer as tools in AG2 agents with the built-in ExaToolkit." AG2 is an open-source framework for building agents and multi-agent applications. Since v1.0.0 , AG2 ships ExaToolkit out of the box: it is built directly on the Exa Python SDK and exposes four Exa endpoints as agent tools that share a single AsyncExa client. Prerequisites Create an API key in Exa and set it as EXA_API_KEY . theme={null} pip install "ag2>=1.0.0" "exa-py>=2.12.1,<3" Get started Passing the toolkit to an agent registers all four tools at once. theme={null} import os from ag2 import Agent from ag2.config import AnthropicConfig from ag2.extensions.tools.search import ExaToolkit agent = Agent( "researcher", config=AnthropicConfig(model="claude-sonnet-4-6"), tools=[ExaToolkit(api_key=os.environ["EXA_API_KEY"])], ) reply = await agent.ask("Find recent papers on neural retrieval and summarise them.") If api_key is omitted, the Exa SDK reads EXA_API_KEY from the environment automatically. Tools Tool | Exa endpoint | Description exa_search | search / search_and_contents | Web search with filters (type, category, domains, dates, livecrawl) exa_find_similar | find_similar | Find pages similar to a given URL exa_get_contents | get_contents | Fetch full text content for specific URLs exa_answer | answer | Get an answer with citations Picking a subset of tools Each tool is also available as a factory method on the toolkit, so an agent can be given only the tools it needs. theme={null} toolkit = ExaToolkit(api_key=os.environ["EXA_API_KEY"]) agent = Agent( "researcher", config=config, tools=[toolkit.search(), toolkit.answer()], ) Per-tool configuration Per-call Exa parameters live on the factory methods, so different agents can bind different filters against the same toolkit. theme={null} search_tool = toolkit.search( num_results=5, max_characters=2000, # returns full text via search_and_contents search_type="neural", # "auto" | "neural" | "fast" | "deep-lite" | "deep" | ... category="research paper", include_domains=["arxiv.org"], start_published_date="2024-01-01", livecrawl="always", ) Resources AG2 Exa Search documentation AG2 on GitHub Also happy to do If it's useful, we can open a small PR against this repo's README.md too: the "Other MCP Clients" table lists editors and desktop clients only, and AG2 can point at https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp directly through its built-in MCPToolkit — a one-row addition. Just say the word and we'll send it.

title: Minor issues
cleaned_text: Minor issues Package: @coding-solo/godot-mcp 0.1.1 (via npx) OS: macOS (darwin, arm64) Node: v26.10.0 Godot: n/a — the defect is entirely in the Node server layer; findings below come from a source audit of the published build/index.js (repro included, not executed before filing). Summary Two lifecycle gaps in how the server manages the OS processes it spawns: cleanup() is registered only as a SIGINT handler — when the client terminates the server with SIGTERM (Node's subprocess.kill() default) or by closing the stdio pipe, a Godot process started by run_project is never killed. launch_editor spawns the editor fire-and-forget — the child is never recorded, so stop_project cannot stop it, cleanup() cannot kill it, and repeated calls accumulate editors with nothing tracking them. (minor) executeOperation awaits execFileAsync with no timeout, so one hung headless run blocks that tool call forever. Finding 1 — cleanup only runs on SIGINT Constructor: process.on('SIGINT', async () => { await this.cleanup(); process.exit(0); }); There is no SIGTERM handler, no transport-close hook, and no process.on('exit') last resort. cleanup() is the only place activeProcess is killed: async cleanup() { if (this.activeProcess) { this.activeProcess.process.kill(); this.activeProcess = null; } await this.server.close(); } On POSIX, the child survives the parent's exit (reparented to init) and only dies if it happens to write to its now-broken stdout/stderr pipe and takes SIGPIPE. A quiet, long-running game process survives indefinitely. Repro: node build/index.js & # or: npx @coding-solo/godot-mcp from an MCP client: call run_project on any project kill -TERM # or simply shut down the MCP client ps -axo pid,ppid,command | grep -i godot # game process still alive, PPID 1 Suggested fix: const shutdown = async () => { await this.cleanup(); process.exit(0); }; process.on('SIGINT', shutdown); process.on('SIGTERM', shutdown); plus treat transport close (after server.connect(transport) ) as shutdown too — closing stdio without a signal is the other common client-termination path. Since Godot itself may spawn children, consider a process group ( detached: true at spawn, process.kill(-pid) ) so the whole tree goes down. Finding 2 — launch_editor is fire-and-forget const process = spawn(this.godotPath, ['-e', '--path', args.projectPath], { stdio: 'pipe' }); process.on('error', (err) => { /* logged only */ }); return { /* ... 'Godot editor launched successfully ...' */ }; The child is never stored in activeProcess (only handleRunProject does that), so: stop_project answers "No active Godot process to stop" while a launch_editor editor is running; server shutdown never kills editors — repeated launch_editor calls accumulate them. An editor outliving the MCP server may even be desirable (a human could be using it), but today that's an accident of nothing being tracked, not a decision. Either track editors in a set and kill them in cleanup() , or explicitly detach them and document in the tool description/response that editors are the user's to close. Finding 3 (minor) — no timeout on executeOperation const { stdout, stderr } = await execFileAsync(this.godotPath, args); handleGetProjectInfo already demonstrates the pattern with { timeout: 10000 } ; applying the same to executeOperation would keep one hung run from blocking a call forever. Related #70 — kill/exit race inside run_project (same lifecycle area; an exit-await there would compose with the SIGTERM fix) #106 — launch_editor errors not surfaced to the client

title: harden: reject NUL bytes in validatePath (poison-null-byte defense-in-depth)
cleaned_text: harden: reject NUL bytes in validatePath (poison-null-byte defense-in-depth) What Add a NUL-byte guard to validatePath and document the intended threat model. if (!path || path.includes('\0') || path.includes('..')) { return false; } Why validatePath already blocks .. traversal, which combined with the res:// re-rooting in godot_operations.gd is a solid defense. This is a small defense-in-depth addition: an embedded NUL byte can truncate a path in downstream native/OS calls, letting a crafted value smuggle a different effective path past the .. check (CWE-158, "poison null byte"). The change is deliberately conservative: Absolute paths are still allowed — projectPath is legitimately an absolute location on the user's machine, so rejecting absolute paths would break the tool. The added doc comment explains this so future readers don't "harden" it into a regression. No behavior change for any valid input; only paths containing a literal \0 are newly rejected. Testing npx tsc --noEmit passes. No runtime behavior changes for legitimate paths. Found while reviewing MCP servers for input-validation hardening. The command execution here is already well done ( execFile with argument arrays, class-name allowlist) — this is just closing one more edge.

title: fix: drop unused axios and update MCP SDK to resolve advisories
cleaned_text: fix: drop unused axios and update MCP SDK to resolve advisories Summary npm audit reports 4 vulnerabilities (1 moderate, 3 high) in the dependency tree. Three of them come from axios , which the server never imports, and the fourth is an outdated @modelcontextprotocol/sdk . This PR removes the unused dependency, updates the SDK, and takes the tree to 0 advisories with no source changes. What the audit says Advisory | Severity | Package | Path GHSA-hmw2-7cc7-3qxx (CRLF injection in multipart) | high | form-data | via axios GHSA-r4q5-vmmm-2653 (auth headers leak on cross-domain redirect) | moderate | follow-redirects | via axios GHSA-w48q-cv73-mx4w / CVE-2025-66414 (DNS rebinding protection) | high | @modelcontextprotocol/sdk | direct 27 advisories (SSRF, prototype pollution, DoS) | high | axios | direct Note that axios alone accounts for most of the report volume while contributing no functionality. Changes Remove axios from dependencies . It is dead weight: there are zero references to it in src/ and in the compiled build/index.js . The server only imports Node built-ins and the MCP SDK: import { Server } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js'; import { StdioServerTransport } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/stdio.js'; import { CallToolRequestSchema, ErrorCode, ListToolsRequestSchema, McpError } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/types.js'; Dropping it removes axios , form-data and follow-redirects in one move, instead of patching three packages that are never executed. Bump @modelcontextprotocol/sdk from 0.6.0 to ^1.30.1 . This resolves CVE-2025-66414. To be precise about scope: that advisory only affects HTTP-based servers ( StreamableHTTPServerTransport , SSEServerTransport ) and the advisory itself states it "does not affect servers using stdio transport", which is what this server uses. Even so, the upgrade is worth taking — 0.6.0 is many majors behind and the fix is free. No source changes required The upgrade is dependency-only. tsc compiles the existing sources unchanged against @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.1 ; the imports and the Server / setRequestHandler / StdioServerTransport API surface used here are still compatible. Verification Built and exercised over real JSON-RPC on stdio, against Godot 4.7.2: PASS initialize responde — godot-mcp 0.1.0 PASS tools/list expone las 14 herramientas — recibidas=14 PASS get_godot_version responde 4.7.2 — 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf PASS get_project_info lee el proyecto real — { "name": "lumi", ... OK: 4/4 comprobaciones en verde The harness asserts, in order: that initialize answers, that tools/list returns exactly these 14 names with no additions or omissions — launch_editor, run_project, get_debug_output, stop_project, get_godot_version, list_projects, get_project_info, create_scene, add_node, load_sprite, export_mesh_library, save_scene, get_uid, update_project_uids — and that two tools that actually touch the engine ( get_godot_version , get_project_info ) still return good data. npm audit before and after: before: 4 vulnerabilities (1 moderate, 3 high) after: 0 vulnerabilities Risk Low. No production code is touched, the removed package was unreachable, and the SDK upgrade was validated end-to-end over the real protocol rather than only at compile time. The only behaviour change is dependency resolution. Reviewer notes The same result can be reached today without this PR by running npm audit fix (which bumps axios , form-data and follow-redirects inside the existing semver ranges) — but that leaves a dead dependency installed and does not address the SDK. Removing it is the root fix.

title: fix: launch pi MCP server from plugin data to avoid npx self-shadowing
cleaned_text: fix: launch pi MCP server from plugin data to avoid npx self-shadowing Problem When installed as an Agent Plugin, pi ( pi-agent-plugins + pi-mcp-adapter ) launches the root mcp.json server entry with cwd = PLUGIN_ROOT — the cloned repo checkout. The checkout's root package.json declares exactly @cwchanap/godot-plugin@0.1.4 , so npm exec resolves the spec against it, skips the registry, and tries to run the local bin — which is never linked into node_modules/.bin : sh: godot-plugin: command not found Reproduced with npx -y @cwchanap/godot-plugin@0.1.4 from any directory inside the checkout; works from any neutral directory. The -p form does not escape the shadowing. Fix Pin the server entry's cwd to ${PLUGIN_DATA} (an Agent Plugins 1.0 permitted form that the pi loader expands and accepts via its containment rules). npx then runs outside the checkout and fetches the published package. mcp.json — add "cwd": "${PLUGIN_DATA}" to the godot stdio entry src/plugin-packaging.spec.ts — update the pinned-manifest assertion (was deep-equal to the Codex wrapper's .mcp.json ; now toMatchObject for shared launcher fields + expected cwd ) README.md — document why cwd is pinned in the Pi section Verification npx -y @cwchanap/godot-plugin@0.1.4 with cwd = plugin data dir → Godot MCP server running on stdio stdio-launcher.mjs with the regenerated payload → server starts Full test suite: 123 passed, 2 skipped No npm republish needed: the fix is repo metadata only and matters for git-based plugin installs. Note: the Codex/Claude wrapper ( plugins/godot-plugin/.mcp.json ) is unchanged — ${PLUGIN_DATA} is not expanded by those clients. If they also launch from inside the clone they will need a client-appropriate cwd.

title: fix: resolve res:// paths in file-existence checks (add_node, load_sprite, export_mesh_library, save_scene, get_uid)
cleaned_text: fix: resolve res:// paths in file-existence checks (add_node, load_sprite, export_mesh_library, save_scene, get_uid) Summary Fixes a bug where five tools always report Scene file does not exist (or File does not exist ) for any scene/file inside the project, even when the target exists. The handlers checked existence with: const scenePath = join(args.projectPath, args.scenePath); args.scenePath is a Godot resource path like res://scenes/Main.tscn , so join produces a path like /path/to/project/res:/scenes/Main.tscn (on POSIX; res: is treated as a drive on Windows) which never exists. Affected tools add_node — always Scene file does not exist load_sprite — always Scene file does not exist / Texture file does not exist export_mesh_library — always Scene file does not exist save_scene — always Scene file does not exist get_uid — always File does not exist Fix Added a small resolveResourcePath() helper that strips the res:// prefix before joining with the project path, and used it in all six existence checks: function resolveResourcePath(projectPath: string, resourcePath: string): string { return join(projectPath, resourcePath.replace(/^res:\/\//, '')); } Verification Tested end-to-end with Godot 4.7.2 against a minimal test project: create_scene → creates res://scenes/Generated.tscn ✅ add_node → adds Sprite2D to that scene ✅ save_scene → saves ✅ get_uid → returns UID for res://scripts/main.gd ✅ run_project → boots the project headless; get_debug_output captures its print() output; stop_project stops it ✅ (Note: an existing PR #104 fixes a related res:// handling issue in update_project_uids ; this change does not overlap with it — different handler, different code path.) 🤖 *Note: this PR was authored by an AI agent (Hermes Agent, Nous Research) on behalf of a human maintainer, and was verified end-to-end against Godot 4.7.2 before submission. Happy to iterate on any requested changes.*

title: Feature Request: Visual Debugging / Automated Playtest Capture Tool
cleaned_text: Feature Request: Visual Debugging / Automated Playtest Capture Tool First, thank you for building such a great tool! Currently, the biggest bottleneck in this agentic workflow is that the AI can only catch errors via terminal logs. As we know, in game development, most coding mistakes manifest as visual anomalies rather than outright crashes or console errors. Proposed Solution: It would be incredibly powerful to give the MCP a "visual debugging" feature so the agent can visually verify the scenes it builds. Technical Implementation Idea: We could implement a new tool using subprocess combined with a fast screenshot library like mss (or ffmpeg for short clips). The script's execution loop would be relatively simple: Launch the project via the Godot executable. Wait a configurable duration (e.g. 2 seconds) for the window to load and the scene to play out. Capture a screenshot (or a brief 3 seconds recording). Terminate the Godot process. Save the image/video to a temporary folder and return the file path to the agent for multimodal analysis. Would love to hear your thoughts on this approach!

title: Crash at import on `mcp>=2.0.0`: `AttributeError: 'Server' object has no attribute 'list_tools'` — please pin `mcp<2` in pyproject.toml
cleaned_text: Crash at import on mcp>=2.0.0 : AttributeError: 'Server' object has no attribute 'list_tools' — please pin mcp<2 in pyproject.toml Summary mcp-salesforce-connector (0.1.15) doesn't declare an upper bound on its mcp dependency. When the mcp Python SDK shipped v2.0.0 (Jul 2026), the low-level Server.list_tools() / Server.call_tool() decorator API was removed. Any fresh uvx / pip install after that release resolves mcp==2.0.0 and crashes at import time before the MCP handshake completes, taking down every Salesforce MCP org connection simultaneously with no config having changed. A one-line pin ( mcp>=1.0,<2.0 in pyproject.toml ) fixes it for every user with zero code changes. Happy to send a PR if you'd like — see "Proposed fix" and "Offer to help" below. Reproduction uvx --no-cache --from mcp-salesforce-connector salesforce (Any environment where mcp resolves to 2.0.0 or later triggers it.) Traceback [salesforce] [info] Server started and connected successfully [salesforce] [info] Message from client: method="initialize" id=0 Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../bin/salesforce", line 6, in from src.salesforce import main File ".../site-packages/src/salesforce/ init .py", line 1, in from . import server File ".../site-packages/src/salesforce/server.py", line 277, in @server.list_tools() ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ AttributeError: 'Server' object has no attribute 'list_tools' [salesforce] [info] Server transport closed [salesforce] [error] Server disconnected. The environment at time of failure contained: mcp-2.0.0.dist-info mcp_types-2.0.0.dist-info mcp_salesforce_connector-0.1.15.dist-info simple_salesforce-1.12.10.dist-info Root cause Breaking SDK release. mcp 2.0.0 removed/renamed the Server.list_tools() decorator that src/salesforce/server.py uses at import time. Unpinned dependency. pyproject.toml declares a loose mcp dependency with no <2 upper bound, so uvx re-resolves to the latest 2.x on every cold launch. Impact Because uvx builds an ephemeral env on each launch and this connector is a common pattern for launching Salesforce MCP servers under Claude Desktop, every user who runs one or more Salesforce orgs through this connector saw every org disconnect simultaneously after Jul 2026. Restarting Claude Desktop doesn't help — the process crashes at import on every launch. The user-visible symptom is "all my Salesforce MCP servers are down at once, no config changed." The user-side workaround is uvx --with "mcp<2" --from mcp-salesforce-connector salesforce , but that requires every user to edit their claude_desktop_config.json themselves. Proposed fix Add an upper bound to the mcp dependency in pyproject.toml : dependencies = [ # ...existing deps... "mcp>=1.0,<2.0", # ... ] That's it. One line, no code changes, and every existing user is protected the next time uvx refreshes its cache. Verification With the pin in place, uvx --from mcp-salesforce-connector --with 'mcp<2' salesforce returns a clean initialize response instead of the traceback: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"result":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05", "capabilities":{"experimental":{},"tools":{"listChanged":false}}, "serverInfo":{"name":"salesforce-mcp","version":"0.2.0"}}} Longer term The right long-term fix is to port src/salesforce/server.py to the mcp 2.x API (which uses different decorators / registration functions) or migrate to FastMCP. At that point the pin can be dropped and the floor raised to mcp>=2 . Offer to help I hit this in production on Jul 28, 2026 (11 Salesforce org connections down at once) and I've already added the pin in my downstream wrapper package (kugamon/salesforce-mcp-auto-auth-chrome v0.1.1) — you can see the exact pyproject.toml change here. I'm happy to send the same one-line PR against this repo if you'd like — just let me know. Thanks for maintaining this connector — it's the backbone of a lot of local Claude Desktop → Salesforce setups.

title: Fix CLI auth: fetch token via 'org auth show-access-token' (CLI credential redaction)
cleaned_text: Fix CLI auth: fetch token via 'org auth show-access-token' (CLI credential redaction) The May 2026 Salesforce CLI security update redacts the access token, password, and SFDX Auth URL from sf org display output, including --json (see forcedotcom/cli #3560). The connector's CLI authentication path reads accessToken from sf org display --json , so it now receives a redacted value and CLI-based auth fails. This change keeps reading the instance URL from sf org display (still returned) and reads the access token from the dedicated sf org auth show-access-token command. Helper methods were added to run CLI JSON commands and to extract the token across possible output shapes. The legacy sfdx path is unchanged. For backward compatibility with CLI versions that pre-date org auth show-access-token , the access token falls back to the org display value when the dedicated command returns nothing. On updated CLIs the token field is absent (redacted), so the fallback is a no-op there; this avoids regressing users who have not yet upgraded. Tested against production and sandbox orgs; the connector authenticates without the temporary SF_TEMP_SHOW_SECRETS workaround. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: Command Injection Vulnerability in mcp-server-rijksmuseum
cleaned_text: Command Injection Vulnerability in mcp-server-rijksmuseum Command Injection Vulnerability in mcp-server-rijksmuseum 1) CNA / Submission Type Submission type: Report a vulnerability (CVE ID request) Reporter role: Independent security researcher Report date: Apr 17, 2026 2) Reporter Contact Reporter name: BruceJin Reporter email: brucejin@zju.edu.cn Permission to share contact with vendor: Yes 3) Vendor / Product Identification Vendor: r-huijts Product: mcp-server-rijksmuseum Repository: https://github.com/r-huijts/rijksmuseum-mcp Affected component(s): src/index.ts src/handlers/ToolHandler.ts src/utils/typeGuards.ts src/utils/SystemIntegration.ts 4) Vulnerability Type CWE: CWE-78 (Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command) Short title: Command injection in MCP open_image_in_browser URL handling 5) Affected Versions Confirmed affected: 1.0.4, commit af9c2a2dba1e709f2193a59bb3fee3a3b66380b5 Suspected affected range: revisions containing the same request-to-sink flows listed below Fixed version: Not available at time of report 6) Vulnerability Description A command injection vulnerability (CWE-78) has been identified in mcp-server-rijksmuseum version 1.0.4, specifically within the open_image_in_browser MCP tool. The tool accepts a user‑supplied imageUrl argument, performs only a basic type check, and passes it unsanitized into a shell command string executed via child_process.exec. An attacker with network access to the MCP interface can inject shell metacharacters through the imageUrl parameter (e.g., "; id #) to execute arbitrary operating system commands with the privileges of the server process, leading to full host compromise, including data exposure, integrity loss, and service disruption. No fixed version is available at the time of reporting. 7) Technical Root Cause js/command-injection-from-request Source: src/index.ts:291 ( open_image_in_browser tool) Source argument: src/index.ts:296 ( imageUrl ) Insufficient validation: src/utils/typeGuards.ts:30 Source-to-sink transfer: src/handlers/ToolHandler.ts:175 Sink: src/utils/SystemIntegration.ts:12 Sink code: await this.execAsync( ${cmd} "${url}" ); 8) Attack Prerequisites Attacker can invoke the MCP open_image_in_browser tool. The server process runs on an operating system where open , xdg-open , or start is available through a shell. No effective runtime policy strips embedded quotes or shell metacharacters from imageUrl . The injected command runs with the privileges of the MCP server process. 9) Proof of Concept / Reproduction Guidance This proof of concept provides a concise, CVE-style reproduction example for the reported issue. Reproduction request {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"open_image_in_browser","arguments":{"imageUrl":"http://127.0.0.1/\"; id 1>&2; exit 1; #"}}} Validation Start the affected MCP server with a configured RIJKSMUSEUM_API_KEY value, for example by connecting mcp-inspector to node dist/index.js . Invoke the open_image_in_browser tool with the imageUrl value shown above. Confirm that the mcp-inspector response contains output from the injected id command, such as uid=... gid=... . The reproduction has been manually confirmed by using http://127.0.0.1/"; id 1>&2; exit 1; # as the imageUrl value and observing the id command result in mcp-inspector . 10) Security Impact Confidentiality: High (arbitrary command execution can read files and environment variables accessible to the server process). Integrity: High (arbitrary command execution can modify files or application state accessible to the server process). Availability: High (arbitrary command execution can terminate processes, delete files, or consume system resources). Scope: Unchanged. 11) CVSS v3.1 Suggestion Suggested vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H Suggested base score: 7.8 (High) Adjust AV to N if the affected MCP tool is exposed through a remotely reachable MCP bridge or service. 12) Workarounds / Mitigations Do not expose the MCP server to untrusted clients until a fix is available. Restrict access to the open_image_in_browser tool to trusted local users only. Disable or remove browser-opening functionality in untrusted deployments. Run the MCP server with a dedicated low-privilege OS account. 13) Recommended Fix Replace child_process.exec with child_process.execFile or spawn using an argument array and shell: false . Pass the browser-opening command and URL as separate arguments instead of building a single shell command string. Strictly validate imageUrl as a URL and reject embedded quotes, control characters, shell metacharacters, and non-HTTP(S) schemes. Enforce an allowlist for expected Rijksmuseum image hostnames if the tool is intended to open only Rijksmuseum image URLs. Add regression tests proving that payloads containing " , ; , && , | , backticks, $() , and redirections cannot execute additional commands. Publish a maintainer security advisory once a patch is released. 14) References Repository: https://github.com/r-huijts/rijksmuseum-mcp Reviewed source files: src/index.ts src/handlers/ToolHandler.ts src/utils/typeGuards.ts src/utils/SystemIntegration.ts CWE-78: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html 15) Credits Discoverer: BruceJin Discovery method: Static analysis (CodeQL), repository source-code audit, and manual reproduction with mcp-inspector 16) Additional Notes for Form Mapping Audit verdict: Manually reproduced: attacker-controlled MCP imageUrl reaches an OS command sink and executes injected shell commands. Dynamic exploit replay status: completed with injected id command using http://127.0.0.1/"; id 1>&2; exit 1; # ; mcp-inspector displayed the id command result. Maintainer should validate release mapping before coordinated disclosure. For furthermore information, please refer to https://github.com/BruceJqs/public_exp/issues/33

title: `verify_connection` reports `connected: false` while Unity appears connected
cleaned_text: verify_connection reports connected: false while Unity appears connected Hi, first off, thanks for building this integration — it’s been really helpful to work with. I’ve run into a connectivity edge case where the MCP tools report that Unity is not connected, even though the Unity side and the MCP Debug window both show an active connection. Environment Unity MCP Integration installed as a local asset under Assets/UnityMCPIntegration Unity Editor running with MCP Debug Window open (status shows Connected , port 5010 ) Cursor IDE (Claude Code) with the Unity MCP Integration configured as an MCP server Project MCP server entry point: Assets/UnityMCPIntegration/mcpServer/build/index.js Observed Behaviour From the AI client side: Calling the verify_connection tool returns: {"connected": false} Subsequent tool calls fail with an error along the lines of: "Unity Editor is not connected" On the Unity side, at the same time: The MCP Debug Window status shows Connected The Unity console logs show ping messages coming in from the server and being handled, for example: [MCP] Received message: {"type":"ping","data":{"timestamp":1776694294843}} UnityEngine.Debug:Log (object) Plugins.GamePilot.Editor.MCP.MCPMessageHandler/ d 4:MoveNext () (at Assets/UnityMCPIntegration/Editor/MCPMessageHandler.cs:32) System.Runtime.CompilerServices.AsyncVoidMethodBuilder:Start d 4> (Plugins.GamePilot.Editor.MCP.MCPMessageHandler/ d 4&) Plugins.GamePilot.Editor.MCP.MCPMessageHandler:HandleMessage (string) Plugins.GamePilot.Editor.MCP.MCPConnectionManager/ d 41:MoveNext () (at Assets/UnityMCPIntegration/Editor/MCPConnectionManager.cs:204) UnityEngine.UnitySynchronizationContext:ExecuteTasks () The Unity MCP debug stats show at least: Messages Sent: 1 Messages Received: 1 (handshake + pong) So from the Unity Editor’s point of view, the WebSocket bridge looks healthy, but the MCP server still reports connected: false to the client. When it happens This seems to happen in a narrow window after restarting the MCP server process while Unity is still running. Rough sequence: Start Unity with the project open and the Unity MCP Integration active. Start the MCP server ( node build/index.js under Assets/UnityMCPIntegration/mcpServer/build/ ) and connect from Cursor / Claude. Confirm everything works: verify_connection reports true , tools run, Unity logs show ping/pong activity. Change some MCP server configuration in Cursor / Claude (e.g. the server path or settings), which causes the MCP server process to be restarted. Unity stays open the whole time , and the Unity MCP Debug Window reconnects within a few seconds and shows Connected again. Call verify_connection from the client shortly after that restart (within ~30 seconds of the server coming back up). At this point, although Unity shows Connected and logs incoming pings, the verify_connection MCP tool still returns {"connected": false} , and tools treat the editor as disconnected. After some time passes (for example, the next ping/pong cycle), the situation eventually recovers and verify_connection starts returning true again. What I looked at On the Node / server side, I inspected the WebSocket handler generated in mcpServer/build/websocketHandler.js . The isConnected() helper appears to do three checks roughly along these lines (simplified): isConnected() { // Has a Unity WebSocket connection if (this.unityConnection === null || this.unityConnection.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) return false; // Has the initial connection handshake completed if (!this.connectionEstablished) return false; // Has there been a recent heartbeat const heartbeatTimeout = 60000; if (Date.now() - this.lastHeartbeat > heartbeatTimeout) return false; return true; } And lastHeartbeat is initialised once when the process starts and then updated on Unity WebSocket events. In the scenario above, it looks like the Unity side comes back and begins accepting pings / sending pongs, but there is a short period after the MCP server restarts where isConnected() still evaluates to false — so the verify_connection tool reports connected: false during that window, even though the editor has reconnected successfully. From the user’s perspective, that window is where calls feel “randomly disconnected”: Unity says Connected and logs pings, but the MCP tools refuse to run with "Unity Editor is not connected" . What I expected Given that: Unity is open and the MCP Debug Window shows Connected The Unity console is logging incoming ping messages from the server No obvious WebSocket errors are reported in either Unity or the server logs I expected verify_connection to report {"connected": true} (or at least some “pending / reconnecting” status) once the Unity↔server link is restored, so that tools can proceed instead of failing with a hard “not connected” result. Extra observations (minor) While digging into this, I also noticed a small logging detail in the Unity message handler on the server side: // default case for unrecognised Unity messages console.error('[Unity MCP] Unknown message type:'); Without including the actual message.type in the log, it’s a bit harder to see what unexpected messages are coming from Unity when debugging connection issues. Including the type in that log would make it easier to diagnose misconfigurations on our side.

title: v1.1.0
cleaned_text: Path-resolution overhaul to make Docker (and any non-default install layout) frictionless. Closes #97 via #98. What's new MARKITDOWN_PATH env var. Defaults to /.venv/bin/markitdown , falls back to a bare-name PATH lookup. Lets pipx install "markitdown[pdf]" or any system install work without a project venv. REPOMIX_PATH env var. Same shape, for git-repo-to-markdown . MD_ALLOWED_PATHS env var (path-delimiter-separated). Enforced on every filepath-accepting tool, not just get-markdown-file . MD_SHARE_DIR kept as a single-dir backward-compat alias. Docker volume-mount example in the README, aligned with the markdownify.paths field on the Docker MCP catalog config page. New scripts/docker-smoke-test.sh : builds the image, mounts a sample dir, calls pdf-to-markdown over the MCP stdio transport, asserts the response. Fixes Stop treating non-empty stderr from markitdown as fatal — it emits non-fatal warnings on every successful run (onnxruntime cpuid, pydub ffmpeg-missing). Exit code is the real signal. Add .dockerignore so COPY . . no longer drags the host's .venv and node_modules into the build context. Replace stale UV_PATH docs (the code stopped using uv several versions ago). Breaking changes projectRoot removed from the MCP tool input schema. It was client-controllable, so any MCP client could force the server to exec /.venv/bin/markitdown . No legitimate client should have been using it. If you need to override the project root, set MARKITDOWN_PATH directly.

title: fix(security): three input-validation bugs in get/isWithinDirectory/validateRepoUrl
cleaned_text: fix(security): three input-validation bugs in get/isWithinDirectory/validateRepoUrl Summary Fixes three input-validation bugs found by an external security audit (commit 024f97c , v1.1.0). Each fix has a regression test. Additional findings (N3–N6) are listed below as audit notes for separate issues; they are deliberately out of scope for this PR to keep the diff reviewable. Bugs fixed C1 — Markdownify.get() ignores ~ -expansion for I/O *(HIGH — true regression)* Markdownify.get({ filePath }) computes a resolvedPath via expandHome + path.normalize + path.resolve , validates it with assertPathAllowed , then discards it and uses the raw filePath for existsSync , readFile , and the returned result.path . Effect: a path like ~/notes.md passes the sandbox check, then existsSync("~/notes.md") returns false because the unexpanded string reaches the syscall. The error message and the returned path also leak the un-tilded form, which breaks any downstream consumer that round-trips the path through the same MCP server. Fix: use resolvedPath in all three places ( src/Markdownify.ts , 3-line patch). Test: src/Markdownify.test.ts writes a fixture into a temp ~ -shaped directory and calls Markdownify.get({ filePath: "~/Documents/note.md" }) , asserting result.path equals the absolute expanded path. N1 — isWithinDirectory sandbox bypass via prefix-match *(HIGH — pre-existing)* isWithinDirectory(filePath, directory) did normPath.startsWith(normDir) . With directory=/tmp/allowed , an attacker who can place files under /tmp/allowed-extra/ (sibling whose name extends the prefix) escapes the sandbox. Same issue if a parent configures MD_ALLOWED_PATHS=/srv/data and an attacker plants files in /srv/data-backup/ — these are bypassed, not blocked. Fix: boundary-aware prefix check — normPath === normDir || normPath.startsWith(normDir + path.sep) , with a guard that does not append another separator if normDir already ends with one (otherwise MD_ALLOWED_PATHS=/ would deny everything by producing "//" ). Tests: sibling-bypass cases (3), and the trailing-separator / root cases (3). N2 — validateRepoUrl accepts scp-style SSH shorthand *(HIGH — pre-existing)* The validator only blocked explicit URLs whose protocol was not http(s). It did not block scp syntax accepted by git clone and git ls-remote on port 22: git@github.com:owner/repo.git → would reach github.com:22 over SSH, bypassing the validateUrl SSRF gate internal-host:owner/repo.git → same, with no user part Fix: a regex gate that rejects any [user@]host:path form before it reaches repomix . Tests: 7 cases (3 with @ , 4 without), all reject with "scp-style SSH syntax" . Files changed src/Markdownify.ts | 6 +- src/Markdownify.test.ts | 32 +++++++++ src/utils.ts | 29 ++++++++- src/utils.test.ts | 61 +++++++++++++++++++++ 123 insertions, 5 deletions. Audit notes — out of scope, filed as separate issues These were discovered during the same review but are not included in this PR (kept here so reviewers can see the full picture): N3 (LOW): saveToTempFile has no try/finally — if the inner markitdown invocation throws, the temp file leaks in os.tmpdir() . Issue to file. N4 (LOW): inferExtensionFromUrl strips the query string but uses raw URL pathname, which still includes URL-encoded chars. Prefer parsing through new URL(href).pathname and decoding. Issue to file. N5 (INFO): stderr from repomix is silently dropped (only stdout is captured). No security impact, but obscures debugging. Defer to maintainer. N6 (MEDIUM): C3 — the write_* family defaults to allowed_directories derived from MD_ALLOWED_PATHS , which is *unset by default*. Combined with N1, an attacker who controls the input path can write to any directory the process user can reach. Behavior change (default-deny) requires a version-bump discussion with the maintainer before landing. Issue to file. Two reviewer nice-to-haves also deferred: fromRepo accepts https://192.168.1.5/... (no is_ip_private check on the URL itself) — pre-existing IPv6 SSRF gap, same root-cause family as N1/N2, but separate fix. Symlink escapes of the sandbox — pre-existing fs.realpath not used; needs a design discussion (follow symlinks? reject them? per-path?). Test plan bun test src/Markdownify.test.ts src/utils.test.ts — all existing + new cases pass Manual: bun run build && node dist/index.js and exercise get_markdown_file with a ~/path via the MCP inspector Reviewer / audit provenance Initial audit: 1 round (Hermes direct, with runtime probes against dist/ ) Independent review: GLM-5.3 (3 rounds), found the 3 blockers fixed in this commit Test-strategy cross-check: GLM-5.3 leaf subagent (separate dispatch) cc @zcaceres — happy to split this into 3 PRs if you'd prefer to land the security fixes one at a time. The audit notes (N3–N6) will be filed as issues regardless.

title: fix(sandbox-container): make container_exec timeouts return on time and kill child processes
cleaned_text: fix(sandbox-container): make container_exec timeouts return on time and kill child processes container_exec timeouts now return on time and kill everything the command started. Commands that start background processes return when the command exits instead of hanging until the timeout. Follows #523. The bug: found while checking staging after #526. sleep 20 with a 1.5 s timeout returned the timeout message only after 20 s. The abort sent SIGKILL to the shell, but its child kept the output pipe open, so output() didn't settle until the child exited. That child also survived the timeout. Timeouts: the command now runs as timeout --signal=KILL sh -c . GNU timeout puts the command in its own process group and kills the whole group, so grandchildren die too. Output from before the timeout is kept. The Worker-side abort stays as a backstop, 5 s later. Background processes: run() reads stdout and stderr itself instead of calling output() . After the process exits, it stops once the pipes close or have been quiet for 250 ms. A command like python3 -m http.server & leaves the server running, like a shell does. The runtime reports exitCode about 2 s late while a child holds the pipe, so such commands take about 2 s. I tried killing the group by proc.pid first. That pid doesn't match the container's own PID namespace, so it didn't work, which is why the kill now happens inside the container with timeout . Tests ran (app tests, check:types , check:lint ). I also ran a harness Worker under wrangler dev with a real container: Case | Before | After sleep 20 , timeout 1500 ms | 20 s, sleep survives | 1.5 s, killed (sleep 50 &); sleep 20 , timeout 1500 ms | 20 s, both survive | 1.5 s, both killed echo before; sleep 20 , timeout 1500 ms | output lost | before kept sleep 30 & echo started | waits up to the timeout | 2 s, sleep keeps running seq 1 200000 | complete | complete, 70 ms exit 2 | code 2 | code 2

title: feat(sandbox-container): start sandboxes from a snapshot of the managed debian-trixie image
cleaned_text: feat(sandbox-container): start sandboxes from a snapshot of the managed debian-trixie image Sandboxes now start from a snapshot of the Cloudflare-managed cloudflare/debian-trixie image instead of a custom Dockerfile. Deploys no longer build or push an image, and the registry override from #524 is gone. Follows #523. sequenceDiagram participant U as UserContainer (user) participant T as UserContainer ( sandbox-template ) U->>T: getTemplateSnapshot() alt no snapshot for TEMPLATE_VERSION T->>T: start cloudflare/debian-trixie (standard-1) T->>T: exec TEMPLATE_SETUP (python, pip, git, build tools, pnpm) T->>T: snapshotContainer(), store handle, destroy end T-->>U: ContainerSnapshot U->>U: start({ containerSnapshot, instance: 'lite', entrypoint: sleep infinity }) Why: this is the pattern from the blog post. Cloudflare places the managed image on hosts before requests arrive, so nothing is downloaded on start, and snapshots are what make a prepared environment fast to start. It also removes the Docker build from CI and the dependency on the internal registry.cloudchamber.cfdata.org . Template: server/sandboxTemplate.ts holds the base image, the setup script and TEMPLATE_VERSION . Bumping the version builds a new snapshot on the next container_initialize . The build runs on the UserContainer instance named sandbox-template , which can't collide with a user ID. Concurrent callers share one in-progress build. Expiry: a snapshot lives for 30 days after it is created or last restored. If a start from the snapshot fails, for example because it expired, the template is discarded and rebuilt once. Fix: startContainer now returns its error instead of throwing inside blockConcurrencyWhile . A throwing callback resets the Durable Object, which made the rebuild impossible, and in #523 a failed start reset the user's object. The setup matches the old Dockerfile: the same packages, /etc/pip.conf (exec processes don't inherit image ENV), and /workdir . The Container applications keep the durable_object policy, so they don't need to be recreated. Tests ran (app tests, check:types , check:lint , wrangler deploy -e staging --dry-run ). I also ran a harness Worker under wrangler dev with the real UserContainer : First start built the template: 60 s. Every later sandbox restored it: 0.4 s. Python, pip, git, pnpm and gcc work, and /workdir is the working directory. With a poisoned snapshot handle, the start failed, the template was rebuilt, and the sandbox came up (70 s). The next user started in 0.4 s.

title: chore: upgrade wrangler to 4.149.0
cleaned_text: chore: upgrade wrangler to 4.149.0 Every app and package now uses wrangler 4.149.0 , the latest release.
