title: feat(docker): opt-in configuration-preserving container recreation with rollback
cleaned_text: feat(docker): opt-in configuration-preserving container recreation with rollback Summary Implements an opt-in, backwards-compatible answer to #62 without silently changing the current recreate_container default contract. Add preserve_existing: bool = false to the existing tool. With the default false , all prior arguments and stop/remove/new-run semantics remain unchanged. With preserve_existing=true , inspect the selected container's actual config and immutable original image; preflight the requested replacement image before stopping anything. Create the replacement from inspected configuration using the existing Docker SDK create-from-config route, preserving environment, restart policy, healthcheck, labels, network endpoint options, mounted volume identity and prior running/stopped state where Docker permits. Reject conflicting caller-supplied overrides in this mode instead of silently dropping environment, network or mount arguments. If replacement creation or startup fails after original removal, attempt to recreate the inspected original configuration and restore its original running state. Return a hard error even when rollback succeeds, and an explicit combined error if rollback also fails. Handle Docker AutoRemove races where the original may disappear during stop. Successful replacement changes container ID; the mode is not atomic. Test-first evidence Official baseline: ckreiling/mcp-server-docker:main at 57a7df208fdc2362505835f670e53c66f3717c48 . Exact candidate: deb6a2e84750c85c7adf39c1c3db539e9cb007e2 . RED → GREEN: 4 initial tests failed because upstream did not accept the new flag; after implementation, 9 tests passed for preserved runtime config, preflight, rollback, original-stopped state, auto-remove behavior, duplicate volume bindings, unsafe override rejection, and legacy default compatibility. User README documentation and an MCP tool-schema regression are now included; preserve_existing is optional in the emitted schema. Full source suite: 15/15 pytest tests passed (including native stdio initialization against the existing minimal fake Docker API); Ruff formatter and lint checks passed. Live Docker Engine 29.8.1 , disposable Alpine 3.22 container only, isolated with --network none , unique temporary label and no production mounts: replacement produced a new ID but retained environment, labels, network and running state. A separate real disposable negative-path test injected a replacement-creation failure after the original had been removed, then allowed the SDK to recreate the original from its immutable image/config. The original runtime state, network, labels and environment were restored; the operation correctly returned a failure. Both disposable targets/helpers were removed after validation. Limitations / review gates This is a draft for a destructive API extension. It does not guarantee restoration when the old image/volume/network is no longer available, and it does not make a Docker recreate atomic. The inspected config may contain host-specific endpoint or networking details that Docker rejects on other engines. An operator still needs a verified backup/rollback path for critical workloads. The added preserve mode intentionally declines extra configuration overrides; maintainers can decide whether a more general override policy is desirable later. This PR does not affect generic build/release tools or trigger any deployment. Full official upstream CI, maintainer approval and official release inclusion remain outstanding.

title: fix(deps): offer patched Paramiko 5 as explicit optional SSH extra

Test-first packaging check failed with the previous mandatory dependency and passed after the optional-extra change. Default package in an isolated Python 3.12/uv installation resolved without Paramiko . ssh extra resolved Paramiko 5.0.0 and initialized Docker SDK 7.1.0's Paramiko SSH transport with a mocked connection boundary. No real SSH server was contacted. All eight official upstream tests passed , including native stdio startup against the existing source-owned fake Docker API, without exposing a real Docker socket. Ruff check and format check passed. The exact source built a source distribution and wheel offline; the wheel metadata included Provides-Extra: ssh and the patched Paramiko dependency with its extra marker. Git diff/whitespace checks passed. Outstanding maintainer review This intentionally changes distribution defaults: existing users who rely on DOCKER_HOST=ssh://... must opt into the SSH extra, and Paramiko 5 itself is not interoperable with some older SHA-1-only servers. This is the security/compatibility decision described in #72. The default upstream Docker image may also need an explicitly documented SSH-capable build variant if SSH support from that image is intended. This is a draft PR until maintainers accept that compatibility break and the upstream CI/test matrix and real SSH interoperability are verified. No live Docker containers, SSH destinations or downstream releases were changed.

title: Modernize Paramiko dependency: patched SSH extra versus vulnerable mandatory 3.x
cleaned_text: Modernize Paramiko dependency: patched SSH extra versus vulnerable mandatory 3.x Problem Current pyproject.toml declares paramiko>=3.5.1,<4.0 as a direct, always-installed dependency, so non-SSH Docker endpoints also install Paramiko 3.x. GitHub's reviewed GHSA-r374-rxx8-8654 / CVE-2026-44405 applies through Paramiko 4.0.0. The now-available Paramiko 5.0.0 (released May 9, 2026) removes SHA-1 SSH algorithms, addressing the relevant issue but also introducing intentional compatibility breaks for legacy SSH servers. A maintained downstream temporarily removed Paramiko and limited itself to non-SSH Docker endpoints. That is a packaging/security delta, not a generic deployment setting, and should converge upstream. Alternatives for maintainer review Preferred candidate: make SSH support an explicit optional extra, e.g. mcp-server-docker[ssh] installing a supported patched paramiko>=5,<6 , while the default distribution uses Unix/TCP Docker endpoints without Paramiko. Document that ssh:// requires the extra and SHA-2-compatible servers. Alternatively, retain always-on SSH but update the direct Paramiko constraint to a patched major version, explicitly accepting potential legacy-client/server breakage and adding compatibility tests. If neither is appropriate, document the accepted support/security policy and verify whether Docker SDK has a supported non-Paramiko SSH path. Please avoid only relaxing the old <4.0 constraint without verifying the shipped resolved version: that could still select a version affected by the advisory. Acceptance Test default installation on fresh Python 3.12: no vulnerable Paramiko package is installed and Unix/TCP endpoints retain existing semantics. Test SSH extra installation: a patched Paramiko release is resolved and the official Docker Python SDK's ssh:// client path initializes correctly with representative credentials. Document major SSH algorithm interoperability changes (notably old SHA-1-only servers), update lock/test matrix and release notes. Run official lint, unit, packaging and daemon-free integration verification; any real SSH test must use a disposable target, never production. This issue is distinct from previously submitted Docker MCP output/cleanup/filter PRs and does not request a production deployment.

title: Bound Docker MCP log and attached-run text output with truncation metadata
cleaned_text: Bound Docker MCP log and attached-run text output with truncation metadata Problem The Docker MCP tools fetch_container_logs and attached run_container(detach=false) can return unbounded command/log text. tail="all" can expose arbitrarily large historical logs, and an attached process can print arbitrarily much output. This is a different problem from #66, which concerns the inspect-level fields of list_containers . A maintained downstream bounds text results to the last 20 KiB, replaces invalid UTF-8 instead of failing serialization and includes truncated and original bytes metadata. We want to converge that generic protocol safety behavior upstream. Upstream-compatible design Keep existing tool names, input schemas and existing logs/output content shape as much as possible; add explicit truncation and original-byte metadata when appropriate. Treat the maximum as a fixed documented output policy (20 KiB is an initial suggested bound), applied before decoding to avoid huge model-facing payloads. Preserve the *tail* of the output, annotate whether the full text was longer, and decode with errors="replace" for invalid UTF-8 or cut multibyte boundaries. Prefer an implementation that does not first eagerly materialize an unlimited tail="all" result in memory when Docker SDK streaming can avoid it; distinguish response bounding from memory / transport input bounding . Attached execution's output contract depends on the already-open PR #61 / issue #69. Avoid duplicating or breaking that fix: submit the logs bound independently, and either incorporate attached-output bounds in a separate follow-up after #61 or agree a compatible PR stacking approach. Add tests for short text, exactly-at-boundary output, over-limit text, invalid UTF-8, metadata accuracy, logs tail=100 and tail="all" , and attached-output safety when the underlying type fix is available. This is source-level generic MCP output policy, not Homelab-specific configuration or container operational monitoring. Acceptance Maintainers agree on output shape and limit semantics; tests and CI cover byte/UTF-8 boundaries; there is no accidental API regression; final upstream release contains the accepted behavior. An upstream issue plus a draft PR is appropriate; a merged PR alone does not authorize removing the downstream patch.

title: ci: add autofix.ci
cleaned_text: ci: add autofix.ci What this does Adds an autofix.ci workflow that automatically pushes lint/format fixes onto pull requests. When a contributor opens or updates a PR, the workflow runs the repo's mutating fixer ( pnpm run lint , i.e. biome check --write ) and, via the autofix.ci GitHub App, commits any resulting fixes straight back onto the PR branch. Contributors never see a red formatting/lint check they have to reproduce and fix by hand. The autofix.ci GitHub App is installed org-wide for marimo-team (confirmed by an org admin), so this works as soon as it merges — no per-repo setup required. How it composes with the existing lint gate CI's biome ci . lint step stays exactly as-is: it's non-mutating and still fails the build on anything that can't be auto-fixed (genuine lint errors are meant to be surfaced, not silently rewritten). autofix.ci is the complement — it handles the *mechanical* fixes (formatting, safe lint autofixes) so that class of failure disappears from the contributor's plate. The fixer step is guarded with || true so unfixable lint errors don't block uploading the fixes that *did* apply; CI remains the source of truth for reporting them. The setup steps (checkout / pnpm / Node) mirror test.yml exactly, with the same SHA-pinned action versions. Verification Cloned, pnpm install --ignore-scripts --frozen-lockfile , ran pnpm run lint → no diff (tree stays clean; only pre-existing non-fixable warnings, which CI already reports). Workflow YAML parses cleanly and passes actionlint . Workflow name is exactly autofix.ci (required — the service identifies the workflow by name for security) and the autofix-ci/action step runs last. Part of the marimo-team engineering-excellence initiative.

cleaned_text: feature: add local file path support Add Local File Path Support for JSON Data Sources Summary This PR adds support for reading JSON data from local files in addition to the existing HTTP URL support. Users can now query local JSON files directly without needing to serve them via HTTP. Changes Made 🔧 Core Functionality Added file system imports : fs.readFileSync , fs.existsSync , and path.resolve Created smart source detection : Automatically distinguishes between URLs and file paths using new URL() validation Enhanced data loading : New loadData() function handles both remote URLs and local file paths Maintained backward compatibility : Existing fetchData() function still works for URL-based workflows 📝 API Updates Parameter renamed : url → source for better clarity (accepts both URLs and file paths) Schema updated : Removed strict URL validation to allow file paths Tool descriptions enhanced : Updated to reflect support for both data source types 📖 Documentation README updated : Integrated local file support documentation naturally into existing structure Usage examples added : Demonstrates both URL and local file usage patterns Notes section enhanced : Added file path resolution and error handling information Key Features ✨ Automatic Detection // Automatically detects URL vs file path isUrl("https://api.example.com/data.json") // → true isUrl("./data.json") // → false 🔄 Unified Interface Both data sources use the same API: // Remote URL (existing functionality) { "source": "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users", "jsonPath": "$[0].name" } // Local file (new functionality) { "source": "./data/users.json", "jsonPath": "$[0].name" } Usage Examples Query Local File { "tool": "query", "arguments": { "source": "./data/users.json", "jsonPath": "$.users[*].name" } } Filter Local Data { "tool": "filter", "arguments": { "source": "./products.json", "jsonPath": "$.products[*]", "condition": "@.price < 50" } } Remote API (Still Works) { "tool": "query", "arguments": { "source": "https://api.example.com/data.json", "jsonPath": "$.items[0]" } } File Structure Changes src/index.ts # Enhanced with file loading capabilities README.md # Updated with integrated documentation build/index.js # Compiled with new features Benefits 🎯 Enhanced Flexibility : Work with local development files, configs, and datasets ⚡ Improved Performance : No network latency for local files 🔒 Better Security : Access local files without exposing them via HTTP 🛠️ Developer Experience : Test and develop with local JSON files easily 📁 Broader Use Cases : Configuration files, local datasets, development data Breaking Changes ❌ None - This is a fully backward-compatible enhancement Migration Guide For users wanting to use the new file path feature: // Before (still works) { "url": "https://api.example.com/data.json" "source": "https://api.example.com/data.json" } // New capability { "source": "./local-data.json" } Ready for review ✅ All functionality tested and documented

This results in the tool reporting time slots as "free" when participants are actually busy. Environment MCP Server : v-3/google-calendar Affected Tool : find_free_time Source : https://github.com/v-3/google-calendar/blob/5644d05abc272a2e8866d677037d735127abecd6/src/index.ts#L298 Bug Description When checking availability using find_free_time , the tool does not properly convert event times to a common timezone before checking for conflicts. This causes events stored in timezones different from the query timezone to be overlooked. Example Scenario Setup: User's timezone: America/Los_Angeles (PST/PDT) Query: Find free time for abc@example.com on January 27, 2026 at 11:30 AM PST Existing event: "Some event" from 2:00 PM - 3:00 PM America/New_York (EST/EDT) Expected Behavior: The tool should convert 2:00 PM EST to 11:00 AM PST Detect that 11:30 AM - 12:00 PM PST overlaps with the existing event Report the time slot as busy Actual Behavior: The tool reports 11:30 AM - 12:00 PM PST as free No conflict is detected The event stored in EST is not properly considered Technical Details When events are returned from the Google Calendar API, they include timezone information in the start and end fields: { "summary": "Some meeting", "start": { "dateTime": "2026-01-27T14:00:00-05:00", "timeZone": "America/New_York" }, "end": { "dateTime": "2026-01-27T15:00:00-05:00", "timeZone": "America/New_York" } } The find_free_time tool appears to not be converting these times to the query timezone before checking for overlaps. Steps to Reproduce Create a calendar event in timezone A (e.g., America/New_York at 2:00 PM) Query find_free_time for availability in timezone B (e.g., America/Los_Angeles at 11:30 AM) Observe that the tool reports the time as "free" despite the overlap when converted properly: 2:00 PM EST = 11:00 AM PST Query: 11:30 AM PST falls within the 11:00 AM - 12:00 PM PST window Impact Critical for multi-timezone teams: Leads to double-booking when scheduling meetings across timezones Requires manual verification of all suggested times Makes the tool unreliable for users with calendars containing events in multiple timezones Breaks the core value proposition of automated scheduling Workaround Until this is fixed, users must: Call find_free_time to get candidate slots (required participants only) Manually fetch events using list_events for ALL participants Implement timezone conversion in client code Manually check each candidate slot against all participants' events

title: mcp[cli] pinned to 1.6.0 (5 published advisories); SECURITY.md has no contact address
cleaned_text: mcp[cli] pinned to 1.6.0 (5 published advisories); SECURITY.md has no contact address Hi, I'm the developer of Presend, a small tool that checks package installs. chroma-mcp 0.2.6 (pyproject.toml and the published package) pins mcp[cli]==1.6.0 . PyPI lists five published advisories for that version: GHSA-9h52-p55h-vw2f (CVE-2025-66416): DNS rebinding protection not enabled by default (fixed in 1.23.0) GHSA-jpw9-pfvf-9f58 (CVE-2026-52869): SSE / Streamable HTTP transport routing issue (fixed in 1.27.2) GHSA-vj7q-gjh5-988w (CVE-2026-59950): WebSocket server transport (fixed in 1.28.1) GHSA-3qhf-m339-9g5v (CVE-2025-53366) and GHSA-j975-95f5-7wqh (CVE-2025-53365): unhandled exceptions / DoS (fixed in 1.9.4 and 1.10.0) Most of them concern the HTTP-based transports, so stdio-only setups are less exposed. The practical problem is the exact pin: because the published package requires mcp==1.6.0 , users can't upgrade the SDK themselves without breaking the install. Suggested change: mcp[cli]>=1.28.1,<2 (1.28.1 has no known advisories; the 1.x line is at 1.30.0). Separately, SECURITY.md still says "send an email to [your-email]", so there's currently no private channel. Private vulnerability reporting isn't enabled on the repo either; turning it on (Settings → Security) would fix both at once. All of the advisories above are already public, which is why I'm filing this as an issue.

title: chroma_add_documents fetches every id in the collection on each call (O(n) per add)
cleaned_text: chroma_add_documents fetches every id in the collection on each call (O(n) per add) chroma_add_documents does its duplicate check like this ( src/chroma_mcp/server.py , line 365 on main): existing_ids = collection.get(include=[])["ids"] duplicate_ids = [id for id in ids if id in existing_ids] That pulls every id in the collection into Python on every call, then does a linear in on a list for each incoming id. The cost grows with the collection, so a bulk load gets slower the further it gets. Measured while backfilling about 1M documents in batches of 100 into a persistent collection (Apple M4 Max, chromadb 1.5.9, chroma-mcp 0.2.6): collection size | docs/s 80k | 45 200k | 27 440k | 15 555k | 12 The python process sat at 100% of one core the whole time. With the change below, same collection, same client: 51 docs/s at 560k and flat after that (65 docs/s at 900k). One line, same behaviour (still raises on duplicates): existing_ids = set(collection.get(ids=ids, include=[])["ids"]) duplicate_ids = [id for id in ids if id in existing_ids] Happy to open a PR if you want it.

title: Unsubstituted {agentId} template in ERC-8004 registration endpoints
cleaned_text: Unsubstituted {agentId} template in ERC-8004 registration endpoints While integrating BSC mainnet ERC-8004 agents (registry 0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432) into a marketplace that resolves agents from their on-chain registrations, we found that every TermiX platform registration we encountered declares service endpoints containing a literal, unsubstituted {agentId} path template. A client that resolves an agent from the registry, as the standards describe, cannot reach it. Reproduction (token 266234, first observed 2026-08-18, re-verified 2026-08-19): tokenURI(266234) returns a metadata URL on termix-platform-prod.s3.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com . That JSON declares, verbatim: "services": [ { "name": "A2A", "endpoint": "https://platform-backend.prod.termix.live/api/v1/a2a/agents/{agentId}/card", "version": "0.3.0" }, { "name": "Termix Platform", "endpoint": "https://platform-backend.prod.termix.live/api/v1/agents/{agentId}/services", "version": "aacp-platform-v1" } ] Fetching the A2A endpoint exactly as declared returns HTTP 404. The metadata contains no agentId field, and neither EIP-8004 registration-v1 nor A2A 0.3.0 defines endpoint templating, so a standards-based client has nothing to substitute. Substituting the ERC-8004 token id resolves. GET https://platform-backend.prod.termix.live/api/v1/a2a/agents/266234/card returns HTTP 200 with the agent record: agentTokenId: "266234" , agent card nested under card (verified 2026-08-19). The metadata does not state this substitution rule. Scope: every TermiX-hosted registration we came across shows the same pattern, including tokens 266229, 266232, 266234 (positioncrew agents) and TradePilot.agent, DeFiBot.agent, CMC.agent, prover.agent, Gelato.agent, RiskOracle.agent, defi_yield_optimizer.agent, DeFi-Yield-Optimizer.agent (same backend domain). Questions: Is the {agentId} template an intended convention for a platform client that already knows the id out of band? If so, could the registration writer either substitute the token id at write time or publish the id in the metadata, so that registry-based consumers can reach TermiX agents? Our marketplace currently lists these agents as offline because the declared endpoints do not answer.

title: Multi-wallet support requires N separate MCP server processes — design improvement proposal
cleaned_text: Multi-wallet support requires N separate MCP server processes — design improvement proposal Problem The current design ties exactly one private key to one MCP server process via the BSC_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY env var (see src/config.ts → getAccount() ). The signing tools ( Send_BNB , transferBEP20Token , pancakeSwap , Send_Token , etc.) take no wallet identifier — they implicitly act on the env-loaded key. To use N wallets, the user has to register N separate MCP server entries in their client config (Claude Desktop / Claude Code / Cursor / etc.), each spawning its own node build/index.js process with its own BSC_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY . Example from a real user config after adding 4 extra wallets: "mcpServers": { "bsc-mcp": { "command": "node", "args": [...], "env": { "BSC_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY": "0x...A" } }, "bsc-wallet-1": { "command": "node", "args": [...], "env": { "BSC_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY": "0x...B" } }, "bsc-wallet-2": { "command": "node", "args": [...], "env": { "BSC_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY": "0x...C" } }, "bsc-wallet-3": { "command": "node", "args": [...], "env": { "BSC_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY": "0x...D" } }, "bsc-wallet-4": { "command": "node", "args": [...], "env": { "BSC_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY": "0x...E" } } } Why this is painful Tool-schema explosion in the LLM context. Every server registers the same ~11 tools, so 5 wallets = 55 tool schemas in the model's context window. Pure token waste. Wallet selection by string prefix. To act on a specific wallet the model has to pick mcp bsc-wallet-3 Send_BNB vs mcp bsc-wallet-2 Send_BNB — easy to get wrong, and there's no way for the model to know *which* wallet has which BNB / token holdings without polling each. N idle node processes + N viem clients + N RPC connections for what is conceptually one signing module. Key fanout in client configs. Even with the recent ObfuscatedSecureBuffer / decryptPrivateKey work, each wallet's encrypted key still has to be pasted into a separate mcpServers[*].env entry. There's no single keystore. No discovery. No listWallets tool — the user has to remember which prefix maps to which address. Proposed design One MCP server, multi-wallet inside, addressed by alias or address on every signing tool. Config. Replace the single env var with a keystore — either: a JSON file ~/.bnbchain-mcp/wallets.json of { alias: encryptedPrivateKey } , decrypted on first use with the existing password flow, or an HD seed + accountIndex parameter (BIP-44 m/44'/60'/0'/0/i ). Backward-compatible fallback: if BSC_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY is the only thing set, treat it as the single default wallet (alias default ). Tool signature. Every signing tool gains an optional wallet field: // transferNativeToken { recipientAddress: z.string(), amount: z.string(), wallet: z.string().optional().describe("Wallet alias or address; defaults to the configured default wallet"), } Then getAccount(wallet?) resolves alias → key (or derives from HD seed). Read-only tools like Get_Wallet_Info already accept any address , so no change there. New tools. List_Wallets → returns [{ alias, address }] Set_Default_Wallet (optional convenience) Migration v1: introduce the keystore + optional wallet param, keep env-var single-wallet behavior. No breaking change. v2 (later): deprecate the env-var path. Why it matters Anyone using this MCP for more than one wallet (trading desks, agent operators, multi-strategy users) hits this. Today the workaround is the config above, which I and others have ended up with after a few rounds of "create another wallet → add another MCP entry". The fix is mostly local to config.ts + a shared zod field across the tool files. Happy to send a PR if the maintainers like this direction.

title: Comments are HTML-encoded, breaking markdown formatting
cleaned_text: Comments are HTML-encoded, breaking markdown formatting Description When creating comments via todoist_comment_create , the content is HTML-encoded before being sent to the Todoist API. This causes markdown formatting to render incorrectly in Todoist. Example Input content: Stage code confirmed: VP API returns Stage="A" for In Pursuit projects What Todoist displays: Stage code confirmed: VP API returns Stage="A" for In Pursuit projects Characters affected include: " → " , / → / , ' → ' , & → & , → > Expected behavior Content should be passed through to the Todoist API as-is. Todoist's API accepts markdown natively and handles its own rendering — the MCP server should not HTML-encode the content. Workaround Calling the Todoist REST API directly (via curl) with the same content produces correctly formatted comments.

Timezone-aware occurrence matching New find_event_occurrence() method with exact datetime matching Automatic UTC fallback for naive datetimes (common in LLM-constructed dates) Uses ±1 minute search window followed by exact datetime equality check Fixes : Wrong occurrence deletion issues from #1 2. Flexible deletion modes Delete single occurrence : occurrence_date only (default) Delete from occurrence forward : occurrence_date + delete_entire_series=True Delete entire series : delete_entire_series=True only Delete non-recurring event : event_id only (unchanged behavior) 3. title: NPM Dist Doesn't Run
cleaned_text: NPM Dist Doesn't Run Trying to run using npx -y keycloak-model-context-protocol fails. It throws a bunch of 'Import not found' errors. After digging through this a lot it turns out it's because the node interpreter isn't automatically invoked, but rather the file is simply executed. You need to specify to run using the node interpreter by adding the following to the top of index.js when publishing to NPM: #!/usr/bin/env node . You can look at other NPM distributions of MCP servers for examples.

title: fix: keep onboarding responsive during background mailbox scans
cleaned_text: fix: keep onboarding responsive during background mailbox scans Onboarding can freeze after selecting a usage mode because automatic mailbox reads occupy Next.js's serialized Server Action queue. Gmail quota retries then delay the intent save and subsequent actions. Global mailbox assessment and writing-style analysis use the same queue. Move optional analyses into after-response work with per-account owned locks, cached-result reuse, failure cooldowns and bounded 20-message samples. Keep startup assessments out of onboarding, load statistics through the existing account-scoped HTTP endpoint, and limit each import to one nonempty page. The statistics loader now deduplicates requests per account/direction and releases loading state after errors or account switches. Manual imports stop on the first error, show one toast and allow retry. Provider throttling no longer persists an incomplete assessment as complete. Validation includes regression tests for unresolved reads, cache reuse, duplicate/expired tasks, account isolation, throttling, bounded pagination and request failures; emulated browser checks show intent saving and Continue remain usable during pending/denied reads. Full unit sweep: 8,718 passed, 1,113 skipped and one five-second assistant-chat import timeout; an isolated rerun of that file and the UI regressions passed all 89 tests with default timeouts. Final emulated browser suite: 3 passed (including OAuth setup). Changed-file Biome and Server Action export checks passed. Production build (Next.js, TypeScript and Serwist) passed. Performance: uncached analyses add a Redis lock lookup/acquisition and poll persona status every two seconds only while running. Startup read volume is substantially smaller; no database schema or dependency changes. Summary by CodeRabbit New Features Persona analysis now runs in the background after eligible onboarding choices, with status updates while it’s processing. Analysis status can indicate when processing is waiting to retry after a provider limit. Improvements Statistics loading avoids duplicate requests and handles overlapping loads and failures more reliably. Each statistics load scans up to one page; older history may require a separate load. Assessment results no longer automatically whitelist Inbox Zero.

title: mail: Isolate messages the sync protocol cannot represent
cleaned_text: mail: Isolate messages the sync protocol cannot represent Every mail sync response is validated as a whole, so a single message outside the protocol limits failed its page on every retry and left the account stuck on "Waiting to sync". #4200 fixed the fields seen so far; this makes the failure mode itself bounded. Fit everything that can be fit : subject, preview, sender and recipients, labels, attachment names/MIME types/sizes, and received time are brought within limits. Oversized display names give way before the trailing ; an oversized external URL is dropped rather than cut; attachments whose ids are too long to request are left out. Isolate the rest : parsedMessagePatch and parsedMessageBodyObservation validate their output and return null (logged at error level with the message id and issue paths) instead of producing something that fails the page. Enumeration, delta changes, hydration, conversation membership and operations skip that one message, along with its body and hydration key. Shared limits : metadata text limits are named constants in mail-core, so the schema and the fitting code can't drift. Tests : an end-to-end enumeration test through the route and client adapter shows a page with one unrepresentable message still syncs the rest. It fails on main. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code Summary by CodeRabbit Bug Fixes Mail sync now retains valid messages even when other messages in the same page exceed supported limits. Oversized or invalid message details are safely trimmed, normalized, or omitted so valid message data can still be processed. Messages that cannot meet protocol requirements are skipped, preventing invalid message updates or body content from being returned.

title: mail: Keep sync from stalling on oversized attachment and recipient fields
cleaned_text: mail: Keep sync from stalling on oversized attachment and recipient fields A message with an attachment filename, MIME type, or recipient entry over the sync protocol limits failed its whole enumeration/changes page on every retry, so the account sat on \"Waiting to sync\" forever. Clamp attachment filename and MIME type, and each to/cc/bcc entry, to the schema limits when building observations (same approach already used for bodies and Content-IDs) Name those limits as shared constants in mail-core so the schema and the clamp can't drift Tests cover an oversized filename/MIME type and an unsplit oversized bcc header; both failed before the fix 🤖 Generated with Claude Code Summary by CodeRabbit Bug Fixes Oversized attachment filenames and MIME types are now capped at supported lengths in message details. Long recipient addresses are capped at the supported length, helping messages with oversized recipient data stay within sync limits.

title: Add HTTP transport and --allowed-host for hosted deployments
cleaned_text: Add HTTP transport and --allowed-host for hosted deployments Companion to #29 , kept separate per your CONTRIBUTING note about one topic per PR. Same caveat as there: I'm a PM, not an engineer, built this with Claude, and would rather be corrected than merged. The problem mcp.run() with no arguments is stdio only, so the server can't be hosted — which rules out ChatGPT connectors, Claude's web and mobile apps, and sharing one instance with several people. The change --transport {stdio,sse,streamable-http} with --host , --port and --path , each with an FPL_MCP_* environment equivalent. stdio stays the default , so no existing configuration changes behaviour. Binds 127.0.0.1 by default, on the assumption that a reverse proxy terminates TLS in front, and warns if told to bind 0.0.0.0 . Also --allowed-host . Hosting this behind a domain, every request came back Invalid Host header (HTTP 421): the SDK's DNS-rebinding protection validates the Host header against a list containing only localhost. The flag wires TransportSecuritySettings into FastMCP , keeping loopback entries. Without it, hosting this is impossible and the error gives no clue why. On #24 This works against your SDK v2 migration and you should weigh that. It adds SDK-coupled code to main .py — settings.host , settings.port , streamable_http_path , TransportSecuritySettings — so the migration surface grows beyond the two lines you mentioned. It's confined to main() and the argument parser rather than spread through the codebase, but it is more than was there before. Happy to adapt this to the v2 API instead if you'd rather migrate first, or to close it and keep only #N, which has no SDK coupling at all. Testing Twelve tests in tests/test_transport_options.py : defaults are unchanged (stdio, loopback), flags and environment variables parse, an unknown transport is rejected, and --allowed-host produces settings that accept the hostname both with and without a port while keeping loopback. 139 tests total, all passing.

title: Serve public FPL endpoints without requiring credentials
cleaned_text: Serve public FPL endpoints without requiring credentials Hi — context on who's writing this first. I'm a product manager, not an engineer. I built this with heavy help from Claude and I'm learning the basics as I go, so please review it more sceptically than a PR from someone who knows what they're doing. If I've misread something about your design, I'd rather be corrected than merged. The problem get_team , get_manager_info , get_league_standings and get_league_analytics route through make_authed_request , which raises when no refresh token is stored. But the FPL endpoints behind them — /entry/{id}/ , /entry/{id}/history/ , /entry/{id}/event/{gw}/picks/ , /leagues-classic/{id}/standings/ — are public and work unauthenticated. So looking up a team or a mini-league by its public ID needs a login it doesn't actually require. The change Added make_optional_auth_request to auth_manager.py : uses credentials when present, so existing users are unaffected; falls back to an unauthenticated request when they're absent; falls back also if an authenticated attempt fails for token reasons, since these endpoints never needed auth. /api/my-team/ stays authenticated. Pointed get_entry_data and get_team_for_gameweek at it — those two wrappers cover nearly every call site — plus two direct calls in leagues.py , and improved the error in managers.py when no team ID is available. The README tool list is updated to match, since four entries were marked "(requires authentication)" and no longer are. Testing Five tests in tests/test_public_fallback.py cover the seam: a public endpoint with no credentials, a private endpoint still refusing with a clear message, expired credentials falling back to public data, and working credentials still taking the authenticated path. I checked the tests actually catch the regression by reverting the change and re-running: two fail, three pass. The three that pass are guarding existing behaviour, which is what I wanted. Existing 127 tests still pass, 132 total. To check yourself: pip install -e ".[dev]" && pytest -q Worth noting package-check.yml builds the package but doesn't run tests, so the green check here won't cover them. Also verified against the live FPL API: team lookups, league lists and mini-league standings all return real data with no credentials configured. Note I have a separate PR for HTTP transport, kept apart per your CONTRIBUTING note about one topic per PR. This one has no SDK coupling, so it's independent of your #24 migration.

title: Version bootstrap schemas per season and stop them rotting
cleaned_text: Version bootstrap schemas per season and stop them rotting Stacked on #23 — targets fix/preseason-and-mcp-pin , so review that one first. Retarget to main once #23 merges. Follow-up to #23, which reduced the schema-validation log noise but left the underlying schema stale. The problem The bundled schema failed on every fetch of the 2026/27 payload, for two independent reasons: FPL retired the mng_* manager fields (from the 2024/25 experiment), which the schema marked required . saves_per_90 was typed integer because the *first* player's value happens to be 0 — a later player reads 1.62 . Validation is advisory ( validate_data 's return value is discarded), so nothing broke. But it logged a ~100KB report on every cold fetch, which trains you to ignore the one warning that might matter. The root cause is the generic schema_extractor.py : it infers each field's type from the first array item only, and marks every non-null field required. Versioning Schemas are now per-season — static_schema_2026-27.json . config.resolve_static_schema_path() picks the newest (season labels sort correctly as plain strings), and FPL_STATIC_SCHEMA_PATH overrides. Old seasons sit alongside the current one, so a schema is never edited in place and stays an accurate record of that season's payload. The stale unversioned static_schema.json is removed; the fallback path to it is kept for robustness. Keeping it from rotting again scripts/generate_static_schema.py generates the bundled schema and can --check live data against it. Three rules: Union types across every array item , not the first. Nullable where any item is null; number where an integer field is elsewhere a float. Fields seen only as null stay unconstrained. Pre-season FPL nulls team strength and form for all 20 teams — freezing that in as "always null" would break the moment matches are played. This is the inverse of the original rot and easy to miss when generating in August. Only a curated core is required ( CORE_REQUIRED ) — the fields the server reads and that identify the payload as FPL data. Requiring all ~105 element fields is precisely what broke on the mng_* removal. Behavior Accepts: live pre-season payload simulated mid-season data ( strength / form populated) FPL retiring peripheral stats FPL adding a new stat Rejects: empty object, players missing web_name , non-FPL element objects, now_cost as a string Live 2026/27 data validates with zero warnings , verified from a clean wheel install (the schema and its README both ship). Tests 116 pass (was 97). New cover for the inference rules, season detection including a century rollover, path resolution (newest / env override / legacy fallback), and the accept/reject behavior above. Docs src/fpl_mcp/schemas/README.md documents the practice and when to regenerate — notably to regenerate once the season is under way , since pre-season data is unrepresentative. scripts/README.md now points at the right tool and explains why the generic extractor is not it. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: Fix pre-season breakage and pin mcp to the 1.x line (v0.1.7)
cleaned_text: Fix pre-season breakage and pin mcp to the 1.x line (v0.1.7) Verified the server against the live 2026/27 pre-season API (GW1 deadline 2026-08-21, no current gameweek) and fixed what that state broke. All 23 tools were exercised against the real API. Release blocker: broken install pyproject.toml declared mcp>=1.2.0 with no upper bound. mcp 2.0 removed mcp.server.fastmcp , which this server is built on, so a fresh pip install fpl-mcp today resolves to a version that cannot import at all: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'mcp.server.fastmcp' It only worked locally because the dev venv already had mcp 1.4.1 pinned via uv.lock . Constrained to <2.0.0 and verified a clean install now resolves mcp 1.29.0 and imports all 23 tools. Pre-season fixes Every player returned zero upcoming fixtures. get_current_gameweek_id() fell back to next - 1 , which is an invalid gameweek 0 before the season starts. That 0 is falsy, so fixture lookups bailed out early — despite the full 2026/27 fixture list being published. This also 404'd the live-score and dream-team endpoints ( event/0/live/ , dream-team/0/ ). Fixture analysis skipped gameweek 1. The window was anchored on current + 1 . Added get_next_gameweek_id() and anchored there instead, which is equivalent mid-season but correct pre-season. Live scores and dream team now report that a gameweek has not been played yet instead of surfacing a raw 404. Genuine failures (500s) still error — covered by a test. Schema validation logged a ~100KB report on every cold fetch , because FPL dropped the mng_* fields and nulls team strength pre-season. Validation was already advisory (return value is discarded), so behavior is unchanged; it now logs a one-line summary (~143 chars). Replaced deprecated datetime.utcnow() ; report "Pre-season" rather than "Unknown" for season progress. Docs The README listed 11 of 23 tools and none of the five added since the last release . It now covers all 23, grouped by category, and is cross-checked against the registered tool list. Added the missing 0.1.7 CHANGELOG entry. Testing 97 tests pass (was 88). Added regression cover for the gameweek-0 case, the next-gameweek helper across pre-season/mid-season/end-of-season, and the 404-vs-500 distinction. Package builds clean and passes twine check . Follow-ups (not in this PR) Migrate to mcp 2.0 ( FastMCP → MCPServer ). Spiked against real mcp 2.0.0: it's a 2-line change and all 23 tools, 7 resources and 5 prompts register and execute. Held back because v2 implements the brand-new 2026-07-28 protocol revision and client-side negotiation needs end-to-end testing before the season starts. title: Migrate to MCP Python SDK v2 (FastMCP → MCPServer)
cleaned_text: Migrate to MCP Python SDK v2 (FastMCP → MCPServer) Background The MCP Python SDK released v2.0 , which removed mcp.server.fastmcp — the module this server is built on. Everything under mcp.server.fastmcp now lives under mcp.server.mcpserver , and the FastMCP class is renamed to MCPServer . PR #23 pinned the dependency to mcp>=1.2.0, =1.2.0 meant a fresh pip install fpl-mcp resolved to mcp 2.0 and failed to import at all. This issue tracks the actual migration. Note: this is the official SDK's v2, not gofastmcp.com's FastMCP v2/v3/v4, which is a separate independent package. Scope: smaller than it sounds I spiked this against real mcp 2.0.0. Our coupling to the SDK is one import, one constructor, one mcp.run() , and 40 decorators whose API v2 preserves. There is no Context , get_context() , low-level Server , Image / Audio , or direct wire-type usage anywhere in the codebase. The entire required diff is 2 lines in src/fpl_mcp/ main .py : -from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP +from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer -mcp = FastMCP( +mcp = MCPServer( With only that change, against mcp 2.0.0 on Python 3.14: all 23 tools, 7 resources and 5 prompts register, and get_gameweek_status , analyze_player_fixtures and search_fpl_players all execute correctly end to end. dependencies= is still accepted, and our constructor already passes name / instructions as keyword arguments, so we avoid the v2 trap where instructions passed positionally silently lands in the new title slot. Why it was not done in PR #23 The blocker is not our code, it is client negotiation. mcp v2 implements the 2026-07-28 protocol revision , released about a week before this was filed. Tools registering in-process does not prove Claude Desktop, Cursor or Windsurf will negotiate the new protocol. With the FPL season starting 2026-08-21 , bundling a protocol-layer change into an urgent install hotfix was not worth the risk. Checklist [ ] Apply the 2-line change [ ] End-to-end test in Claude Desktop , Cursor and Windsurf — the real unknown [ ] Confirm behavior on the oldest client versions we claim to support [ ] Decide: hard cut to 2.x, or a try / except ImportError shim supporting both 1.x and 2.x so users are not forced to upgrade [ ] Update pyproject.toml pin accordingly [ ] Update tests — tool.inputSchema becomes tool.input_schema (camelCase → snake_case across wire types) [ ] Check the httpx → httpx2 dependency swap against our own direct httpx usage in fpl/api.py [ ] Release as 0.2.0 Notes v2 requires Python >=3.10 , same as this project — no blocker there. v1.x is in indefinite maintenance with critical and security fixes, so there is no forced deadline. Other v2 changes we should confirm we are unaffected by: sync handlers now run on a worker thread, resource URIs are plain str rather than AnyUrl , and McpError is renamed MCPError . References Migration Guide: v1 to v2 What's new in v2 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: Add live gameweek scores, dream team, transfer history, captain advice, and price changes
cleaned_text: Add live gameweek scores, dream team, transfer history, captain advice, and price changes Summary Fourth PR in the improvement series. Stacked on #19 — only the last commit is new; rebases cleanly as earlier PRs merge. Adds six new tools built on FPL endpoints the server didn't expose, headlined by live gameweek scores — the most-requested FPL feature and previously completely uncovered. New tools Tool | Endpoint | What it does get_gameweek_live_scores | event/{gw}/live/ + event-status/ | Live player points/stats during a gameweek, sorted by points, with bonus-processing status and an optional player_ids filter. 60s cache. get_dream_team | dream-team/{gw}/ | Official highest-scoring XI with names, teams, positions, points. get_manager_transfer_history | entry/{id}/transfers/ | Any manager's transfers with player names and prices, grouped by gameweek. get_my_current_team | my-team/{id}/ | Wires up the endpoint that was implemented in auth_manager but never exposed: current squad with purchase/selling prices, chips, and transfer state. suggest_captain | (composes existing data) | Ranks a squad by a weighted blend of FPL's own expected points ( ep_next ), form, points per game, and fixture difficulty; doubtful players scaled by availability. Returns the full per-component breakdown so the reasoning is transparent. get_price_changes | (cached bootstrap) | Gameweek price risers/fallers with ownership and transfer momentum. Implementation notes Thin FPLAPI methods with @cached TTLs — they automatically inherit the shared client, timeouts, retries, and rate limiter from #17, and suggest_captain 's per-player fixture fetches use the bounded concurrency from #18. New fpl/tools/live.py and fpl/tools/advice.py follow the existing register_tools(mcp) pattern; the other tools join their natural existing modules. The registration guard test now locks all 22 tools. Tests Every new tool and API method covered with respx/AsyncMock (no live network in tests): live-score sorting and filtering, cache behavior of the live endpoint, transfer formatting/grouping, price-change direction filters, captain ranking incl. the availability penalty, and auth-missing error paths. pytest : 56 passed .

title: Extract shared helpers, split __main__.py, remove dead code, clean up packaging
cleaned_text: Extract shared helpers, split main .py, remove dead code, clean up packaging Summary Third PR in the improvement series. Stacked on #18 (which stacks on #17) — only the last commit is new here; it rebases cleanly as the earlier PRs merge. This is the deduplication/structure pass. The public MCP surface is unchanged — tool names, signatures, and response shapes are identical, and a new test locks the exact set of registered tools, prompts, and resources. Shared helpers (new fpl/utils/ modules) difficulty.py — single home for the (6 - avg) * 2 fixture score and the Excellent/Good/Average/Difficult ladder, previously copy-pasted in 4 places. gameweek.py — one get_current_gameweek_id() (current, else next − 1), previously reimplemented ~5 times. params.py — unwrap() for the dict-wrapped-parameter quirk, replacing ~75 lines of boilerplate per inline tool. main .py split (~1,400 → ~300 lines) The eight inline tools move into fpl/tools/ modules using the existing register_tools(mcp) pattern: new gameweeks.py , fixtures.py , analysis.py ; check_fpl_authentication joins team.py . main .py now only holds server setup, resources, prompts, and registration calls. Small behavior fix (flagged for review) compare_players with include_gameweeks=True used to return an empty best_performers section: the metric values had already been re-nested under {"stats_type", "values"} before the winner calculation ran, so the numeric check always failed. The calculation now unwraps the nested form. Also, blank/double gameweek data is fetched once per comparison instead of once per player. Dead code & data hygiene Deleted fpl/tools/comparisons.py (207 lines, never registered), tests/mock_mcp.py (unused), and a commented-out block in leagues.py . Nickname map moved to resources/player_nicknames.py as plain data; dropped departed players (Ronaldo, Firmino, Mané, Aubameyang, Lewandowski, Kane). Remaining hand-rolled tuple caches in team.py migrated to cache.get_or_fetch . Packaging Deleted setup.py — it disagreed with pyproject.toml on dependencies (listed cryptography>=3.4.0 , omitted requests ). Its package_data moved to [tool.setuptools.package-data] ; the built wheel verified to still ship schemas/static_schema.json . init .py now reads version from package metadata — the version lives in exactly one place ( pyproject.toml ). Tests Pure-function tests for all three utils; a registration guard asserting the exact tool/prompt/resource sets. pytest : 46 passed . Wheel build verified.

title: feat(tekton): add structured PipelineRun diagnosis
cleaned_text: feat(tekton): add structured PipelineRun diagnosis What Add a callable, read-only tekton_pipelinerun_diagnose tool with versioned structured output. Collect PipelineRun conditions, deterministically ordered failed TaskRuns and steps, failed-step log tails, and related Warning Events. Bound the TaskRun API request, failed steps, Events, and log reads while reporting truncation and partial collection errors. Verify TaskRun controller ownership before including TaskRuns or their related Event targets. Classify returned workload data as untrusted and document that it may contain sensitive or adversarial content and is not credential-redacted. Hide Tekton tools when the tekton.dev/v1 PipelineRun API is unavailable. Add five real-controller diagnosis tasks with exact tool-call assertions and prompt-injection checks. Why Current clients consume callable MCP tools rather than MCP prompt registration. A bounded diagnosis tool lets them retrieve the evidence needed to investigate failed PipelineRuns without mutation operations, direct Secret API reads, or unbounded workload logs. Kubernetes authorization remains the resource-access boundary. Testing make format make lint make test Five controller-backed failure scenarios reached Succeeded=False . Direct diagnosis calls passed for image pull, missing Secret, permission denied, OOM, and non-zero exit failures. Denied log, denied Event, denied Secret, and cross-namespace access paths were validated with a restricted identity. Evaluation status The five MCPChecker tasks and exact-selection assertions are included. The model-backed 5/5 selection evaluation requires configured evaluator authentication and can be run by a maintainer.

cleaned_text: chore: add codeowners/triage tooling This is the first step towards having more of a contributor ladder and toolset specific governance. Some key things to note: CODEOWNERS requires users to have write access to the repository. Pending approval from the containers org more broadly, we can add toolset maintainers in here and give them actual approver powers CODEOWNERS only allows one rule per path. As such, core maintainers need to be a owner of every toolset as well if they want to be able to merge PRs that may touch those toolsets (e.g. changing Toolset api). Also, this means that wherever there is overlap between two toolsets on some shared "toolset" code, both sets of approvers need a CODEOWNER rule for those files As a result of the CODEOWNERS complexity, and because we wanted to separate "pinging people for review" from who has write/merge powers, I built out some internal tooling to read out from our own json file and generate a correct CODEOWNERS file. This json file is also now the source of truth for our triage workflow

Action: The tool is called with a prompt. Result: It successfully generates an image, which is correctly displayed in the Cursor user interface. API Response: The tool's response contains only an opaque Image object and a Seed . It does not provide a URL, file path, or any other reference that can be used to access the image file. *Example API Response:* Tool: FLUX_1-schnell-infer, Result: Image Tool: FLUX_1-schnell-infer, Result: Seed: 834280363 This response creates a "dead end." The primary function of creating a persistent artifact is lost, as the generated image cannot be saved or referenced from the tool. Expected Behavior An image generation tool should always return a direct, accessible URL to the generated artifact. cleaned_text: Add policy enforcement for Firestore and Storage operations This server gives agents CRUD access to Firebase: firestore_delete_document -- permanently removes documents firestore_update_document -- modifies existing documents storage_upload -- uploads files to Firebase Storage An agent can delete Firestore documents, modify data across collections, or upload arbitrary files to Storage. Suggestion: Consider documenting support for PolicyLayer/Intercept, an open-source MCP proxy that enforces policies on tool calls before execution. Example policy: version: "1" default: allow tools: firestore_delete_document: rules: - action: require_approval storage_upload: rules: - rate_limit: 10/hour firestore_update_document: rules: - rate_limit: 30/minute One line to set up: npx -y @policylayer/intercept init

title: firestore_list_documents crashes on documents with null fields
cleaned_text: firestore_list_documents crashes on documents with null fields The firestore_list_documents tool crashes with a schema validation error when reading documents that contain null values in Firestore fields. Error Message Error: None is not one of ['NULL_VALUE'] Failed validating 'enum' in schema['properties']['documents']['items']['properties']['fields']['additionalProperties']['properties']['nullValue']: {'description': 'A null value.', 'enum': ['NULL_VALUE'], 'type': 'string', 'x-google-enum-descriptions': ['Null value.']} On instance['documents'][0]['fields']['suspendedAt']['nullValue']: None Steps to Reproduce Create a Firestore document with null fields: { "fullName": "MFarhan", "phoneNumber": "3029106430", "suspendedAt": null, "archivedAt": null, "dateOfBirth": null } Try to list documents: firestore_list_documents({ parent: "projects/studioops-app-dev/databases/(default)/documents/gyms/{gymId}", collectionId: "members", pageSize: 100 }) Tool crashes with validation error Expected Behavior Tool should handle null values gracefully and return documents with null fields. title: Feature request: Nano (XNO) as a feeless settlement option beside Lightning
cleaned_text: Feature request: Nano (XNO) as a feeless settlement option beside Lightning Idea Fewsats currently settles payments on the Lightning Network (Bitcoin). Lightning works, but every payment pays routing fees and the payer needs inbound liquidity. For the sub-cent agent-call prices Fewsats is used for, the fee floor and the setup cost are material. Nano (XNO) is a feeless, single-block-final DAG cryptocurrency that uses the same x402 (HTTP 402 Payment Required) scheme Lightning uses. For an L402 agent that already handles 402 Payment Required responses, adding a Nano compute-unit settlement path means: Zero fee per payment — the whole call price reaches the seller. Sub-second finality — one publish = one confirmation, no mempool, no reorg risk. No liquidity management — a sender just needs a Nano wallet with a balance; no inbound capacity, no channel open/close. What it looks like in practice The exact same flow as L402, just with x402nano/exact instead of the Lightning scheme: GET /api/data 402 Payment Required X-402-Scheme: x402nano/exact X-402-Accepts: nano:mainnet X-402-Offer-Amount: 0.000001 The agent pays via Nano block, retries with X-402-Payment: nano: , and gets the response. What this would mean for Fewsats The MCP server already has a pay_offer tool. A Nano settlement arm would let the SDK pay or accept offers on a rail that costs nothing to settle — useful for agents making thousands of micro-payments where Lightning routing fees would add up. There is already a working self-custodied implementation for the OpenAI Agents SDK that follows the exact scheme — openai-agents-nano-x402 (https://github.com/PANDeveloper001/openai-agents-nano-x402) — and a reference facilitator at 402nano.org. Ask Would Fewsats consider adding a Nano (XNO) settlement option — as a payment_method alongside lightning — in the MCP server or the Python SDK? Happy to open a PR for the Nano payment leg if the maintainers are interested.

title: Bug: MCP tool return type mismatch (raw tuple returned)
cleaned_text: Bug: MCP tool return type mismatch (raw tuple returned) Summary Several MCP tools in the Fewsats MCP server declare their return type as str in the tool signature and documentation, but actually return a t uple (status_code: int, payload: object) at runtime. This can mislead MCP agents that rely on the declared return type. Tools balance payment_methods pay_offer payment_info billing_info create_x402_payment_header Expected Behavior (Specification) Each tool is declared as returning a str(or dict): https://github.com/Fewsats/fewsats-mcp/blob/b0bd632807ab99adfa5517bc1febcc9ca4b2ecdb/src/fewsats_mcp/server.py#L15 Actual Behavior (Implementation) All tools return the result of handle_response, which returns a tuple : https://github.com/Fewsats/fewsats-mcp/blob/b0bd632807ab99adfa5517bc1febcc9ca4b2ecdb/src/fewsats_mcp/server.py#L9-L11 Actual return type: tuple[int, dict | str] Example: (200, {"id": 1, "balance": 4394, "currency": "usd"}) This is Return Type / Format Mismatch. Suggested Fixes 1. Balance Before https://github.com/Fewsats/fewsats-mcp/blob/b0bd632807ab99adfa5517bc1febcc9ca4b2ecdb/src/fewsats_mcp/server.py#L14-L19 After from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError @mcp.tool() async def balance() -> dict: """Retrieve the balance of the user's wallet. You will rarely need to call this unless instructed by the user, or to troubleshoot payment issues. Fewsats will automatically add balance when needed.""" status, payload = handle_response(Fewsats().balance()) if status != 200: raise ToolError(str(payload)) return payload Referenced API documentation https://fewsats.github.io/fewsats-python/core.html#fewsats.balance 2. payment_methods Before https://github.com/Fewsats/fewsats-mcp/blob/b0bd632807ab99adfa5517bc1febcc9ca4b2ecdb/src/fewsats_mcp/server.py#L21-L26 After from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError @mcp.tool() async def payment_methods() -> list[dict]: """Retrieve the user's payment methods. You will rarely need to call this unless instructed by the user, or to troubleshoot payment issues. Fewsats will automatically select the best payment method.""" status, payload = handle_response(Fewsats().payment_methods()) if status != 200: raise ToolError(str(payload)) return payload Referenced API documentation https://fewsats.github.io/fewsats-python/core.html#fewsats.payment_methods 3. pay_offer Before https://github.com/Fewsats/fewsats-mcp/blob/b0bd632807ab99adfa5517bc1febcc9ca4b2ecdb/src/fewsats_mcp/server.py#L28-L50 After from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError @mcp.tool() async def pay_offer(offer_id: str, l402_offer: dict) -> dict: """Pays an offer_id from the l402_offers. The l402_offer parameter must be a dict with this structure: { 'offers': [ { 'id': 'test_offer_2', # String identifier for the offer 'amount': 1, # Numeric cost value 'currency': 'usd', # Currency code 'description': 'Test offer', # Text description 'title': 'Test Package' # Title of the package } ], 'payment_context_token': '60a8e027-8b8b-4ccf-b2b9-380ed0930283', # Payment context token 'payment_request_url': 'https://api.fewsats.com/v0/l402/payment-request', # Payment URL 'version': '0.2.2' # API version } Returns payment status response. If payment status is needs_review inform the user he will have to approve it at app.fewsats.com""" status, payload = handle_response( Fewsats().pay_offer(offer_id, l402_offer) ) if status != 200: raise ToolError(str(payload)) return payload Referenced API documentation https://fewsats.github.io/fewsats-python/core.html#fewsats.pay_offer 4. payment_info Before https://github.com/Fewsats/fewsats-mcp/blob/b0bd632807ab99adfa5517bc1febcc9ca4b2ecdb/src/fewsats_mcp/server.py#L52-L56 After from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError @mcp.tool() async def payment_info(pid: str) -> dict: """Retrieve the details of a payment. If payment status is needs_review inform the user he will have to approve it at app.fewsats.com""" status, payload = handle_response(Fewsats().payment_info(pid)) if status != 200: raise ToolError(str(payload)) return payload Referenced API documentation https://fewsats.github.io/fewsats-python/core.html#fewsats.payment_info 5. billing_info Before https://github.com/Fewsats/fewsats-mcp/blob/b0bd632807ab99adfa5517bc1febcc9ca4b2ecdb/src/fewsats_mcp/server.py#L58-L63 After from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError @mcp.tool() async def billing_info() -> dict: """Retrieve the user's billing information. Returns billing details including name, address, and other relevant information. This information can also be used as shipping address for purchases.""" status, payload = handle_response(Fewsats().billing_info()) if status != 200: raise ToolError(str(payload)) return payload Referenced API documentation https://fewsats.github.io/fewsats-python/core.html#fewsats.billing_info 6. create_x402_payment_header Before https://github.com/Fewsats/fewsats-mcp/blob/b0bd632807ab99adfa5517bc1febcc9ca4b2ecdb/src/fewsats_mcp/server.py#L66-L97 After from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError @mcp.tool() async def create_x402_payment_header( chain: str, x402_payload: dict ) -> dict: """ Creates a payment header for the X402 protocol. The chain is base-sepolia or base The x402 payload must be a dict with this structure: { "accepts": [ { "asset": "0x036CbD53842c5426634e7929541eC2318f3dCF7e", "description": "Payment for GET https://proxy402.com/7Yhuf2O3zs", "extra": { "name": "USDC", "version": "2" }, "maxAmountRequired": "10", "maxTimeoutSeconds": 300, "mimeType": "", "network": "base-sepolia", "payTo": "0xbA5Ae80f48E0C74878c1a362D69c27c2135Aa594", "resource": "https://proxy402.com/7Yhuf2O3zs", "scheme": "exact" } ], "error": "X-PAYMENT header is required", "x402Version": 1 } Returns a dict with the payment_header field that must be set in X-PAYMENT header in a x402 http request. """ status, payload = handle_response( Fewsats().pay_x402_offer(x402_payload, chain) ) if status != 200: raise ToolError(str(payload)) return payload Referenced API documentation https://fewsats.github.io/fewsats-python/core.html#fewsats.pay_x402_offer

title: Security Vulnerability: Bypass of Command Restriction in execute_command Tool
cleaned_text: Security Vulnerability: Bypass of Command Restriction in execute_command Tool Describe the vulnerability A significant security bypass vulnerability exists in the execute_command tool of the terminal-controller-mcp server (version 0.1.7), allowing attackers to execute restricted commands through crafted input that evades the existing keyword-based filtering mechanism. The vulnerability arises from the inadequate command validation approach: The current security check in terminal_controller.py lines 115-118 uses a simple keyword matching system: dangerous_commands = ["rm -rf /", "mkfs"] if any(dc in command.lower() for dc in dangerous_commands): return "For security reasons, this command is not allowed." This implementation only blocks exact or contiguous occurrences of the prohibited keywords. The fundamental flaw is that attackers can split restricted commands into fragments using shell features like command concatenation and execution substitution ( $() ), then reassemble them dynamically. For example: The restricted "mkfs" command can be bypassed with: echo "$($(echo -n m; echo -n k; echo -n f; echo -n s))" This approach avoids using the prohibited keyword in a contiguous string, thus evading detection. The validation occurs in the execute_command function (terminal_controller.py line 103) which accepts a full command string, processes it through the insufficient filter, and then presumably executes it in a shell context that allows such dynamic command construction. This creates a critical security gap where the intended protection against dangerous commands can be easily circumvented through basic shell scripting techniques. To Reproduce Send the following request to a vulnerable terminal-controller-mcp server: { "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "execute_command", "arguments": { "command": "echo \"$($(echo -n m; echo -n k; echo -n f; echo -n s))\"", "timeout": 30 }, "_meta": { "progressToken": 23 } } } Observe that: The command successfully bypasses the keyword filter The prohibited command ("mkfs" in this example) executes despite not appearing as a contiguous string in the input This demonstrates how any restricted command can be similarly constructed and executed Expected behavior The application should implement a more robust command validation system that: Recognizes and blocks attempts to dynamically construct prohibited commands Considers the actual command that will be executed after shell parsing, not just the literal input string Uses a whitelist of allowed commands rather than a blacklist of prohibited ones Avoids executing arbitrary command strings in a shell context when possible Affected versions Version 0.1.7

Prefer \JWTVerifier\, fall back to \BearerAuthProvider\. Both take the same \jwks_uri\/\issuer\/\udience\/\ equired_scopes\ keywords, so the call site is unchanged and old installs keep working. title: `--use-tls` incorrectly applied to both AMQP and Management API connections?
cleaned_text: --use-tls incorrectly applied to both AMQP and Management API connections? Thanks for a very useful package - I found a subtle edge-case bug around HTTP/HTTPS configuration of admin console vs AMQP - see below. Summary The --use-tls flag is incorrectly applied to both AMQP and Management API connections, making it impossible to use configurations where AMQP uses SSL but the Management API uses HTTP (a common Docker setup pattern). Environment mcp-server-rabbitmq version : 2.2.0 Python version : 3.11 Setup : Docker RabbitMQ with mixed SSL/HTTP configuration OS : Linux (WSL2) Expected Behavior The --use-tls flag should only affect AMQP connections (via --port ), while Management API connections (via --api-port ) should have independent protocol detection or a separate configuration flag. Actual Behavior When --use-tls true is set (required for SSL AMQP connections), the Management API connection also tries to use HTTPS instead of HTTP, causing SSL connection errors: Failed to list exchanges: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='localhost', port=15682): Max retries exceeded with url: /api/exchanges (Caused by SSLError(SSLError(1, '[SSL: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER] wrong version number (_ssl.c:992)'))) Reproduction Steps Docker RabbitMQ Setup Our RabbitMQ Docker configuration maps internal SSL/HTTP services to external ports: AMQP SSL : Internal 5671 → External 5681 (SSL/TLS) Management API HTTP : Internal 15672 → External 15682 (HTTP, not HTTPS) Web STOMP SSL : Internal 15673 → External 15683 (SSL/TLS) Configuration That Fails mcp-server-rabbitmq --rabbitmq-host localhost --port 5681 --api-port 15682 --username USER--password PASSWORD --use-tls true Result: ✅ AMQP connection on port 5681 works correctly with SSL ❌ Management API connection on port 15682 fails with SSL error (tries HTTPS on HTTP port) Manual Verification Direct API access works perfectly: $ curl -u USER:PASSWORD http://localhost:15682/api/exchanges [{"name":"","type":"direct",...}] # Returns data successfully Root Cause Analysis In mcp_server_rabbitmq/admin.py , line 12: def init (self, host: str, port: int, username: str, password: str, use_tls: bool): self.protocol = "https" if use_tls else "http" # ← Problem here self.base_url = f"{self.protocol}://{host}:{port}/api" The issue is that use_tls is designed for AMQP connections but is incorrectly used to determine the Management API protocol. These should be independent: AMQP Connection ( RabbitMQConnection ): Correctly uses use_tls for SSL/TLS Management API ( RabbitMQAdmin ): Incorrectly uses same use_tls flag for HTTP/HTTPS Use Case / Why This Matters This is a common Docker deployment pattern where: AMQP uses SSL for secure message passing Management API uses HTTP for admin operations (often behind reverse proxy/firewall) Different security models for different protocols Many production Docker setups separate these concerns for security and operational reasons. Suggested Solutions Option 1: Add separate flag parser.add_argument("--api-use-tls", type=bool, default=None, help="Use TLS/SSL for management API (auto-detect if not specified)") Option 2: Auto-detection Try HTTPS first, fall back to HTTP: def init (self, host: str, port: int, username: str, password: str, use_tls: bool): # Try to auto-detect protocol for management API for protocol in ["https", "http"]: try: test_url = f"{protocol}://{host}:{port}/api/overview" response = requests.get(test_url, auth=(username, password), timeout=5) if response.status_code in [200, 401]: # 401 = auth required but protocol works self.protocol = protocol break except: continue else: # Fallback to original behavior self.protocol = "https" if use_tls else "http" Option 3: Separate the concerns Split the use_tls parameter into separate flags at the argument level: --amqp-use-tls for AMQP connections --api-use-tls for Management API connections Current Workaround We've created a wrapper script that monkey-patches the RabbitMQAdmin class: File: scripts/mcp_rabbitmq_wrapper.py #!/usr/bin/env python3 """ Wrapper script for mcp-server-rabbitmq that forces HTTP for management API while allowing SSL for AMQP connections. This works around the issue where Docker maps SSL AMQP to external non-SSL but the management API is also non-SSL. """ import sys import os Add the mcp-server-rabbitmq package to the path sys.path.insert(0, '/home/foo/bar/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages') Monkey patch the RabbitMQAdmin class to always use HTTP for management API from mcp_server_rabbitmq import admin original_init = admin.RabbitMQAdmin. init def patched_init(self, host: str, port: int, username: str, password: str, use_tls: bool): # Force HTTP for management API regardless of use_tls setting self.protocol = "http" # Always HTTP for management API self.base_url = f"{self.protocol}://{host}:{port}/api" import base64 self.auth = base64.b64encode(f"{username}:{password}".encode()).decode() self.headers = {"Authorization": f"Basic {self.auth}", "Content-Type": "application/json"} Apply the patch admin.RabbitMQAdmin. init = patched_init Now import and run the main server from mcp_server_rabbitmq.server import main if name == " main ": main() Usage: Instead of using mcp-server-rabbitmq directly: python scripts/mcp_rabbitmq_wrapper.py --rabbitmq-host localhost --port 5681 --api-port 15682 --username USER --password PASSWORD --use-tls True This successfully works around the issue by: Allowing --use-tls True for proper AMQP SSL connections Forcing HTTP protocol for Management API calls regardless of the TLS flag Preserving all original functionality Impact This bug prevents the MCP server from working with common Docker RabbitMQ configurations that use mixed SSL/HTTP protocols. The workaround demonstrates that both protocols can work simultaneously when configured correctly. Additional Context Related to issue #X where user had single HTTPS port, but this is different (mixed protocols) The RabbitMQConnection class correctly handles AMQP SSL via use_tls Only the RabbitMQAdmin class has the protocol coupling issue Docker RabbitMQ configurations commonly use this pattern for security/operational separation Files Affected mcp_server_rabbitmq/admin.py (main issue) mcp_server_rabbitmq/server.py (argument parsing could be enhanced)

title: Unauthenticated DoS via unhandled panic in search_files (malformed glob pattern)
cleaned_text: Unauthenticated DoS via unhandled panic in search_files (malformed glob pattern) Summary The search_files tool passes the user-supplied pattern argument directly to glob.MustCompile() (gobwas/glob v0.2.3) with no validation. A malformed glob pattern (e.g. an unclosed character class like [ ) causes an unrecovered panic that crashes the entire server process. No recovery middleware is registered anywhere in the stack ( main.go , or mcp-go 's ServeStdio / Listen / processInputStream chain), so the panic propagates all the way up and terminates the process — ending the session for every connected client from a single tool call. Affected file/line filesystemserver/handler/search_files.go:140 Steps to reproduce Build: go build -o mcp-filesystem-server . Create a scratch directory with one file in it, pass it as the sole allowed directory Send this sequence over stdio: initialize notifications/initialized tools/call → search_files with {"path": " ", "pattern": "["} tools/call → list_allowed_directories (canary, to prove the process is dead) Exact requests used (attached as mcp_requests.jsonl ): \ \ \ json {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"audit-client","version":"0.1"}}} {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"} {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"search_files","arguments":{"path":"./poc_scratch","pattern":"["}}} {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"list_allowed_directories","arguments":{}}} \ \ \ Result Exit code: 2 (unrecovered Go panic) poc_stdout.log contains only the initialize response — no response was ever sent for id 2 or id 3 poc_stderr.log contains the full panic and stack trace: \ \ \ panic: unexpected end of input goroutine 1 [running]: github.com/gobwas/glob.MustCompile(...) glob@v0.2.3/glob.go:57 github.com/mark3labs/mcp-filesystem-server/filesystemserver/handler.searchFiles(...) filesystemserver/handler/search_files.go:140 +0xf2 github.com/mark3labs/mcp-filesystem-server/filesystemserver/handler.(*FilesystemHandler).HandleSearchFiles(...) filesystemserver/handler/search_files.go:84 +0x59c github.com/mark3labs/mcp-go/server.(*MCPServer).handleToolCall(...) mcp-go@v0.32.0/server/server.go:1028 +0x3f0 github.com/mark3labs/mcp-go/server.(*MCPServer).HandleMessage(...) mcp-go@v0.32.0/server/request_handler.go:305 +0xc5f \ \ \ (full trace attached in poc_stderr.log ) Impact Complete, trivially reproducible denial of service. Any MCP client — including an LLM agent that forwards untrusted external text into the pattern parameter — can kill the server with one malformed input. No authentication beyond ordinary tool-call access, no filesystem write access, no user interaction required. Suggested fix Replace glob.MustCompile(pattern) with glob.Compile(pattern) at line 140 and return the compile error as a normal IsError: true tool result — this exact pattern is already used elsewhere in this codebase for regexp.Compile errors in modify_file.go . As defense-in-depth, wiring server.WithRecovery() into NewFilesystemServer would prevent any other unhandled panic in a handler from taking down the whole process. CVSS v3.1 estimate AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H ≈ 5.5 (Medium) Happy to provide any further detail or help verify a fix. Evidence files poc_exitcode.txt.txt poc_stderr.log.log poc_stdout.log.log
