title: fix(dashboard): start auto-refresh interval on load
cleaned_text: fix(dashboard): start auto-refresh interval on load The dashboard's Auto checkbox renders checked by default, but scheduleAuto() is only wired to the checkbox and interval-slider onchange handlers — it is never invoked at startup. As a result the refresh interval never starts: fetchAll() runs exactly once per page load, and the dashboard silently stops tracking editor state (play mode, hierarchy, console) until the user toggles the checkbox or presses Refresh manually. One-line fix: call scheduleAuto() once after wiring the handlers, so the interval honors the initial checkbox state. Verified by watching the dashboard poll on its 3s cadence after load and follow play/stop and hierarchy changes without manual refreshes. npm test : 123/123 pass. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: Server ignores UNITY_PORT and resolves McpUnitySettings.json from cwd, so the documented config always falls back to 8090
cleaned_text: Server ignores UNITY_PORT and resolves McpUnitySettings.json from cwd, so the documented config always falls back to 8090 UNITY_PORT is documented but never read The README states that Unity sets a UNITY_PORT environment variable when the port is changed. A code search over the repository finds UNITY_PORT only in README.md , README-ja.md , README_zh-CN.md and Server~/smithery.yaml and never under Server~/src . McpUnity.parseAndSetConfig reads the port from the settings file only: const configPort = config.Port; this.port = configPort ? parseInt(configPort, 10) : 8090; // Check environment variable first, then config file, then default to localhost const configHost = process.env.UNITY_HOST || config.Host; UNITY_HOST *is* honoured, which makes the asymmetry look unintentional. The settings file is resolved from cwd const MCP_UNITY_SETTINGS_PATH = path.resolve(process.cwd(), './ProjectSettings/McpUnitySettings.json'); The README's own client config sets no working directory, so process.cwd() is whatever the MCP client happens to use, rarely the Unity project root. The file is then not found, and the port silently falls back to 8090. Nothing surfaces the mismatch: the log line reads Using port: 8090 as if that were the configured value. Anyone running a project on a non-default port is therefore connecting to the wrong port (or to another project's Editor) while the configuration looks correct. It is also a silent breaking change At bdee0cb5accd the same constant was: const MCP_UNITY_SETTINGS_PATH = path.resolve(process.cwd(), '../ProjectSettings/McpUnitySettings.json'); Configurations whose cwd was the Unity project's Assets folder (for which the old relative path was exactly right) break on update with no error message. Suggestions Honour UNITY_PORT as documented, mirroring UNITY_HOST . That alone makes the port independent of cwd. And/or resolve the settings file by walking up from the server's own location ( import.meta.url ) rather than from cwd. In all cases, log a warning when the settings file cannot be read, instead of defaulting silently.

title: Batch mode guard also disables the bridge for headless Editors used as a persistent MCP host
cleaned_text: Batch mode guard also disables the bridge for headless Editors used as a persistent MCP host Since #107 (cbd505a, "Skip initialization in batch mode to prevent Unity Cloud Build hang"), an Editor started with -batchmode never creates its WebSocket server, so the MCP bridge is unreachable. That is correct for CI, but batch mode is not only CI. my setup I run several Unity Editors permanently headless (one per git worktree, each on its own port) as MCP hosts for coding agents: Unity -batchmode -nographics -projectPath -logFile -batchmode is the point: a full Editor per worktree costs several GB of RAM and constant CPU, which is exactly what we I am avoiding. These are long-lived services, not builds. This worked until the package auto-updated past cbd505a; now nothing listens on the configured port and the Unity log contains no MCP line at all. Why it is total McpUnityServer.Instance returns null in batch mode, and every entry point goes through it, so no WebSocketServer is ever constructed: public static McpUnityServer Instance { get { // Don't create instance in batch mode to avoid hanging builds if (Application.isBatchMode) { return null; } ... Same guard in [DidReloadScripts] AfterReload() , OnEditorQuitting , OnBeforeAssemblyReload , OnAfterAssemblyReload and OnPlayModeStateChanged . There is no setting to opt back in. Suggestion The hang #107 fixed came from InstallServer() running npm synchronously during [InitializeOnLoad] not from the WebSocket server itself. Those two are separable: Narrow fix: keep skipping the npm install/build in batch mode (that is what hangs a machine without npm), but still start the WebSocket server when AutoStartServer is true. A CI job that never connects is unaffected — it just has an idle socket. Explicit fix: add an AllowBatchMode setting to McpUnitySettings , default false so today's behaviour is preserved and CI users notice nothing. Either way the distinction worth encoding is "headless build" vs "headless service" Application.isBatchMode alone cannot tell them apart, and it currently assumes the first. Environment Unity 6000.3.9f1, macOS 26.3 (arm64) Broken at bbfb1c068151 , working at bdee0cb5accdd3c4fd125c4b2dbe08f4963efd44 Workaround: pin the package in Packages/manifest.json : "com.gamelovers.mcp-unity": "https://github.com/CoderGamester/mcp-unity.git#bdee0cb5accdd3c4fd125c4b2dbe08f4963efd44"

title: stripe-agent-toolkit v0.7.x silently ignores the removed `configuration.actions` policy, fail-opening the toolset handed to LangChain and CrewAI agents
cleaned_text: stripe-agent-toolkit v0.7.x silently ignores the removed configuration.actions policy, fail-opening the toolset handed to LangChain and CrewAI agents Affected repo: stripe/ai, tools/python (shipped as stripe-agent-toolkit 0.7.0+) Pinned commit: 3ca4090c2aef3fc1fd21754c5ef82efe0d56149e (main, 2026-08-28) Compared release: stripe-agent-toolkit 0.6.1 (PyPI sdist) PUBLIC-READY R05P2-M1 (policy-dialect fail-open), instance R06P2-F1 Honesty ledger: EXECUTED (PoC at pin, offline stub MCP), PROVED (code diff 0.6.1 vs pin), DERIVED (LangChain docs drift observed 2026-08-27) Summary The v0.6.x Python toolkit filtered its tool list through is_tool_allowed(tool, configuration) using the configuration["actions"] dialect (deny by default: a tool is exposed only if every action it declares is explicitly enabled). The v0.7.x MCP rewrite removed that filter entirely. Configuration is now a TypedDict(total=False) with only a context key, and nothing validates, warns about, or rejects unknown keys. As a result, code written for 0.6.x that passes a least-privilege actions policy, plus any code copied from the live LangChain integration docs (which still show configuration={"actions": {"payment_links": {"create": True}}} at the time of writing), silently hands the agent every tool the Stripe API key permits, including create_invoice , send_invoice , create_refund , and create_payment_intent . The only remaining bounds on the agent's payment calls are the key's server-side permissions and a non-fatal recommendation to use restricted keys. There is no amount bound, no payee allowlist, and no human gate anywhere in the package (zero occurrences of an approval mechanism in the Python source at the pin). Steps to reproduce (offline, dummy key) PoC: poc/f1_stripe_actions_dropped.py in the R06P2 workspace. It stubs StripeMcpClient._do_connect and call_tool with a rule-based fake that returns a fixed ten-tool list (the snake_case names documented in MIGRATION.md), so no network or real key is used. Construct the pinned toolkit with the exact 0.6.x dialect config: {"actions": {"payment_links": {"create": True}}} Call get_tools() . Invoke the create_refund tool with an agent-chosen amount. Observed (deterministic across two runs, poc/out/f1_run1.txt equals f1_run2.txt ): tools handed to the agent (10): create_customer, list_customers, create_product, create_price, create_payment_link, create_invoice, send_invoice, create_refund, create_payment_intent, list_balance warnings mentioning the removed actions key: NONE direct create_refund call with amount: 999999 reached the MCP layer and returned {"id": "fake_create_refund", "status": "succeeded"} reference: under 0.6.1 is_tool_allowed semantics the same config exposes exactly one tool, create_payment_link Impact A developer who upgrades from 0.6.x (or copies the current LangChain docs example) keeps a config they read as "payment link creation only", while the upgraded toolkit exposes all write and refund paths the API key allows to the LLM agent. Because the config dict is accepted without error or warning, the regression is invisible until an agent misuses a tool. This is a fail-open policy dialect transition: the policy layer did not tighten or error, it vanished. Suggested fix Any of the following, in rough order of value: Validate configuration in ToolkitCore. init : reject or at least DeprecationWarning on unknown top-level keys, with a dedicated message when actions is present ("tool permissions moved to your Restricted API Key; this key is ignored"). Emit the same warning from create_stripe_agent_toolkit when actions is present. Offer an in-toolkit allowlist or denylist of MCP tool names so framework users can bound the toolset client-side again, and document it as the replacement for actions . Coordinate with LangChain to update the integration docs page for StripeAgentToolkit to the v0.7.x API. Notes Side observation at the pin: the sync path StripeTool._run calls asyncio.get_event_loop() when no loop is running, which raises RuntimeError on Python 3.12; the async path works. Worth a separate bug report. MIGRATION.md does document the actions removal for users who read it; the security issue is that the package accepts the old dialect silently and a major docs surface still teaches it.

title: Refactored plugin hook implementation to not be provider-specific
cleaned_text: Refactored plugin hook implementation to not be provider-specific NOTE: the files in claude/plugin/scripts and shared-provider-scripts/provider-hooks are exactly the same. To make it easier to review, I would recommend reviewing the files in claude/plugin/scripts since it will actually show the diff with the original hook implementations Summary Moved the files in claude/plugin/scripts into new folder shared-provider-scripts/provider-hooks to make copying over files used by different providers easier Wrote a script copy-hooks-scripts that copies hooks and relevant dependencies from shared-provider-scripts/provider-hooks into a provider's scripts folder. Only copies over the hooks the provider supports (for now, only claude has hook implemented so it just copies everything over into Claude). Refactored the hook script implementation to not be dependent on a particular provider's hook structure. Instead, the flow is now: When a hook event gets received, it gets passed into that specific provider's adapter which normalizes the event's field into an object that gets passed into a hook handler (one handler per event type) The handler takes the event object and returns an EventOutput which states an output type (e.g. adding context) as well any additional fields that will be needed for the hook's JSON output This gets passed back in the adapter, which serializes the EventOutput back into a format that the provider would expect for that particular hook. The idea is that if you were to add hooks to a new provider, for pre-existing hooks you ust need to add a new adapter for that provider which would normalize/denormalize event information. Motivation DEVAI-1253 We want to add hooks to Cursor similar to the ones we have in Claude. Since a lot of the underlying logic for these hooks will be similar, the refactor was done to hopefully make it easier to add hooks to new providers without having to copy over too much similar logic. Testing cd tests/providers/provider-hooks && node --test *.test.mjs Next Steps Add hooks to cursor, starting with PostToolUse , PostToolUseFailure , and SessionStart since the use case maps directly to the claude hooks we already have Add a workflow to automatically sync the provider scripts to the ones defined in shared-provider-scripts

title: Agent-level retry creates duplicate charges — no idempotency guard above the tool layer
cleaned_text: Agent-level retry creates duplicate charges — no idempotency guard above the tool layer Describe the bug The SDK correctly generates idempotency keys for network-level retries within a session. The gap is at the agent level: when an agent framework retries a tool call as a new invocation (after a timeout, crash, or model loop), a new session starts with a new auto-generated key. The result is a second charge. This is distinct from the SDK's retry handling — it's an orchestration-layer problem. The fix belongs above the tool, not inside it: generate a stable request_id from the tool call arguments before execution, claim it in durable storage, and return the cached receipt on any retry with the same ID. I built a small Python guard that does exactly this: SafeAgent. Happy to show how it wraps the Stripe toolkit tools if useful, or contribute a reference implementation. To Reproduce Build a LangChain or CrewAI agent using the Stripe toolkit Call create_payment_intent or create_charge as a tool Simulate a timeout before the agent receives confirmation Agent retries the tool call as a new invocation Two charges are created Expected behavior A retry of the same logical tool call with the same arguments should return the original receipt without executing a second charge. Code snippets OS Linux Language version Python 3.10+ Library version Latest API version Current Additional context This is an orchestration-layer problem, not an SDK bug. The fix belongs above the tool: generate a stable request_id from tool call arguments before execution, claim it in durable storage, return cached receipt on retry. Built a reference implementation: https://github.com/azender1/SafeAgent

Extended defaults : ACCESS_TOKEN_LIFETIME=7d, REFRESH_TOKEN_LIFETIME=30d. title: mcp‑server‑llamacloud 0.1.1 prints non‑JSON logs to stdout → Claude Desktop “Unexpected token … is not valid JSON”
cleaned_text: mcp‑server‑llamacloud 0.1.1 prints non‑JSON logs to stdout → Claude Desktop “Unexpected token … is not valid JSON” When starting @llamaindex/mcp-server-llamacloud@0.1.1, the server writes two plain‑text lines (“Created …”, “Starting MCP …”) to stdout before the first JSON‑RPC message. Claude Desktop expects a pure JSON stream and immediately throws Unexpected token parse errors, then disconnects. Versions mcp‑server‑llamacloud: 0.1.1 (latest on npm) Node.js: v18.19.1 OS: macOS 14.4 (Apple Silicon) Claude Desktop: 1.0.9 Steps to reproduce Run the server exactly as Claude Desktop does: LLAMA_CLOUD_PROJECT_NAME=Default \ LLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY=llx- *redacted * \ npx -y @llamaindex/mcp-server-llamacloud@0.1.1 \ --index Castoretpollux-talents-a --description "premiere base de CV" \ --index Castoretpollux-talents-b --description "Deuxieme base de CV" Observe the first two lines printed to stdout: Created index tool for tool-a Starting MCP server… Claude Desktop immediately shows Unexpected token 'C', "Created in"... is not valid JSON and the connection drops Actual behaviour Two non‑JSON log lines are emitted on stdout. Claude fails to parse them, raises an error, and disconnects. Expected behaviour All log lines should go to stderr. stdout should contain only valid JSON‑RPC objects so that Claude (or any MCP client) can parse the stream. Minimal log (stdout) Created index tool for Castoretpollux-talents-a Starting MCP server… {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"mcp-bootstrap","params":{ … } } Environment node -v # v18.19.1 npm view @llamaindex/mcp-server-llamacloud version # 0.1.1 uname -a # Darwin arm64 23.4.0 Suggested fix Move the two informational console.log statements to process.stderr (or remove them) so that stdout remains a valid JSON‑RPC channel. Happy to open a PR if that helps.

title: chore(deps): bump Quarkus to 3.35.0.CR1 and MCP server to 1.11.1
cleaned_text: chore(deps): bump Quarkus to 3.35.0.CR1 and MCP server to 1.11.1 Summary Supersedes closes #90. Fixes #91 Bumps quarkus.platform.version from 3.20.1 → 3.35.0.CR1 and mcp.server.version from 1.2.0 → 1.11.1 . Fixes #91 (Kubernetes native MCP breaks on newer Quarkus) by picking up quarkusio/quarkus#53425, which moves the kubernetes-client configuration back to ConfigPhase.RUN_TIME . On 3.27.x – 3.34.x the class was @ConfigRoot(phase = BUILD_AND_RUN_TIME_FIXED) , meaning quarkus.kubernetes-client.api-server-url , namespace , trust-certs etc. were baked into the native image and the test harness's -D... CLI overrides silently hit the real kubeconfig cluster. 3.35.x is the first release line that ships the fix. Additional changes required to build on 3.35 shared/pom.xml : import the Quarkus BOM so the module compiles against the declared Quarkus version instead of the 3.20.1 inherited transitively via quarkus-mcp-server-stdio . Without this, javac emitted an invokestatic call to the (pre-3.26) static LaunchMode.isDev() , which then failed native-image linking with Discovered unresolved method during parsing: io.quarkus.runtime.LaunchMode.isDev() . (The source was already updated in #78 to use LaunchMode.current().isDev() , it just needed to be compiled against matching Quarkus classfiles.) kubernetes/.../KubernetesResourceEncoder.java : switch javax.annotation.Priority → jakarta.annotation.Priority ; the old artifact is no longer on the classpath. jvminsight/.../MCPServerJvmInsight.java : replace @ToolArg with @PromptArg on @Prompt parameters (from #90).

title: Private-Network SSRF via read_webpage in adenot/mcp-google-search
cleaned_text: Private-Network SSRF via read_webpage in adenot/mcp-google-search Summary The read_webpage MCP tool accepts a caller-controlled url and passes it directly to axios.get . The current validation only checks that url is a string, so a tool caller can make the MCP server request loopback, private-network, or other internal URLs from the server's network position. This is a private-network SSRF risk when the MCP server runs in an environment that can reach internal services unavailable to the client. Affected Version @adenot/mcp-google-search 0.3.1 Affected Component src/index.ts MCP tool: read_webpage Parameter: url Technical Details The handler extracts the URL from tool arguments: const { url } = request.params.arguments; It then uses that value as the outbound request destination: const response = await axios.get(url, { proxy: proxyConfig, }); I did not find allowlist validation, private-address filtering, DNS/IP checks, or redirect destination checks before this request is made. Impact An MCP client that can call read_webpage can cause the server to send HTTP requests to attacker-chosen destinations reachable from the server. If the server can reach internal services, localhost-only APIs, or metadata endpoints, their HTTP responses may be returned through the tool output. Reproduction Summary I reproduced this locally with a loopback listener: Start a local HTTP listener on 127.0.0.1: . Invoke the same axios.get(url) path used by read_webpage with the loopback URL. Observe that the listener receives the server-side request and the response content is returned. Observed result: requestReceived : true received.host : 127.0.0.1: result.status : 200 disclosureSucceeded : true returned text contained MCP_GOOGLE_SEARCH_SSRF_POC Scope note: I understand that read_webpage is designed to fetch web pages. The issue is specifically that internal/private destinations are not blocked. Suggested Fix Block loopback, private, link-local, multicast, and other non-public IP ranges. Resolve hostnames and validate all resolved IPs before connecting. Revalidate redirect targets. Consider a domain allowlist or deployment-level policy for permitted outbound destinations.

title: feat: support unix: (Unix domain socket) transport for SearXNG instance URLs
cleaned_text: feat: support unix: (Unix domain socket) transport for SearXNG instance URLs Summary This PR adds native support for unix: instance URLs, so mcp-searxng can talk to a SearXNG instance that is exposed over a Unix domain socket (for example a Granian listener on /run/searxng/searxng.sock ) with no TCP port in between. Today the instance URL validator only accepts http: / https: , so packaging SearXNG behind a Unix socket required hand-patching the package. With this change, SEARXNG_URL=unix:///run/searxng/searxng.sock works out of the box. Included src/searxng-instances.ts : extended the protocol allow-list in validateSearxngInstanceUrl and redactSearxngInstanceUrl to include unix: . src/proxy.ts : imported getSearxngInstances ; replaced the pass-through fetchSearxng with a version that detects unix: request URLs, resolves the configured socket path, creates a cached undici Agent pinned to that socket, rewrites the URL to an http:// placeholder so undici accepts it, and passes the socket agent as dispatcher . Non-unix requests are unchanged. Intentionally out of scope No changes to packaging/build tooling or metadata (version, README, CONFIGURATION.md). No new tests were added; the existing live SearXNG test suite requires a configured endpoint and was not exercised locally. Testing npm run build (TypeScript compile + executable bit) succeeds on Node via the patched tree. npm run lint and npm test were not run locally; recommend the maintainer runs them, especially the proxy/search suites, plus an end-to-end search against a Unix-socket SearXNG instance. title: feat: bound stateful HTTP request concurrency
cleaned_text: feat: bound stateful HTTP request concurrency Add strict per-session and process-wide admission limits for retained stateful HTTP POSTs and standalone GET streams. Saturated requests receive the existing retryable 503 without refreshing activity or terminating the session. Initialization shares the POST pool with bounded headroom for established sessions; DELETE remains available. Accepted work holds capacity until completion, disconnect, failure or session termination, with idempotent cleanup. Defaults are 16 POSTs and 4 GET streams per session, and 256 of each per process. The configuration guide documents tuning and the one-slot initialization policy. Validation: HTTP integration tests, lint, build, full coverage and configured live E2E pass, including real slow SDK work, streaming lifetime, initialization headroom and duplicate terminal signals.

title: Fix render_map dropping layers whose CRS differs from the canvas
cleaned_text: Fix render_map dropping layers whose CRS differs from the canvas Fixes #38. Problem render_map builds its QgsMapSettings without ever calling setDestinationCrs() , so destinationCrs() is invalid and the render performs no reprojection. Layers already in the canvas CRS come out fine; layers in any other CRS are drawn at raw coordinates, land outside the metre-based extent, and vanish from the image with no error or warning. There is a second, independent problem in the same function: layers = list(QgsProject.instance().mapLayers().values()) mapLayers() returns a dict, so the draw order is arbitrary and unrelated to the layer tree. An opaque layer can be handed to setLayers() first and cover everything beneath it. Both bugs bite at once in a multi-CRS project. In mine (EPSG:5186 DEM + EPSG:4326 OSM vectors + an XYZ basemap), render_map returned a flat blue rectangle: the XYZ basemap happened to sort first and was drawn on top, and because the 5186 extent numbers were consumed as if they were 3857 metres, the tiles fetched were open ocean in the Gulf of Guinea. Fix Take the CRS, the transform context, and the layer list from the map canvas — which is what "render the current map view" already means: canvas = self.iface.mapCanvas() ms.setDestinationCrs(canvas.mapSettings().destinationCrs()) ms.setTransformContext(QgsProject.instance().transformContext()) layers = canvas.layers() if not layers: layers = list(QgsProject.instance().mapLayers().values()) ms.setLayers(layers) canvas.layers() returns the visible layers in draw order, so the output now matches what the user sees on screen. The project-layers path is kept only for the case where the canvas reports no layers. The transform context matters on its own: with a destination CRS but no context, QGIS picks a default datum transform, which can shift features by metres between datums. Verification QGIS 3.44.13, project with EPSG:5186 canvas, a 5m DEM in EPSG:5186, and two OSM vector layers in EPSG:4326. Before: rendered PNG contained only one layer; both EPSG:4326 layers were silently absent. After: all layers render, correctly reprojected and in canvas draw order, labels included. I checked the discriminator named in #38 directly — canvas.mapSettings().destinationCrs().authid() is EPSG:5186 while the two missing layers report EPSG:4326 — and they render after the change. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: render_map omits layers whose CRS differs from the canvas (missing setDestinationCrs)
cleaned_text: render_map omits layers whose CRS differs from the canvas (missing setDestinationCrs) Summary render_map builds its QgsMapSettings with setLayers() and setExtent() (using the canvas extent, which is in the project/canvas CRS) but never calls setDestinationCrs() . With no destination CRS, the render performs no reprojection . As a result: Layers already in the canvas CRS render correctly (e.g. an XYZ/web basemap in EPSG:3857). Layers in a different CRS (e.g. a vector in EPSG:4326) are drawn at their raw coordinates, fall outside the metre-based extent, and are silently missing from the output image — no error, no warning. get_canvas_screenshot is unaffected because it grabs the live canvas widget, which has a proper coordinate transform. This mismatch (screenshot looks right, render_map is missing layers) makes the bug surprisingly hard to diagnose. Environment QGIS 4.0.2 (also applies to 3.x — the code path is version-independent) qgis_mcp plugin, render_map command handler Steps to reproduce New project; set project CRS to EPSG:3857 . Add an XYZ basemap (e.g. OpenStreetMap https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png ). Add a vector layer in EPSG:4326 (any GeoJSON of points). Zoom to the vector layer. Call render_map . Expected: the rendered PNG shows the basemap *and* the vector features. Actual: the PNG shows only the basemap; the EPSG:4326 vector is absent. Confirmation: reprojecting the vector to EPSG:3857 (so its CRS matches the canvas) makes it appear in render_map . So the discriminator is exactly *layer CRS == canvas CRS*. Root cause In the render_map handler the map settings are built without a destination CRS: ms = QgsMapSettings() ms.setLayers(layers) rect = self.iface.mapCanvas().extent() ms.setExtent(rect) # extent is in the canvas/project CRS ms.setOutputSize(QSize(width, height)) no ms.setDestinationCrs(...) -> destinationCrs() is invalid/empty -> no reprojection I verified the empty destination CRS directly: building the settings exactly as above yields ms.destinationCrs().authid() == '' (invalid) , while adding the line below yields 'EPSG:3857' , and the previously-missing layer then renders. Proposed fix Set the destination CRS to the canvas CRS (and pass the project transform context for correct datum transforms) right after setting the extent: ms.setExtent(rect) ms.setDestinationCrs(self.iface.mapCanvas().mapSettings().destinationCrs()) ms.setTransformContext(QgsProject.instance().transformContext()) This is a 2-line change with no API additions; it makes render_map reproject layers the same way the live canvas does. Notes Forks that rewrote this handler reproduce the same omission — e.g. render_map_base64 in nkarasiak/qgis-mcp has no setDestinationCrs either, so the same patch applies there. A related symptom: with the project in EPSG:4326 and an XYZ basemap, render_map returns a blank image (basemap absent) for the same reason; the fix resolves that too. *Reported with a verified local fix; happy to open a PR.*

ZIP folder structure on macOS When I zipped the plugin using Finder (right-click → compress), QGIS gave the error: “This is not a valid QGIS plugin – no root folder found.” Turns out QGIS expects the ZIP file to contain a single root folder (the plugin folder), not just loose files. I fixed it by zipping from the terminal using: zip -r qgis_mcp_plugin.zip qgis_mcp_plugin/ That worked perfectly. ✅ Working Plugin ZIP To help others, here’s a version that I just repackaged and that can be loaded via plugin ZIP installation. qgis_mcp_plugin_fixed.zip Thanks again for the awesome work on this — it’s a super promising project. As a side note: I was hoping to explore the full integration with Claude, but unfortunately, my Claude account was just blocked by Anthropic, so I haven’t yet been able to test whether this ZIP version causes any downstream issues.

title: fix(setup): don't reuse an unrelated "blender" name for Claude Code and Codex
cleaned_text: fix(setup): don't reuse an unrelated "blender" name for Claude Code and Codex Problem mcp-for-blender setup gives JSON clients (Cursor and the rest) a free name when an unrelated server already uses blender , so the new entry becomes blender-2 . Claude Code and Codex always got the fixed name blender . If a user already has a different MCP server called blender (one that runs neither mcp-for-blender nor blender-mcp , so setup sees the client as "new"): Claude Code : claude mcp add --scope user blender ... fails with MCP server blender already exists in user config . Setup exits with code 1 and Claude Code is never configured. Codex : codex mcp add blender ... silently replaces the user's [mcp_servers.blender] table. Setup prints ✓ Added , and no backup is written. The dry-run text for JSON clients also always said add "blender" , even when the entry would actually be written as blender-2 . Fix New entries for Claude Code and Codex now get a free name through the existing _free_key . The names already in use come from the top-level mcpServers in $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json (or ~/.claude.json ) and from Codex's [mcp_servers.*] tables ( _codex_mcp_sections ). Outdated entries still keep their existing name. The key is picked once in configure_cli_client . The success message uses that same key instead of re-reading the config after the add. --dry-run shows the name that will actually be used, for both CLI and JSON clients. The Codex tool_timeout_sec hint names the table that was actually written. Codex server names are no longer read only from plain [mcp_servers. ] headers. Previously a header with a trailing comment ( [mcp_servers.blender] # mine ), an inline table under [mcp_servers] , or dotted keys at the top of the file ( mcp_servers.blender.command = ... ) were not recognised, so the name looked free and codex mcp add blender still overwrote that server. On Python 3.11+ mcp_servers is now read with tomllib , so every form Codex accepts is covered. On 3.10, which has no tomllib (the project supports >=3.10 ), the regex fallback understands these three forms but not a root-level inline table ( mcp_servers = { blender = { ... } } ); that form was already unrecognised before this change. codex_state uses the same reader, so an existing install written in one of these forms is now detected too. _cli_commands takes an optional key . Without it, it behaves as before, so the existing tests are unchanged. Tests New tests in tests/test_setup_cli.py . They exercise the public entry points ( configure_cli_client , describe_change , codex_state ) with _run_cli stubbed: Claude Code and Codex pick blender-2 when an unrelated blender exists, and blender when nothing conflicts. Outdated entries keep their name. The success message, the actual mcp add arguments and the dry-run text all use the same key. Each of the three hand-written Codex forms is run twice, once with tomllib and once with the 3.10 regex fallback forced: - an unrelated blender gets blender-2 ; - an old blender-mcp install is detected as outdated, and an mcp-for-blender install as configured. The regex fallback ignores non-server keys and other tables, such as [profiles.blender] . All new tests fail on main and pass with this change. pytest : 483 passed, 1 skipped, 6 failed. The 6 failures are test_addon_status_always_answers ( No module named 'blender_mcp.config' ). They fail the same way on main and are addressed by #397. End-to-end runs of run_setup(assume_yes=True, skip_addon=True) with the real Claude Code 2.1.282 and codex-cli 0.162.1, using a fake uvx , an isolated HOME / CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CODEX_HOME and a dead proxy: Standard [mcp_servers.blender] plus a Claude mcpServers.blender : - Before: Claude Code failed with already exists (rc=1), and Codex's table was overwritten. - After: both CLIs add blender-2 , the user entries are kept, and the dry run shows blender-2 . The three hand-written Codex forms, with an extra startup_timeout_sec field: - Before: Codex's own view ( codex mcp list --json ) shows blender replaced by the uvx command. - After (with tomllib , and with the regex fallback forced): Codex lists blender and blender-2 , and blender keeps its original command, args and startup_timeout_sec . - When codex mcp add rewrites config.toml , Codex itself normalises the formatting: comments are dropped and inline or dotted keys become tables. The values are kept. Scope and known limits Verified on Linux only, with Python 3.11, the real Claude Code 2.1.282 and codex-cli 0.162.1, and a fake uvx . Not tested: macOS, Windows, a real uvx install of mcp-for-blender , or the MCP server actually starting. The Python 3.10 path was exercised by forcing the regex fallback on 3.11 and by parsing the changed files with the 3.10 grammar. It has not been run on a real 3.10 interpreter. On 3.10 a root-level inline mcp_servers = { ... } table is still not recognised by the fallback (pre-existing, unchanged here). 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: feat: add Meshy with users' API keys
cleaned_text: feat: add Meshy with users' API keys Summary Adds Meshy as a 4th generator behind generate_3d , using the user's own Meshy API key. Follows the existing own-key generator pattern. No new MCP tools. Text to model runs as a Meshy preview (mesh), then one refine (texture). Image to model is one task. Every task asks for auto_size + origin_at: bottom , so models import at real-world height. The reply after import tells the agent not to rescale, so it doesn't undo that. Sidebar: Meshy box under AI Model Generation with Model (Meshy 7.1 / Meshy 6) and API Key. Key also in Preferences and BLENDERMCP_MESHY_API_KEY . The key button reads "meshy.ai keys" like the other providers; the paid-plan requirement is in the README and in the setup message the agent relays. Own key only. Not in Premium and not picked by auto while Premium is on. With Premium selected, provider="meshy" relays the addon's own Meshy status, so it says why even when no Premium generator is ticked. Errors: 401/402/429 map to fixed messages. The key never appears in tool args, replies or errors. Preview -> refine resume One preview gets at most one refine, because each refine is paid. When a preview succeeds, the server starts the refine, records preview -> refine in pending-generations.json , and points the pending request at the refine. The job switches to the refine in place, so every resume hint after that names the refine. Refine records are kept after import and only age out (2h). So resuming an old preview handle, re-sending the same request, or restarting the MCP server reuses the existing refine. The addon also remembers preview -> refine. That covers a refine whose reply got lost to a socket timeout, and two MCP servers on one Blender. Known gap: a socket timeout during the refine call plus a Blender restart before the next resume could still start a second refine. If the refine call itself is rejected (bad key, out of credits, rate limit), the preview stays pending and the error carries its handle, so the user can fix it and resume without paying for a new preview. Tests tests/test_meshy.py (addon, stubbed bpy/requests): status states, request bodies, data URI for local images, input checks, 401/402/429 messages, key never leaked, refine dedupe in the addon, poll endpoints, import, command registration. tests/test_generation.py (FakeAddon): preview -> refine -> import with one refine; timeout mid-preview; resume with the old preview handle after the refine; same request re-sent across restarts; stale handle after import; image URL and path; failed preview/refine; relayed API errors; 800-char limit; provider choice incl. Premium; reply wording; setup messages. PYTHONPATH=src pytest : everything passes except the 6 test_addon_status_always_answers cases, which fail the same way on main locally without the gitignored blender_mcp/config.py . Manual test (Blender + Claude Desktop) Ran against this branch's addon and server with a dedicated Meshy key. [x] Text: teapot imports textured, on the ground, plausible size [x] Image: local path and URL [x] Timeout + resume: one preview + one refine in Meshy [x] MCP server restart mid-generation, same request: resumes, no extra tasks [x] Bad key: readable error, key not shown [x] Out of credits (402): covered by unit tests [x] Meshy off / no key: setup message [x] Premium on: Meshy shows "Own key only, not in Premium" and explains itself [x] diff addon.py src/blender_mcp/bundled/addon.py is empty Open for Sid Auto-pick position: Meshy is last in OWN_KEY_ORDER for now. Protocol version: not bumped. A new server with an old addon gets the "update the addon / tick Meshy" message. Who maintains the Meshy README section and the model list. Refine records age out after 2h, same as pending jobs. We could keep them longer since they're tiny. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: Question: would a "render this scene on a remote GPU" path fit blender-mcp? (offer to contribute)
cleaned_text: Question: would a "render this scene on a remote GPU" path fit blender-mcp? (offer to contribute) Hi, and thanks for blender-mcp. I've been using it to let an agent build scenes in a local Blender, and the part that stays slow for people without a discrete GPU is the render at the end. I run a small service called JANCTION Render (https://render.janction.jp, client code MIT at https://github.com/JasmyLab-JANCTION/janction-render). It is a cloud GPU render farm for Blender that an agent calls as an MCP server or an HTTP API: send a .blend, a bpy script or a 3D file (glTF / FBX / USD), get a fast 720p preview the agent can look at, a time estimate, then the final frames or an MP4. When I opened this issue (2026-10-05) it was a free beta with 10 GPU-minutes per key per day; that ended on 2026-10-08. Current terms (updated 2026-10-15): a 100 JPY welcome credit per new key (400 JPY more after saving a card that is not charged), then 0.1 JPY per GPU-second, with previews free up to 2 GPU-minutes a day; Blender 5.0 / 5.2, Cycles and EEVEE; inputs deleted 24 hours after last use. https://render.janction.jp/pricing Today the two already work side by side: a user can have both MCP servers connected, build with blender-mcp, save the .blend, and hand the file to JANCTION Render (stdio) or a script to the remote server. That needs no change on your side, and if that's the answer, I'm happy with it and would only ask whether a line under a "related projects" section in the README is welcome. If you think a tighter path is useful, two shapes I can see, offered without attachment: A tool in blender-mcp such as render_remote that saves the current scene to a temporary .blend (packing external data) and POSTs it to a user-configured render endpoint, returning the job id and a status/download link. The endpoint would be generic (URL plus API key in the environment), so it wouldn't be tied to my service; JANCTION Render would simply be one backend that speaks that API. Documentation only: a short "rendering elsewhere" section describing how to pack and export the scene so that any external renderer (a farm, a remote Blender, JANCTION Render) can take it. I'd write the code or the docs and keep it small, and I'd defer to you on naming, placement and whether this belongs in the project at all. If it doesn't fit the direction of blender-mcp, no hard feelings; I'll keep recommending the side-by-side setup. Thanks for reading.

title: fix: keep tools working without private telemetry config
cleaned_text: fix: keep tools working without private telemetry config get_addon_status fails in a public source checkout with Error checking addon status: No module named 'blender_mcp.config' . The collector imports the private, gitignored backend configuration before checking the telemetry-disable environment variables, so even DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true does not prevent the failure. Check the hard-off switches before importing that configuration. If the configuration module itself is absent, initialize a disabled collector so Blender tools and consent reporting remain available. Disabled collectors do not persist an install UUID or start the event worker. An installed, enabled configuration still starts collection normally, and missing dependencies inside an installed configuration are not silently hidden. The environment override no longer mutates the imported configuration object. Against the unmodified base, the same tests produce 9 failures and 2 passes ; with this change all 11 pass. Ruff checks and formatting on the new tests, fatal syntax/name checks on the changed module, and git diff --check pass. Existing broader lint findings in telemetry.py are outside this change. The new tests stub backend configuration, worker startup, and Blender replies; they make no requests to a real telemetry backend. README documents the source-checkout behavior. title: fix: preserve queued responses after client half-close
cleaned_text: fix: preserve queued responses after client half-close Fixes #391. A client that sends a request and calls shutdown(SHUT_WR) currently receives EOF before Blender's main thread can send its queued response. _handle_client() closes the socket even though _drain_command_queue() still needs it. Track pending responses under the existing client lock. On receive EOF, the handler exits and transfers socket ownership to the main-thread drain, which closes it after the last response attempt. This includes a command already dequeued and executing when EOF arrives. Receive errors still close immediately, and stop() closes retained sockets and clears pending state. Both addon copies contain the same fix. The regression tests use real socket pairs, queue notifications, and thread joins to force EOF before response delivery, without sleeps. They cover queued and executing commands, multiple pending responses, command errors, connection reuse, incomplete requests, server shutdown, send failures, and receive errors against both addon copies. Validation on Linux with Python 3.14.8: Final regression suite against the original addon: 10 failed, 10 passed . Each failure receives no response because the socket was closed early. Socket, Unicode, and threading tests: 26 passed . Full suite: 487 passed, 1 skipped, 6 failed . The unmodified base has 467 passed, 1 skipped, the same 6 failures : every test_compat_matrix.py::test_addon_status_always_answers parameter ( e0e8095 , 25b16af , aa592fa , f721eb5 , 8b4e062 , current ) fails because blender_mcp.config is missing. Both runs also report the same four existing utcfromtimestamp deprecation warnings. git diff --check , Python compilation, and byte equality of the two addon files pass. Blender itself was not available; the tests execute the actual server class using the repository's existing Blender timer stubs.

title: feat: point at part of a mesh, and let users see look images
cleaned_text: feat: point at part of a mesh, and let users see look images The problem. I was using this with a client that doesn't support MCP Apps, on an imported Model 3 interior (693 objects; the whole dashboard, door trims and a dozen trim parts are one merged mesh, Object_30.002 , 28k faces, one material). The task was "separate the raised trim strip on top of the dashboard". It took around 15 back-and-forth rounds, and two things in the tool surface made it much harder than it needed to be: A pick names the object, never the part. pick_viewport_object ray-casts, gets the face index, and drops it. On a merged mesh every click returns Object_30.002 , which tells the model nothing. Yet the trim is its own connected piece of that mesh (644 faces); knowing the clicked face is enough to find it. Without MCP Apps there is no way to point, and no way for the user to see. viewport_pick is app-only, and look images reach the model only, so the model ended up building its own render pipeline to show the user anything, and the user resorted to Shift+right-clicking while the model polled the 3D cursor with a timer. The fix. blender_scripts.PICK : given a click (view and window matrices plus x , y , as the Viewport app already stores) or the 3D cursor, it returns the object, face, material, and the connected piece around that face: face count, world bounds and size. Vertices at the same position count as joined, since exporters split vertices along UV seams and hard edges and Select Linked stops there (on this model, Select Linked from the clicked face stops at 328 of the trim's 644 faces). It is vectorised with numpy, so it takes ~0.1 s on the 28k-face mesh. viewport_pick : for a mesh, adds surface and appends the face and piece to detail , so the link description and the attached text already carry it to the model. The app's note now says the user means that piece, not the whole object. If the script fails (or the ray hits a different object than the native pick), the click picks the object exactly as before. get_scene_info(fields=["cursor"]) : one extra header line saying what the 3D cursor sits on, with the same face and piece. If the cursor is far from any surface (never placed, or left in mid-air), it says so and how to place it. This is how a user of any client points at something. look(save_to="/path.png") : also writes the image to a file on the server's machine and says where, so the model can hand it to the user. Validated before touching Blender, only .png , and a failed write is reported in the result instead of raising. SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS : two sentences pointing at save_to and at Shift+right-click + fields=["cursor"] (1456 → 1685 characters, under the 2500 cap). Everything new runs as a script through execute_code , like look and get_scene_info , so it works with every installed addon: no addon change and no protocol bump . PICK uses numpy the same way LOOK does. Example output on the model above, after the user Shift+right-clicks the trim: 3D cursor at (10.03, -7.028, 1.9104) is on 'Object_30.002', face 15709 (material 'Material.016'), in a connected piece of 644 of its 28484 faces, 2.602 x 0.2602 x 0.0674 m, from (9.459, -7.116, 1.8562) to (12.061, -6.8558, 1.9236). Vertices at the same position count as joined, so seams from export don't split it, though Select Linked stops there. and for a Viewport app click on the same part, detail becomes: Mesh object in collection '3'; face 15540 (material 'Material.016'), in a connected piece of 644 of its 28484 faces, 2.602 x 0.2602 x 0.0674 m, from (9.459, -7.116, 1.8562) to (12.061, -6.8558, 1.9236) Testing. New tests/test_pick_surface.py (16 tests): cursor line (hit, nothing hit, far from the surface, whole-object piece, faces after modifiers, script failure, only runs when asked); Viewport clicks (face and piece added, and the object is still picked when there's no face: non-mesh, old addon, ray hit another object, no hit); save_to (writes the file and keeps the image for the model, rejects non-PNG before touching Blender, nothing written without it, a failed write is reported). PICK is added to the compile/no- SystemExit check, and the existing click test now allows the follow-up script call. Full suite on macOS, Python 3.11: 489 passed, 1 skipped. (On a clean checkout, 6 test_addon_status_always_answers cases fail with No module named 'blender_mcp.config' because config.py is gitignored; that's unrelated, and they pass with a local stub.) End to end against Blender 5.2.2 on macOS, running this branch's addon.py (unchanged) with the model above: the get_scene_info and viewport_pick outputs above are real; a cursor at the world origin and one floating in the cabin are both reported as not placed; a cube with a Subdivision modifier reports face 11 of the mesh after modifiers, in one connected piece: the whole object . look(mode="viewport"|"angles", save_to=...) against a live Blender wrote valid PNGs and still returned the image. Relation to open PRs. #378 moves the viewport screenshot over the socket and #353 adds multi-view montages; neither touches picking, and save_to sits in look after the image comes back, so it composes with either.

title: Bug: client half-close (`shutdown SHUT_WR`) closes the connection before the async response is sent — the command is never answered
cleaned_text: Bug: client half-close ( shutdown SHUT_WR ) closes the connection before the async response is sent — the command is never answered Summary BlenderMCPServer._handle_client() in src/blender_mcp/bundled/addon.py closes the client socket as soon as recv() returns b"" (EOF). But responses are not sent back on the handler thread — commands are handed to Blender's main thread via command_queue , and the response is sent later by _drain_command_queue() (which runs on a 0.05 s poll). If a client does a standard TCP half-close after sending its request ( socket.shutdown(SHUT_WR) in Python, socket.end() in Node.js — a legal "done sending" pattern), the handler sees EOF, break s and closes the socket while the command is still queued . The later client.sendall(response) hits a dead socket, and the BrokenPipeError is swallowed by a bare except at the send site. The client, which has already stopped writing and is now only reading, receives FIN and never gets its response — a read loop that waits for a complete payload hangs forever. The protocol is *server-side asynchronous write-back*, so a client-side half-close is not a safe "I'm done sending" signal here. The official FastMCP path ( server.py ) does not half-close, so bundled MCP clients are unaffected — this bites third-party automation that talks to the addon socket on port 9876 directly, which is exactly how we drive it ( traced with two live experiments against a stock addon install, no server-side modification; details below). Affected src/blender_mcp/bundled/addon.py , _handle_client() / _drain_command_queue() Source-reviewed against upstream main @ 7a0373ec9199 (2026-10-06; addon bl_info version (1, 8) , ADDON_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 13 ) Live-reproduced against a local stock install of the same version (Blender 5.2, Windows 10) Reproduction No MCP client needed — stdlib only. This hangs on the first command: import socket, json s = socket.create_connection(("localhost", 9876)) s.sendall(json.dumps({"type": "get_scene_info", "params": {}}).encode()) s.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR) # half-close: "no more requests" (legal TCP pattern) Read-until-complete-JSON loop (a typical waiting-style client): buf = b"" while not buf.endswith(b"}"): buf += s.recv(8192) # after the server's FIN, recv() returns b'' forever print(json.loads(buf)) # never reached — infinite loop Observed: Blender's console prints Client disconnected immediately after the command is queued, then Failed to send response - client disconnected . The client hangs indefinitely. (In theory the response could win the race if the main-thread drain fired between command_queue.put() and the handler's client.close() — but that window is sub-millisecond against a 50 ms poll, so the close wins essentially every time.) The same hang reproduces with real payloads, e.g. execute_code . Root cause (two cooperating parts) _handle_client() treats EOF ( recv() == b"" ) as "client is gone" and closes — but in this protocol a half-close only means "no more *requests*", not "no longer interested in the *response*". _drain_command_queue() sends the response inside a bare except Exception: that only prints — the dead-socket write leaves no traceback and there is no status surface to notice it. Relevant code paths (current main): _handle_client() data = client.recv(8192) if not data: print("Client disconnected") break # <- socket closed while response still pending ... self.command_queue.put((command, client)) _drain_command_queue() — Blender main thread try: client.sendall(response_json.encode('utf-8')) except Exception: print("Failed to send response - client disconnected") # <- BrokenPipe swallowed Suggested fix (client-side, one line — this is what we verified) A waiting-style client should not half-close: keep the socket open after sendall() and read the response normally. before (hangs) s.sendall(payload) s.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR) # or s.end() in Node.js after (works — verified live against a stock addon, two round-trip experiments) s.sendall(payload) do NOT shutdown(SHUT_WR) / end() buf = b"" while not buf.endswith(b"}"): buf += s.recv(8192) Suggested hardening (server-side, optional — sketched, not yet patched locally) To make the addon robust against any client that half-closes (LLM-generated clients do this a lot, and half-close is a legal TCP pattern), either: A. Only treat EOF as disconnect when the buffer is empty — if EOF arrives while a request is buffered, queue it first, then exit the loop: data = client.recv(8192) if not data: if buffer: try: command = json.loads(buffer.decode('utf-8')) self.command_queue.put((command, client)) except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError): pass buffer = b'' break (This keeps the current single-request-per-connection framing working for half-closing clients; fully-open clients are unaffected.) B. Fail loud instead of silent — in _drain_command_queue() , log the failed send with traceback (and/or surface a counter), so a dead-socket write is diagnosable from Blender's console instead of one swallowed print line. Environment Blender 5.2, addon installed under scripts/addons/blender_mcp/ Windows 10 (10.0.19045) Addon: MCP for Blender 1.8, ADDON_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 13 Source review: upstream main @ 7a0373ec9199 ; repro: live local install of the same version 中文摘要（供维护者参考） 一句话 ：等待型客户端发完请求后做标准半关闭（ shutdown(SHUT_WR) / Node 的 socket.end() ）， _handle_client 收到 EOF 就 break 并关连接，而响应要等 Blender 主线程 _drain_command_queue （50ms 轮询）异步回发——socket 已死， BrokenPipeError 被裸 except 吞掉，只等响应的客户端永久挂起。 教训一句话 ：在「响应由第三方时序异步回写」的协议里，半关闭不是合法的"我说完了"信号——协议语义优先于 TCP 惯例。 建议 ：客户端不调半关保持连接（一行修复，已实测双通）；服务端可选加固：①EOF 时若 buffer 有完整请求先入队再退出 ②回发失败改为带 traceback 的响亮日志。

title: [BUG] Cloud MCP endpoint stopped answering for about 10 minutes (2026-10-16, 19:50–20:00 UTC)
cleaned_text: [BUG] Cloud MCP endpoint stopped answering for about 10 minutes (2026-10-16, 19:50–20:00 UTC) Bug Description On 2026-10-16 the hosted MCP endpoint ( https://cloud.basicmemory.com/mcp , OAuth bearer, Streamable HTTP) stopped answering authenticated requests for about 10 minutes. Every request sent between about 19:49:50 and 19:58:55 UTC got no answer within 30 seconds. It recovered without anyone changing anything. Steps To Reproduce I can't reproduce it on demand. These are the times and calls: Last success before the gap: three search_notes calls sent around 19:42:35 UTC (3.7 s, 6.2 s, 9.8 s). 15 calls from four separate client sessions failed from 19:49:50 to 19:58:55 UTC ( search_notes ×11, read_note ×3, find ×1). The largest burst was four search_notes calls sent together at about 19:55:09. Each call opens a fresh MCP session (initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/call, DELETE). Each time the server didn't answer initialize within the client's 30 s connect timeout. The failures ended at 30.05–30.81 s. First success after the gap: search_notes sent around 19:59:44 UTC, 10.6 s. Expected Behavior initialize gets an answer within a few seconds. When the backend is overloaded or restarting, it fails fast (for example 503 with Retry-After ) instead of leaving the connection open with no reply. Actual Behavior No response at all within 30 s, for about 10 minutes. The client (an MCP gateway) reported it as: AppEvaluationFailed (HTTP 502): The app's MCP server did not respond in time while connecting. The 502 comes from the gateway's timeout. It isn't a status the server sent. Environment Basic Memory Cloud (hosted), MCP over Streamable HTTP with OAuth Client: Executor Cloud, using @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.1 OS / Python / local install: not applicable (server-to-server) Additional Context I didn't test unauthenticated requests during the gap. Afterwards, an unauthenticated initialize gets a 401 in about 0.2 s. So the front door is quick and the stall was probably behind authentication. Typical latency when healthy, from the same client on the same day: list_memory_projects 0.7–2 s, read_note 2.5–8 s, search_notes 4–20 s, edit_note / write_note 5–14 s. A search_notes running in parallel doesn't delay list_memory_projects (1.9 s next to a 5.2 s search), so ordinary concurrency doesn't explain it. The load was small: about 15 requests over 10 minutes, at most four at once. Possible Solution I can't see the cause from outside. If it was long searches holding the tenant's database or workers (#1746 measures Cloud searches at up to 100 s), these might help: cancel server-side work when the client disconnects, answer initialize without touching the database, or return 503 with Retry-After under load. A public status page would also help clients tell an outage from a credential problem.

title: perf(core): cut database round trips in note read and write paths
cleaned_text: perf(core): cut database round trips in note read and write paths Purpose Make Basic Memory's note tools do less database work per call, so each tool call costs fewer round trips. On a remote Postgres that cost is paid per query, so query count drives latency. Context In Basic Memory Cloud, each tenant runs on Neon Postgres, so every query is a network round trip of roughly 40 ms from the Cloud API, and the queries in a tool call run one after another. Over 2026-10-16/17 the Cloud side removed most of its own per-call overhead: auth caching, workspace-discovery caching, pool sizing and idle-only pings. Measured on development with per-statement SQL spans ( LOGFIRE_SQL_SPANS ), Cloud's control-plane work per tool call is now about 0.2 s. What remains is the core read and write path on the tenant database. One agent read_note (full content) on development: Tenant SELECTs | 49, sequential Tenant SQL time | ~1.9 s of a ~3.4 s server-side call Per-statement p50 | ~40–46 ms Grouped by statement: Statement | Count | Where project row lookup | 23 | Every hop and dependency ( GET /v2/projects/ , POST /v2/projects/resolve , knowledge/resolve , resolve_entity , get_entity ) entity lookup | 9 + 4 | resolve_entity observations and both relation directions | 2× each | Loaded in resolve_entity , then again in get_entity entity , observations, relations, note_content | 1× each | get_entity , after resolve_entity already loaded the same entity In one run, agent tool-call p50s were: read_note 3.5 s, edit_note 4.0 s, ls 1.8 s, grep 2.7 s. A read_note with include_content=false needs only about 4 tenant queries and returns in about 0.38 s, which shows how much of the cost comes from the content and entity-graph path. These numbers come from Cloud, but the work happens in core's services and repositories ( knowledge resolve and get, project resolution, entity hydration), and every backend pays for it. On local SQLite each query is cheap, so the duplication is invisible there. Goals Measure. A per-tool query count for the main tools ( read_note , edit_note , write_note , search_notes , build_context , ls / cat ), against SQLite and Postgres, with a test helper that counts statements so counts can be asserted. Find the duplication. For each tool: which statements repeat, which entity loads overlap (resolve, then get), and where an N+1 pattern appears. Cut round trips. Candidate directions, to be confirmed by the investigation: Resolve the project once per request and pass it down, instead of re-selecting it in each dependency. Have resolve_entity return the loaded entity graph, so get_entity doesn't reload it. Or give read_note one combined endpoint. Eager-load observations and relations in one round trip ( selectinload or joinedload ) where they're always needed. Guard against regressions. Query-count assertions in tests, so the numbers can't creep back up. Non-goals Changing Cloud's control-plane or auth path, which was done separately. Moving databases between regions, which is tracked as a Cloud issue. Caching note content across requests. This issue is about doing less work per request. First step: investigation Write up the query count and repeated statements for each tool, then propose the changes in order of round trips saved. On Cloud development, LOGFIRE_SQL_SPANS=true is on, so per-statement spans show up under each tool call in Logfire.

title: Make litellm an optional extra (basic-memory[litellm])
cleaned_text: Make litellm an optional extra (basic-memory[litellm]) Why litellm>=1.60.0,<1.92.0 is a core dependency, so every install pulls it in, including environments that never use the litellm embedding or rerank providers (basic-memory-cloud uses fastembed). litellm constrains openai itself: every release from 1.84.0 through the latest (1.105.0) requires openai>=2.20.0, =3.19 for its OpenAI extra, so upgrading Cloud's agent runtime to the latest Pydantic AI (basic-memory-cloud#2470) downgraded litellm from 1.90.2 to 1.83.0. Removing our <1.92.0 cap would not help, because litellm's own openai cap remains. That cap exists because litellm 1.92 added a Rust bridge whose PyO3 version rejects Python 3.14 (#1051). Proposal Move litellm from dependencies to [project.optional-dependencies] litellm = ["litellm>=1.60.0,<1.92.0"] . The import is already lazy ( litellm_provider._import_litellm() , used by the embedding and rerank providers). When the package is missing, raise a clear error naming the setting and the fix: pip install "basic-memory[litellm]" / uv tool install "basic-memory[litellm]" . Add a test that the litellm provider raises that error when litellm is not importable, and that fastembed/default paths never import it. Docs: semantic search provider pages and the CHANGELOG note that litellm users add the extra. Check whether core's direct openai>=1.100.2 dependency is still needed, or belongs in the same extra. After it lands basic-memory-cloud re-pins core and drops litellm from its lockfile.

title: [BUG] Duplicate rows in `search_index` on the SQLite backend — no uniqueness guard, non-atomic reindex, and the stale-row purge cannot remove duplicates
cleaned_text: [BUG] Duplicate rows in search_index on the SQLite backend — no uniqueness guard, non-atomic reindex, and the stale-row purge cannot remove duplicates On the SQLite backend, search_index is an FTS5 virtual table. Unlike the Postgres backend — which has uix_search_index_permalink_project (a UNIQUE index on (permalink, project_id) ) — the SQLite table has no unique constraint and no secondary indexes at all, so nothing at the database level prevents duplicate rows. The index update path is also non-atomic across transactions: SearchService.index_entity() (background task on every note write) first calls repository.delete_by_entity_id() in one committed session, then bulk_index_items() (plain INSERTs) in another. Multiple independent processes write the same database concurrently — every MCP server instance does on-demand indexing, plus the file watcher. When two writers interleave (A deletes → B deletes → A inserts → B inserts), both inserts survive as duplicate rows. Observed in practice: the same (project_id, 'entity', id) appearing 2–3 times, byte-identical content, adjacent rowids, timestamps within 1 ms; the visible count for a single note fluctuating between 1/2/3 across consecutive writes. Once observed, 34 entities across all projects were affected simultaneously. Additionally, purge_stale_search_index_rows() cannot fix this: its three DELETE statements only remove rows whose backing entity / observation / relation row no longer exists. Duplicate rows have a live backing row, so they survive — a reindex reports 0 stale search rows purged while duplicates demonstrably exist. There is also no dedupe-only maintenance mode, and reindex (the documented remedy for index issues) does not dedupe either. Impact recent_activity / search results list the same note N times; counts are inflated. The 0 stale search rows purged output actively misleads diagnosis while duplicates exist. Users who try the documented remedy ( reindex --full ) cannot clean the duplicates and, per the separate created_at issue, lose creation timestamps as a side effect. Steps to reproduce Intermittent (timing-dependent), so reproducible only probabilistically: Run several MCP server instances against the same basic-memory home (one per client session, which is the normal multi-client setup). Write/update the same note from two clients near-simultaneously (or write while the file watcher processes the same file). Inspect: SELECT project_id, type, id, count(*) FROM search_index WHERE type='entity' GROUP BY project_id, type, id HAVING count(*) > 1; Actual Duplicate, byte-identical rows accumulate silently; no maintenance command removes them. Expected A re-index of an entity replaces its previous index rows exactly ("last write wins"), or at minimum a maintenance command exists that deduplicates. Versions basic-memory 0.23.2, Windows 11, SQLite backend.

title: [BUG] bm status` and `bm doctor` don't surface index inconsistencies (duplicate rows, orphans, inverted timestamps)
cleaned_text: [BUG] bm status and bm doctor don't surface index inconsistencies (duplicate rows, orphans, inverted timestamps) bm status reports only per-project observed file counts. It showed 10 observed files for a project whose search_index held 13 rows for 10 entities — the divergence was invisible. bm doctor exercises a happy-path write→index→search round trip only. It passes with duplicate search_index rows, orphan entities, and inverted created_at present in the database. Diagnosing any of these currently requires hand-written SQL against the internal database. Impact Users see "doctor checks passed" / normal status while their search index is silently corrupted; index problems are discovered only through visible symptoms (duplicated search hits) long after the fact. Expected bm doctor (the natural home) checks structural invariants, e.g.: duplicate (project_id, type, id) groups in search_index ; search_index rows whose backing entity no longer exists; count of entity rows with created_at > updated_at . bm status could include per-project index row counts vs entity counts. Versions basic-memory 0.23.2, Windows 11, SQLite backend.

title: [BUG] reindex --full` overwrites `entity.created_at` with the reindex timestamp for notes without a frontmatter `created:` — irreversible
cleaned_text: [BUG] reindex --full overwrites entity.created_at with the reindex timestamp for notes without a frontmatter created: — irreversible For notes that don't declare created: in frontmatter, bm reindex --full (and the full project-index path generally) sets entity.created_at to the moment the reindex runs, destroying the original creation timestamp. The chain: indexing/input_file_adaptation.py — build_index_input_files() hardcodes created_at=None for every file, even though file creation time ( st_ctime ) is available and is in fact used elsewhere ( services/file_service.py builds created_at from stat_result.st_ctime ). indexing/batch_indexer.py — passes ctime=file.created_at to the markdown parser, i.e. always None on this path. markdown/entity_parser.py — with ctime=None and no frontmatter created: , the fallback is datetime.now() . services/entity_service.py — _apply_markdown_entity_fields() unconditionally assigns entity.created_at = markdown.created . updated_at keeps the file mtime, so afterwards created_at > updated_at (inverted). In one run, every note in a project without frontmatter created: received created_at equal to the reindex moment to the millisecond, while the underlying files' creation times were hours older and untouched. Across the whole installation, hundreds of entity rows are inverted this way. The original value cannot be recovered from the database. Side effect: find_related -style time-window filtering ( created_at >= since ) silently returns wrong results. Main search-result ordering is unaffected (it uses search_index.updated_at ). Aggravating factor: the recommended remedy for index inconsistency is reindex --full , so users hit this repeatedly while trying to fix other index problems. Impact Any installation with notes lacking frontmatter created: loses real creation timestamps on every full reindex. Data loss is silent and irreversible. Steps to reproduce Create a note without created: in frontmatter; note its file creation time. Wait (or edit it so updated_at < reindex time), then run bm reindex --full . SELECT title, created_at, updated_at FROM entity WHERE created_at > updated_at; Actual created_at equals the reindex timestamp (later than updated_at ), regardless of the file's real creation time. Expected created_at is preserved (from the existing entity row, or from the file's creation time, which is available via st_ctime ) when frontmatter does not declare created: . Versions basic-memory 0.23.2, Windows 11.

title: fix(api): delete omitted frontmatter keys on a full-document PUT
cleaned_text: fix(api): delete omitted frontmatter keys on a full-document PUT Fixes #1768. Problem Cloud's web editor saves the whole note through core's PUT /v2/projects/{id}/knowledge/entities/{entity_id} . prepare_update_entity_content started from the stored frontmatter and laid the new metadata on top of it, so a key the person deleted came back after save. Change New replace_frontmatter: bool = False argument, threaded through NoteContentMutationService.update_note , AcceptedNoteUpdateMutation , prepare_accepted_note_replace , the AcceptedNoteReplacePreparer protocol, and prepare_update_entity_content . When it is true, the existing frontmatter is not merged. The written frontmatter is exactly what the schema supplies, plus the resolved permalink. The PUT route passes True only when the request supplies frontmatter, either as a frontmatter block in content or as a non-empty entity_metadata . A writer that sends frontmatter sends all of it, so an omitted key was deleted. A body-only PUT did not mean to change the keys, so it keeps the merge. Cloud's editor sends the document's YAML as entity_metadata , so its saves replace. Everything else keeps the default merge. That covers MCP write_note(overwrite=True) , whose merge is documented, and Cloud's document-ingestion update_note call. #1653, the write_note overwrite contract, is not changed here. Tests test_prepare_update_entity_content_replace_frontmatter_drops_omitted_keys : the default merge keeps the omitted key; replace_frontmatter=True drops it. test_update_entity_by_id_deletes_omitted_frontmatter_keys : through the PUT route, with frontmatter sent as entity_metadata and as a block in content , the omitted key is gone from both the file and note_content . The existing test_update_entity_by_id_freshens_external_file_metadata_before_accepting still passes: a body-only PUT keeps the stored keys. test_write_note_overwrite_keeps_unset_frontmatter_keys : confirms MCP overwrite still merges. Cloud follow-up when re-pinning core api/deps/note_content_gateway.py overrides update_note . It has to accept replace_frontmatter and pass it on, or the PUT route raises a TypeError . services/review_search.py implements prepare_update_entity_content . title: Frontmatter keys cannot be deleted through a full-document save
cleaned_text: Frontmatter keys cannot be deleted through a full-document save What happens A frontmatter key removed from a note's document is not removed from the file. A replace or overwrite keeps any key that the incoming document leaves out. Seen in Basic Memory Cloud's web editor: A note's frontmatter has eaccess: write . The person deletes that line in the frontmatter editor and saves. The full new document goes to the save path without the key. After a reload, eaccess: write is back in the file. Why Core's update path merges the incoming metadata over the note's existing raw frontmatter before it dumps the YAML: services/note_preparation.py , prepare_update_entity_content (around line 465), after schema_to_markdown . A key that is absent from the new document survives from the old one. This merge is intended for MCP write_note with overwrite=True , whose docs say: "Overwrite replaces the body but merges frontmatter: keys the existing note has and this write does not set are kept". That rule is wrong for a caller that sends the whole canonical document. An editor saving the full file means "this is the file", and the only way to delete a key should be to leave it out. Expected When a write supplies the complete document (frontmatter plus body), the resulting frontmatter is exactly what was supplied. Keys left out are removed. The MCP overwrite merge can stay as it is for callers that only set some fields, but a full-document replace needs a path that does not merge. Repro Note with frontmatter title , type , extra: 1 . Save the full document without extra through the accepted-note replace path, which is what Cloud's PUT /api/v2/notes/{id} uses. Read the file: extra: 1 is still there. Related Cloud had a separate bug on the same save path: frontmatter booleans and numbers were stringified ( enabled: true became enabled: 'True' ) because the payload was built from the normalized index metadata. That one is being fixed in Cloud. This issue is only about deleted keys coming back.

title: Hermes integration cannot use an existing streamable-http server: provider is hard-wired to a stdio subprocess
cleaned_text: Hermes integration cannot use an existing streamable-http server: provider is hard-wired to a stdio subprocess Summary integrations/hermes always starts its own bm mcp stdio subprocess. There is no way to point the provider at an already-running streamable-http Basic Memory server, so every host that enables the plugin adds a full basic-memory process even when a shared server is already available on the machine. Why this matters operationally Basic Memory supports --transport streamable-http , and on a multi-agent machine that is the difference between one server and one-per-host. We moved to a single shared server for exactly this reason: measured 2026-09-26, 13 stdio copies were ~14 MB RSS each but ~198 MB phys footprint each — about 2.6 GB on a 16 GB laptop, for a server that had seen zero tool calls in 233 transcripts over 14 days. The shared server now runs under launchd at http://127.0.0.1:18796/mcp and nine agent CLIs point at it. Enabling the Hermes plugin reintroduces the per-host copy. Observed with Hermes alone: six bm mcp children at 118–146 MB RSS each, ~640 MB total (see the companion leak report, which is why they accumulated rather than staying at one). Where it is hard-wired Traced by the Hermes agent reading its own installed copy of the plugin (credit to it for the trace): _server_argv() returns [bm, "mcp"] . _BmMcpActor._main() builds StdioServerParameters(...) . It then calls stdio_client(params) . No streamable-http URL/transport setting exists anywhere in the provider config path. Request Let the provider reuse an existing server rather than spawning one. Either: a config option for an MCP streamable-http endpoint (e.g. basic_memory.mcp_url ), using the streamable-http client transport against it; or route through the host's existing MCP connection when one is already configured — in Hermes' case mcp_servers.basic-memory already carries the URL, so the information is present and simply unused. Happy to test a branch on this setup (macOS arm64, basic-memory 0.23.2 plugin, shared server on 18796). Being able to opt into the shared server is the single change that would let us enable these plugins at all; as it stands the per-host subprocess cost rules them out across nine sessions.
