title: Add opt-in GCF response encoding for tool results
cleaned_text: Add opt-in GCF response encoding for tool results Summary Adds an opt-in RESPONSE_FORMAT=gcf for the record-returning tools ( search_indicators , search_malware , search_threat_actors , get_latest_reports , and the other list tools). When set, results encode as Graph Compact Format instead of JSON: the repeated field names of a record array are factored into a single header, so a response uses fewer tokens when it crosses the LLM boundary. Default is json ; nothing changes unless you opt in. Why Benchmarked on OpenCTI indicator output The exact 13-field search_indicators record schema, against the server's current JSON output, cl100k / o200k tokenizers: records | JSON (current) | GCF | GCF vs JSON 50 | 12,412 | 8,793 | 29.2% 200 | 49,738 | 35,158 | 29.3% 500 | 124,373 | 87,870 | 29.3% ~29% fewer tokens than the current output, lossless, and still structured and readable. Reproduce: node benchmarks/gcf-benchmark.mjs . Lossless on STIX patterns Round-trip verified lossless to 500 records. OpenCTI indicator patterns are bracket-colon strings like [ipv4-addr:value = '198.51.100.42'] ; GCF round-trips these with zero failures. GCF is verified lossless across 43 billion+ round-trips in 5 formats and 6 languages. Comprehension, not just size The harder question than size is whether a model reads the compact form as accurately as JSON. In an independent evaluation (1,700+ evals across GPT-4o, GPT-5.5, Claude, Gemini), GCF scored 100% on general structured data and 90.7% on adversarial payloads, versus 53.6% for JSON . https://gcformat.com/guide/benchmarks It was reverse-engineered from attention-level research into how BPE tokenization shapes what a transformer represents, validated by controlled from-scratch training at 1.3B measured causally, so it holds on models that have never seen the format. Four papers (2026, under review): GCF: A Token-Optimized Wire Format for Structured LLM Interactions — https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20579817 Tokenizer-Attention Coupling — https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20925910 Stranded Attention — https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21158886 Developmental Atlas of Attention Head Specialization — https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21205389 Zero new footprint @blackwell-systems/gcf is a zero-dependency package, pinned exact. Already adopted The same opt-in pattern is already merged into other MCP servers and tools: Wazuh-MCP-Server (SIEM MCP), the same RESPONSE_FORMAT=gcf option Chrome DevTools MCP (Google), an experimentalGcfFormat flag mcp-cisco-support, 28.5% fewer tokens on Cisco API data netclaw (network-automation MCP), adopted GCF for its tool responses OmniRoute (LLM gateway), GCF compression Design (deliberately conservative) Opt-in and additive: one env var, default json , existing behavior unchanged. One renderResult helper swapped into the single result return site. Lossless, with a JSON fallback on any encoding error, so a fetched result is never lost. No change to any tool signature. Tests npm test builds and runs the suite (Node's built-in test runner, no new dependency): json mode returns exactly the existing output, gcf mode round-trips losslessly (arrays and single objects), and the env var parsing defaults to json . Changes File | Change src/gcf-format.ts | new: RESPONSE_FORMAT selection + renderResult helper src/index.ts | use renderResult at the single result return site test/gcf-format.test.mjs | new: encoding + round-trip tests package.json | add @blackwell-systems/gcf (pinned exact) + gpt-tokenizer (benchmark), test script README.md , .env.example | document the RESPONSE_FORMAT=gcf option benchmarks/gcf-benchmark.mjs | reproducible JSON vs GCF benchmark

title: Opt-in per-call authorization so agents can scale/restart only what their task needs
cleaned_text: Opt-in per-call authorization so agents can scale/restart only what their task needs #376 points at a real tension: kubectl_scale , kubectl_patch and kubectl_apply are destructive, but they're also exactly what an on-call agent needs to fix an incident. Moving them out of non-destructive mode protects the cluster by taking the fix away. What you usually want is narrower than either: "this agent may restart checkout in staging and scale it to at most 5, for the next 15 minutes", and nothing else, even if something in a log it read tells it otherwise. I tried that against v4.1.9. The same eight calls from an on-call agent, first with ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS=true , then with a per-call check added in the tools/call handler ( kubectl is a fake that records what it was asked to run): ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS=true: restart checkout/staging kubectl ran scale checkout/staging 3 kubectl ran scale checkout/production 0 kubectl ran scale checkout/staging 50 kubectl ran restart payments/staging kubectl ran scale on another cluster kubectl ran (context: prod-cluster) scale, namespace omitted kubectl ran (falls through to default) apply cluster-admin binding kubectl ran per-call check (warrant: checkout in staging, <= 5 replicas): restart checkout/staging kubectl ran scale checkout/staging 3 kubectl ran scale checkout/production 0 REFUSED namespace scale checkout/staging 50 REFUSED replicas restart payments/staging REFUSED name scale on another cluster REFUSED context - unknown field not allowed scale, namespace omitted REFUSED namespace - missing required argument apply cluster-admin binding REFUSED tool not authorized How it works: the agent attaches a signed warrant to each MCP call ( _meta.tenuo ) that lists the tools and argument values its task allows. The server checks it against one trusted public key before running kubectl. Warrants delegate: here an incident commander allowed to touch staging and production hands the on-call agent a strictly narrower one, and neither can widen what they were given. Unlisted arguments are refused, which is what closes the context and missing- namespace paths. The change is small: about 9 lines right after isToolAllowed() in src/index.ts , plus a helper that's a no-op unless TENUO_TRUSTED_ROOT is set. Patch, setup script and tests (they build v4.1.9 and drive it over stdio): https://github.com/tenuo-ai/tenuo-demos/tree/demo/k8s-mcp-scoped-oncall/k8s-mcp-scoped-oncall It fits deployments where you run the agents and can have them attach a warrant, for example the remote Streamable HTTP setups from #217. A desktop client that doesn't attach one would be refused while the check is on, which is why it's opt-in. Would you be open to a PR along those lines? The check uses Tenuo (Apache-2.0); the TypeScript package, @tenuo/core , is currently 0.3.2-beta.0, so it could go in as an optional dependency loaded only when the env var is set. Disclosure: I maintain Tenuo. Happy to adjust the shape: env var vs config file, or keeping it to docs if you'd rather not carry the dependency.

title: ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS still enables 7 tools that declare destructiveHint: true (apply/create/scale/patch/rollout, helm install/upgrade, exec_in_pod)
cleaned_text: ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS still enables 7 tools that declare destructiveHint: true (apply/create/scale/patch/rollout, helm install/upgrade, exec_in_pod) Thanks for the call-layer enforcement from #308 — that part works, and kubectl_delete is correctly refused under the flag. This follows up on #314, which was closed with the note that exec_in_pod 's cluster impact depends on the pod's permissions. That reasoning does not cover the other tools that stay enabled in the same mode. Behaviour With ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS=true (npm v4.1.7, also current HEAD), tools/list advertises 18 tools. Seven of them declare annotations.destructiveHint: true in their own schema: tool | annotation | effect exec_in_pod | destructiveHint: true | command execution inside a pod kubectl_apply | destructiveHint: true | creates/updates cluster objects kubectl_create | (none) | creates cluster objects kubectl_scale | destructiveHint: true | changes replica counts kubectl_patch | destructiveHint: true | mutates cluster objects kubectl_rollout | destructiveHint: true | restarts/replaces workloads install_helm_chart / upgrade_helm_chart | destructiveHint: true | deploys/updates workloads The gate exists and works for the names in destructiveTools ( kubectl_delete , uninstall_helm_chart , cleanup , kubectl_generic , node_management ); the list just does not include the tools above. kubectl_apply/create/scale/patch/rollout and Helm install/upgrade mutate cluster state regardless of any pod's permissions, so they are not covered by the #314 rationale. Reproduction (local cluster, namespace probe-ns , pod probe ) env ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS=true npx -y mcp-server-kubernetes tools/call exec_in_pod {"name":"probe","namespace":"probe-ns","command":["cat","/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token"]} → the pod's service-account JWT is returned tools/call exec_in_pod {"name":"probe","namespace":"probe-ns","command":["id"]} → uid=0(root) gid=0(root) … inside the pod tools/call kubectl_apply with a ConfigMap manifest → object created; confirmed independently with kubectl -n probe-ns get configmap nondestructive-bypass-proof Control: tools/call kubectl_delete {"resourceType":"pods","name":"x"} → Tool 'kubectl_delete' is not allowed under the current server configuration Suggested fix Derive the destructive set from the tools' own annotations ( destructiveHint ) instead of a hand-maintained name list, or invert the default to a read-only allow-list with explicit opt-in for every mutating tool. A regression test asserting that every tool with destructiveHint: true is refused under ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS=true would keep this from drifting as tools are added. Happy to test a patch.

title: Treat exec_in_pod as destructive under ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS
cleaned_text: Treat exec_in_pod as destructive under ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS Refs #376. Problem With ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS=true , exec_in_pod was still allowed. It permits arbitrary command execution in a pod (e.g. reading the service-account token), and it is not listed in either the README's disabled or allowed lists. Change Add exec_in_pod to destructiveTools in src/index.ts . Add it to the README "Disabled" list. Test that exec_in_pod is blocked. Drift test: fails if any tool with destructiveHint: true is neither blocked nor in the documented-allowed list, so new tools can't silently bypass the mode. Not changed Apply/create/scale/patch/rollout/Helm install+upgrade stay allowed, since the README documents non-destructive mode as keeping create/update operations. Blocking those would be a breaking change and is better as a separate, stricter flag; happy to do that if you prefer. Verification tsc --noEmit clean; tests/non_destructive_tools.test.ts 4/4 pass. The spawn-based integration tests need bun , which wasn't available locally.

title: Server crashes at module load with `No active cluster!` when kubeconfig has no current-context
cleaned_text: Server crashes at module load with No active cluster! when kubeconfig has no current-context Summary mcp-server-kubernetes@4.1.4 builds the Kubernetes API client during module load , so a kubeconfig without a usable current-context kills the process before it can answer initialize . The client never gets a protocol-level error it can act on — it just sees the pipe close mid-handshake. Reproduce export KUBECONFIG=/tmp/empty-kubeconfig.yaml cat > "$KUBECONFIG" <<EOF apiVersion: v1 clusters: null contexts: null current-context: "" kind: Config users: null EOF echo "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":0,\"method\":\"initialize\",\"params\":{\"protocolVersion\":\"2026-06-18\",\"capabilities\":{},\"clientInfo\":{\"name\":\"probe\",\"version\":\"1\"}}}" \ | node dist/index.js Result — exit 1, no JSON-RPC response at all: Error: No active cluster! at KubeConfig.makeApiClient (@kubernetes/client-node/dist/config.js:375:19) at new KubernetesManager (dist/utils/kubernetes-manager.js:82:31) at dist/index.js:130:20 This state is produced by ordinary operations — minikube delete , kind delete cluster , or any teardown that removes the last context. Why this is worth fixing beyond the message The failure surfaces in the host as something unrelated to configuration. In Claude Desktop it reads: Version negotiation failed: the connection closed during the server/discover probe That names the transport layer, not the config layer, so the search starts in the wrong place. It cost us about two days before we ran the server by hand and saw the real stack. Evidence that only the *existence* of a context matters With a context pointing at a deliberately unreachable server ( https://127.0.0.1:1 , nothing listening), the server starts fine and answers: EXIT=0 {"result":{"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25","serverInfo":{"name":"kubernetes","version":"4.1.4"}},...} So the constructor is not validating reachability — only that makeApiClient() does not throw. Tool calls would fail per-call anyway, which is the behaviour a degraded start should have. Suggestion Defer client construction to first use, or catch at load and start in a degraded mode where initialize succeeds and each tool call returns the configuration error. The server would then report No active cluster! in a place the user can actually see it. Happy to send a PR if you agree with the approach. Environment: macOS 15 (Darwin 25.6.0), Node v24.19.0, mcp-server-kubernetes 4.1.4, installed as a Claude Desktop extension.

title: fix: allow null for optional attribute list arguments
cleaned_text: fix: allow null for optional attribute list arguments The four query tools ( query_patients , query_studies , query_series , query_instances ) declare additional_attributes: List[str] = None and exclude_attributes: List[str] = None . FastMCP turns that into {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "default": null} : the schema advertises a null default on a field that doesn't accept null. A client that sends the default back explicitly, e.g. query_studies with "additional_attributes": null , gets a validation error ( Input should be a valid list [type=list_type, input_value=None] ) instead of a result. Fix Annotation-only: List[str] → List[str] | None on those 8 parameters in 4 tools in src/dicom_mcp/server.py . The default stays None and the function bodies already handle None , so behaviour for callers that omit the arguments is unchanged. The schema now reads anyOf: [array of string, null] . Testing New test test_tool_params_with_null_default_accept_null in tests/test_dicom_mcp.py builds the server from tests/test_dicom_servers.yaml , lists its tools (the lifespan never runs, so no DICOM connection), and checks that every parameter with a null default also allows null . It fails on main listing all 8 parameters and passes with this change. title: Fix: serialize PersonName values so JSON tool results don't fail
cleaned_text: Fix: serialize PersonName values so JSON tool results don't fail Problem DicomClient._dataset_to_dict stores elem.value directly into the result dict. For elements with VR PN (e.g. PatientName , ReferringPhysicianName ), pydicom returns a PersonName object, which is not JSON-serializable . When the MCP framework serializes a tool result with json.dumps() , it raises: TypeError: Object of type PersonName is not JSON serializable so query_patients (and any query whose preset includes a PN attribute) fails and patient names can't be returned. The existing try/except around the value assignment doesn't help — it only guards element *access*, not the later JSON serialization done by the framework. Fix Convert PN values to their string form before putting them in the dict: if elem.VR == "PN": result[elem.keyword] = str(elem.value) Also included While touching the PDF retrieval path, this commit also makes extract_pdf_text_from_dicom report actionable errors instead of a generic "C-GET operation failed" : distinguishes *no instance matched* (stale/unknown UIDs) from *matched but the C-STORE sub-operation failed* (e.g. a Structured Report that the PDF-only SCP role can't carry), using the C-GET sub-operation counts; catches C-GET send / dcmread / PyPDF2 exceptions and returns a clear message instead of letting a traceback bubble up to the MCP client; validates the retrieved SOP class; factors the shared C-GET retrieval into a _retrieve_pdf_dataset helper. Testing Verified end-to-end against Orthanc 1.12.11: patient-name queries now serialize correctly, and the PDF error paths return the differentiated messages (stale UIDs / non-PDF instance / malformed PDF).

title: Fail the release workflow when npm stage publish fails
cleaned_text: Fail the release workflow when npm stage publish fails The Release workflow's staging step piped npm stage publish into tee under GitHub's default bash -e , which has no pipefail , so a failed publish still passed the step. This sets pipefail on that step, as the workflow's other multi-line steps already do. What happened The v1.3.1 Release workflow ran twice. The second run (38112041476) got E409 Conflict ... Cannot stage previously published version "1.3.1" from npm, but finished green, and its "Next steps" summary said the version was staged. Nothing was changed on npm: the first run's stage was the only one, and it was the one approved. With this change, a failed npm stage publish fails the step, and the "Next steps" summary is skipped because it only runs after the earlier steps succeed. Other piped commands Every other piped command in release.yml already runs under set -euo pipefail . Every step in verify-release.yml either sets shell: bash , which GitHub runs with -eo pipefail , or sets pipefail itself. ci.yml has no piped commands. Verification The step's old and new forms, run under bash -e with a failing command in place of npm: the old form exits 0 and the new form exits 1. With a succeeding command, the new form exits 0. release.yml parses as valid YAML, and the parsed step script starts with set -euo pipefail . The Release workflow itself was not run, because it would stage a package.

title: Release 1.3.1 as a single bundled file with no runtime dependencies
cleaned_text: Release 1.3.1 as a single bundled file with no runtime dependencies Bundles the server and its dependencies into one file, loads Express only when the HTTP transport starts, and sets the version to 1.3.1. Tools and their output are unchanged. Why On 2026-10-10, Claude Desktop's shared MCP pool (which serves its Code and Cowork sessions) gave up waiting for initialize after about 42 seconds. That launch came about 80 seconds after a reboot and was the first since 1.3.0 was published: npx spent about 40 seconds checking and installing the new version, then the server took another 25 seconds to start (normally about 1 second). This release reduces what the server and npx have to load and install; it does not change npm's own startup or the registry check that @latest makes on every launch. Changes Express loads only for HTTP. startHttp requires the Express app and the Streamable HTTP transport itself, so a stdio launch loads 291 modules instead of 423. It uses require() rather than import() so they share the SDK's CommonJS build with the rest of the server. One bundled file. scripts/bundle.mjs runs esbuild after tsc and writes the whole server to dist/index.js . The package publishes only that file and the .d.ts files, and the runtime dependencies moved to devDependencies , so npx installs one package instead of 91. tsc still emits the per-module files locally for scripts/generate-tool-docs.mjs . License notices. The notices of the 79 bundled packages are appended to the end of dist/index.js , since their code now ships inside ours. Library types. The .d.ts files still import types from @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and zod , which are no longer installed with the package. The changelog says so. deps.dev lists no dependents, and every public use found on GitHub launches the server with npx. Measurements Warm runs on one Windows machine (Node 22.13.1), 1.3.0 against this branch: Scenario | 1.3.0 | 1.3.1 Server start only ( node dist/index.js to initialize reply, median of 14) | 778 ms | 288 ms Launch through npx, already installed (median of 10) | 3.06 s | 2.57 s npx full install, tarballs already in the npm cache (median of 5) | 13.6 s | 4.7 s npx first launch with an empty npm cache (1 run each) | 15.5 s | 3.7 s npx reinstall of only this package, as on 2026-10-10 (median of 5) | 3.6 s | 3.9 s The last row shows no gain: when only this package changes, npx reinstalls one package either way. Nothing here measures startup right after a reboot. Verification npm run lint , npm run typecheck , a clean build and npm run docs:check pass. npm test passes 158/158. The package gate passes on the 1.3.1 tarball: it installs with no other packages, importing it loads 1 module, and the stdio and Streamable HTTP MCP tests pass against the installed bin. An MCP SDK client compared 1.3.0 and this build over stdio on 21 checks: list responses, nine tool calls, error cases, the legacy nasa/apod method, a resource read, a prompt and list-changed notifications. 20 are identical with JSON key order ignored (JPL's APIs vary key order between calls). The remaining one is a per-request timestamp inside CMR's cursor, which also differs between two calls to 1.3.0. HTTP mode: initialize returns 200 with a result and tools/list returns 35 tools. Claude Code CLI test: both tarballs were launched through cmd /c npx with claude -p --mcp-config … --strict-mcp-config . Both connected with 35 tools and made the same four calls with the same results: APOD for 2024-01-01 with its image, SBDB for Bennu, jpl_jd_cal for 2000-01-01, and an APOD date before 1995 that is rejected with the same message.

title: Release 1.3.0 with MAST observation, data product and TESS full-frame image tools
cleaned_text: Release 1.3.0 with MAST observation, data product and TESS full-frame image tools Adds three tools for the Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes (MAST), NASA's archive for TESS, Hubble, JWST, Kepler and other missions, and sets the version to 1.3.0. Existing tools are unchanged. New tools nasa_mast_observations : observations of a named object, a TIC ID or a sky position. For TESS (the default), it matches TESS Input Catalog stars and lists their light curves by sector: SPOC 2-minute and 20-second light curves, plus high-level science product (HLSP) light curves made from full-frame images (QLP, TESS-SPOC, TARS and others). Other collections ( HST , JWST , Kepler , all and others) use MAST's position search. nasa_mast_products : the files of up to 20 observations, with type, size and a download URL for each. It lists science files by default; subgroups and minimum_recommended narrow Hubble and JWST observations, which can list hundreds of files. nasa_tess_ffi : the TESS sectors, cameras and CCDs whose full-frame images cover a position, with sector dates and a TESSCut cutout URL for each sector. The tools return download links, not files, because the FITS files are often tens of megabytes and an MCP client can't read them anyway. Notes for review TESS searches go by TIC ID. MAST's footprint-based position search took 65–115 seconds uncached for TESS targets, and once ran past a 90-second timeout. TESS light curves carry the TIC ID as their target name, so the tool matches TIC stars first ( Mast.Catalogs.Tic.Cone ) and then filters on that ID, which takes about a second. Other collections still use the position search (2–9 seconds in testing). Multi-sector searches aren't counted as sectors. SPOC and TESS-SPOC multi-sector transit searches (obs_id …-s0001-s0039-… ) carry only their last sector as sequence_number . They're listed as sector ranges and left out of the sector lists, which otherwise reported sectors the star was never observed in. Position searches default to a 60″ radius. Recent observations of fast-moving nearby stars lie far from their catalog (J2000) position. TRAPPIST-1 is now about 25″ away, so a 10″ circle missed all 121 of its NIRSpec slit observations. TESS TIC matching keeps 10″. Stalled MAST requests are re-sent. MAST latency is heavy-tailed: a request that usually takes half a second sometimes stalls for a minute, while the identical request sent next answers at once. Each attempt gets 30 seconds, with at most 3 attempts within a 90-second budget. All of these requests are read-only. The optional sector-date lookup in nasa_tess_ffi gives up after 15 seconds and the sector list is returned without dates. Results are sorted locally. MAST's row order changes between identical queries, so each search fetches one large page and sorts it, rather than paging. Small refactor. The comma-separated list helper moved from the SSC tool to util/validation.ts so the new tools can share it; SSC behavior is unchanged. Verification npm run lint , npm run typecheck , a clean build and npm run docs:check all pass. npm test passes 158/158, including 14 new unit tests with mocked MAST and TESSCut responses. The package gate passes: the 1.3.0 tarball installed outside the repo passes the stdio and Streamable HTTP MCP tests. NASA_MCP_LIVE=1 npm run test:live passes 10/10 against the real services, FIRMS included, with four new MAST checks; one of them confirms a light-curve download link answers. An MCP SDK stdio client against dist/index.js sees 35 tools; all three new tools and the nasa/tess-ffi alias answer. Claude Code CLI test: the local build was run as an MCP server with claude -p --mcp-config … --strict-mcp-config on both new README prompts. *"Which TESS sectors observed Pi Mensae, and where can I download its 2-minute light curves?"* returns 24 sectors with a download link for each ( nasa_mast_observations , nasa_tess_ffi and nasa_mast_products , 51 s). *"Has JWST observed TRAPPIST-1, and with which instruments?"* returns MIRI imaging (257 observations), NIRSpec slit (121) and NIRISS SOSS (13) from one call (46 s). The first run of this prompt led to the instrument counts and the 60″ radius above.

title: Release 1.2.0 with compact DONKI output
cleaned_text: Release 1.2.0 with compact DONKI output Release PR for 1.2.0 . It contains the APOD/DONKI migrations and nine new tools from #15, plus the DONKI output change below. It sets the version in package.json / package-lock.json and turns the CHANGELOG's "Unreleased" section into ## 1.2.0 , as RELEASING.md step 1 expects. DONKI: compact output by default nasa_donki returned DONKI's full JSON. A month of CMEs (108 records) produced about 270,000 characters, which failed with the server's 250,000-character limit. A month of CMEAnalysis records (about 66,000 characters) was too large for some clients' tool-output limits. response_mode: "compact" (default) returns one line per event with the fields that matter for its type: Type | Fields FLR | class, peak, begin/end, source and region CME | start, source, speed, half-angle and type from the most accurate analysis, and the modeled Earth arrival (glancing or impact, highest Kp) GST | highest Kp and when IPS | time and location WSA | CMEs used and modeled Earth and spacecraft arrivals Notifications | type, ID, summary and link SEP, MPC, RBE, HSS | time, instruments and linked events Every line also lists linked events. A month of CMEs is now about 21 KB. response_mode: "raw" returns the full records as before. The retained resource always holds the full records. limit keeps the most recent N events. DONKI: 30-day window The CCMC API rejects ranges over 30 days ( 400 API Error: Date range cannot exceed 30 days. You requested 31 days. , as text/plain ). With only endDate , it counts its default start back from *today*, so an older endDate fails with "startDate cannot be after endDate". The tool now: rejects spans over 30 days in the schema; rejects a lone startDate more than 30 days ago, suggesting an endDate ; rejects a future startDate ; sends startDate = endDate - 30 days when only endDate is given, which matches the default the tool already documented. Release notes The CHANGELOG 1.2.0 intro flags that nasa_apod and nasa_donki parameters and output changed, and that APOD and DONKI no longer work in 1.1.0. npm currently has latest = 1.0.14 and next = 1.1.0. 1.2.0 is not on npm. Verification npm run lint , npm run typecheck , npm test (144 tests) and npm run docs:check pass. node dist/index.js --version prints 1.2.0 . New unit tests cover: the 30-day rules and the endDate -only start; exact compact lines for FLR, CME (with a modeled Earth arrival), GST, notifications and SEP; raw together with limit . Over MCP stdio with the Inspector CLI and NASA_API_KEY blanked for the server: a September CME month returned 108 records in about 21 KB; wsa with response_mode: "raw" and limit: 1 returned the latest record; a lone startDate of 2026-01-01 returned the 30-day message. The README solar-storm prompt, run through an MCP client with only this server enabled, now finishes with every DONKI call succeeding (FLR, GST, CMEAnalysis and IPS for September).

title: Migrate APOD and DONKI to their new APIs and add InSight, TLE, SSC, TechPort, TechTransfer, Trek and Mission Design tools
cleaned_text: Migrate APOD and DONKI to their new APIs and add InSight, TLE, SSC, TechPort, TechTransfer, Trek and Mission Design tools APOD migration api.nasa.gov/planetary/apod returns 503/504, and the api.nasa.gov catalog says the legacy API goes offline on 2026-12-01. nasa_apod , the nasa://apod/image resource template and both APOD prompts now use the NASA Science API ( science.nasa.gov/wp-json/wp/v2/apod-basic ), which needs no key. What I found while probing it: date_from / date_to only accept YYMMDD ( 260901 ). 2026-09-01 , 20260901 and ISO timestamps all return HTTP 400. Single dates use /apod-basic/{YYMMDD} . per_page is capped at 25, so ranges (still up to 100 days) are paged using x-wp-totalpages and returned oldest first. url is the article permalink, not the image. The picture is the first in basic_html . Posts from before about 2005 have a generic placeholder hdurl ( …/cosmic-origins/images/misc/news-thumbnail.png ), which is ignored. Videos have no video URL in the JSON. It is read from the or in basic_html , and hdurl is shown as the still frame. Missing days return 404 apod_basic_not_found , which is reported as "has no picture for YYYY-MM-DD". Changes: count and thumbs are retired through retiredParameters : the new API has no random mode, and the catalog says thumbs is disabled. They were also removed from the prompts. Dates before 1995-06-16 and future dates are rejected before any request. Future dates are rejected because YYMMDD would wrap around after 2094. Title, credit/copyright and explanation are plain text. HTML is stripped and entities decoded (new src/util/html.ts ). Embedded images use a 1024 px rendition from assets.science.nasa.gov/dynamicimage , falling back to the original (resized GIFs return 404). The resource template returns one entry, without the 6–9 KB basic_html page. DONKI move CCMC moved the public DONKI API from kauai.ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/WS/get/... to ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI-API/get/... on 2026-09-30, and api.nasa.gov/DONKI/* now returns a 301 to CCMC's news page even with a valid key. The new endpoints returned 404 during the maintenance window and started serving data at 16:43 UTC (12:43 PM EDT). Before switching I checked all 11 endpoints (GST, CME, CMEAnalysis, IPS, FLR, SEP, MPC, RBE, HSS, WSAEnlilSimulations, notifications) on the new host: All return application/json arrays, with the same record fields as before ( flrID , beginTime , classType , activityID , ...). No key is needed; an api_key parameter is ignored. Empty ranges return [] . Without dates, DONKI defaults to the last 30 days. Paths are case-sensitive ( /flr and /FLR/ return JSON 404s), and the tool already uses the documented case. nasa_donki now calls the new host through httpRequest instead of nasaApiGet , with no key. Its unit test, description, the key lists in .env.example , the README, --help and config.ts , the Inspector examples and the CHANGELOG are updated. New tools Each tool was probed live before being added. Tool | Source | Key nasa_insight_weather | api.nasa.gov/insight_weather/ | NASA_API_KEY nasa_tle | tle.ivanstanojevic.me/api/tle (CelesTrak data) | none nasa_ssc_observatories , nasa_ssc_locations | sscweb.gsfc.nasa.gov/WS/sscr/2 | none nasa_techport | techport.nasa.gov/api (GET search and project) | none nasa_techtransfer | technology.nasa.gov/api/api/{patent,patent_issued,software,spinoff}/{q} | none nasa_trek_layers , nasa_trek_tile | trek.nasa.gov catalog and WMTS (Mars, Moon, Vesta) | none jpl_mission_design | ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/mdesign.api (modes A and Q) | none Notes: InSight is labelled historical in the description and in every result. The feed still returns sols 675–681 (2020-10-19 to 2020-10-26), and the catalog says "Last Updated: 3/30/2021". Its PDF documentation calls AT "degrees Celsius" in the quick start but "°F" in the field table. The values (−97 to −16) match Celsius, so the tool labels them °C. SSC returns Jackson-typed JSON ( ["java.util.ArrayList", [...]] ), which is unwrapped. A month of ISS positions at 60 s is 7.8 MB, so resolutionFactor is chosen automatically to keep each call to about 8,000 values, or rejected with a suggested minimum when the caller sets one too small. TechTransfer : every api.nasa.gov/techtransfer/... form I tried (with the key) returns the HTML help page, and that page points to technology.nasa.gov/api/api/... , which returns JSON without a key. The service ignores paging and returns all matches, so limit is applied locally. TechPort : GET /api/projects/search and /api/projects/{id} work without a token. POST search returns 401 (it needs a session nonce), so it isn't used. GET search honours limit but ignores offset . Contact emails are kept out of text and resources. Trek : the catalog filter mirrors the one the Trek API docs page uses, plus the layer's trekProjection , because the polar index mixes north and south layers. Tiles are addressed through each layer's WMTSCapabilities.xml , and matrices inside XML comments are ignored (the Moon WAC mosaic has some). Tiles can also be picked by latitude/longitude on global equirectangular grids. Tile URLs outside trek.nasa.gov are refused. SSD/CNEOS : the catalog entry lists CAD, Fireball, Mission Design, NHATS, Scout and Sentry. Mission Design was the only one without a tool. The TLE API's {"response":{"message":…}} error bodies are now summarized. No new credentials are needed, so config.ts gets no new registerSecret . .env.example , the README table, the --help text and the config.ts comment now list which tools use NASA_API_KEY . Not added, and why Mission Design modes M and T : mode M returns porkchop grids (104 KB for about 1,300 points, up to 1.5 million points). Mode T took 29 s for a 30-day span and over 120 s for the documented one-year example, beyond the 30 s request deadline. Ceres Trek : its catalog returns HTTP 500. The api.nasa.gov entry only covers Vesta, Moon and Mars. SSD APIs outside the catalog entry ( sb_ident , sb_radar , sb_sat , sbdb_query , sbwobs , horizons_lookup ): not in scope of the catalog comparison. They are candidates for a follow-up. Known issue (not changed here) nasa_donki still returns the full upstream JSON. With the solar-storm prompt, a month of CMEs (106 records) exceeded the server's 250,000-character limit, and a month of CMEAnalysis output was too large for the client's tool-output limit. The client recovered using the FLR, GST and IPS results, but compact per-record summaries for DONKI would be a worthwhile follow-up. This behavior predates the move. Verification npm test (143 tests), npm run lint and npm run docs:check pass. NASA_MCP_LIVE=1 runs the new live APOD check, which passes without a key. Unit tests use test/helpers/fake-fetch.ts for every new tool and for APOD (range paging, placeholder hdurl , GIF fallback, video URLs, retired parameters). Every new or changed tool was called over MCP stdio with the Inspector CLI ( node dist/index.js , keys read from .env ) and returned real data. That covered tools/list (32 tools); APOD for latest, 2015-07-14, a 7-day range, count (migration error), resources/read and prompts/get ; InSight; TLE by ID and by search; SSC observatories and locations; TechPort search and project; TechTransfer patents and software; Trek layers (Mars, Vesta south pole) and tiles (Mars by lat/lon, Moon zoom 2, Vesta south pole); and Mission Design objects and lists. No key value appeared in any output. README example prompts were added only for tools that returned real data, including the solar-storm prompt once DONKI was live. nasa_donki was called over MCP stdio for all 11 types (2026-09-20 to 2026-09-29) with NASA_API_KEY blanked for the server process, and every call returned data or an explicit "No DONKI ... events". Each new README example prompt was also run through an MCP client in a non-interactive session with only this server enabled. Every prompt selected the intended tools (for example nasa_trek_layers then nasa_trek_tile by latitude/longitude for Olympus Mons, and jpl_mission_design with crit: 3 for the lowest delta-v NEOs) and answered from live data.

title: 1.1.0: validated tool registry, CMR compact output and cursors, FIRMS fix, tested release pipeline
cleaned_text: 1.1.0: validated tool registry, CMR compact output and cursors, FIRMS fix, tested release pipeline Reliability fixes and CMR improvements for 1.1.0 . Baseline: main at 8d66b2b, npm latest = 1.0.14. CI on main had been red since 1.0.13 because there were no tests. What changed Reliability One typed, allowlisted registry now drives tools/list , validation and dispatch. Defaults are applied before handlers run, on every entry point: tools/call , the legacy nasa/* methods, prompts/execute and resource templates. Tool names are never turned into import paths. Unknown tools return JSON-RPC -32602 ; invalid arguments return isError results. Documented aliases ( nasa/apod , nasa/mars-rover , jpl/jd_cal , …) are explicit. nasa/mars-rover was broken before. No fabricated data. The startup sample records and fake template generators are gone, and templates now fetch real data. Images are embedded only when the download really is an image from a nasa.gov host. Resources: Each server instance has its own bounded store (50 entries, 16 MB). Entries are keyed by the full canonical arguments and carry source and retrieved_at . The stateless HTTP transport creates a store per request, so nothing is shared between clients. FIRMS: Uses FIRMS_MAP_KEY and the documented path /api/area/csv/KEY/SOURCE/w,s,e,n/DAYS[/DATE] , with bbox as the canonical area. latitude / longitude now need radius_km and are converted to a bbox; polar and antimeridian cases are rejected. Uses an RFC 4180 CSV parser, and detects error text or HTML even when FIRMS returns HTTP 200. The key is redacted everywhere. Upstream errors: every request has a deadline and a size limit. 429s, timeouts, HTML and non-JSON errors become MCP errors; they are never reported as successful empty results. Packaging: Exact dependency ranges and a regenerated lockfile. Removed axios, express, cors, @anthropic-ai/sdk and form-data in favour of built-in fetch / FormData . npm audit --omit=dev reports 0 vulnerabilities (8 before). build no longer runs npm install . The package is an explicit file allowlist with a prepack guard, so tests, .env and fixtures can't ship. The CLI starts only when run directly, not on import. The version comes from package.json , and stdout carries only MCP messages. CMR ( nasa_cmr ) Filters: All verified collection and granule filters are exposed and validated, including collection_concept_id , geometry, platform/instrument/project, processing level, data format, download/browse/online flags, facets and verified sort keys. bbox is translated to bounding_box (CMR rejected bbox with HTTP 400). Filters that don't apply to the chosen search type are rejected instead of dropped. Output: Compact typed envelope by default: status , search_type , results , returned_count , total_hits from CMR-Hits , next_cursor , source , retrieved_at , warnings . response_mode: "raw" returns the upstream metadata; fields selects fields and shapes both the structured and text output. Separate JSON and UMM-JSON adapters. Search After cursor: Stateless ( cmr1. + base64url JSON), versioned, capped at 8 KB and re-validated on decode. Continue with {"cursor": …} alone. Conflicting filters, sort or search type are rejected, never silently restarted. page / offset remain as a deprecated, mutually exclusive compatibility path. JPL / other tools. Every advertised parameter was checked against the live APIs. Ones that never worked now return a migration message: Sentry date_min / date_max ; Scout orbit_id / summary ; Fireball req_energy / req_impact_e . Scout plot / file values were fixed, and Sentry/Scout limit is now applied locally. Other fixes: Tool | Fix GIBS | Sent WMS 1.3.0 bounding boxes in the wrong axis order, so it requested a different region. POWER | time_standard was ignored upstream; it is now sent as time-standard . Exoplanet | nstedAPI rejects ps and ignores top ; now uses TAP. EONET | Silently broadened queries that returned nothing; now reports no results. Mars Rover Photos | Upstream is retired (HTTP 404 "No such app"); the tool reports that accurately. Compatibility decisions Version 1.1.0, chosen by the maintainer. The release still contains changes clients can notice, and CHANGELOG.md lists them as breaking with migration notes: CMR returns the compact envelope by default. Adding response_mode: "raw" alone does not restore the old raw-by-default response. Strict schemas reject unknown parameters. FIRMS needs FIRMS_MAP_KEY and an explicit area. Requires Node ≥ 22 (Node 20 is EOL). The unused global.mcp * functions and the nasa/subscribe no-op were removed. Kept: TypeScript, the package name, the CLI command, stdio, Streamable HTTP, and all 23 tools. The cursor is unsigned by design. It only carries values a caller could pass directly, the server fixes host, path and headers, and decoded contents go through the same schema as normal input. No per-request secret and no in-memory map are needed. Test evidence npm test : 118/118 pass locally on Windows, Node 22.13.1. That is unit tests on local fixtures plus stdio and Streamable HTTP integration tests driven by the MCP SDK client against the real CLI, including a raw stdout contamination check, clean shutdown and 8 concurrent HTTP clients. The stdio integration file ran 15× in a row without a failure after fixing an ordering flake in the test. Package gate ( scripts/package-smoke.mjs ), locally on Windows: Tarball with 90 files, sha512 integrity checked. Installed outside the repo with runtime dependencies only; no development packages present, and nothing resolves from the checkout. Bin --version prints 1.1.0, and 5/5 transport tests pass against the installed bin. Live scenario through an MCP client against the installed tarball : CMR collections ( total_hits from CMR-Hits ), cursor-only page 2 with no repeated records, and granules with fields . Invalid granule+keyword request rejected; APOD with DEMO_KEY , SBDB, EONET, Exoplanet TAP and CAD all worked. FIRMS without a key gives a clear configuration error; Mars Rover reported DEMO_KEY rate limiting accurately. Claude Code connected to the installed tarball through a temporary --mcp-config and registered all 23 tools. A full model-driven run is pending a Claude Code re-login on the maintainer's machine. Not yet run: live FIRMS (no authorized FIRMS_MAP_KEY available). The deterministic FIRMS tests all pass. Security note 1.0.0–1.0.14 on npm shipped a hard-coded FIRMS MAP_KEY ( dist/tests/direct-api-test.js ), and 1.0.0–1.0.12 shipped dist/.env containing a NASA API key. Cause: setupEnvironment() copied .env into dist/ . Both keys must be rotated by the owner. Git history was not rewritten. Release plan CI green on Linux, Windows and macOS × Node 22/24, plus the audit job; then merge. Tag the merged commit v1.1.0 (annotated) and draft the GitHub Release. One-time owner setup: configure the npm trusted publisher (ProgramComputer / NASA-MCP-server / release.yml / environment npm-release ). The existing local npm tokens return 401, and the 2025 NPM_TOKEN secret is not used. gh workflow run release.yml -f tag=v1.1.0 -f dist_tag=next . This re-tests the tag, packs once, runs the package gate, publishes that exact tarball under next with provenance, then verifies registry integrity, a fresh install, and the MCP tests on Linux and Windows. Owner promotes: npm dist-tag add @programcomputer/nasa-mcp-server@1.1.0 latest . OIDC cannot run dist-tag . Verify latest and a fresh npx run, then publish the GitHub Release. See RELEASING.md for the full runbook.

title: Invalid JSON error when starting
cleaned_text: Invalid JSON error when starting When I added the npx installation to my local MCP server in Claude, I get the error: Unexpected token '◇', "◇ injected"... is not valid JSON I dug into the source code and found out that it was because of the package json declaring an empty dotenv version and dotenv 17 onwards prints out a startup banner by default on every startup and stdio mcp servers uses stdout exclusively as its JSON-RPC channel so the default startup banner corrupts the stream which results in the client failing to parse the handshake. I have opened a PR #8 which solves this by pinning the dotenv version and also suppressing the banner.

title: feat(plugin-token): add RugShield 402 pre-trade honeypot and simulation action
cleaned_text: feat(plugin-token): add RugShield 402 pre-trade honeypot and simulation action feat(plugin-token): add RugShield 402 pre-trade honeypot and simulation action Summary Adds the RugShield 402 pre-trade honeypot simulation and token safety tool & action ( RUGSHIELD_AUDIT ) to @solana-agent-kit/token-plugin . Autonomous Solana agents executing DEX swaps (via Jupiter, Pump.fun, or Raydium) frequently face honeypots, developer token-lock dump traps, and excessive sell taxes. RugShield executes real state-override calldata simulations to verify tokens can be liquidated before an agent commits capital. Capabilities Added fetchRugshieldScan(mint) : Queries RugShield 402 ( https://rugshield-402.onrender.com/v1/scan/preview ) returning: is_honeypot : Boolean flag indicating whether sell simulation reverts or fails. buy_tax_bps / sell_tax_bps : Detected token tax in basis points. liquidity_usd : Verifiable pool depth. sybil_clusters : Number of coordinated developer/insider wallet clusters. recommendation : "SAFE_TO_SWAP" or "DO_NOT_TRADE" . blink_url : 1-click Dialect Solana Blink link for in-feed verification. RUGSHIELD_AUDIT : Standard Action definition compatible with SolanaAgentKit , LangChain, and ElizaOS agent runtimes. Integration Details Follows the identical architectural pattern to rugcheck in packages/plugin-token . Zero additional dependencies required. Includes automated zero-fee preview fallback so agents can audit tokens without pre-funding custom API credentials.

title: fix(plugin-token): bound token-2022 close loop and report accurate closed count (#628)
cleaned_text: fix(plugin-token): bound token-2022 close loop and report accurate closed count (#628) Summary of Changes Bounds the Token-2022 instruction loop by Math.min(remainingSlots, token_2022.length) to prevent out-of-bounds indexing and undefined instructions from being passed to transaction.add() . Calculates size accurately as splCount + token2022Count (actual instructions added to the transaction) instead of naive total candidates spl_token.length + token_2022.length . Returns early with { signature: "", size: 0 } immediately when both candidate arrays are empty before instantiating Transaction . Root Cause / Technical Context Fixes #628. In closeEmptyTokenAccounts : When token_2022.length < (MAX_INSTRUCTIONS - spl_token.length) , the loop for (let i = 0; i < Math.max(0, MAX_INSTRUCTIONS - spl_token.length); i++) indexed past token_2022.length , executing transaction.add(undefined) which throws a runtime TypeError: Cannot add undefined or null instruction to Transaction . When candidate accounts exceeded MAX_INSTRUCTIONS (40), size was reported as spl_token.length + token_2022.length (e.g. 50) rather than the actual 40 instructions assembled into the transaction. Verification & Testing Validated across all permutation boundary cases: === Testing Fixed Logic === • 0 classic / 0 token_2022: PASS ✅ (size=0, ixs=0) • 1 classic / 0 token_2022: PASS ✅ (size=1, ixs=1) • 0 classic / 1 token_2022: PASS ✅ (size=1, ixs=1) • 10 classic / 5 token_2022: PASS ✅ (size=15, ixs=15) • 40 classic / 0 token_2022: PASS ✅ (size=40, ixs=40) • 50 classic / 10 token_2022 (overflow): PASS ✅ (size=40, ixs=40) • 20 classic / 30 token_2022 (split): PASS ✅ (size=40, ixs=40) ALL TEST CASES PASSED WITH 100% SUCCESS! Impact & Compatibility Breaking changes: None. Pure bugfix restoring reliability of closeEmptyTokenAccounts .

title: Would an external escrow plugin (pay on verified delivery, USDC) be welcome in the docs or examples?
cleaned_text: Would an external escrow plugin (pay on verified delivery, USDC) be welcome in the docs or examples? Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. Agents built with Solana Agent Kit can pay per request (x402 and similar), but not "pay when the work is verified". When an agent hires another agent or a service for a deliverable (a dataset, a report, a file), neither side is protected: pay up front, and nothing may be delivered; pay afterwards, and the provider carries all the risk. Describe the solution you'd like We maintain an MIT plugin for this: @selecto-infra/agent-adapters 0.4.3, distributed as a GitHub Release (not on the npm registry yet), subpath @selecto-infra/agent-adapters/solana-agent-kit , peer solana-agent-kit ^2.0.10 . import { createRufusSakPlugin } from "@selecto-infra/agent-adapters/solana-agent-kit"; agent.use(createRufusSakPlugin(cfg)); It adds RUFUS_PREVIEW_TASK , RUFUS_CREATE_TASK , RUFUS_GET_TASK , RUFUS_GET_RECEIPT , RUFUS_REQUEST_REFUND and RUFUS_SUBMIT_EVIDENCE , all with strict schemas. The payer funds a USDC escrow on Solana. Funds are released when the delivered artifact's SHA-256 matches the hash fixed at funding time, or on the payer's signed approval. After the deadline the payer can refund without anyone's permission. The kit's own wallet is never used for escrow signing. Spending goes through a host-side authorize() bound to an exact cost preview, plus a spend policy the LLM cannot change. Tested inside SolanaAgentKit.use() and executeAction() at 2.0.10, with no network or LLM calls in the tests. Install: npm install https://github.com/SiiahK/rufus-agent-adapters/releases/download/v0.4.3/selecto-infra-agent-adapters-0.4.3.tgz . Would a small examples/select-escrow/ folder, or a docs entry pointing to the package, be in scope? No change to kit code. If you prefer third-party plugins to stay external, that is fine, and we will not open a PR. Describe alternatives you've considered Pay-per-request (x402) covers single calls well. We see escrow as the complement for deliverables, not a replacement. Each integrator writing its own escrow logic duplicates sensitive payment code. Additional context Disclosure, so you can judge it: Program: the escrow program is E3XAx7qEKHte9kmWKhuyAVxb8CgE2g4k5FqkrRx2kdsF on mainnet. Its deployed binary is reproducible from source in a pinned Linux container. Fees: a 2% creation fee, of which 25% goes to the integrator that ships the plugin. Audit: no external audit yet . Pilot limit: 10 USDC per task. Track record: six end-to-end mainnet lifecycles so far, all between our own wallets; no external users yet. Links: SDK: https://github.com/SiiahK/rufus-agent-adapters Developer docs: https://api.tryaigility.com/developers Public receipts: https://api.tryaigility.com/v2/receipts We ask for no promotion.

title: fix(deps): resolve jito-ts nested @solana/web3.js conflict breaking plugin-defi load
cleaned_text: fix(deps): resolve jito-ts nested @solana/web3.js conflict breaking plugin-defi load Fixes #466. Problem Importing @solana-agent-kit/plugin-defi threw Error: Cannot find module 'rpc-websockets/dist/lib/client' . Root cause: jito-ts@3.0.1 (transitive via @drift-labs/sdk → @pythnetwork/pyth-solana-receiver → @pythnetwork/solana-utils ) nests @solana/web3.js@1.77.4 , which hardcodes require('rpc-websockets/dist/lib/client') . That deep path was renamed to .cjs in rpc-websockets 7.11+, so module resolution fails whenever a modern rpc-websockets is hoisted. I confirmed the exact require strings in the published tarballs: web3.js@1.77.4 → require('rpc-websockets/dist/lib/client') ❌ web3.js@1.95.0+ → require('rpc-websockets') (package entry) ✅ Fix Added a pnpm override in the root package.json (dependency convergence, no runtime patching): "pnpm": { "overrides": { "jito-ts>@solana/web3.js": "^1.95.0" } } The regenerated lockfile shows jito-ts now nesting @solana/web3.js@1.98.2 , and zero copies of 1.77.4 remain anywhere in the tree. This matches the workaround the issue reporter confirmed working (npm overrides forcing web3.js ^1.95.0 under jito-ts), implemented at the repo level so every contributor/CI run gets it. Also added a troubleshooting section to packages/plugin-defi/README.md with the equivalent root-level pin for npm, pnpm, yarn, and bun app consumers — package-manager overrides don't propagate from a published library, so consumers need the one-line pin at their own app root. Verification (reproduced both ways) In a scratch project with plain jito-ts@3.0.1 : Without override → nested @solana/web3.js@1.77.4 ; requiring lib/index.cjs.js (the exact module from the issue's stack trace) throws Error: Cannot find module 'rpc-websockets/dist/lib/client' — the reported error, reproduced exactly. With this override → nested @solana/web3.js@1.99.0 ; the same require loads successfully . Lockfile audit: grep -c "1\.77\.4" pnpm-lock.yaml → 0 . jito-ts snapshots resolve @solana/web3.js to 1.98.2 in this repo. Why this approach (vs alternatives) Runtime patching (#522) : monkey-patching node_modules or shimming at import time is fragile — it breaks on every fresh install, fights with bundlers, and has to be maintained forever. Dependency convergence fixes the actual resolution graph. Bumping @drift-labs/sdk : the repo pins 2.108.0-beta.6 ; latest is 2.163.x-beta — 55 beta versions of churn, and the newest @pythnetwork/solana-utils *still* pulls jito-ts@^3.0.1 , so the broken nesting would survive the bump anyway. Waiting on jito-ts : upstream "fixed" it in v4 by pinning rpc-websockets@7.10.0 , but the chain resolves jito-ts@^3.0.1 → 3.0.1 , which has no such pin. The override is the minimal, targeted, reversible fix. Notes Deliberately scoped to the version pin only; no code changes, no new dependencies The override is narrowly targeted ( jito-ts>@solana/web3.js ) so it can't disturb other consumers' web3.js ranges Lockfile diff is minimal — only the overrides: section, removal of the stale 1.77.4 tree, and the jito-ts snapshot updates (no registry metadata churn)

title: feat(plugin-misc): add TxWhy transaction repair (repair, send with repair)
cleaned_text: feat(plugin-misc): add TxWhy transaction repair (repair, send with repair) What Adds TxWhy to plugin-misc : two tools and two actions that let an agent repair a failing transaction inside its send loop instead of giving up on custom program error: 0x1771 . txwhyRepairTransaction(agent, { transaction | signature }) → exact cause (failing instruction, decoded error) and, when fixable, a rebuilt unsigned transaction with a simulation proof. Actions: REPAIR_SOLANA_TRANSACTION . txwhySendWithRepair(agent, transaction) → simulate on the agent's own RPC; if it passes, sign and send (no external call at all); if it would fail, repair, verify the repair locally , sign with the agent's wallet, send. Honours config.signOnly . Action: SEND_TRANSACTION_WITH_REPAIR . What gets repaired: compute unit limit, expired blockhash, priority fee, loaded-accounts data limit, and Jupiter slippage (the swap instruction is replaced with a fresh quote for the same trade; the user's tolerance is never widened). Everything else comes back as a diagnosis. Why an agent can trust it A service that hands back a transaction to sign could hand back anything. So @txwhy/sdk ships the check, it runs on the agent's machine before the wallet sees the transaction, and this plugin always runs it: same fee payer, same signers, every non-ComputeBudget instruction byte for byte in the same order, at most one Jupiter swap replaced by an equivalent one (same wallet, source and receiving token accounts, output mint, amount, slippage). Anything else is refused and never signed. The verifier has no network access and is tested against 15 tampering attacks (extra transfer, redirected fee, new signer, widened slippage, proceeds redirected). Notes New dependency @txwhy/sdk (11 KB, peer dep @solana/web3.js which the plugin already has). No API key, no config. No wallet keys leave the process; TxWhy only ever sees and returns unsigned bytes. Service: https://txwhy.vercel.app (MIT). Also exposed as an MCP server and HTTP API. Built for Colosseum's Crypto World's Fair; happy to reshape to whatever structure you prefer. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: Mac Messages MCP v1.1.0
cleaned_text: Security MCP tool and resource output derived from Messages and Contacts is serialized at a single untrusted-output boundary ( present_untrusted_output ). Newlines become the literal two-character sequence \n ; invisible, bidi, and format Unicode is escaped; fence terminators inside content are defanged; and the payload is wrapped in so it is not treated as instructions. Fence idempotence uses an in-process marker, so attacker text that only looks already-fenced is still re-serialized. This is not an anti-injection guarantee. Clients must still gate tool_send_message . The locked mcp 1.3.0 FastMCP API has no elicitation, and a confirm=True argument is not human confirmation. Coordinated reports from Grégoire Compagnon (obeone) prompted this output-boundary work. CodeQL actions are pinned to commit SHAs and analyze Python with security-extended queries. Dependabot covers the uv and github-actions ecosystems. A Semgrep OSS scan ( semgrep scan in the official semgrep/semgrep image) replaced the unused GitHub-starter Semgrep workflow that required SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN . Added Added MAC_MESSAGES_REGION to override the region used when parsing national-format numbers, for Macs configured for a different region than their phone numbers belong to. Added phonenumbers as a dependency, replacing the hand-rolled country-code heuristics. Fixed Phone numbers written in national format are now expanded to E.164 against the region the Mac is configured for instead of being assumed North American. A French number such as 06 39 98 00 01 was previously turned into +10639980001 , which made contact listings show the wrong country code and made message lookups, attachment lookups and iMessage availability checks miss handles that exist in the database. Handle matching now compares numbers on their canonical E.164 form, so an E.164 input finds a handle stored in national format and the reverse. Lookups that find nothing through the indexed query fall back to a canonical scan of the handle table. _looks_like_phone_input accepts dot separators, so 05.39.98.00.03 is treated as a phone number rather than a contact name. Address book entries whose number cannot be read as a phone number, such as SMS short codes, entries carrying a trailing label, and foreign numbers saved without their + , keep a digits-only key instead of being dropped from the contacts map. Contact name resolution looks up the canonical form, the digits, and the national number, so both sides of the comparison meet whichever form the entry was stored under. The region is read from a macOS regional override when there is one. A Mac running in English with its Region set to France reports en_US@rg=frzzzz , whose effective region is France rather than the United States, and its national numbers were still being given a +1 . Email handles are compared case-insensitively on both sides, so an address stored in mixed case is found whichever way it is typed. Email addresses are looked up as handles instead of being sent to fuzzy contact-name matching, which answered "No contacts found" for any address that is not in the address book and returned before the handle query could run. Recipients are refused for being dialable only from inside their own local area rather than for having fewer than ten digits. The digit floor rejected every numbering plan shorter than the North American one, an eight-digit Norwegian number among them, while still letting through the seven-digit North American local form it was meant to catch. Several numbering plans consider a short national form possible, a seven-digit North American local among them, so a half-typed number was being expanded and handed to Messages.app. Credit: Grégoire Compagnon (obeone) for the region-aware phone and email handle work (#64). Changed Upgraded Pillow from 12.2.0 to 12.3.0. Updated indirect dependencies: python-dotenv 1.2.2, idna 3.15, and pygments 2.20.0. GitHub Actions: actions/checkout v7.0.1 (SHA-pinned), astral-sh/setup-uv v10, and pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish 1.14.2. CI jobs now set timeout-minutes so a stuck macOS runner acquire fails closed.

title: Send into an existing iMessage group chat
cleaned_text: Send into an existing iMessage group chat The send-only adapter accepts only one raw phone number. Kevin's client work often targets an existing iMessage group (a couple, a household), and the only route today is driving Messages.app by hand. Wanted: tool_send_message accepts the exact Messages chat id of an existing group ( ;+;chat , which is chat.guid and Heimdall's sourceThreadId ), stays iMessage-only, correlates the outgoing row through the chat, and returns a fixed token. The sender must not resolve, list, or search chats (ADR-0001 boundary). Constraints found while scoping: outgoing group rows have handle_id = 0 , and group iMessages never report delivery on macOS 26, so the result can only ever be "sent".

title: feat(mcp): reactions, paging, scoped search, attachments, scheduling
cleaned_text: feat(mcp): reactions, paging, scoped search, attachments, scheduling Repro Issue #95 asked which capabilities were missing from the MCP surface; the maintainer answered "all of them". Reading mac_messages_mcp/messages.py and mac_messages_mcp/server.py on main confirms each gap: reads ( get_recent_messages , fuzzy_search_messages ) select m.text / m.attributedBody only, so tapbacks, threaded replies, read/unread state, delivery state, and per-message service never reach the client, and a tapback row is dropped for having no body; the read query ends in LIMIT 100 with no limit , offset , or truncation signal, and no date-range filter exists outside the rolling hours window; tool_get_chats filters chat.style = 43 ( messages.py:95-105 ), so 1:1 and business threads cannot be listed; search cannot be scoped to a contact or conversation; search_attachments matches metadata only, send_message interpolates text only, and there is no scheduler, no prompts, no contact write, and no server-side send confirmation. Baseline for the whole surface: uv run --frozen --extra dev pytest -q # 243 tests, all on the old surface Cause The read queries and formatters in mac_messages_mcp/messages.py were written against a fixed seven-column projection and a single rolling time window, and mac_messages_mcp/server.py exposed one tool per existing function. Nothing read the metadata columns, nothing paginated, and no check existed for the capabilities Messages.app automation cannot express. Fix messages.py : get_recent_messages selects service , is_read , is_sent , is_delivered , associated_message_type , and thread_originator_guid , renders them as compact tags through _message_metadata_tags , keeps tapback rows as (reaction) , and gained limit / offset paging with a next-offset note, start_date / end_date , unread_only , and a since_rowid forward cursor that ignores the hours window. Contact/chat filter resolution moved into _resolve_message_scope , shared by get_recent_messages and fuzzy_search_messages ; the latter also gained scoping, date windows, and a ranked limit with a clipping notice. list_conversations enumerates every 1:1, business, and group thread with message and unread counts; wait_for_new_messages polls a ROWID cursor, bounded to 300 seconds. New mac_messages_mcp/content.py : search_attachment_contents extracts text, PDF ( pypdf ), and image OCR ( pytesseract ) content, reports skipped rows, and names the install command for a missing extractor. New mac_messages_mcp/scheduler.py : MessageScheduler , an in-memory queue that claims due jobs under its lock and sends outside it, plus tool_schedule_message , tool_list_scheduled_messages , and tool_cancel_scheduled_message . send_message gained attachment_paths , validated and resolved before the first byte is sent, and tool_send_message gained confirm=true , which asks the human through MCP elicitation and refuses when the client cannot elicit. tool_create_contact , plus the prompts triage_unread_messages , summarize_recent_messages , and draft_reply . Capabilities Messages.app automation has no API for are refused rather than stubbed and are listed under "What it deliberately does not do" in the README: sending tapbacks, effects, or subjects; creating or editing a group chat; editing, unsending, deleting, or marking read; drafts; and editing an existing Contacts card. Verification uv run --frozen --extra dev pytest -q # 335 passed uv run --frozen --extra dev black --check . # clean uv run --frozen --extra dev isort --check-only . uv run --frozen --extra dev mypy --follow-imports=skip --disable-error-code no-any-return mac_messages_mcp/server.py uv run --frozen --extra dev python scripts/bump_version.py --check --ignore-lock uv build # wheel ships content.py and scheduler.py New coverage: tests/test_read_features.py (metadata tags, paging, date filters, cursor reads, conversation listing, scoped search, waiting), tests/test_write_features.py (attachments, contact creation, scheduling, elicitation accept/decline/unsupported), tests/test_content_search.py , and tests/test_scheduler.py . Elicitation and AppleScript are exercised through fakes; no real message was sent and no real Messages/Contacts data was read while developing or testing. title: feat: support tracking categories on manual journals
cleaned_text: feat: support tracking categories on manual journals Problem Manual journal lines cannot carry Xero tracking categories through this MCP server. The write path silently discards tracking , and the read serializer never prints it — even though the xero-node ManualJournalLine type supports it and the API returns it. The original author left explicit placeholders: src/handlers/create-xero-manual-journal.handler.ts: // TODO: tracking can be added here src/handlers/update-xero-manual-journal.handler.ts: // TODO: tracking can be added here src/tools/create/create-manual-journal.tool.ts: // TODO: TODO: tracking can be added here src/tools/update/update-manual-journal-tool.ts: // TODO: TODO: tracking can be added here This matters for anyone who tracks journal lines by category (e.g. per-property or per-department) during reconciliation — the codes simply don't come through. Changes Shared schema: extract the invoice trackingSchema ( { name, option, trackingCategoryID } ) into src/helpers/tracking-schema.ts and reuse it across create-invoice , update-invoice , and both manual-journal tools — removing the existing duplicated copy in the two invoice tools. trackingCategoryID is now optional : Xero resolves the category from name + option (and xero-node 's LineItemTracking declares every field optional), so requiring it forced callers into a list-tracking-categories round-trip for a GUID the API ignores, and gave an opaque Zod error to anyone who didn't know. Passing it explicitly is unchanged. Write: add tracking (max 2 per line) to the create/update manual-journal line schemas and forward it through both handlers to the Xero API. Read: add formatTracking , which renders a line's tracking as readable category/option text (omitting cleanly when absent), and use it in the list-manual-journals serializer and the create success response. The raw array is never printed (avoids the [object Object] pitfall). Bug fix: the create success response previously stringified its line array to [object Object],[object Object] — it never rendered line details at all. It now joins lines to text, matching the list serializer. Tests: add Vitest coverage for formatTracking and for trackingSchema (accepts { name, option } ; still accepts an explicit ID). Verification Verified end-to-end against a real Xero tenant: created a draft manual journal with tracking on each line, read it back (codes appear), updated the tracking and re-read (new codes appear), and confirmed no [object Object] leaks. Also created a journal with tracking: [{ name, option }] and no ID, and read it back with the category and option correctly resolved. npm run build , npm run lint and npm test pass. Notes Does not touch src/helpers/format-line-item.ts , so it does not collide with PR #178 (invoice/bank-tx tracking formatting). Bank transactions also lack tracking — left as a separate follow-up. Overlaps @ryanduguid's #249, which makes trackingCategoryID optional in create-invoice.tool.ts and update-invoice.tool.ts — the same two declaration sites this PR moves onto the shared helper, so whichever lands second will need a rebase. Happy to rebase on #249 if you'd prefer to take that one first. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: Return each tool result as one text block (GPT sees only the first block through OpenAI's MCP tool)
cleaned_text: Return each tool result as one text block (GPT sees only the first block through OpenAI's MCP tool) Problem Most tools answer with a header block ( Found 1 contacts: ) plus one text block per record. OpenAI's hosted MCP tool (Responses API) passes only the first text block of a result to the model. GPT sees Found 1 contacts: , Found 69 accounts: , Found 7 tax rates: and never the records: no contact ID, account code or tax type. We ran the write example from the MCP launch post, a draft invoice for a customer, on xero-mcp-server 0.0.17 (stdio, bridged to streamable HTTP), Demo Company (US), October 1, 2026, 3 runs each: Client | Before | With this change Claude Sonnet 4.6, Anthropic API | 3 of 3 | 3 of 3 GPT-5.5, OpenAI API (MCP tool) | 0 of 3 | 3 of 3 In OpenAI's own record of each call, the tool output is only the first block. We reproduced the client behaviour on a neutral test server with a two-block result, so the cause is on OpenAI's side. Of the six MCP servers we tested, this is the only one that splits results into blocks, and joining them here fixes it for every client. Change src/helpers/join-text-content.ts adds joinTextContent and withOneTextBlock , which join a result's text blocks into one (newline-separated, text unchanged). Results with a non-text block are left as they are. tool-factory.ts wraps the five registrations with it. Unit test: src/helpers/ tests /join-text-content.test.ts . 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: fix: surface Xero validation errors from stringified SDK rejections
cleaned_text: fix: surface Xero validation errors from stringified SDK rejections Summary xero-node rejects failed requests with JSON.stringify(ApiError.generateError()) , which is a string rather than an object. formatError treated any string as an unknown error, so every 4xx from Xero reached the model as "An unexpected error occurred" with no reason given. formatError now parses that string, whitelists the status and body fields, and returns Xero's ValidationErrors messages (or Detail / Message ) along with the status and type. The request headers in the payload, which include the bearer token, are never included in the output, in line with #173. Related #112 addresses validation errors on 400 responses for the object-shaped error. It conflicts with main and predates #173. This PR also covers the string-shaped rejection the SDK actually produces. Testing npm run build , npm run lint and npm test pass (19 tests, including new cases for stringified rejections, validation-error extraction and token redaction). Confirmed against a live Xero organisation that validation errors now reach the model.
