title: Maintenance status, and the gap between `main` and open community PRs
cleaned_text: Maintenance status, and the gap between main and open community PRs Hi, and thanks for publishing this server. It's been very useful. The last merge to main was on 2026-06-05, and there are now 77 open pull requests, many of them fixes for bugs reported here (validation errors being swallowed, [object Object] in output, update-bank-transaction failing with 400s, invalid manual journal lineAmountTypes , and so on). Could a maintainer say whether the project is still actively maintained, and whether there's a plan for working through the PR queue? To make the question concrete, I tried to find out what it would take to get the fixes and features I needed out of the open PRs, and ended up building a combined branch. It shows how far main has fallen behind what the community has already written. It also shows the kind of review and integration work a maintainer would face, and would keep facing as new PRs arrive: Triage: 77 open PRs, 38 shortlisted for a UK bookkeeping use case, 28 merged, plus one closed PR (#231) whose author offered to reopen it. Duplicates: 7 groups of PRs doing the same thing (e.g. four separate [object Object] fixes, three P&L fixes, two attachment implementations that register the same tool name), each needing one PR picked. Review: 3 PRs failed review, #295 and #126 as written and #200 without a locking fix (details in my comments on each). Several others add tools that make consequential writes to live books with no confirmation step. Conflicts: about 15 of the shortlisted PRs conflict with each other, mostly in shared tool files. Two pairs only work together after extra changes (#110 + #289, #216 + #296). Dependencies: xero-node is seven major versions behind (13 → 20). The upgrade (#314) inserts new positional parameters, which breaks call sites in main and in three of the PRs until adjusted. tsc catches this, but the compiled JavaScript misbehaves without any error. Result: the combined build has 79 tools against 51 on main , and passes npm ci , tsc , lint and 92 unit tests. The branch is on my fork. I'm not proposing it as an alternative to this repo or volunteering as an unofficial maintainer; it's a reference for what's ready to land. Since it exists, others may find it useful in the meantime: Branch (may occasionally be rebuilt and force-pushed ; no maintenance commitment, so pin a tag if you need stability): https://github.com/aspiers/xero-mcp-server/tree/best-of-breed Snapshot tag to pin to: https://github.com/aspiers/xero-mcp-server/tree/best-of-breed-2026-09-23-2 Even a short note from the maintainers either way would help people decide whether to wait, contribute, or fork. What's in the branch, how it was checked, and caveats Base main + #314 (xero-node 13 → 20.0.0). v20 includes the upstream fix that redacts request headers, including the bearer token, from SDK error objects. It also inserts new optional positional parameters before options in several API methods, so some PRs needed small compatibility fixes (see my comments on #187 and #296). PRs included Area | PRs Error handling / security | #305, #214, #290 Auth | #200 ( XERO_TOKEN_FILE self-refreshing token), plus my locking fixes described in https://github.com/XeroAPI/xero-mcp-server/pull/200#issuecomment-5793123449 Manual journals | #182, #181 (includes #180's code) Bank transactions | #190, #153 Output formatting | #207, #231 (closed, reopen requested) Reports | #186 (includes #198's fix) Credit notes / allocations | #187, #194, #195, #291 Invoices / bills | #216, #221, #293, #294, #296, #308, #110 + #289 (combined so date filters and where are ANDed together) Listing | #176 ( pageSize on list tools) New tools | #191 (linked transactions), #298 (general ledger journals), #145 (history & notes), #109 (attachments; without its unrelated xero-client.ts changes), #127 (invoice PDF / online URL) Left out after review: #295 (a partial line update can delete the other lines; see my comment there), #126 (package rename and stale client rewrite; see my comment there), and duplicates superseded by the PRs above (#180, #197, #215, #313, #204, #178, #198, #161, #201). AU payroll, quotes and remote-hosting PRs are out of scope for my use, so I didn't evaluate them. How it was checked An AI coding assistant reviewed each included PR's diff, and I read the results. The review looked at secret handling, network destinations, dependency and lockfile changes, and risks of corrupting accounting data. This is not a professional security audit. I exercised the read tools against a live UK organisation in token-file mode. That included the token file refreshing itself, with three server processes refreshing at the same moment. Bearer-token mode was only tested live with the v20 upgrade on its own. I have not exercised the write tools live. Caveats Several included tools make consequential writes with no confirmation step: #221 can approve, void or delete invoices #191 can delete or void linked transactions #145 adds history notes, which Xero doesn't let you edit or delete #194 deletes credit-note allocations #195 can re-date authorised credit notes Read the diffs before relying on them. A Xero lock date is a sensible safety net. Some tools need scopes the default setup doesn't request: accounting.attachments.read (#109) and accounting.journals.read (#298). With XERO_TOKEN_FILE , set XERO_TENANT_ID . Otherwise writes go to the first connected organisation. package.json still says @xeroapi/xero-mcp-server . Please don't publish it under that name. Using it git clone -b best-of-breed https://github.com/aspiers/xero-mcp-server.git cd xero-mcp-server npm ci && npm run build Then point your MCP client at node /path/to/xero-mcp-server/dist/index.js , with the same environment variables as the README. #200's README section covers the XERO_TOKEN_FILE mode.

title: feat: add XERO_TENANT_ID env override for tenant selection
cleaned_text: feat: add XERO_TENANT_ID env override for tenant selection Problem When an app or bearer token is authorised for more than one organisation, the server always operates on the first tenant returned by Xero's connections endpoint, in both authentication modes: Bearer token: MCPXeroClient.updateTenants() sets this.tenantId = this.tenants[0].tenantId Client credentials: CustomConnectionsXeroClient.requestToken() sets this.tenantId = connectionsResponse.data[0].tenantId There is no way to target any other organisation, so multi-org tokens silently read and write against whichever org happens to be first. Change Adds an optional XERO_TENANT_ID environment variable, honoured by both authentication modes via a shared helper ( src/helpers/select-tenant-id.ts ): Set and matching an authorised connection → that tenant is used. Set but not matching → the server fails with a configuration error rather than silently falling back to a different organisation. The error doesn't list the tenant IDs the credentials can reach. Matching ignores case and surrounding whitespace. Unset → behaviour is unchanged (first tenant), so this is non-breaking. Testing Unit tests for the helper, plus tests that go through both authentication modes (bearer token and Custom Connection) — npm test : 25 passed. npm run build and npm run lint clean. Docs README gains a "Selecting a tenant (multi-organisation support)" section with a config example.

title: feat: gate list-trial-balance on exact movement and YTD integrity
cleaned_text: feat: gate list-trial-balance on exact movement and YTD integrity Adds an integrity gate to list-trial-balance . It recomputes current-month Debit/Credit and as-at YTD Debit/YTD Credit totals from account rows using scaled BigInt arithmetic. Both pairs must balance exactly. Summary totals are excluded from the calculation. The gate validates required columns even when no Section follows the header, rejects unsupported row types and blocks reports with no account rows. Malformed or unbalanced reports return BLOCKED and withhold the JSON pack. PASS retains the existing report output and explicitly does not approve a close. Verification, 23 September 2026: npm test : 33 tests passed, including five incomplete or unsupported report shapes and balanced controls. npm run lint and npm run build passed. npm ci --ignore-scripts fails on the unchanged upstream lockfile, which lacks optional @emnapi test-tool entries; tests ran after a local lock repair that is not part of this PR. This PR does not change package.json or package-lock.json . No hosted checks are currently reported on this PR. No live Xero request was made. An empty report is blocked because the helper cannot establish its integrity from zero account rows.

title: feat: add bank, budget, and executive summary report tools
cleaned_text: feat: add bank, budget, and executive summary report tools Summary Adds the Accounting API reports that xero-node already exposes and that #183 called out as missing from a quarterly pack. Tools list-bank-summary — opening/cash in/cash out/closing by bank account ( fromDate , toDate ) list-budget-summary — budget vs actual ( date , periods 1–12, timeframe MONTH/QUARTER/YEAR) list-executive-summary — cash / P&L / balance-sheet snapshot ( date ) These match the existing P&L / trial balance / balance sheet tools. Not in this PR: General Ledger, GST/BAS, Cash Summary, and payroll activity reports. Those endpoints are not in xero-node v13 ( getReport* ). Attachments, fixed assets, and invoice approve/void already have other open PRs. Scopes Default Custom Connection scopes are unchanged (same lesson as journals: requesting an unapproved granular scope fails token exchange with invalid_scope ). Legacy apps: already covered by accounting.reports.read Granular apps: add accounting.reports.banksummary.read , accounting.reports.budgetsummary.read , and/or accounting.reports.executivesummary.read via XERO_SCOPES and on the Custom Connection Validation npm test — 26 passing npx tsc --noEmit npm run lint

title: feat: add repeating invoice tools (list, get, create, update, delete)

Adds the five Repeating Invoices tools requested on that issue, using the existing invoice/quote tool pattern and the xero-node Accounting API: list-repeating-invoices — filter by contact, status, or type ( ACCREC / ACCPAY ) get-repeating-invoice — fetch one template, including line items and schedule create-repeating-invoice — create a template ( DRAFT by default; AUTHORISED starts generating invoices) update-repeating-invoice — update DRAFT or AUTHORISED templates delete-repeating-invoice — set status to DELETED (Xero has no dedicated delete verb) The list endpoint is not server-paginated, so results are sliced locally to 10 per page to match the other list tools. title: Error and point to the remote MCP server instead of running the local one
cleaned_text: Error and point to the remote MCP server instead of running the local one Problem The logfire-mcp package (the local stdio MCP server) is deprecated in favour of the remote Logfire MCP server, but it is still installable from PyPI and fully functional. A working local server can mislead agents into standing it up and using it instead of the maintained remote server. Change Make the CLI exit with a message pointing to the remote server instead of starting the local one. This covers both entry points ( logfire-mcp console script and python -m logfire_mcp ), since both go through main() : The logfire-mcp package (the local stdio MCP server) is deprecated and no longer maintained. Use the remote Logfire MCP server instead: https://logfire.pydantic.dev/docs/how-to-guides/mcp-server/ Details: --version and --help still work, and --help now surfaces the deprecation notice in its description. The legacy flags ( --read-token , --base-url , --test ) are still accepted so existing invocations land on the message rather than an argparse "unrecognized arguments" error. Removed the now-dead test() / get_read_token() helpers. tests/conftest.py now imports app_factory from its real module logfire_mcp.main (it previously piggybacked on the import in main ). Added tests/test_deprecated.py asserting the CLI exits with the redirect message and that --version still works. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

title: Support sslcert / sslkey (client certificate authentication) for PostgreSQL
cleaned_text: Support sslcert / sslkey (client certificate authentication) for PostgreSQL Problem Follow-up to #293. DBHub now verifies the server certificate ( sslmode=verify-ca / verify-full + sslrootcert ), but it cannot present a client certificate. PostgreSQL servers that enforce certificate authentication in pg_hba.conf ( hostssl ... cert , or clientcert=verify-ca / verify-full ) reject the connection: FATAL: connection requires a valid client certificate The standard libpq parameters sslcert and sslkey are currently ignored. PostgresDSNParser in src/connectors/postgres/index.ts only reads sslmode and sslrootcert from the query string, and the TOML config has no matching fields. There is no workaround short of putting a TLS-terminating proxy (e.g. pgbouncer) in front of DBHub. Proposed solution Support sslcert and sslkey the same way #293 added sslrootcert , in both the DSN and the TOML source fields: postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db?sslmode=verify-ca&sslrootcert=/path/ca.crt&sslcert=/path/client.crt&sslkey=/path/client.key [[sources]] id = "dev" type = "postgres" host = "db.example.internal" database = "app" user = "app" password = "${PG_PASSWORD}" sslmode = "verify-ca" sslrootcert = "~/.certs/ca.crt" sslcert = "~/.certs/client.crt" sslkey = "~/.certs/client.key" In the connector, pass the files to node-postgres, which forwards them to Node's TLS options: poolConfig.ssl = { rejectUnauthorized: true, ...(sslrootcert && { ca: fs.readFileSync(sslrootcert, "utf-8") }), ...(sslcert && { cert: fs.readFileSync(sslcert, "utf-8") }), ...(sslkey && { key: fs.readFileSync(sslkey, "utf-8") }), }; Suggested details, mirroring the existing sslrootcert handling: src/types/config.ts : add sslcert? / sslkey? src/config/toml-loader.ts : ~/ expansion, DSN/field conflict check, file-exists/readable validation, PostgreSQL-only, and require both-or-neither Also honour them with sslmode=require (libpq sends the client certificate in every SSL mode), not only with verify-* Keys must be PEM (Node's TLS does not read DER). An encrypted key ( sslpassword ) could be a later follow-up. docs/config/toml.mdx : document the two new fields Use case We run DBHub against multiple self-hosted PostgreSQL databases across several environments, and all of them require client certificate authentication. Today we have to keep a separate MCP server per database only because DBHub cannot authenticate with a certificate. With sslcert / sslkey we could consolidate them into a single DBHub process with multiple [[sources]] . I'm happy to open a PR for this if you're open to the contribution.

title: HTTP transport: subscriptions/listen is held open but never used, so clients behind buffering proxies wait ~25s for tools
cleaned_text: HTTP transport: subscriptions/listen is held open but never used, so clients behind buffering proxies wait ~25s for tools Problem Over the HTTP transport, DBHub advertises capabilities.tools.listChanged: true . That's the MCP SDK's default once tools are registered; DBHub doesn't set it itself. But DBHub never sends notifications/tools/list_changed , and it can't: createMcpHandler builds a fresh stateless server for every request, so no server instance outlives the request that would have to carry the notification. 2026-07-28 clients take the capability at face value and open subscriptions/listen right after server/discover , a POST the server holds open as a notification stream. With DBHub that stream never carries anything. Directly against DBHub, this costs nothing. Behind a proxy that buffers responses, the held-open request does real damage. AWS API Gateway HTTP APIs, for example, don't stream: they hold the whole response, and after their 30s integration timeout they answer 503 {"message":"Service Unavailable"} themselves. And Claude Code (2.1.296) doesn't list a server's tools until subscriptions/listen resolves. What we saw DBHub 1.5.0, --transport http , behind an API Gateway HTTP API → VPC link → ECS. Our other MCP servers behind the same gateway use the same SDK v2 createMcpHandler with maxSubscriptions: 0 , and they see none of this. A new Claude Code session gets no DBHub tools for about 25s. Agents that look for the tools in that window conclude the server isn't connected. About 29% of all requests to DBHub end in the gateway's 503, and for Claude Code the ratio is a steady 4 503s per successful tools/list . That's the listen stream timing out every time. Reproduction Put a proxy in front of DBHub that buffers responses and cuts at 30s, the way API Gateway does, then point Claude Code at it. Timeline of one run: +0s server/discover -> 200 +26s POST (no mcp-method) -> 202 +26s tools/list -> 200 <- tools only now +30s tools/call -> 200 +30s subscriptions/listen -> 503 (cut at 30000ms, opened at +0s) Same run, with the proxy answering subscriptions/listen straight away with JSON-RPC -32601 Method not found : +0s server/discover -> 200 +0s subscriptions/listen -> -32601 +0s tools/list -> 200 <- tools immediately +2s, +4s, +8s subscriptions/listen -> -32601, then the client stops retrying Suggested fix Pass maxSubscriptions: 0 to createMcpHandler in src/server.ts . DBHub never emits notifications, so it loses nothing, and the SDK then refuses subscriptions/listen in-band instead of holding it open: const mcpHandler = createMcpHandler(createServer, { maxSubscriptions: 0, onerror: logMcpError("handler"), }); The SDK also reports each refusal through onerror ( subscriptions/listen refused: subscription limit reached (0) ). That message is the configured answer, not a failure, so logMcpError should probably skip it. If list-changed notifications are ever wired up for TOML hot reload, the limit could become a setting then. Happy to open a PR. Note on #472 This replaces #472. Its keep-alive diagnosis was wrong: we deployed that workaround and the 503 rate didn't change. The 503s we saw were the listen stream reaching the gateway timeout, and the access log records each request's start time, which made them look fast.

title: fix(http): refuse subscriptions/listen instead of holding it open
cleaned_text: fix(http): refuse subscriptions/listen instead of holding it open Fixes #474 Problem Over the HTTP transport the SDK advertises tools.listChanged once tools are registered, so 2026-07-28 clients open subscriptions/listen right after server/discover and wait on it before listing tools. DBHub never emits change notifications ( createMcpHandler builds a fresh stateless server per request), so that stream never carries anything. Directly against DBHub this is harmless. Behind a buffering proxy such as AWS API Gateway, the held-open POST is cut at the gateway timeout with a 503, and Claude Code sees no DBHub tools for ~25s per session. Fix Pass maxSubscriptions: 0 to createMcpHandler in src/server.ts . The SDK then refuses the listen in-band (JSON-RPC -32603 Subscription limit reached , HTTP 200) and clients fall back to plain polling immediately. The SDK reports each refusal through onerror . With the limit at 0 that is the configured answer, so logMcpError skips that message instead of logging an error per client connect. A code comment notes that the limit should become a setting if list-changed notifications are ever wired up for TOML hot reload. Test Adds an integration test in src/ tests /json-rpc-integration.test.ts that sends a 2026-07-28 subscriptions/listen and asserts an immediate application/json response carrying the -32603 error, with nothing logged. Without the fix the same request gets a text/event-stream the server holds open, and the test fails on the content type. Verified locally: tsc --noEmit clean, the JSON-RPC and plugin-consistency test files pass. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code https://claude.ai/code/session_01MP8xzhrNEUicuyjXqGdK44 _Generated by Claude Code_

title: HTTP transport: default 5s keep-alive causes intermittent 502/503s behind load balancers and API gateways
cleaned_text: HTTP transport: default 5s keep-alive causes intermittent 502/503s behind load balancers and API gateways Problem src/server.ts creates the HTTP server with http.createServer(app) and keeps Node's defaults: keepAliveTimeout = 5s , headersTimeout = 60s . Proxies that pool upstream connections often hold them idle for longer than 5s. AWS API Gateway via VPC link does, ALB defaults to 60s, and so does nginx with keepalive . When such a proxy writes a request into a socket DBHub is already closing, it answers the client itself with a 502/503. DBHub never sees that request, so nothing shows up in its logs. What we saw DBHub 1.2.1 with --transport http , behind an AWS API Gateway HTTP API → VPC link → ECS. 1.5.0 creates its server the same way. About 25–30% of requests to DBHub got the gateway's own 503 {"message":"Service Unavailable"} , typically on the request right after a successful initialize / tools/list . It wasn't the gateway's 30s integration timeout: the client was already reconnecting a few seconds later. Our other MCP servers behind the same gateway set keepAliveTimeout = 65s and saw close to none. Some MCP clients (Claude Code) drop a server whose startup requests fail, so DBHub's tools never load for them. Reproduction Start DBHub with --transport http on the default port, then keep one connection idle past 5s: const http = require("node:http"); const agent = new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 1 }); const t0 = Date.now(); agent.on("free", (socket) => { socket.once("close", () => console.log( server closed idle socket at +${((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1)}s )); }); const send = () => new Promise((resolve) => { const req = http.request( { host: "localhost", port: 8080, path: "/mcp", method: "POST", agent, headers: { "content-type": "application/json", accept: "application/json, text/event-stream" } }, (res) => { res.resume(); res.on("end", () => resolve( ${res.statusCode} reused=${req.reusedSocket} )); }); req.on("error", (e) => resolve( ERR ${e.code} )); req.end(JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "tools/list" })); }); (async () => { console.log(await send()); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 10_000)); console.log(await send()); })(); On 1.5.0 this prints: 200 reused=false server closed idle socket at +6.0s 200 reused=false With the timeouts raised, the socket survives the 10s idle and the second request reuses it ( reused=true ). A proxy that writes into the socket around the moment DBHub closes it gets a reset, and that reset is what reaches clients as the 502/503. Suggested fix Keep the server's idle timeout longer than the proxy's. The AWS ALB docs ask for a backend keep-alive longer than the load balancer's idle timeout, which defaults to 60s: const httpServer = http.createServer(app); httpServer.keepAliveTimeout = 65_000; httpServer.headersTimeout = 66_000; The values could also be made configurable (e.g. --http-keep-alive-timeout / DBHUB_HTTP_KEEP_ALIVE_TIMEOUT ), but a higher default alone fixes the setups above. Happy to open a PR for it. Workaround Preload this with node --require ./keep-alive.cjs dist/index.js … : const http = require("node:http"); const listen = http.Server.prototype.listen; http.Server.prototype.listen = function (...args) { this.keepAliveTimeout = 65_000; this.headersTimeout = 66_000; return listen.apply(this, args); };

title: fix(http): raise keep-alive timeout above proxy idle timeouts
cleaned_text: fix(http): raise keep-alive timeout above proxy idle timeouts Fixes #472 Problem The HTTP transport created its server with http.createServer(app) and kept Node's default keepAliveTimeout of 5s. Proxies that pool upstream connections (AWS ALB, API Gateway VPC links, nginx keepalive ) hold them idle for 60s. When such a proxy writes a request into a socket Node is closing at that moment, the proxy answers the client with its own 502/503 and the request never reaches DBHub's logs. Fix Set keepAliveTimeout to 65s and headersTimeout to 66s so the proxy is always the side that closes an idle connection. Node requires headersTimeout to be strictly greater than keepAliveTimeout , hence the 1s gap. The values are hard-coded on purpose; no new flag or env var. src/utils/http-keep-alive.ts : constants plus configureHttpKeepAlive(server) with the rationale in comments src/server.ts : call it right after http.createServer(app) src/utils/ tests /http-keep-alive.test.ts : asserts the values are applied and that the headers timeout stays above keep-alive, so a future refactor of the server setup can't silently drop them Verification Ran the reproduction script from the issue against the built server. Before, the server closed the idle socket at ~6s and the second request got a fresh connection. After: 200 reused=false 200 reused=true The socket survives the 10s idle and the second request reuses it. pnpm exec vitest run on the new test plus the HTTP bind-host and JSON-RPC integration suites: 17 passed. The connector integration suites need Docker and were not run here. 🤖 Generated with Claude Code https://claude.ai/code/session_013piqks7dS3HsaAKC6YVWLN _Generated by Claude Code_

title: Feature: per-source `[sources.session]` settings applied on each new connection
cleaned_text: Feature: per-source [sources.session] settings applied on each new connection Follow-up to #449. This proposes the shape you suggested there; I would follow your design on the details. [[sources]] id = "prod_mysql" dsn = "mysql://..." [sources.session] transaction_read_only = 1 lock_wait_timeout = 5 [[sources]] id = "prod_pg" dsn = "postgres://..." [sources.session] lock_timeout = "5s" Why a table rather than more options Session-level knobs have been added one option at a time: search_path (#244), charset / collation (#354), timezone , and max_execution_time via query_timeout (#465). The two needs below would add two more, with names that differ per engine. One table ends that. It also meets the three points in #449: no SQL in config, applied once per new connection rather than per execution, and the values are meant to stay on the connection as its defaults. Concrete needs Our sources are shared production databases with no dedicated replica for DBHub. 1. MySQL: transaction_read_only = 1 . The source is used only by read-only tools, and we want DDL stopped by the server too. As src/utils/readonly-transaction.ts notes, DDL ends the per-execution START TRANSACTION READ ONLY with an implicit commit, so today only the classifier stops it. The deadline does not help: a DROP TABLE takes milliseconds. Checked on mysql:8.0 and mariadb:10.11 : Statement | START TRANSACTION READ ONLY | + SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY CREATE TABLE | OK, persists after ROLLBACK | ERR 1792 ALTER / DROP / TRUNCATE / RENAME | — | ERR 1792 2. MySQL lock_wait_timeout / PostgreSQL lock_timeout . We run migrations while serving traffic, so a SELECT can queue behind an ALTER TABLE ; MySQL's default limit is one year, PostgreSQL's none. We want a long query_timeout for heavy analytical reads but a lock wait that gives up in a few seconds; one deadline cannot express both. Proposed behaviour Scope : we run MySQL and PostgreSQL; other engines are your call. Applying : MySQL runs one escaped SET SESSION in the #465 hook; PostgreSQL passes -c name=value startup options like search_path . Validation (minimal) : names must be identifiers (PostgreSQL also allows ext.name ); values must be strings, numbers or booleans. Names DBHub already sets are rejected with a pointer to the dedicated option ( statement_timeout , search_path , max_execution_time ). Anything else is the operator's call. Failure : unlike the max_execution_time hook, which ignores a failed SET , a failure here should stop startup, so a typo cannot leave the source silently unprotected. PostgreSQL already fails at connect. Questions Which engines should the first version cover? On MySQL, is failing startup on a rejected SET acceptable? Happy to send a PR with tests and docs once the shape looks right.

title: fix(sqlite): run multi-statement batches in source order
cleaned_text: fix(sqlite): run multi-statement batches in source order Summary The SQLite connector splits a multi-statement batch into writes and reads and runs all writes before any reads. A read that comes before a write in the batch therefore sees the write's effects: SELECT a AS before_delete FROM t; -- t has 3 rows DELETE FROM t; SELECT count(*) AS after_delete FROM t; returns DELETE (3) , then before_delete: [] , then after_delete: 0 . The first SELECT comes back empty and the result sets are reordered. PostgreSQL (and MySQL/MariaDB via native multi-statement) run in source order. The split dates from when writes were batched through .exec() for speed (16e870b). Writes now run one at a time via prepare().run() , so it no longer buys anything. This PR runs each statement in the order written and branches on returnsRows() per statement. The per-statement PRAGMA query_only = ON re-assert and the maxRows truncation probe are unchanged. I updated should handle maxRows in multi-statement execution , which asserted the writes-first order. If that order is intended, happy to close this and keep the behavior documented instead. Test plan [x] New should execute multi-statement batches in source order (fails on main, passes here) [x] Updated should handle maxRows in multi-statement execution , which asserted the writes-first order [x] pnpm test:unit : 1201/1201 [x] sqlite, multi-sqlite, execute-sql and json-rpc integration tests pass [x] Read-only mode still rejects SELECT ...; PRAGMA query_only = OFF; DELETE ...

title: All 10 tools return internal error (-32603) instead of isError for missing API token
cleaned_text: All 10 tools return internal error (-32603) instead of isError for missing API token When BANKLESS_API_TOKEN is not set, all 10 tools return a JSON-RPC internal error ( -32603 ) instead of a proper tool error ( isError: true ). This means agents receive a protocol-level crash instead of a recoverable error message. FAIL read_contract internal error: Authentication Failed: BANKLESS_API_TOKEN environment variable is not set FAIL get_proxy internal error: Authentication Failed: BANKLESS_API_TOKEN environment variable is not set ... (all 10 tools) Why it matters: MCP distinguishes between: isError: true : the tool ran but something went wrong. The error message is user-facing and the agent can recover (e.g. prompt the user for the token). -32603 : something broke inside the server. The agent treats this as a fatal error and can't help the user. The error message itself is excellent ("Authentication Failed: BANKLESS_API_TOKEN environment variable is not set"). It just needs to be returned as a tool error instead of an internal error. Suggested fix: Instead of throwing/rejecting, return the error through the MCP tool result: if (!process.env.BANKLESS_API_TOKEN) { return { content: [{ type: "text", text: "Authentication Failed: BANKLESS_API_TOKEN environment variable is not set" }], isError: true }; } Additionally: the network parameter appears in 7 tools but has no enum listing valid values. Agents must guess whether it's "ethereum", "eth", "1", or "mainnet". Adding enum: ["ethereum", "polygon", "arbitrum", ...] to the schema would reduce agent errors. Found via: mcp-assert audit --server "npx -y @bankless/onchain-mcp" and mcp-assert lint . If you want to add CI regression testing for your server: github.com/blackwell-systems/mcp-assert.

title: fix: email threading with RFC 5322 compliance and automatic References chain
cleaned_text: fix: email threading with RFC 5322 compliance and automatic References chain Problem Email replies sent via send_email tool weren't threading properly in Gmail's UI. Emails appeared as separate messages instead of being grouped in a conversation thread. Root Cause After systematic testing and header analysis: Missing angle brackets : Message-IDs in In-Reply-To and References headers lacked RFC 5322 required angle brackets Incomplete References chain : Only immediate parent Message-ID included, not full conversation chain Manual chain building : Required users to manually build References chain (unlike Gmail/Thunderbird auto-behavior) Solution 1. RFC 5322 Compliance Add angle brackets <> around Message-IDs in threading headers Support explicit references parameter for custom chains Update both simple and nodemailer email creation 2. Automatic References Chain Building When replying ( inReplyTo set) without explicit references : Automatically fetches complete thread via threadId Extracts all Message-IDs in chronological order Builds proper References chain matching Gmail behavior Graceful fallback if threadId missing or API fails Changes src/index.ts: Added references parameter to SendEmailSchema Extract Message-ID and References headers in read_email Auto-build References chain from threadId when replying Include threading headers in output for debugging src/utl.ts: Add angle brackets around Message-IDs Support explicit references chain or fallback to inReplyTo Update nodemailer configuration Technical Details Before (broken): In-Reply-To: abc123@example.com References: abc123@example.com After (working): In-Reply-To: References: Usage Simple (automatic): // References chain built automatically from threadId { inReplyTo: "abc123@example.com", threadId: "thread123", // references auto-built! } Advanced (manual override): { inReplyTo: "xyz789@example.com", references: " " // explicit chain used } Testing [x] Code builds successfully [x] Manual testing: emails thread correctly in Gmail UI [x] Manual testing: emails thread correctly in Thunderbird [x] Automatic chain building verified working [x] No breaking changes to existing functionality Impact Fixes : Email threading for Gmail API users Backwards Compatible : Yes (new features are optional) Breaking Changes : None Behavior : Matches Gmail/Thunderbird automatic threading References RFC 5322: Internet Message Format Gmail API Threading Documentation
